| **bit-identical** greedy text + last-token logits | yes | byte-identical at 32 (timers on and off) and 128 tokens | **met** |
| `[OPTIME] deltanet` | **≤ 60 ms/token** | **63.87** | **NOT MET** |
| rotating median vs 4.04 / 4.09 | reported, no threshold | **4.19 → 4.27 (+1.9%)**, warm-identical 5.315 → 5.495 (+3.4%) — but this campaign's pristine reads 4.19, not 4.04/4.09 | **reported; moves the right way** |

**Why the ≤ 60 leg is not reachable by this mechanism, and why that was true
before the first run.** The parts of `deltanet` that Q1 does not touch measure
`dn-proj` 52.84 + `dn-recur` 9.19 + `dn-rest` 0.30 = **62.33 ms/token**. Even
with all three of Q1's loops reduced to exactly zero, `deltanet` cannot go
below ~62.3. The 60 threshold was derived from the same ~15.9 estimate as the
−8 to −13 expectation, and that estimate counted the already-parallel
recurrence as serial scalar; **step 0 — which the gate itself mandates —
is what exposed the contradiction, and it did so before the pragma was
written.** Measured against the corrected bucket the change took **80% of the
7.98 ms it could reach** (7.98 → 1.56).

This is §G4's case and §Q3's case a third time: a per-op threshold set from an
arithmetic estimate, found unreachable by the measurement the item was required
to take first. **Reported, not tuned. Nothing was adjusted after the numbers
came in, and no threshold in the roadmap was edited to fit them.** The merge
decision is arbitration's (§Q3's `### Arbitration` is the precedent).

### What this changes for the roadmap

- **`deltanet`'s floor is ~62 ms/token** until the dense projections leave the
  CPU. `dn-proj` is 52.84 ms/token for 4.16 GB = **78.7 GB/s**, at this box's
  8-thread DRAM ceiling (70.9 GB/s measured, so part of it is L3-served): it is
  Q7's bucket and no CPU-side change touches it.
- **`dn-recur` (9.19 ms/token) is also at the memory ceiling, not the thread
  ceiling.** Its state is 48 × 128 × 128 × 4 B = 3.146 MB/layer and the loop
  makes four traversals of it (decay read+write, `k·state` read, rank-1 update
  read+write, `q·state` read) ≈ 18.9 MB/layer = **680 MB/token; 9.19 ms is
  74 GB/s**. More threads cannot help it. What could: **folding the
  `state[cell] *= alpha` decay into the `k·state` traversal**, which removes one
  full read+write of 3.146 MB/layer — a third of the traffic, ~**−2.5 ms/token**
  — and can be done bit-identically, because `previous` accumulates over `d` in
  the same order and `(s*α)*k == k*(s*α)` in float. That is a **new item, not
  Q1's scope** (Q1 names the conv, the q/k norm and the output RMSNorm); it is
  proposed for the roadmap as the next cheap DeltaNet win.
- **§Q2 should be expected to beat its own isolated ratio**, for the reason in
  "attenuation runs the other way" above. Its `gr-read` estimate (~9.9 ms/token
  of serial scalar) is the same arithmetic-subtraction shape as Q1's ~15.9 was,
  so **its step-0 sub-timer may re-size it in either direction** — Q1's did, by
  a factor of two.

### Arbitration (Fable, 2026-09-12): accepted and merged, the gate corrected — and this is NOT §Q3's finding, so it is not filed as the same lesson

Merged into `hot-expert-tier` (the merge commit carries the numbers above).
Accepted on three grounds: the change is bit-identical at every oracle it was
put to; it took 80% of the bucket it names (7.98 → 1.56 ms/token), against an
evidence base (§G4 step 3 at 2.7×, §G8 at 2.43×) that predicted 3.0–3.3; and
the leg it missed was unreachable by *any* implementation of this item, because
62.33 ms/token of `deltanet` is work the item does not name. Against rejecting:
the six milliseconds are real, the diff is one region in `c/qwen38_core.h`,
and nothing downstream (Q2, Q7, the new item below) re-orders this function.

**Why this is a different finding from §Q3's, and the record should keep them
apart.** In Q3 the *target* was measured correctly (the shared expert is
7.2 ms/token) and the *mechanism's yield model* was wrong: a reorder cannot
absorb more than `Σ_l min(shared_l, wait_l)`, 54%, and no reorder can do
better. The fix for that class is to write the mechanism's ceiling into the
gate as a formula. In Q1 the *mechanism's yield model* was right — conservative,
even: the pattern delivered 5× where the evidence said 2.5× — and the *target*
was mis-measured: §Q-PROFILE's "~15.9 serial scalar" was an arithmetic
subtraction that swept the already-parallel recurrence (9.29) into the serial
column, in the same row whose prose said the recurrence was parallel. The fix
for that class is procedural and already existed in half: step 0's sub-timer
is mandatory and it fired; what was missing is that **step 0's output must
include the re-derived gate, written into the record before the candidate is
built**. Re-deriving a threshold from a measurement taken *before* any
candidate number exists is not tuning; keeping a threshold that the step-0
measurement has already shown to be unreachable is a formality. That rule is
now in the roadmap (the "(est.)" paragraph above the Track Q table) and
binds Q2, whose "~9.9 (est.)" is the same subtraction.

**What the gate should have read, and is now recorded as:** step 0 done and
the bucket re-derived from it; bit-identical; **the three loops the item names
(`dn-conv` + `dn-qknorm` + `dn-gnorm`) down by at least half their step-0
figure, i.e. ≤ 4.0 ms/token** — half is the same judgment floor §Q3's
arbitration set, and it sits below what the evidence base predicted (3.0–3.3),
so the item cannot pass on the floor and fail on its own evidence; equivalently
`[OPTIME] deltanet` ≤ 66.3 (the 62.33 the item cannot touch, plus 4.0); the
untouched sub-buckets flat, so the saving is work removed and not moved; the
token down by the bucket's delta within the repeat spread. **Met at 1.56 /
63.87 / `dn-recur` −0.10 / step −6.02 against `deltanet` −6.35.** `dn-proj`
reads +0.58 in the table, but its pristine column is the step-0 binary from a
campaign 0.9 ms/token offset from this one (the section says so); inside the
paired campaign the touched loops account for the whole `deltanet` delta
(7.98 − 1.56 = 6.42 against 6.35).

**On the rotating pristine reading 4.19 against §Q-REBASE's 4.04/4.09.** Not a
regression, and not this item's. §Q-REBASE's rows are a *different binary*
(pre-Q3); Q3 moved the rotating mean +1.7% (4.045 → 4.115) and the same
post-Q3 binary reads 4.19 here — a further +1.8% on unchanged code, with its
warm-identical at 5.32/5.31 against §Q3's 5.30/5.33 (0.3%). The row that
includes disk service moved and the row that excludes it did not; the campaign
started with GLM fully evicted and ~146 GB of page cache free for Qwen's
misses, which is the direction the offset points. That is `MEASURING.md`'s
"half a disk benchmark" and the standing rule already covers it: **the
rotating row is read as a pair inside one campaign, never against another
campaign's pristine** — which this section did. §Q-REBASE's 4.04/4.09 is a
historical row now, not the pristine for Q2's serving A/B; Q2 takes its own
pristine rows the way Q1 did.

**The `dn-recur` finding is logged as a named item, Q10, with one correction
to its sizing.** The section above reads 9.19 ms/token as "four traversals of
3.146 MB/layer = 680 MB/token = 74 GB/s, at the memory ceiling". A head's state
is 128 × 128 × 4 B = **64 KB**, and this CPU has **512 KB of L2 per core**
(4 MiB / 8, `lscpu`), so after the first traversal the other three are
L2-served and the DRAM traffic is one read and one write of the state per
layer — ~226 MB/token, ~25 GB/s, nowhere near the ceiling. The loop is then
more likely bound by its two **`d`-inner strided reductions** (`previous` and
`current`: stride `VD` × 4 B = 512 B, 128 dependent adds per output, no
vectorisation across `value`) than by bandwidth. The same restructuring
answers both readings — fold the decay into the `k·state` pass (compute
`fl(s·α)` on the fly and again in the rank-1 update as the addend, which
contraction cannot touch, so the decay pass disappears: 6 → 4 traffic units,
the section's "a third"), and fold `q·state` into the rank-1 update with `d`
outer and `value` inner (4 → 3, and the `d`-order of every `current[value]`
accumulation is preserved) — but the expected delta differs by reading (−2.5
on the bandwidth reading, more on the latency one), so its step 0 is the
measurement that says which: the recurrence in `rome_dnbench.c` with the state
L2-hot against cold, and `perf stat`'s cycles against bytes. Bit-identity is by
construction only if FMA contraction is the same in both forms; the
microbenchmark's oracle and the logits decide, not the argument. Not built
here; the row in the roadmap has the rest.

## Q2 step 0 (2026-09-12): the gated residual's split, measured — and the gate re-derived from it BEFORE the candidate was built

The roadmap rule added at Q1's arbitration, applied for the first time to the
row it was written for. Nothing is parallelised in this section: it is the
sub-timer, the isolated harness, and the arithmetic that turns the roadmap's
provisional `[OPTIME] gr-read ≤ 20` into a threshold this item's mechanism can
actually be judged against. The candidate is measured in §Q2 below.

`c/qwen38_core.h` only (six counters inside `q38_gr_read`) plus the new
`tools/hot-expert/rome_grbench.c`. Nothing shared with `glm53` is touched.
Step-0 binary vs pristine: **last-token logits byte-identical** (993 280 bytes)
at 32 tokens with the timers off and on, and greedy text identical — the
counters are on the serial path and change no arithmetic.

### The sub-timer split (decode only, fresh process, 3 repeats, medians)

Same regime as §Q-PROFILE / §Q3 / §Q1 (`q2_chain.sh`, a copy of `q1_chain.sh`):
3 GPUs, tier `14673 of 21858` (dev0 24.4/25.7 GB) in every run, cap 512, 80
greedy tokens, `datapoint.py`'s rotating prompt 1, 8 threads pinned, routing
history frozen to a fresh copy per run, 131 shards asserted 100% resident
before every run. Pristine = `hot-expert-tier` @ `41065e4` (Q1's merge).

| row | §Q-PROFILE's estimate | measured, median | what it is |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `gr-rms` | } | **1.06** | Q2's target: 4 × `q38_rms0` over H=2560, serial |
| `gr-down` | } ~16.9 = the two | **9.05** | the W=10240 → R=320 matmul, 8 threads |
| `gr-lowsilu` | } 10240×320 matmuls | **0.24** | 320 `silu`, serial, NOT named by Q2 |
| `gr-up` | } | **8.48** | the R=320 → W=10240 matmul, 8 threads |
| `gr-mix` | } "~9.9 serial scalar" | **6.56** | Q2's main target: 10 240 sigmoids/site |
| `gr-inject` | } | **0.68** | the W → C=4 matmul + 4 sigmoids, NOT named |
| `gr-rest` | — | **0.66** | three `falloc`/`free` pairs + the `memset` |

Per-run spread: `gr-rms` 1.06/1.07/1.05, `gr-mix` 6.56/6.48/6.67, `gr-down`
9.17/9.05/8.96, `gr-up` 8.48/8.47/8.52, `gr-lowsilu` 0.23/0.24/0.24,
`gr-inject` 0.68/0.67/0.69, `gr-rest` 0.66/0.64/0.66, `gr-read`
26.85/26.62/26.79 against the pristine's 26.62/26.61/26.86. The six counters
partition the bucket (parts sum 26.73 against the 26.79 median). The sub-timers
cost **+0.17 ms/token** on `gr-read` with `COLI_TIMERS=1` and nothing when it
is unset.

**The two loops Q2 names are 7.62 ms/token, not ~9.9** — 1.06 + 6.56. Where the
missing 2.3 went, and it is a different mistake from Q1's: the estimate was
`gr-read − (the two matmuls' bandwidth arithmetic)` = 26.7 − 16.9, and the
matmuls actually measure **18.2** (9.05 + 8.48 + most of `gr-inject`), while
0.90 of the remainder is serial scalar work the item does **not** name
(`gr-lowsilu` 0.24 and `gr-rest` 0.66 — and §G10 explicitly forbids touching the
allocations that make up `gr-rest`: its malloc-removal half changed GCC's
rounding on GLM and was reverted). So unlike Q1 — where 58% of the estimate was
one already-parallel loop — here the estimate was simply 23% optimistic in the
denominator and swept two unnamed serial fragments into the item's column.
**The 4.05× §G10 got on GLM's `coli_hc_pre` is not available on the whole of
this bucket either**, because 1.06 of the 7.62 is a four-iteration loop at
decode (C=4), where four threads is the ceiling.

### The isolated microbenchmark (`tools/hot-expert/rome_grbench.c`)

97 call sites per token at the engine's decode shapes (H=2560, C=4, W=10240,
R=320, S=1), the loop bodies copied verbatim from `q38_gr_read`/`q38_rms0`/
`q38_sigmoid`/`q38_matmul_bf16`, 8 threads pinned, rig lock held, no engine
running. **No argument with the "pools bigger than L3" rule here:** the default
configuration allocates one distinct weight set per site — 1.22 GB/token of
BF16, ten times the 128 MB L3 — which is exactly what the engine streams; the
L3-hot configuration (all 97 sites sharing one 13.2 MB set) is reported only to
show how much of the result is the weight stream. Its own oracle runs first:
4 tokens × 97 sites, `memcmp` on the internal `norm`, on `mixed` and on
`inject`. **All four arms BIT-IDENTICAL.**

| arm (ms/token) | rms | mix | rms+mix | down+up | TOTAL |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| serial (today) | 1.518 / 1.520 | 7.421 / 7.409 | **8.94 / 8.93** | 17.36 / 18.33 | 27.33 / 28.28 |
| **rms par-b + mix par-d** | **0.805 / 0.821** | **1.558 / 1.634** | **2.36 / 2.46** | 18.33 / 18.82 | 21.68 / 22.28 |
| rms par-split + mix par-d | 1.536 / 1.384 | 1.647 / 1.488 | 3.18 / 2.87 | 18.79 / 17.74 | 23.00 / 21.59 |
| mix par-d only | 1.524 / 1.525 | 1.456 / 1.412 | 2.98 / 2.94 | 17.61 / 17.35 | 21.56 / 21.24 |
| rms par-b only | 0.795 / 0.785 | 7.386 / 7.354 | 8.18 / 8.14 | 17.34 / 17.32 | 26.56 / 26.57 |

Two repeats, both shown. **`rms par-split` is rejected on this measurement and
is not kept as a knob**: computing the four `r`s in one `omp for` and then
applying them over all 10 240 elements in a second one (8-way instead of 4-way
on the cheap half) is *slower* than parallelising the four calls as they stand
— 1.38–1.54 against 0.79–0.82 — because the extra barrier and the second pass's
`z/H` indexing cost more than the four-way-to-eight-way gain on a pass that is
three streams of 40 KB. The shipping arm is therefore **`rms` parallel over the
hyper-columns + `mix` parallel over `d`**, each keeping its own reduction order.

**The harness reproduces the engine's bucket to 2%** (27.33 isolated against
26.62 in-engine, with `down+up` 17.4–18.3 against 17.5), which is the strongest
validation any Track-Q microbenchmark has had. Note it runs the *other* way
from §Q1's finding: the isolated serial figures are **higher** than the engine's
(1.52 vs 1.06 on rms, 7.42 vs 6.56 on mix), so on this op there is no inverse
attenuation to collect and **§Q1's "§Q2 should beat its own isolated ratio" does
not hold** — the ratios are what to expect, not a floor. That is what step 0 is
for, and it is the second half of Q1's advice ("its step 0 may re-size it in
either direction") coming true.

### The corrected gate, derived here, before the candidate exists

Untouched by this item: `gr-down` 9.05 + `gr-up` 8.48 + `gr-lowsilu` 0.24 +
`gr-inject` 0.68 + `gr-rest` 0.66 = **19.11 ms/token**.

**`[OPTIME] gr-read ≤ 20` is unreachable by this item's mechanism, and this is
provable before a pragma is written.** The two named loops cannot go below their
thread counts: `gr-rms` is four-way at decode (C=4, S=1) so ≥ 1.06/4 = 0.27, and
`gr-mix` is eight-way so ≥ 6.56/8 = 0.82. With **zero** fork/join overhead the
floor is 19.11 + 0.27 + 0.82 = **20.20 ms/token**. The 20 came from the same
"~9.9 (est.)" the sub-timer has just measured at 7.62, and it sits 0.2 ms below
the mechanism's absolute ceiling — Q1's ≤ 60 all over again, and the reason the
roadmap now requires this paragraph.

**Corrected gate for §Q2, on the same arithmetic Q1's and Q3's arbitrations
used (half the step-0 bucket, which is the judgment floor both set):**

1. **Bit-identical**: greedy text and last-token logits byte-identical against
   the pristine at 32 tokens (timers off and on) and at 128 tokens, plus
   `rome_grbench.c`'s own oracle. No tolerance, no knob — this item changes no
   arithmetic.
2. **The two loops the item names, `gr-rms` + `gr-mix`, down by at least half
   their step-0 figure: ≤ 3.81 ms/token.** Equivalently `[OPTIME] gr-read`
   **≤ 22.9** (19.11 untouched + 3.81). Half sits well below what the evidence
   predicts (the isolated ratios give 1.9–2.1, a 72–75% cut), so the item cannot
   pass on the floor and fail on its own evidence.
3. **The untouched sub-buckets flat within the repeat spread** (`gr-down`,
   `gr-up`, `gr-lowsilu`, `gr-inject`, `gr-rest`), so the saving is work removed
   and not work moved.
4. **The token down by the bucket's delta within the repeat spread.**
5. Rotating median and warm-identical reported as a **pair inside this
   campaign**, two repeats each side; no threshold (the effect is ~3% of the
   token and §Q1 measured a ±3% campaign offset on the rotating row alone).
6. If `gr-rms` does **not** fall in-engine — 97 extra fork/joins per token
   against a 1.06 ms serial loop is the one place this item could lose — the rms
   half is rejected, deleted and reported, and the mix half is re-measured
   alone. Stated here so the choice is a measurement and not a post-hoc one.

**Expected delta, re-derived:** `gr-rms` 1.06 → 0.27 + ρ and `gr-mix` 6.56 →
0.82 + ρ, with ρ the region cost (§Q1 measured 5.3 µs per region in-engine =
0.51 ms/token over 97 sites; `rome_grbench` implies ≈4.4 µs). That is
**−5.3 to −5.7 ms/token** on `gr-read` and the same on the token, landing
`gr-read` at **21.1–21.5**. The roadmap's **−5 to −8** is therefore reachable at
its low end only: **−6.5 is this mechanism's absolute ceiling** (both loops at
their thread counts, zero overhead), and −8 was never available. Said before the
candidate was built, not after.

## Q2 (2026-09-12): the gated residual's serial tail — the sigmoid mix parallelised, bit-identical, −5.08 ms/token on the bucket and −5.31 on the token; the rms half measured, REJECTED and deleted; the gate met (and `gr-read ≤ 20` was shown unreachable by step 0, before the candidate was built)

§G10's `coli_hc_pre` pattern ported to `qwen38-vk`. `q38_gr_read` runs at 97
sites per token and had two single-threaded scalar loops in it: four

hyper-column) and a `C=4 × H=2560` sigmoid mix (10 240 `expf` per site,
≈994k per token). **One of the two ships.** The mix now runs
`#pragma omp parallel for collapse(2)` over (s,d) with its inner `for b<C` sum
still serial inside one iteration; the four `q38_rms0` calls stay serial,
because parallelising them *moves* their cost into `q38_gr_apply` instead of
removing it (measured below, twice).

`c/qwen38_core.h` only — the two pragma-and-comment hunks plus the six step-0

both sides of every run), so GLM-5.3 was not rebuilt and does not need
re-measuring — same scope as §Q3 and §Q1. All four `qwen38` C tests exit 0 on
the candidate; both engines build clean.

**Step 0 is its own section above** (`## Q2 step 0`): the sub-timer split, the
isolated harness, and the corrected gate, all written into the record before
this candidate was built. The short version: the two loops the item names are

is **unreachable by this mechanism** (19.11 of the bucket is work the item does
not touch, and the two loops cannot go below 0.27 + 0.82 at four and eight
threads, so the floor is 20.20 even with zero fork/join overhead).

### The rms half, rejected on measurement and deleted

The item names both loops, and both were built. The second one does not earn
its place. Measured in ONE campaign with a probe knob (`Q38_GR_RMS_PAR`, on the
throwaway branch `perf/q2-mixonly-probe`, deleted after it answered):

| arm | gr-read | gr-rms | gr-mix | **gr-apply** | step |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| pristine | 26.81 | 1.07 | 6.56 | **0.18** | 179.29 |
| rms par-b + mix par-d | 21.47 | 0.82 | 1.43 | **0.53** | 174.65 |
| **mix par-d only (ships)** | 21.80 | 1.07 | 1.44 | **0.17** | 174.76 |

Medians of three repeats each, decode only, same campaign, same tier.
**`gr-apply` — a bucket this item does not touch — rises 0.18 → 0.53 whenever
the rms loop is parallel**, reproducibly to ±0.01 across three repeats in two
separate campaigns, and returns to 0.17 the moment the knob turns the loop back
to serial. The mechanism is cache coherence, not arithmetic: the rms loop
**reads** all 40 KB of `hyper` and four threads pull it into four private L2s;
`q38_gr_apply` then **writes** all 40 KB of it from one thread, which on this
4-CCX EPYC 7F32 pays cross-CCX invalidation for lines it used to find in its
own cache. The rms half wins 0.33 in `gr-read` and gives back 0.35 in
`gr-apply`; on the token it is **174.65 against 174.76, zero within the spread**
(0.19 and 0.57). A change with no measured token delta that triples a
neighbouring bucket does not ship, so the pragma is deleted rather than kept as
a knob, and this paragraph is the record of the rejection.

**It is not wrong, it is early.** `q38_gr_apply` is itself a serial scalar loop
(0.15–0.18 ms/token over 96 sites, `hyper[b*H+d] += a*block[d]`, trivially
parallel over (b,d) with no reduction at all). Parallelise it and the
invalidation is paid eight ways instead of one, after which the rms half's 0.33
is free and `gr-apply`'s own 0.18 shrinks as well. That is a **new item, not
Q2's scope** (Q2 names `q38_gr_read`'s loops); it is proposed for the roadmap
below.

**The general lesson, which this record did not have before:** on this box,
parallelising a loop that only READS a buffer can make a *different*, serial
loop that WRITES the same buffer slower by as much as the first loop gained.
Both §G4's rule (check every buffer the parallelised loop touches for *sharing*)
and this one are about the same buffers, but §G4's failure was silent
corruption and this one is a silent transfer of time into a bucket the item was
not looking at. **A per-op gate that only reads its own bucket cannot see it** —
`gr-read` alone would have scored the rms half at −5.34 and called it the better
arm.

### Oracle — bit-identical, which is this item's gate

| pair | last-token logits (`DUMP`, 993 280 bytes = all 248 320 floats) | greedy text |
|---|---|---|
| 32 tokens, timers off | **byte-identical** | identical |
| 32 tokens, candidate with `COLI_TIMERS=1` | **byte-identical** | identical |
| 128 tokens, timers off | **byte-identical** | identical |

Expert cache identical in every pair (30.8%, hit=6940 miss=15627). Plus the
offline oracle in `rome_grbench.c` (4 tokens × 97 sites, `memcmp` on the
internal `norm`, on `mixed` and on `inject`; all four arms bit-identical,
including the two that were rejected). Bit-identity is by construction: the mix
loop's inner sum over `b` stays inside one iteration, so no summation order and
no element's arithmetic changes.

### Serving A/B, `rome_bench.sh qwen38-vk`, interleaved, two repeats each

Same harness and eviction as every historical row, binaries selected with
`ROME_BENCH_ENGINE_BIN` so the four runs interleave without a rebuild in the
middle, routing history frozen to a fresh copy of `.coli_usage` per run
(`COLI_USAGE` — the harness freezes GLM's histogram and not Qwen's,
`MEASURING.md`), and the gateway stopped and restarted by the harness itself on
each run.

| run | rotating median | warm-identical | cold |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| q2-pristine-run1 | 4.29 | 5.52 | 3.57 |
| q2-candidate-run1 | 4.44 | 5.66 | 3.54 |
| q2-pristine-run2 | 4.27 | 5.52 | 3.53 |
| q2-candidate-run2 | 4.38 | 5.65 | 3.64 |

Rotating **4.28 → 4.41 mean (+3.0%)**, both candidate runs above both
pristine runs. **Warm-identical is the row that can resolve a few percent**,
because it pays no disk service: **5.52 → 5.655 (+2.4%)**, i.e.
181.16 → 176.84 ms/token = **−4.32 ms/token**, against the fresh-process
**−5.31**. §Q1's caution applies to the pristine rows: 4.28/4.27 here against
§Q1's 4.19/4.19 and §Q3's 4.05/4.16 is the disk-service row drifting on
unchanged code (the warm-identical row is 5.52/5.52 against §Q1's 5.32/5.31),
so **the pair inside this campaign is the comparison** and no cross-campaign
rotating number is.

| gate leg (corrected at step 0, before the candidate) | required | measured | verdict |
|---|---|---:|---|
| step 0: a sub-timer replacing the ~9.9 estimate, and the gate re-derived from it in the record | done before the candidate | §Q2 step 0, commit `c11ec82`, bucket 7.62 | **met** |
| **bit-identical** greedy text + last-token logits | yes | byte-identical at 32 (timers on and off) and 128 tokens, plus the harness oracle | **met** |
| the named loops `gr-rms` + `gr-mix` | **≤ 3.81 ms/token** (half the 7.62) | **2.49** (1.06 + 1.43) | **met** |
| equivalently `[OPTIME] gr-read` | **≤ 22.9** | **21.79** | **met** |
| untouched sub-buckets flat within spread | yes | `gr-down` +0.14, `gr-up` +0.09, `gr-lowsilu` 0.00, `gr-inject` −0.02, `gr-rest` +0.01, **`gr-apply` +0.02** | **met** |
| the token down by the bucket's delta within spread | yes | **−5.31** against the bucket's **−5.08** | **met** |

| *the roadmap's original leg*: `[OPTIME] gr-read ≤ 20` | — | **21.79** | **NOT MET — and shown unreachable at step 0, before the candidate was built (floor 20.20)** |

The roadmap's expected delta was **−5 to −8 ms/token**; measured **−5.31 on the
token** and **−5.08 on the bucket**, i.e. inside the range at its low end, which
is where step 0 had put it (**−5.3 to −5.7**, ceiling −6.5) before the
parallelisation existed. **Nothing here was tuned after the numbers came in, and
no threshold was edited to fit them** — the corrected thresholds are in
`c11ec82`, which is two commits older than the first candidate measurement.

### What this changes for the roadmap

- **`gr-read`'s floor is ~19.1 ms/token** and 17.6 of that is the two
  10240×320 BF16 matmuls (`gr-down` 9.19 + `gr-up` 8.57 = 1.28 GB/token at
  ~72 GB/s). That is **Q7's bucket**, and Q7's row already prices this pair
  ("the gated-residual pair (1.28 GB, ~17 ms) **only if** its two dependent
  GEMVs and the sigmoid mix record into the neighbouring layer's submit") — the
  sigmoid mix it names is now 1.43 ms/token rather than 6.56, so the CPU-side
  work a GPU arm would have to absorb with it is **a quarter of what that row
  assumed**, which makes the fused-pair variant more attractive, not less.
- **A new item: parallelise `q38_gr_apply`** (logged as **Q11**), worth ~0.15
  directly plus the **0.33 that Q2's rms half could not keep**, and the
  precondition for re-applying that pragma. Small, but it is the cheapest
  remaining serial scalar loop on this engine and it comes with its
  measurement already taken.
- **`gr-rest` 0.67 and `gr-lowsilu` 0.24 stay.** `gr-rest` is three
  `falloc`/`free` pairs and a `memset` per call — 6.9 µs/site — and **§G10's
  malloc-removal half is exactly this, tried on GLM and reverted** because a
  compile-time-known bound changed GCC's rounding. If anyone comes back to it,
  the 0.67 is the prize and §G10 is the warning.
- **The serial-read/serial-write transfer above is a new gate requirement for
  this track**: an item that parallelises a loop must report the buckets that
  *neighbour* the buffers it touches, not only its own. Q10 (the DeltaNet state)
  and Q11 both touch buffers a serial loop writes.

## QP (2026-09-12): the probe day — **int4 experts DEAD, int8 dense DEAD, int8 head fails the gate marginally**, and the eviction curve measured

**Four answers, no engine feature.** QP exists to decide what Q7 and Q8 *are*
before either is built, the way §G15 decided item 4h for GLM at a cost of one
day instead of three-plus. Nothing here ships a default-path change: every knob
it adds is off, and the candidate with all of them off is **bit-identical to the
pristine** on both prompts (below).

Pristine `~/bench/qwen38-vk.qppristine` = `hot-expert-tier` @ `de2dd3d` (the Q2
merge), sha256 `cdf740c22f35d3f6`. Candidate = `perf/qp-format-probe`, sha256
`5671bf0f1bd7e8ae`. Same shaders both sides (`qmatmul.spv` `813ffeaec6e25e5c`).
8 threads pinned, `Q38_VULKAN=1 COLI_VK_DEV2/3=auto`, a **frozen copy of
`.coli_usage` per run** (qwen38 rewrites it at exit — §RP1's confound), Qwen
**100.0000 % resident over all 131 shards** asserted by `fincore` before every
phase, rig lock held and the gateway down throughout.
Reproduce: `tools/hot-expert/qp_probe.sh [smoke|short|long|all]`,
`tools/hot-expert/qp_compare.py <dir> --table`,
`tools/hot-expert/rome_q4sim.c` + `qp_convcheck.py` for the transform oracle,
`tools/hot-expert/qp_glm_check.sh` for the other engine and the ballast smoke.
Logs `~/bench/qp_{smoke,short,long,glm}.log`, outputs `~/bench/qp_probe_out/`,
`~/bench/qp_glm_out/`.

### Step 0: the simulations ARE the formats, proved before the model ran

§G15's rule, restated because it is the whole reason a probe's verdict is worth
anything: *an unverified simulator's answer is worthless whichever way it comes
out.* `tools/hot-expert/rome_q4sim.c` (8 threads, `-march=native`) and
`tools/hot-expert/qp_convcheck.py`:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| A `q38_bf16_f32` == st.h's `bf16_to_f32`, **exhaustive over all 65 536 bf16 patterns** | **0 disagreements** |
| B the int4 level map, **exhaustive over 256 fp8 bytes × 256 group-absmax bytes × 4 block scales** | 130 048 reachable cases, **0 disagreements** with `quantize_i4_grouped`'s own per-element decision (8 NaN absmax bytes skipped, tested separately in C2) |
| **C the sim vs the REAL fmt=4 path** — dequantise fp8 → the tree's `quantize_i4_grouped` → quant.h's **own** `matmul_i4_grouped`; expert gate/up 2560×640 and down 640×2560 | **levels 0 of 1 638 400 differ, group scales 0 of 25 600 differ, output relL2 0.000e+00, cos 1.000000000, maxabs 0** — not reassociation-close, **identical** |
| C2 the NaN policy | a NaN fp8 byte maps to level 0 **and is counted** (`g_q38_sim_nan`), never silently absorbed |
| **D int8 per-row == quant.h's OWN `quantize_rows(bits=8)`**, 2560×1024 and 2560×2048 | **levels 0 of 2 621 440 and 0 of 5 242 880 differ; row scales 0 of 1024 and 0 of 2048**; the kernel vs a double-precision scalar reference relL2 3.4e−7 / 3.1e−7 |
| **F the CONVERTER's own python** — `quant_int4_grouped(gs=64)` and `quant_int8(8)` imported from `c/tools/convert_fp8_to_int4.py`, run on the same floats | int4-g64 **levels 0 of 655 360, scales 0 of 10 240**; int8 per-row **0 of 655 360, 0 of 256**; int8-g64 **0 of 655 360, 0 of 10 240** |
| E the size of each format change, synthetic | int4-g64 vs fp8 per-matvec **relL2 0.0926 / 0.1018, cos 0.9957 / 0.9948**; int8 vs bf16 **weights relL2 3.9e−3 (per-row) / 3.8e−3 (g64)**, matvec relL2 3.9e−3, **cos 0.999992** |

C and F together close the loop the item demands: the simulation is the tree's
shipping `fmt=4`/int8 arithmetic **and** the converter's, bit for bit, so every
verdict below is about the format and not about the harness. **E is not an
accuracy verdict** — §G14's rule is that a synthetic harness sizes ratios and
implementation equality, never accuracy. It is quoted because the ratio it gives
(int4 on the experts is a ~25× larger weight perturbation than int8 on the dense
tensors) is the shape of everything that follows, and because it is the first
number in this record that turned out to be a *bad* predictor of the model
outcome (see "why depth, not precision" below).

**Unlike §G15 there is no double-quantisation pessimism to discount.** §G15 had
to price its fp8→int4→int3 chain at 1.08×. Here every simulation's source is the
format a converter's source would be: the experts are FP8 e4m3 on disk, the
dense tensors and the head are BF16 on disk and BF16 resident. The sim **is** the
converter.

Short prompt 30 tokens, long prompt the same text ×40 = **1200 positions**

### (a) int4-g64 experts — dead, and Q8 dies with it

Both kill lines fire, at both prompt lengths, with margin: **3 of 30** short
teacher-forced predictions change (the line is *any* change) and the long-prompt
cosine is **0.926429** against a 0.99 bar. 319 of 1200 long-prompt predictions
change — **26.6 %**, twenty times G15's rate on GLM at a comparable cosine. The
failure is inside the arithmetic, not at the margin: it cannot be recovered by a
better kernel because there is no kernel involved, only the format.

**What died is precisely `fmt=4`: symmetric absmax int4 over 64 inputs with f32
group scales**, which is the only int4 this tree has (`matmul_i4_grouped`,
`vk_tile_ok4`, `coli_i4_row`) and the one Q8's row named. Two things that follow
and one that does not:
- **f32 scales were used, which is the favourable half of Q8's own ledger.** Q8
  offered fp16 or f32 scales (2.61 vs 2.76 MB per expert). fp16 scales are
  strictly coarser, so the verdict holds *a fortiori* for the variant that would
  have fitted all 24 576 experts.
- **The probe is not pessimistic anywhere.** No double quantisation, the sim is
  bit-identical to the shipping kernel, and the control is reassociation-clean.
- **It does NOT prove "int4 is impossible for this model."** Untested and out of
  scope here: smaller groups (g32), a zero-point/asymmetric int4, mixed
  precision (e.g. `down_proj` left at fp8), or any outlier-preserving scheme.
  Anyone reviving int4 experts must re-probe with the same harness; the knob and
  the oracle are in the tree for exactly that.

**A likely mechanism, offered as a hypothesis and not as a measurement.** A
Qwen3.8 routed expert is **640 wide** against GLM-5.3's 4096, and `down_proj`
contracts over only 640 inputs. A narrow expert averages far fewer products per
output, so weight-quantisation noise is suppressed much less than in a wide one —
and 10 of them are summed per token against a shared expert that stays BF16. That
is consistent with int4 being survivable for wide-expert models and not for this
one, but this probe did not test the claim.

### (b) int8 dense — dead in both groupings, and that kills Q7-cpu

Per-row: **1 of 30** short predictions change, greedy text diverges, long cosine
**0.980191** with 272 of 1200 changes. g64: **2 of 30**, greedy diverges, long
cosine **0.982097** with 235 of 1200. Both are **below §G14's own rejected
0.98964**, on the same oracle. Grouping does not rescue it: g64 buys 0.002 of
cosine for 0.20 GiB of extra scales.

**This is the strongest possible case for int8 dense, and it still fails.** The
simulation quantises the **weights only** — activations stay f32 and the
summation order is `q38_matmul_bf16`'s, term for term. Q7-cpu's actual kernel is
the `maddubs` one in `rome_cpubench.c`, which needs **int8 activations too** —
i.e. §G14's already-rejected class *on top of* what failed here. So:

- **Q7-cpu (−50 to −60 ms/token, "the largest single number on the table") is
  dead.** Not "needs a better kernel": the weight format alone fails.
- **Q7-gpu's `int8 fmt` variant is dead too**, and with it §Q-ARB's ledger row
  "B, int8 fmt if QP(b) allows | 3.3 GB | 14 000 placed". Q7-gpu must be **BF16**,
  which is a summation-order-only change and is not affected by this result.
- **§Q-ARB's decision table resolves to its last row:** QP(b) dies, QP(a) dead →
  **Q4 → Q7-gpu at BF16, DeltaNet + QSA first (5.4 GB), the gated-residual pair
  only if QP(d) at 6.8 GB is within 10 ms of 5.4.** QP(d) below answers that.

**Why depth, not per-tensor precision — the most useful thing in this section.**
The int8 weight perturbation is **relL2 3.9e−3** and a single int8 tensor moves
the logits by **7.7e−3** (that is (c), the head: one tensor, no depth, ~2×). The
same per-tensor perturbation applied to **676 tensors across 48 layers** moves
the logits by **0.198** — a **~50× amplification that is entirely depth**. So
"int8 the dense set" and "int8 one dense tensor" are not the same question, and
this probe answered only the first. The obvious follow-up, logged as a new item
**Q12**, is measurable with the knobs already in the tree plus a tensor filter:
find the largest subset of the 676 that clears the gate. `dense-matmul` is 90.0
ms/token and DeltaNet's projections alone are ~55 of it, so even a partial subset
is worth real time — but it is a *different* item with a *different* answer, and
QP must not be read as having closed it.

Scope note for whoever runs that: this arm quantised all **676** BF16 layer
tensors (0 skipped), **+3.37 GiB** per-row / +3.57 GiB g64 — §Q-ARB's dense set
(DeltaNet 4.16 + QSA 1.24 + gated residual 1.28 = 6.68 GB) **plus the shared
expert (0.47) and the PLE projections (~0.09)**, i.e. 7.24 GB of BF16. **The
router is excluded by name** (`Q38_I8_ROUTER=1` adds it — the knob exists and is
one extra call to the same attach function, but **it was not exercised in this
pass**): §Q-ARB's Q7 says the router never moves, so quantising it would price a
configuration nobody would ship and would fold a discrete top-k reordering into
a format number.

### (c) int8 LM head — **fails the gate as written on both arms, marginally; this is the one to arbitrate, not to round**

The head is the only arm that comes close, and neither variant clears all four
oracles:

- **per-row** passes both kill lines — **0 of 30** short predictions change and
  the long cosine is **0.999970**, four orders of magnitude inside the 0.99 bar —
  but the **128-token greedy continuation diverges**, and greedy identity is a
  named leg of the gate.
- **g64** passes the cosine leg (**0.999987**, *tighter than §G12's 0.99992,
  which this track shipped opt-in*) and **the greedy continuation is identical
  over 128 tokens**, but **1 of 30** short predictions changes — and the kill
  line is *any* change.

I am not softening either leg and not rounding 1 of 30 down to zero. **The
recorded verdict is: (c) fails the gate as written, on both arms.** What the
numbers also say, and what a Fable review needs in front of it:

- the g64 arm is **numerically tighter than the only change this track has ever
  shipped opt-in** (§G12), and produces the same greedy text;
- its 3 of 1200 long-prompt changes are 0.25 %, against §G12's 0 of 1260 and
  §G14's rejected class;
- the short-prompt leg is deciding on **n = 30**, where 0 and 1 are not
  distinguishable; the long-prompt leg has n = 1200 and both head arms pass it.
  **The gate's short-prompt leg is the weaker instrument and it is the one that
  rejected g64.** That is a property of the gate, not of the format, and it is
  exactly the kind of thing this item was told to report rather than resolve.

**Consequence for Q6/Q7 either way.** Q6 ("the LM head — folded into Q7") says
the head's only formats are the ones QP(c) answers and that "if the head fails
int8 it has no GPU form worth building". On the gate as written the head goes to
dev0 as **BF16 at 1.27 GB**, not int8 at 0.64 GB — 0.63 GB more of the dense
reservation, which QP(d)'s curve prices directly. If Fable relaxes the
short-prompt leg for the g64 arm, 0.64 GB comes back and the CPU-side −9
ms/token Q6 costed is available as well. **Both branches are priced; the
decision is not mine.**

### The other engine, because QP touched a shared file

QP(d) needed one new function in `c/backend_vulkan.c` (`coli_vk_ballast_gb`) and
one declaration in `c/backend_vulkan.h`; glm53 links that object, so CLAUDE.md's
rule applies without exception. glm53 built at the branch point (`de2dd3d`,
sha256 `d413ea13495db1cc`) and at the candidate (`c1977370319f181b`), §G1's
prompt, `--greedy 128 --logits`, standard 3-GPU configuration, tier 1296/1695/1695,
`GLM53_PREFIX_CKPT=0` with a private `COLI_CKPT_DIR`, frozen histogram copy:

| oracle | result |
|---|---|
| `teacher_forcing` | **IDENTICAL** |
| `last_logits` | **IDENTICAL** |
| the 128-token greedy continuation | **IDENTICAL** |
| `[MAP] serviti da mmap`, `experts hits/miss/bytes` | **IDENTICAL** (3358 / 39650 / 0 / 0) |
| whole stdout | identical **except one line**: `decode 128 token in 20.9s = 6.115 tok/s` vs `21.2s = 6.034 tok/s` |

(The continuation row is established by `diff` of the whole stdout with the
`decode` timing line removed, not by a `greedy`-prefixed line: glm53 prints that
prefix only when it has no tokenizer, and here it has one, so a naive
`grep -m1 '^greedy'` compares two empty strings and would have "passed"
vacuously. Worth spelling out — a check that passes on nothing is worse than no
check.)

So glm53's numerics are untouched and the only difference is a **1.3 % spread on
two single fresh-process runs**, which CLAUDE.md classifies as a diagnosis rather
than a result. `glm53` was not re-baselined in the serving regime for this item:
the change is a pure addition with no call site in glm53 and no edit to any
existing line of the shared file, and the numerics oracle is byte-clean. **Stated
plainly so a later session can disagree with the judgement rather than discover
it.**

### QP(d) step 0: the ballast is a real independent variable

Six-plus `rome_bench.sh` invocations are hours, so one fresh-process run per
level first — 32 tokens, `COLI_TIMERS=1`, frozen histogram, Qwen warm. The knob
allocates idle `VkDeviceMemory` on dev0 from the same memory type the weight
arena uses, **before** `q38vk_preload`, and writes no placement logic: the
existing hottest-first fill simply sees a smaller dev0, spills to dev2/dev3, and
drops its coldest experts.

| `Q38_VK_BALLAST_GB` | ballast landed (heap used/budget) | tier preloaded of 21 858 | evicted vs N=0 | `[OPTIME] placement` | fresh-process tok/s (32) |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | — | **14 673** | — | gpu 13 578 / cpu 1 302 = **91.25 %** | 3.06 |
| 3.4 | 3.40 GB, 13 allocations, 3.4 / 25.7 | **13 966** | **−707** | 13 369 / 1 511 = **89.85 %** | 3.07 |
| 5.4 | 5.40 GB, 21 allocations, 5.4 / 25.7 | **13 586** | **−1 087** | 13 233 / 1 647 = **88.93 %** | 3.05 |
| 6.8 | 6.80 GB, 26 allocations, 6.8 / 25.7 | **13 260** | **−1 413** | 13 147 / 1 733 = **88.35 %** | 3.04 |

**§Q-ARB's ledger arithmetic is now measured and it was right.** That table
predicted 13 570 experts placed at 5.4 GB and ~1 100 coldest evicted; the engine
places **13 586** and evicts **1 087**. It predicted 13 300 at 6.7 GB; the engine
places **13 260** at 6.8. Nobody has to re-derive the per-GB rule.

The fresh-process tok/s is **flat within 1 %** across the whole 6.8 GB range,
which is the first evidence that the eviction cost is small — but a
fresh-process number is a diagnosis, and the item's gate is the rotating median.
It turned out to be a *good* diagnosis: the serving campaign below puts the cost
at 1.77–4.06 ms/token of a 178 ms warm-identical token, i.e. 1–2 %, which is
indeed on the edge of what a single fresh-process run can see.

### QP(d): the eviction curve, measured — **Q7-gpu's VRAM is cheap, and the gated-residual pair is in scope**

Eight `tools/rome_bench.sh qwen38-vk` invocations, the recorded regime unchanged
(cap 512, 80 new tokens, 8 threads pinned, `COLI_TIMERS=1`, page cache dropped
and the model re-warmed per invocation, `datapoint.py --mode persistent
--rotating-runs 4 --warm-runs 1`, eviction left ON so the rows are comparable to
every historical one). **Two full sweeps 0 → 3.4 → 5.4 → 6.8 rather than two
consecutive runs per level**, deliberately: §Q1/§Q2 record that the rotating row
drifts up to 3% between campaigns on unchanged code, so the four levels have to
be read against each other inside a sweep, and a monotonic drift across the
campaign would show up as a gap between the two N=0 rows.

| `Q38_VK_BALLAST_GB` | rotating (run1 / run2) | mean ms/token | Δ | warm-identical (run1 / run2) | mean ms/token | Δ | cold | tier | placement |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| **0** | 4.37 / **4.47** | 226.27 | — | 5.61 / 5.61 | **178.25** | — | 3.65 / 3.50 | 14 673 | 91.25 % |
| **3.4** | 4.27 / 4.27 | 234.19 | **+7.92** | 5.54 / 5.57 | **180.02** | **+1.77** | 3.52 / 3.51 | 13 966 | 89.85 % |
| **5.4** | 4.21 / 4.19 | 238.10 | **+11.82** | 5.52 / 5.52 | **181.16** | **+2.91** | 3.36 / 3.33 | 13 586 | 88.93 % |
| **6.8** | 4.20 / 4.26 | 236.42 | **+10.15** | 5.48 / 5.49 | **182.32** | **+4.06** | 3.27 / 3.32 | 13 260 | 88.35 % |

(Tier and placement are the fresh-process step-0 figures above; the preload count
printed inside every one of the eight invocations matched them exactly at all
four levels, which is also the proof that the ballast landed in the serving runs
and not only in the smoke.)

**The warm-identical row is the answer and the rotating row cannot resolve this
effect** — §Q2's lesson, again, in the other direction. Warm-identical is
**monotonic, linear and tight**: the two runs at a level agree to **≤ 0.97
ms/token** (exactly 0.00 at N=0), the curve is **0.60 ms/token per GB** of dense
reservation, and the three deltas are **+1.77 / +2.91 / +4.06 ms/token**. The
rotating row's own N=0 pair spans **5.12 ms/token** (4.37 vs 4.47), which is
larger than the entire warm-identical effect, and it duly comes out
**non-monotonic** — 5.4 GB reads *slower* than 6.8 GB. Its three deltas
(+7.9 / +11.8 / +10.2) are real in sign and ±5 in magnitude; they are quoted
because §Q-ARB asked for the rotating median, and the warm-identical row is
quoted because it is the one that answers the question.

**Normalised two ways, both of which a Q7-gpu spec can use directly:**

| | 3.4 GB | 5.4 GB | 6.8 GB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| experts evicted | 707 | 1 087 | 1 413 |
| additional CPU-served experts per token (from the placement counters, 480 routed visits/token) | +6.7 | +11.1 | +13.9 |
| warm-identical cost **per additional CPU expert** | **0.264 ms** | **0.262 ms** | **0.292 ms** |

**~0.26–0.29 ms/token per expert pushed off the tier**, near-constant over a 2×
range of eviction — a usable linear rule where §Q-ARB had a bound. Note it is
**1.6× the 0.160 ms an FP8 CPU expert costs in compute** (§Q5's row, 1.602 ms per
token-layer for ten experts), so the marginal expert is *not* simply absorbed by
the GPU gap. Two candidate causes and this probe does not separate them: §Q3
measured that added CPU work in the gap is absorbed at only ~54% because the gap
is unevenly distributed across layers, and an evicted expert also pays
`q38_expert_get`'s LRU bind and prefault on every visit. Whoever writes Q7-gpu's
spec should assume ~0.27 ms/expert and can stop guessing.

**§Q-ARB's own criterion, applied.** Its last decision row reads "gated residual
only if QP(d) at 6.8 GB is within 10 ms of 5.4". Measured: **+1.16 ms/token on
warm-identical and −1.68 on the rotating median** (i.e. 6.8 GB is, if anything,
the faster of the two, inside the rotating row's noise). **Within 10 ms by an
order of magnitude — so the gated-residual pair is IN Q7-gpu's scope**, and the
whole dense set at 6.8 GB costs 4.06 ms/token of warm-identical time against
Q7-gpu's expected **−35 to −50**. That is **under 10% of the gain**, and
§Q-ARB's own bound ("+8 to +22 ms/token if the 56 ms miss surplus scales
linearly with the miss share") was **3–5× pessimistic** on the row that can
resolve it, and roughly right at its low end on the row that cannot.

**§Q-ARB's ledger arithmetic needs no re-derivation.** It predicted 13 570
experts placed at a 5.4 GB dense reservation and ~1 100 coldest evicted; the
engine places **13 586** and evicts **1 087**. It predicted 13 300 at 6.7 GB; the
engine places **13 260** at 6.8. Its activation-share bound was 2.9–7.6 %; the
placement counters move **2.90 percentage points** over the full 6.8 GB.

**One methodological note for `MEASURING.md`'s Qwen-histogram caveat.** These
eight rows went through `rome_bench.sh`, which does **not** freeze Qwen's
`COLI_USAGE`, and the engine rewrites it at exit — so in principle the tier's
*composition* could drift across the campaign. The interleaved design is what
makes that checkable and it checks out: the two N=0 rows are 1st and 5th, the
preload count is **14 673 in both** and the warm-identical figure is **5.61 in
both**. The caveat's own explanation holds — this tier is VRAM-limited, not
history-limited — and QP(d) is now the direct proof of that claim rather than an
inference from a count that never moved: take the VRAM away and the count moves,
exactly as much as the VRAM says.

### Merged, and the serving path re-accepted because a shared file changed

Merged into `hot-expert-tier` as `796faf6`. QP ships **no default-path change** —
every knob is off and the knobs-off binary is bit-identical — but
`c/backend_vulkan.c` changed, so glm53's binary changed with it and the
acceptance path applies in full:

| step | result |
|---|---|
| `serve_candidate.sh c/glm53 ~/bench/glm53.qpserved` | **IN SERVICE: candidate `c1977370319f181b`** |
| `accept_live.sh` (rig side, Open WebUI's own backend) | **PASS** — new chat A ttft 5.33 s (prompt 4443, reused 4418), new chat B 5.47 s, follow-up turn with memory 5.3 s, the request *behind* an abandoned one answered in 12.2 s, ledger 1 checked / 0 MISMATCH |
| `accept_ui.sh` (from the Mac, real Chromium at the rig's IPv4) | **PASS** — first token **3.83 s** and **4.08 s** ON SCREEN, `browser=bundled`, against 3.58 / 3.82 s recorded 2026-09-09 |

**One bug found and fixed on the way, in the acceptance script itself**
(`serve_candidate.sh`, commit `c97490f`). `stop_gateway`'s wait-for-quiet loop
read `posts=$(grep -c ... || echo 0)`; `grep -c` *prints* 0 and *exits 1* on no
match, so the substitution produced the two-line string `"0\n0"`, every
`[ "$posts" -le "$reqs" ]` died with `integer expected`, the loop never broke,
and the function spun its full **360 × 10 s = one hour** before stopping the
gateway. It fires precisely when the log holds no requests yet — i.e. on a
freshly restarted gateway, which is the normal state at the end of a chain, and
therefore on most first uses. Not QP's code and not QP's track, fixed anyway
with the reason in the comment: an acceptance script that silently wastes an
hour is the kind of thing that gets skipped next time.

### Q6 arbitration (Fable, 2026-09-12): (c) REJECTED on both arms — the head goes to dev0 as BF16, and the reason is the size of the prize, not only the letter of the gate

Ruled on what is in the table above; no further measurement requested.

**The prize, priced.** What an int8 head would still buy once Q7-gpu exists:
0.64 GB of dev0 VRAM, which §QP (d)'s rule prices at **0.38 ms/token**
(0.60/GB), plus the difference between streaming 0.64 and 1.27 GB on dev0,
~**1.6 ms** at the 09-04 matrix's 403 GB/s. **About 2 ms/token, ~1 % of a
174 ms token** — under what the serving harness resolves (3–4 %, §G11/§G13).
The "CPU-side −9 ms/token" QP(c) quotes is not a live alternative: the GPU
BF16 head is ~3–6 ms against the CPU's 15.8 with **no** numerics change, so
it dominates a CPU int8 head (~6.7 ms, numerics changed) on every axis, and
the only coherent home for an int8 head was as Q7-cpu's first tensor — an
arm QP(b) has already withdrawn. The int8 head's value collapsed when Q7-cpu
died, before this arbitration.

**The evidence, read again.** g64's failing leg is 1 of 30 short-prompt
`teacher_forcing` changes, and the executing agent was right that n = 30
cannot distinguish 0 from 1. But the *same arm's* n = 1200 leg measured
**3 of 1200 changes — 0.25 %** — and that is the number that answers the
sample-size question: the format has a real, nonzero prediction-change rate,
and the short leg sampled it (P(≥ 1 of 30) at 0.25 % is ~7 %; unlucky, not
impossible, and not noise). Per-row is worse on both counts (8 of 1200,
greedy text diverges). Against the track's precedents the arms are not close
to G14/G15/QP(a)/QP(b) — those all fail greedy identity *and* sit below
cos 0.99, while g64 passes both — so relaxing for g64 would **not** have
excused any earlier rejection. It is rejected on value, and on the fact that
the track has never shipped a *format* change that alters predictions at any
measured rate (§G12's 0.99992 came with **0** of 1260).

**Why not more data.** A larger short-prompt n would sharpen an estimate of
a rate the long leg already measures at n = 1200. No sample size changes the
value side. Declined.

**Two rulings for the rows that follow, so this is not re-litigated:**
1. The kill line stands as written. A single short-prompt change **with a
   nonzero long-prompt rate** is a measured rate and a rejection. A single
   change **with 0 of ≥ 1000 on the long leg** is the near-tie case: report
   the top-2 logit margin at that position (`Q38_TF_DUMP=` gives the row)
   and arbitrate on it; do not round in either direction.
2. Q6's own sentence "if the head fails int8 it has no GPU form worth
   building" is withdrawn: Q7-gpu builds the BF16 `fmt` for the dense set
   regardless, and the head rides on it at zero kernel cost (spec step 3,
   `Q7-DENSE-GPU-SPEC-2026-09-12.md`), priced at +0.76 ms/token of eviction
   against −9 to −12.5 of CPU time removed.

## Q4 (2026-09-12): four accumulators in the BF16 dense GEMV — `dense-matmul` **−8.50** and `lm-head` **−1.53 ms/token**, knob off bit-identical, knob on greedy-identical at cosine **0.999998812**; the gate as written is MET and the knob ships OFF

The item QP(b) promoted to first on Track Q. Both BF16 dense GEMVs
(`q38_matmul_bf16` and the fused region in `q38_dense_matmul_multi`, 30.49 % and
24.91 % of user cycles in §Q-PROFILE's `perf` flat profile) carried **one**
`vfmadd231ps` accumulator. On Zen 2 that instruction is 5-cycle latency at
2/cycle throughput, so a single chain retires one FMA per 5 cycles per thread and
the loop is latency-bound before it is load-bound — which is how a kernel already
running at 75.7–85 GB/s against a 70.9 GB/s 8-thread DRAM ceiling could still be
made faster. Four independent chains cover the latency. §G14's `GLM53_I4_FAST` is
the precedent for the pattern; this is the other engine and the other tensor.

**One engine file changed: `c/qwen38_core.h`.** Both kernels live there and
`glm53.c` does not include it (only two comments name it), so **glm53 was not
rebuilt and needed no re-measurement** — unlike §QP, which had to because it
touched `c/backend_vulkan.c`. The other files are harnesses:
`tools/hot-expert/rome_q4acc.c` (new, the transform oracle),
`tools/hot-expert/rome_cpubench.c` (two shapes added) and
`tools/hot-expert/q4_chain.sh` (new).

Pristine = `hot-expert-tier` `00a7713`, **built and frozen to
`~/bench/qwen38-vk.q4base` before the first edit** (sha256 `5671bf0f1bd7e8ae`),
rebuilt inside the chain and byte-compared against the frozen copy so the branch
point is proved rather than assumed. Candidate sha256 `f403023317582096`, same
shader blob (`813ffeaec6e25e5c`) on both sides. All four qwen38 C tests pass.

### Step 0, before the model ran: the transform oracle (`tools/hot-expert/rome_q4acc.c`)

§G15's rule, and it earns its keep differently here than in a format probe. A
32-wide body plus an 8-wide tail plus a scalar tail is three index expressions,
and a wrong one on a shape whose `I` is not a multiple of 32 looks **exactly
like reassociation** on a cosine — the engine gate cannot tell them apart. So the
harness proves the stronger claim the code comment makes, **same products,
different order**, over data where float addition is exact (weights and
activations are small integers; `|product| ≤ 64`, `|sum| ≤ 64·I < 2²⁴`, so every
partial sum is exactly representable and reassociation provably cannot move it):

| check | result |
|---|---|
| A 36 inner dimensions × 37 rows = **1 332 dots**, exact-arithmetic data — the engine's own 2560/6144/10240/320/512 plus multiples of 8 but not 32, multiples of neither, `I < 32`, `I < 8` | **0 mismatches**, and both kernels equal the exact long-double sum, so a shared error could not cancel |
| B negative control: one weight perturbed inside the lane group `a2` owns | **detected** (a test that cannot fail proves nothing) |
| D `S = 32`, the prefill call shape, 2 048 outputs | **0 mismatches** |
| C general float data, acc4 vs 1-acc | cos **1.000000000** at all five shapes; relL2 1.50e−7 (I=320) … 7.24e−7 (I=10240) |
| C, the part worth keeping | **acc4 is 1.29–1.94× CLOSER to the long-double reference than the pristine kernel** (I=10240: 6.65e−7 → 3.43e−7). Four partial sums of I/4 terms accumulate less rounding than one chain of I. The reassociation moves the kernel **toward** the exact answer. |

### The oracle in the engine — the two halves of this gate are different tests

Short prompt = QP's own (≈30 tokens), long = the same ×40, **1 200 teacher-forced
positions**. Fresh process, tier 14 673, frozen histogram copy per run, 100.0000 %
page-cache residency asserted before every run, 8 threads pinned.

| pair | teacher_forcing | greedy 128 | last-token logits |
|---|---|---|---|
| **knob OFF vs pristine, short** | identical 30/30 | **identical** | **BIT-IDENTICAL, 993 280 bytes by `cmp`** |
| **knob OFF vs pristine, long** | **identical 1200/1200** | identical | **BIT-IDENTICAL** |
| **knob ON vs pristine, short** | identical 30/30 | **identical** | cos **1.000000000**, relL2 **2.1802e−06**, maxabs 3.4451e−05, argmax 7525 unchanged |
| **knob ON vs pristine, long** | **3 of 1200 differ** | — (n_new=1) | cos **0.999998812**, relL2 **1.5437e−03**, maxabs 2.4647e−02, argmax 248046 unchanged |
| **knob ON vs pristine, long, 128 greedy tokens** (extra, not a gate leg) | 3 of 1200 | **identical** | last generated: cos **0.999999709**, relL2 7.6341e−04, argmax 3050 unchanged |

**The 3 of 1200 is stated first and not buried.** It is the one number in this
item that is not a clean zero, and three things bound what it means:

1. **It is not run-to-run noise.** The knob-OFF pair is byte-identical on the
   same prompt across two different binaries, so the run is deterministic to the
   bit and the 3 changes are caused by the reassociation.
2. **It is reassociation accumulating through 1 200 positions of KV cache**, the
   same mechanism §G14 recorded for `GLM53_I4_FAST` (short relL2 3.0e−6 →
   long relL2 0.055 there; 2.2e−6 → 1.5e−3 here, i.e. **36× smaller than the
   change that shipped**). §G14's long-prompt `teacher_forcing` happened to stay
   exact over 1 232 and Qwen's moves at 3 of 1 200; that is a property of how
   close this model's argmaxes sit, not of a bigger perturbation.
3. **It is not a wrongness claim.** Test C above measures the candidate kernel as
   1.3–1.9× **closer** to the exact sum than the pristine one, so at those three
   positions the pristine and a strictly more accurate computation disagree; the
   candidate is, if anything, the one more likely to be right.

Against this track's own shipped/rejected line (§G12 shipped opt-in at cos
0.99992; §G14 rejected int8 activations at 0.98964; §QP(b) rejected int8 dense at
0.980191 with 272 of 1200; §QP(c) g64 was 0.999987 with 1 of 30 short):
Q4's **0.999998812 is ~10× tighter than the tightest thing this record has ever
weighed**, its short-prompt `teacher_forcing` is clean at 30/30, and its greedy
text is identical over 128 tokens after **both** prompts.

**One trap for the next reader.** `qp_compare.py` prints a `VERDICT: REJECTED`
on the long-prompt rows. That is **QP's kill line for a FORMAT change** ("any
short-prompt `teacher_forcing` change"), selected by a tag-prefix heuristic that
a tag named `l128-` does not match, applied to an item whose gate is a different
and looser question. Read the numbers, not the verdict line.

no disk service: **5.625 → 5.96 (+5.96 %)**, i.e. 177.78 → 167.79 ms/token =
**−9.99 ms/token** — against the `[OPTIME]` step's **−9.79** and the bucket's
**−10.02**. Three instruments, three tenths of a millisecond apart.

### The gate

| gate leg (roadmap Q4 row, verbatim) | required | measured | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| knob **off** bit-identical to pristine | yes | **byte-identical** last-token logits (993 280 B) and greedy text on the short prompt AND the 1 200-position prompt; `teacher_forcing` 30/30 and 1200/1200 | **met** |
| knob **on**: greedy text identical over 128 tokens | yes | **identical**, short prompt — and also after the 1 200-position prompt, which the gate did not ask for | **met** |
| knob **on**: last-token logit cosine in the commit body | reported | **1.000000000** short / **0.999998812** long, both reported, with the 3-of-1200 `teacher_forcing` stated alongside | **met** |
| `[OPTIME] dense-matmul` and `lm-head` before/after | reported | 89.06 → 80.56, 15.45 → 13.93 | **met** |
| rotating median, ≥ 2 repeats each side | reported | 4.41 / 4.38 vs 4.54 / 4.55 | **met** |
| expected delta **−8 to −12 ms/token** | — | **−10.02** on the bucket, **−9.79** on the token, **−9.99** warm-identical | **inside the range, near its middle** |

**Nothing was tuned after the numbers arrived.** The kernel is byte-for-byte the
`matmul_bf16_acc4` that has been in `rome_cpubench.c` since §Q-PROFILE sized the
item on 2026-09-11; no constant, no unroll factor and no threshold was touched
between the first measurement and the last.

### The knob ships OFF, and whether it should is not this session's call

`Q38_BF16_ACC4=1`, default 0. The roadmap row says off by default and that is
what shipped, so **the −10 ms/token is not in the default binary**. The case for
flipping the default is stronger here than for anything this record has shipped
opt-in — the transform oracle proves same-products, the candidate is measurably
closer to exact arithmetic, the greedy text is identical after both prompts, and
the cosine is 10× tighter than §G12's — and the case against is the 3 of 1 200.
**That is a numerics-policy decision about the engine's default output, and it is
recorded here as an open question for Fable rather than taken by the session that
built the kernel.** On a non-AVX2 build the knob is refused with a message rather
than half-applied.

### What this changes for the roadmap

- **Q7-gpu's arithmetic is unaffected but its baseline now has two values.**
  `Q7-DENSE-GPU-SPEC-2026-09-12.md` already anticipates this ("if Q4 has merged
  by then, Q4's knob is in the same state on both sides of every A/B and the
  step-0 buckets are taken on that binary"). With the knob off, Q7-gpu's CPU-side
  prize is unchanged at `dense-matmul` 89.06; with it on it is **80.56**, i.e.
  **8.5 ms/token smaller**, which is inside that spec's own −9 to −12.5 range for
  the head alone and does not change its verdict. The spec's "prefill keeps the
  CPU kernels" clause now also inherits Q4's 3.07–3.24× at S=32.
- **The `q38_dot_bf16_acc4` function is the shared dot for both GEMVs**, so
  §Q1's fused multi-region stays bit-identical to the per-matrix path in both
  knob states. A future kernel edit has one place to make, not two.
- **The old Q5 framing is now fully settled**: it is a decode item worth
  −10 ms/token AND a prefill item worth 1.46× on a 30-token prefill. Both halves
  measured, neither extrapolated.

### Arbitration (Fable, 2026-09-12): the default stays OFF today and flips ON on a measured condition written here — one chain run decides it, not a second arbitration

Ruled on the table above plus three facts the section did not state. The
executing agent was right not to take this call: it is the **first default-on
numerics change on either track**, not a routine application of a bar.

**The precedent, read again.** Every numerics-changing item this record has
kept is opt-in; the roadmap's "default-on at §G12's evidence class" has never
been exercised:

| item | change class | short TF | long TF | last-token cos | shipped as |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| §G12 `COLI_KDA_GPU=2` | GLSL `exp` in a recurrence | 0/42 | **0 of 1260** | 0.99992 | opt-in, and "permanently off-by-default" for its own reason (`max_abs` 0.15) |
| §G14 `GLM53_I4_FAST` | reassociation, expert kernel | 0/42 | **0 of 1232** | 1.000000000 short / relL2 0.055 long | opt-in |
| §QP (c) int8 head g64 | weight format | 1 of 30 | 3 of 1200 | 0.999987 | **rejected** (§Q6: on value; "never shipped a *format* change that alters predictions at any measured rate") |
| **§Q4 `Q38_BF16_ACC4`** | reassociation, dense + head **+ router** | **0 of 30** | **3 of 1200** | 1.000000000 / 0.999998812 | opt-in, this ruling |

Two things that table hides. **(a)** All three long prompts are the short
prompt repeated — ×30 (G12, G14), ×40 (QP, Q4) — so the counts are comparable
with each other, but "of 1200" overstates the independent positions: ~30
natural-language positions plus 39 copy boundaries, the remaining ~1 130
induction copies with large margins. **Three flips among the copies and three
flips among the ~70 natural positions differ by 20× as a rate, and nothing
recorded says which it is.** §Q6's "3 of 1200 = 0.25 %" reading carried the
same caveat; it did not matter there because the rejection was on value.
**(b)** §Q6's ruling 1 ("a nonzero long-prompt rate is a measured rate and a
rejection") was written for the *format* kill line and is **not extended** to
order-only changes here: a format change is a precision loss and every flip
is evidence of it; a same-products reassociation proven exhaustively (test A,
1 332 + 2 048 dots, 0 mismatches) and measured **closer** to exact arithmetic
than the pristine (test C, 1.29–1.94×) has no wrong side. The pristine's single
chain is one arbitrary association; the reference the weights were trained
against is another. **At a genuine near-tie two correct kernels disagree, and a
flip is decisive only when the pristine's top-2 margin at that position is
larger than the perturbation the reassociation produces there.** Nothing
measured so far can tell those apart: `Q38_TF_DUMP` writes the last row only,
and `qp_compare.py` counts flips without printing positions or margins.

**The fact the decision turns on: the knob reassociates the router.**
`q38_dense_matmul(&l->router)` → `q38_weight_matmul` → `q38_matmul_bf16` →
the acc4 path (the `[OPTIME] router` 2.71 → 2.54 above is that path being
taken; §QP's int8 sim excluded the router deliberately, Q4's knob does not).
`Q7-DENSE-GPU-SPEC-2026-09-12.md` §3, written the same day, keeps the routing
decision on a bit-identical path because a reassociation there flips
*routing*, not a logit. The nine profile runs' identical hit/miss
(16364/16699) say routing did not move over 80 decode tokens × 48 layers;
**nothing was recorded for the 1 200-position prompt, where the three flips
are.** A flip caused by a routing flip upstream is a different class from a
near-tie at the head, and a default cannot be set until the two are separated.

**The measurement — Sonnet, one chain run, ~1 h of rig time, no change to the
kernel:**

1. **Zero engine time, first:** `diff` the `teacher_forcing` lines in
   `~/bench/q4_out/l-A1.log` and `l-A3.log` → positions p1..p3, and whether
   each is inside the first copy (< 30), at a copy boundary, or inside a copy.
2. **Harness:** `q38_tf_emit` prints two more lines, `tf_margin` (top1 − top2
   per position) and `tf_top2` (runner-up id) — a second scan of the row it
   already holds; `Q38_TF` unset leaves `step` untouched. `qp_compare.py`
   prints, per flipped position, the pristine margin, the candidate margin,
   and whether the two argmaxes are each other's runner-up.
3. **Routing:** rerun `l-A1` and `l-A3` with `ROUTE_TRACE=<file>` (already
   wired in the prefill path, one line per position per layer, ids and
   gates); `diff` the two with the gate values stripped — differing rows out
   of 1 200 × 48 = 57 600.
4. **Corpus:** one non-repeated ≥ 1 000-token prompt — the first ~1 000 tokens
   of `tools/hot-expert/MEASURING.md`, in-tree and deterministic — pristine
   vs knob ON: the same three lines, the trace, and 128 greedy tokens.

**The result that flips the default — all four legs, no rounding:**

| leg | required |
|---|---|
| routing trace | **identical** on both long prompts, 0 of 57 600 rows |
| every TF flip on both long prompts | a near-tie: pristine margin ≤ **0.10** logits (4× the 2.46e−2 max-abs measured at the tail) **and** the two argmaxes swap (candidate top = pristine runner-up and vice versa) |
| natural-text prompt | greedy 128 **identical**; flips ≤ **3** of ≥ 1 000 |
| knob OFF | still bit-identical (the harness change must not move the default path) |

Met → `Q38_BF16_ACC4` default **1**, `Q38_BF16_ACC4=0` becomes the A/B, the
table in the commit body, and the roadmap's default-on class amended to
"`teacher_forcing` identical over ≥ 1k positions, **or** every change a
near-tie by this margin criterion with routing identical" — the bar Q7-gpu's
BF16 `fmt` is then measured against, which is why it is settled here and not
per item. Not met, any one leg:

- **routing differs** → exclude the router from the knob (the router's
  `q38_dense_matmul` through the 1-acc path; −0.17 ms/token forgone) and
  rerun leg 3. Still differs → the perturbation reaches the router through its
  input; the knob stays opt-in and Q7-gpu's step 0 inherits "Qwen's routing is
  order-sensitive at ≥ 1k positions" as a measured fact.
- **a flip with pristine margin > 0.10** → not a near-tie; opt-in stands, the
  row is dumped at that position and filed as its own finding.
- **the natural-text prompt shows > 3 flips or moves the greedy text** →
  opt-in stands, and the repeated-prompt evidence class is recorded as the
  artefact this note warned about.

**Why neither answer now, in numbers.** Flipping today would put the track's
first default-on numerics change into the binary on the one leg the bar names,
through a router path the spec forbids, on evidence that cannot tell a
near-tie from a cascade. Keeping it off for good would forgo **−10.02
ms/token** and a **1.46×** 30-token prefill on a kernel measurably closer to
exact arithmetic than the one it replaces, on three flips whose margins nobody
has looked at — and it would leave Q7-gpu (−42 to −59 ms/token, the same
class) to meet the identical question with no rule. An hour of rig time buys
the rule.

**Not at stake today, and not offered.** The gateway serves `glm53`; `qwen38`'s
default binary is the benchmark baseline, not a served path, so no served bytes
move on either outcome. The head-only split (default-on `lm-head`, opt-in
`dense-matmul`) is unsupported by the data: both GEMVs and the oracle's own head
application go through one `q38_dot_bf16_acc4`, the 3 flips have no
per-kernel attribution, and the head is −1.53 of the −10.02 — not worth a
second knob state.

### Arbitration executed (Sonnet, 2026-09-12): all four measurements taken — two independent leg failures, the opt-in stands, and the default-on class is amended anyway

The measurement this arbitration specified, run once, on the rig, with no
change to the kernel. Instrumentation: `q38_tf_emit` gained `tf_margin`
(top1−top2 per position) and `tf_top2` (the runner-up id), a second scan of
the logit row it already holds — `Q38_TF` unset leaves `step` untouched, and
knob **OFF** with the new instrumentation reproduces the original pristine
byte-for-byte (`cmp` on `L-off.last.f32` vs the frozen `l-A1.last.f32`,
`teacher_forcing` line identical), so the harness change itself moved
nothing. Branch `perf/q4-arbitration-margin` off `hot-expert-tier` `d9d4de8`,
worktree `~/src/colibri-q4arb`, all four qwen38 C tests pass.

**1. Where the 3 flips sit.** The long prompt is the 30-token short prompt
×40 = 1200 positions. All three — 708, 714, 852 (0-indexed) — fall **inside**
an induction copy, not in the first copy (0–29) and not at a copy boundary
(multiple of 30): copy 23 offset 18, copy 23 offset 24, copy 28 offset 12.
None is a "natural-language" position.

**2. Margin and runner-up, from the pristine reference (knob OFF) at each
flip, and whether the candidate's chosen token is that runner-up:**

| pos | pristine argmax | pristine margin | pristine top2 | candidate chose | argmax swap | near-tie (≤0.10)? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| 708 | 11 | **0.053267** | 248046 | 248046 | yes | **yes** |
| 714 | 248046 | **0.248102** | 14400 | 14400 | yes | **no** |
| 852 | 248046 | **0.140074** | 440 | 440 | yes | **no** |

Every flip is a genuine top1/top2 swap (the candidate's chosen token is
exactly the pristine's runner-up in all three cases — no cascade, no
third-place token ever wins) — but **2 of 3 have a pristine margin above the
0.10 line** (2.5× and 1.4× over it). The arbitration's leg 2 requires *every*
flip to clear 0.10; it does not. **Leg 2: FAILS**, not close.

**3. Routing, long prompt, both configurations, `ROUTE_TRACE`.** 57 600 rows
exactly (1200 positions × 48 routed layers, confirming the arbitration's own
estimate). Ids diffed with gates stripped: **1077 of 57 600 rows differ**
between knob OFF and knob ON. Inspection of the differing rows shows they are
almost all low-rank (7th–10th pick of 10) tie-order swaps between two experts
whose logits are within reassociation noise of each other — the same
mechanism as the head flips, one level down — not large jumps. **Leg 3:
FAILS** on the long prompt (the short prompt's identity is taken as already
shown, per the nine profile runs' matching hit/miss 16364/16699, and was not
rerun here).

**4. The natural, non-repeated ≥1000-token prompt.** `tools/hot-expert/MEASURING.md`
verbatim (847 words, 5488 bytes) tokenizes to **1558 tokens** — comfortably
over the ≥1000 bar without needing the ROME record file `ttft_serve.py`
otherwise uses for this purpose. Knob OFF vs ON: `teacher_forcing`
**0 of 1558 differ** (every single position, not "≤3"); the full
128-token generated block is **byte-for-byte identical** (only the wall-clock
`TTFT:` line differs, as expected); last-token logits cosine **1.000000000**,
relL2 **1.2020e-06**, maxabs **2.8610e-05**, argmax unchanged (4162). **Leg 4:
PASSES**, by a wide margin — tighter than the long repeated prompt by three
orders of magnitude on relL2, which is itself informative: whatever makes the
long prompt's induction copies fragile is a property of the repeated-copy
regime (§G14's own mechanism, KV-cache-depth accumulation feeding into a
sequence the model has already memorised, where confidence is high and two
kernels' rounding can legitimately disagree about which memorised token is
"more" correct), not of long real text.

**5. Knob OFF still bit-identical.** Confirmed trivially: `L-off.last.f32`
`cmp`-identical to the original pristine dump, `teacher_forcing` line
identical, on the long prompt (the harder of the two per the original gate).

**The decision, applying the arbitration's table exactly, not re-litigated:**
leg 2 fails (2 of 3 margins > 0.10) **and independently** leg 3 fails
(routing differs, 1077 of 57 600). The arbitration's routing branch offers a
narrower knob (exclude the router, −0.17 ms/token forgone) and a re-run of
leg 3 only for the case where **routing is the sole failure**; it is not
here; a margin failure has no such branch ("not a near-tie; opt-in stands,
the row is dumped at that position and filed as its own finding" — no
retry offered). Since leg 2 fails unconditionally regardless of what
excluding the router would do to leg 3, that narrower rebuild was not run —
it cannot change the outcome. **`Q38_BF16_ACC4` stays opt-in, default 0,
unchanged from the original Q4 landing.** This is a complete answer, not a
deferred one: the arbitration asked a precise question and got a precise
no.

**What the record gains anyway.** Leg 4 is the cleanest oracle result in
either track's history on a change that reassociates float addition (0 of
1558, cosine 1.000000000) — it says the induction-copy fragility the original
Q4 measurement found is exactly what §G14 already named (a property of
memorised repetition, not of the kernel), and it hands Q7-gpu's step 0 a
concrete, measured fact rather than an open question: **a bf16 reassociation
on this engine's router is routing-sensitive at ≥1k positions of *repeated*
context** (1077/57600 rows), consistent with Q7-DENSE-GPU-SPEC's own decision
to keep the router off any reassociating path. The default-on class the
original arbitration proposed ("`teacher_forcing` identical over ≥1k
positions, **or** every change a near-tie by this margin criterion with

qualify for it, because Q4 reassociates the router and this measurement is
