## Q7-gpu steps 0 and 1 (2026-09-12): the BF16 `fmt=9` dense path on dev0 — step 0 PASSES and predicts 19.6; step 1's oracle is clean and the token falls **−31.53 ms (18.4%)**, but `dn-proj` lands at **26.98** against a **≤ 26.4** gate and a **1.25× of 19.6** gate, and the 1.37× attenuation is measured to be the DUTY CYCLE, not the kernel. **Two numeric legs NOT MET — step 1 goes to arbitration, steps 2–3 not started, step 4 REFUSED on its own step-0 number.** Arbitrated 2026-09-12: step 1 ACCEPTED on a corrected gate, merge pending the serving A/B (`### Arbitration` at the end of this section).

Built from `tools/hot-expert/Q7-DENSE-GPU-SPEC-2026-09-12.md`, on branch
`perf/q7-gpu-dense-stream`, pristine = `hot-expert-tier` at **313f1f5** (i.e.
with Q4 merged, Q4's knob OFF on both sides of every A/B, as that spec requires).

### Step 0: the shader, and the two things the oracle caught before any timing

`fmt = 9` in `qmatmul.comp` / `rowwords` / `scale_floats` / `upload_tensor`: two
BF16 per uint32 word, low half = even column — which is what a little-endian
`uint16_t` row already is, so `upload_tensor` memcpys it verbatim. Dequant is
`bits << 16` / `bits & 0xffff0000`. No per-row scale (9 added to the shader's
no-scale list; a one-float `sbuf` keeps the descriptor set layout unchanged).
Four words per lane per step into four accumulators.

**Two process findings, both recorded because both would have produced a
confident wrong number:**

1. **`c/shaders/qmatmul.spv` is a TRACKED file** (the only tracked `.spv`;
   `6da3910` last regenerated it with the fmt=8 `.comp`). A fresh worktree
   checkout stamps the `.comp` and the `.spv` with the **same mtime**, so `make`
   considers the shader up to date and silently keeps the pristine one. Step 0's
   first run returned **−8 for every bf16 code** — which is the int4 `else`
   branch's `i4(0) = −8`, i.e. the bench had loaded the pre-Q7 `.spv`. The chain
   now deletes the `.spv` before building; the tracked artefact is regenerated in
   the commit.
2. **A measurement chain must rebuild the ENGINES, not just the shader.** The
   first `q7_probe.sh` run measured a `qwen38-vk` two commits old, so
   `Q38_DENSE_GPU_SCAN` existed in the source and not in the binary and its line
   simply never printed. `q7_build_engines` now runs before any run and prints
   the three sha256s.

**Correctness (`rome_vkbench <spv> q7`, two repeats, identical):**

| leg | result |
|---|---|
| EXHAUSTIVE dequant: all 65 536 bf16 codes × both lane parities, against the engine's own dot over the same 2-element row | **508 of 131 072 disagree, all 508 DENORMAL, 0 other — PASS** |
| LAYOUT: bit-exact vs `ref_engine` on integer data whose sums are order-independent, at 2560×10240, 6144×2560, 2560×12288, 10240×320, 320×10240, 2560×48, **2561×777** (odd I, odd O) | **0 rows differ at 7 of 7 shapes** |
| ACCURACY vs an f64 accumulation of the same products | gpu **1.02 / 1.19 / 1.00 / 1.27 / 0.83 / 1.08 / 1.01 e−7**; engine **3.16 / 4.84 / 3.14 / 6.11 / 1.27 / 3.28 / 3.10 e−7**; scalar 8.8e−7 … 1.6e−6 |

**The GPU kernel is 0.21–0.65× the CPU kernel's own error** — 1.5–4.8× *more*
accurate than what it replaces. Two corrections to the spec's own step-0 bar,
both of which were the bar being wrong rather than the kernel:

- The spec's "relL2 ≤ 1e−6 on random data" was stated against a **scalar f32**
  reference, which over I = 6144 random terms carries ~√I roundings of its own.
  Measured against it the GPU read 1.36e−6 and 1.58e−6 and "failed" — while
  being the *more* accurate of the two. The leg now uses an f64 truth and gates
  on **gpu ≤ engine**, which is what "summation order only, not a precision
  loss" actually asserts and does not have to be re-derived per shape.
- The exhaustive leg first compared against the raw `bf16_to_f32`, which made
  code `0x8000` (**negative zero**) a "disagreement": a sum that starts at +0.0
  turns −0.0 into +0.0 by IEEE 754, and the CPU kernel does the same. Comparing
  **dot against dot** removes it. That left exactly one real class.

**The one real class, and it is unreachable here.** RADV runs compute with fp32
denormals flushed to zero, so a bf16 with exponent field 0 and nonzero mantissa
(|v| < 2^−126) reads as ±0 on the device and as itself on the CPU.
`Q38_DENSE_GPU_SCAN=1` counted them in exactly the tensors this item uploads:
**0 of 3 977 707 520 bf16 values are denormal.** So on this checkpoint the fmt=9
dequant is bit-identical to `bf16_to_f32` on every value that exists, and the
numerics of the whole item reduce to summation order, as the spec claims.

**Timing — one submit per site, median of 10, pools > 96 MB Infinity Cache,
two repeats:**

| shape | MB/submit | median ms (r1 / r2) | GB/s | sites | **ms/token (r1 / r2)** |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| deltanet-A, 4 tensors I=2560 | 84.38 | 0.3353 / 0.3372 | 251.6 | 36 | **12.07 / 12.14** |
| deltanet-B, `out` I=6144 | 31.46 | 0.2101 / 0.2137 | 149.7 | 36 | **7.57 / 7.70** |
| qsa-A, 4 tensors I=2560 | 71.43 | 0.3620 / 0.3486 | 197.4 | 12 | **4.34 / 4.18** |
| qsa-B, `o` I=6144 | 31.46 | 0.2074 / 0.2718 | 151.7 | 12 | **2.49 / 3.26** |
| lm-head, 1.27 GB | 1271.40 | 2.7365 / 2.8499 | 464.6 | 1 | **2.74 / 2.85** |
| **gr-pair, chained, ONE submit** | 13.19 | 0.3930 / 0.2185 | 33.6 | 97 | **38.12 / 21.19** |

Compute-only rates (median less the 60 µs round trip): deltanet-A **306**,
deltanet-B **209**, lm-head **475 GB/s**. The kernel scales up well and is
overhead/occupancy-bound at small submits — the same shape the 09-04 matrix
found for int8 (190 small, 403 on the head).

**The four gates, re-derived from step 0 before step 1 was gated:**

| set | step-0 prediction | spec's gate | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `dn-proj` (A+B) | **19.64 / 19.83** | ≤ 26.4 | **CLEARS** — step 1 is built |
| `qsa-proj` (A+B) | **6.83 / 7.44** | ≤ half its measured bucket | see below |
| `lm-head` | **2.74 / 2.85** | ≤ 7.9 | CLEARS by 2.8× |
| **gr-pair** | **38.12 / 21.19** | **≤ 9.2** | **NOT MET by 2.3–4.1× — step 4 is NOT BUILT** |

**Step 4 is refused on its own step-0 number, which is the spec's own rule**
("Step 0's measured per-submit figure for this shape × 97 must be ≤ 9.2
ms/token or the step is not built and the reason is the measurement"). It is not
a near miss: the one-submit form costs **21.2–38.1 ms/token against the pair's
18.45 on the CPU**, i.e. the GPU arm is *slower than the CPU arm* before the
1.28 GB of VRAM is paid for. The cause is visible in the rate — 13.19 MB at
**33.6–60.4 GB/s**, an order below the head's 465 — because the pair is three
tiny dispatches (O = 320, O = 4, O = 10240 off a 320-wide input) with a pipeline
barrier in the middle, i.e. latency-bound at every stage. The `act` push
constant was therefore never built, `struct PC` is unchanged, and glm53's
push-constant range is untouched. **No arbitration is needed for step 4** — the
spec pre-authorised this refusal — but the consequence is that Q12 can no longer
move anything either (its only remaining lever was the pair's placement).

### Step 0 in the engine: `qsa-proj`, and the knob-off identity

The one set in §Q-PROFILE's table with no sub-timer. Measured, decode only,
three fresh-process repeats, median: **`qsa-proj` 15.803 ms/token** (split of

### Step 1: DeltaNet on dev0 (`Q38_DENSE_GPU=1`) — the oracle

Submit A = `{qkv, z, b, a}` all `src = −1`; submit B = `out`. Decode only
(S = 1); prefill keeps the CPU kernels. Against the **knob-off** binary, same
frozen histogram, same tier:

| leg | short | long (1200 positions) | spec's bar |
|---|---|---|---|
| greedy 128 | **identical** | **identical** | identical |
| `teacher_forcing` | **identical 30/30** | **identical 1200/1200** | identical, any change arbitrated |
| last-token relL2 | **1.9388e−06** | **4.1945e−07** | **≤ 1e−5** |
| cosine (9 dp) | **1.000000000** | **1.000000000** | 1.000000000 |
| max-abs (reported, not gated) | 2.7418e−05 | 5.7220e−06 | — |
| argmax | 328 = 328 | 248046 = 248046 | unchanged |

**Every numeric leg of the oracle is met, with 5× and 24× of headroom on the
relL2 bar.** And the class is exactly the one the spec calibrated against:
§QP's R3-vs-R1 measured **4.9e−7 long / 1.9e−6 last-token** for 1 440
reassociated GEMVs per token; this item reassociates 180 larger ones and reads
**4.19e−7 / 1.94e−6**. The prediction and the measurement agree to the digit.

One confirmation worth stating separately: on the short prompt the **last
PROMPT position is bit-identical** (relL2 0.0000e+00) while the generated tokens
differ. That is the `S == 1` gating working — prefill is computed by the CPU in
both arms — and it is why this item does not touch TTFT.

**The VRAM ledger, and it is exact.** Printed line: `Q7 dense on dev0: 180

the spec's 4.16 GB. Tier preloaded **13 827** in all three repeats against the

without adjustment. At mask 15 the whole set prints **7.96 GB / 531 tensors**
against the spec's 7.95 GB (531 not 532 because the final gated residual has no
`inject`).

**The token fell MORE than its own bucket, and the reason is measured, not
assumed:** −31.53 against `Δdn-proj` −25.88. The extra −5.6 is `moe` −6.95,
which decomposes as `vk-take` −6.01 and `cpu-experts` +1.36 — the dense
reservation evicted 846 experts, so the GPU expert group is smaller, the idle
wait for it shrinks, and the extra CPU experts are partly absorbed in the gap.
§Q3's finding that the gap is unevenly distributed is the reason "partly". **In
a fresh-process 32-token run the eviction is a net GAIN, not the +2.5 ms/token
§QP(d) priced on warm-identical serving.** Those are different regimes and
§QP(d) is explicit that a fresh-process number is a diagnosis; the serving A/B
is what prices it, and it was not run (see the stop).

### Why it undershoots: the duty cycle, and it is NOT the kernel

Step 0 predicted 19.64 from back-to-back submits; the identical dispatches cost
26.96 in the engine — a **1.37× in-engine attenuation**, the failure CLAUDE.md
names ("a kernel that is fast in L3 and slow in the engine is the usual
failure"). Per submit that is 0.374 ms in-engine against 0.273 isolated.

`bench_q7_dutycycle` replays **exactly those two submits** with a busy-wait
between them of the engine's own measured length (`dn-recur` 9.28 ms/token over
36 layers = 0.26 ms between A and B) and nothing else changed:

| gap A→B / B→A | ms/layer (r1 / r2) | ×36 = ms/token |
|---|---|---:|
| 0.00 / 0.00 — the back-to-back control | 0.5169 / 0.5169 | **18.61 / 18.61** |
| 0.26 / 0.00 | 0.5412 / 0.5280 | 19.48 / 19.01 |
| **0.26 / 1.50 — the engine's own gaps** | 0.9631 / 0.7629 | **34.67 / 27.46** |
| 0.26 / 3.00 | 0.6234 / 0.6749 | 22.44 / 24.30 |

**The engine measures 26.98 and the idle gap alone reproduces it** (27.46 at the
closest-matching gap, bracketing it between 19.0 and 34.7). Same code, same
shapes, same VRAM, same pool: the only variable is that dev0 idles in
sub-millisecond bursts 72 times a token and never reaches the clocks a
back-to-back loop holds it at. **So the spec's step-0 remedy — "the fix is in
the kernel (wider loads, `uvec4` per lane)" — would not close this gap**, and
neither would a threshold. The remaining levers are on the duty cycle (keeping
dev0 busy across the gap), which is a different item and interacts with §Q3's
finding that the gap is unevenly distributed across layers.

Note the non-monotonicity at 3.00 ms, and that the two repeats of the 1.50 ms
row span 7.2 ms/token — this effect is real in sign and noisy in magnitude,
which is itself consistent with a power-state explanation rather than a
throughput one.

### Arbitration (Fable, 2026-09-12): step 1 ACCEPTED on a corrected gate — the miss is the microbenchmark's, not the mechanism's; merge INCREMENTAL and on the serving A/B the spec always required; the half floor moves from the step to the arm

Ruled on the tables above; no further diagnostic requested. The spec's
escalation clause fired as written (26.98 is outside the 14.8–25.2 step-0
bracket) and the executing agent was right to stop at step 1 rather than
proceed past an ungated step. `hot-expert-tier` (`a19b938`) was merged into
the branch at `32b6e26` before this was written: the code merged clean as the
section above says; the record did NOT — both sides had appended at the end —
and was resolved by hand with §Q4's two arbitration sections placed before
this one.

**What kind of miss this is, and it is a third kind.** §Q3: the target was
right and the mechanism's yield model wrong — the fix was a ceiling formula.
§Q1: the mechanism was right and the target mis-measured — the fix was step 0
re-deriving the gate. Here the target is measured (52.86) and the mechanism
delivered exactly what step 0 said a two-submit-per-layer BF16 dispatch
delivers — 18.61 back-to-back in `bench_q7_dutycycle`'s control against 19.6
in step 0 — and the miss is in the *transfer* from the microbenchmark to the
engine: step 0 timed the submits back-to-back, and the engine issues them 72
times a token separated by 0.26 and ~1.5 ms of CPU work, in which dev0 idles
and de-clocks. The same two submits at the engine's own gaps cost 27.46–34.67;
the engine measured 26.98, *below* the replay. The 1.25× allowance was a guess
written before any BF16 submit had run on this box; the measured in-engine
attenuation of this dispatch shape is 1.37× and its cause is not in the kernel
(the spec's own remedy, wider loads, acts on a term that is not the one that
grew). CLAUDE.md names this failure — "a kernel that is fast in L3 and slow in
the engine" — and the record already has it the other way round for serial
loops (§Q1's inverse attenuation, which §Q2 then showed is not a rule either).
The lesson, filed as its own: **a step-0 microbenchmark that predicts an
in-engine bucket for a GPU dispatch must replay the engine's inter-submit
gaps, not run back-to-back.** The case exists now (`rome_vkbench … q7`,
duty-cycle) and binds steps 2–3, with ≥ 5 repeats — the two repeats at
0.26/1.50 span 7.2 ms/token, so two are not a prediction.

**What the gate should have read, and is now recorded as** — per step: knob
off bit-identical (met); knob on greedy and `teacher_forcing` identical at 30
and 1200 positions, relL2 ≤ 1e−5 (met at 1.94e−6 / 4.19e−7, the exact class
§QP's R3-vs-R1 calibrated, to the digit); the bucket ≤ 1.25× step 0's
prediction **taken at the engine's own inter-submit gaps** (met — 26.98
against a replay of 27.46–34.67, no allowance consumed); the untouched
sub-buckets flat (met); the preload within ±50 of the ledger (met, ±3); the
serving A/B per step against the floor below. **The half floor moves from the
step to the arm:** `dn-proj` + `qsa-proj` + `lm-head` ≤ **42.2 ms/token**
(half of 52.86 + 15.80 + 15.8 = 84.5) when step 3 lands. That is where the
spec's own merge condition already sat ("the branch merges when steps 1–3
have met their gates") and where its −42 to −59 was stated; per-step halves
were the spec applying §Q3's and §Q1's floor one level too low, to an arm
whose three steps share one mechanism and one attenuation. At the measured
1.37× the arm predicts 26.98 + 9.4–10.2 + 2.8–4.0 = **39–41**: it clears the
floor by 1–3 ms and can fail it, which is what a floor is for. Step 2's
per-step half (7.90) is *expected* to be missed at this attenuation
(9.4–10.2) and that is not a stop — step 2 is gated on its replayed prediction
and the arm on 42.2. A miss of 42.2 with every per-step gate met comes back
here on the arm's warm-identical token delta; the half is not lowered per
step to avoid that.

**Why not reject, and why not re-plan the submits.** The duty-cycle table
locates the cost: the A→B gap (the 0.26 ms recurrence) costs 0.4–0.9
ms/token; the B→next-A gap (the rest of the layer) costs 8–16. Fusing A and B
— the one-submit-per-layer form, a G12-class kernel — would recover under
1 ms of attenuation plus 36 round trips (~2.2), for days of work; the spec's
choice of two submits stands. The QSA layers have the same gap shape
(0.29 ms of `qsa-attn` between A and B, the rest of the layer after) and
inherit the same attenuation; the head is one 2.7 ms submit with 2.8× of
headroom against its gate even if it attenuates as badly. The arm's viability
is the arithmetic above: it lands at the spec's own pessimistic end, on a
clean oracle, with an exact ledger. What the finding does open is a lever the
spec did not have — dev0's idle clocks between submits, worth up to
26.98 − 19.6 ≈ 7 ms/token on step 1 alone and something on every submit the
engine makes — and it is logged as **Q13** with a zero-code step 0 (the DPM
performance level, which needs the owner's sudo), not folded into this item.

**Merge: incremental, and not today.** Step 1 merges on its own once its
serving A/B is taken — not held for steps 2–3 — for three reasons. The step-0
artefacts (`fmt=9`, the regenerated tracked `.spv`, the `backend_vulkan.c`
cases, the `rome_vkbench` legs, `q7_probe.sh`, `q7_glm_check.sh`) are the
foundation steps 2–3 build on, and a foundation on a branch that
`hot-expert-tier` has already moved under once is a foundation that drifts.
The knob is off by default and glm53 is verified identical on its own
shaders, so the merge changes no default bytes and no served path. And steps
2–3 are expected to change `qwen38_core.h` only (the shader and backend cases
are step 0's), so the shared-file re-acceptance (`serve_candidate.sh` /
`accept_live.sh` / `accept_ui.sh`) is paid once, at this merge, whichever way
the item is split — if step 3's cached readback does need a backend change,
the glm53 check is per step anyway. The spec's "merges when 1–3 have met
their gates" was written for one Opus session in one stretch; that session
stopped at the gate as it should, and this is the place to amend it.

**What the merge waits for — two things the spec already required, written
here so that a chain decides and not a second arbitration:**

1. **The serving A/B.** `rome_bench.sh qwen38-vk`, interleaved two-and-two,
   knob off vs `Q38_DENSE_GPU=1`, both from the merged tip (`32b6e26` or
   later); Qwen 100 % resident by `fincore` before every phase; a frozen
   `.coli_usage` copy; the rig lock. **Merge when** the warm-identical token
   is down by ≥ **15.8 ms/token** against its paired pristine (half of the
   fresh-process −31.53, the track's floor applied to the regime transfer;
   ≈ ≥ 6.2 tok/s against ~5.63; the prediction is −23 to −29: the bucket's
   −25.9 less §QP (d)'s +2.5 rule price, plus whatever of the fresh-process
   `vk-take` −6 survives serving), both candidate runs above both pristine
   runs, **and** the rotating median not below its paired pristine rows read
   inside the campaign (§Q1's rule; §QP (d) measured +7.9 rotating at 3.4 GB
   of ballast, so the eviction is priced there and a rotating gain of roughly
   −26 + 9 is still expected). Either leg missed → back here with the four
   rows; the floor is not moved.
2. **`tworeq.py` for qwen38** (`TWOREQ_ARCH` / `TWOREQ_SNAP`, Sonnet, hours)
   and three identical requests in one persistent engine byte-identical with
   the knob on — the spec put this in step 1's commit and it is not on the
   branch. Cheap, and "the state a request leaves behind" is the rule P7b
   was.

Then: the knob-off identity re-confirmed against a pristine rebuilt from
`a19b938` (`~/bench/qwen38-vk.q7base` is 313f1f5), the six tests (four
qwen38, two glm53 — `backend_vulkan.c` changed), the merge with the tables in
its body, glm53's binary re-accepted through `serve_candidate.sh`, and steps
2–3 from `hot-expert-tier`.

**The default.** Not decided at step 1 and not by this ruling. §Q4's executed
arbitration amended the default-on class to "`teacher_forcing` identical over
≥ 1k natural positions with the router off any reassociating path" and named
Q7-gpu as the kernel it was written for. Step 1 clears the harder prompt
(0 of 1200 on the repeated one where Q4's knob flipped 3), but the natural
1558-token prompt and the routing trace have not been run for it, and the
router's *input* is reassociated here even though the router is not. The
default is decided once, at the arm's merge, with all landed bits on: the

so a default-on moves every later Q-item's pristine by ~−40 ms and nothing
the owner uses.

**Step 4 and Q12.** The refusal stands as the spec pre-authorised it and
needs nothing from here: 21.2–38.1 against 18.45 is not a near miss, and the
`act` push constant was rightly never built. One correction to the sentence
"Q12 can no longer move anything": what is gone is Q12's *placement*
consequence — the pair stays on the CPU whatever an int8 subset shows. Its
prize on the token is not gone: the pair is 18.45 ms/token of CPU BF16 and an
int8 pair would be ~7.9, so a surviving subset is worth ~−10 ms/token there,
more than step 4 ever promised. It is also the subset least likely to survive
(194 tensors at 97 sites, against a kill line one tensor already failed,

gate. The row now says that, and it is sequenced after Q7 steps 2–3 and Q13.

One measured surprise that is NOT in the moved buckets: ~7 ms/token of CPU-side inflation in `gr-read` and the routed path at mask 7, stable across three repeats and reported here rather than tuned away.

### Step 0 for steps 2 and 3: the gap replay, which is now the required form

`rome_vkbench <spv> q7s23`. `bench_q7_dutycycle` is generalised to
`bench_q7_layer(name, I1, OsA, nA, I2, OsB, nB, gap_ab, gap_ba, copies, reps,
outer, per_token, engine)`: `nB = 0` is the one-submit form (the head), and
`outer` whole-configuration repeats each produce an independent median, so the
**span across repeats** is printed next to the median-of-medians. Five outer
repeats per configuration, per the arbitration ("the two repeats at 0.26/1.50
span 7.2 ms/token, so two are not a prediction").

The LM head's shape had never been checked for correctness, only timed. It is
now:

| leg, `I = 2560`, `O = 248 320` | result |
|---|---|
| LAYOUT vs `ref_engine` on order-independent integer data | **0 of 248 320 rows differ** |
| ACCURACY vs an f64 accumulation | gpu **9.999e−08**, engine 3.181e−07, scalar 8.821e−07 → **gpu is 0.31× the engine's own error** |
| gpu-vs-engine max-abs (reported) | 6.485e−05 |

**QSA, 4-tensor A (71.4 MB) + `o` B (31.5 MB), ×12 layers.** The engine's own
gaps with `Q38_DENSE_GPU=1`: A→B is `qsa-attn` 3.46 + `qsa-index` 0.13 over 12
layers = **0.30 ms**; B→next-A is the rest of a QSA layer, bracketed 1.00–3.00.

| gap A→B / after B | med-of-5 ms/site | span across the 5 | **×12 = ms/token** |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| 0.00 / 0.00 — the back-to-back control | 0.3167 | 0.3072..0.4833 | **3.800** |
| 0.30 / 0.00 | 0.6126 | 0.6108..0.6286 | 7.351 |
| 0.30 / 1.00 | 0.7416 | 0.7336..0.8366 | 8.900 |
| **0.30 / 1.50 — the engine's own gaps** | **0.7981** | 0.7924..0.8048 | **9.577** |
| 0.30 / 3.00 | 0.9043 | 0.8871..0.9055 | 10.852 |

**The LM head, one 1.27 GB submit, ×1 per token.**

| gap after the submit | med-of-5 ms | span | **ms/token** |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| 0.00 — the back-to-back control | 2.2726 | 2.2694..3.1861 | **2.273** |
| 1.50 | 3.3682 | 3.3621..3.3909 | **3.368** |
| 3.00 | 3.3711 | 3.3550..3.4236 | 3.371 |
| 10.00 | 3.3924 | 3.3876..3.4221 | 3.392 |
| 30.00 | 4.8368 | 4.8121..4.8594 | 4.837 |

**Two things this replay says that the back-to-back table could not.** The QSA
attenuation at the engine's gaps is **2.52×** (3.800 → 9.577), a good deal
worse than DeltaNet's 1.37× — twelve layers means proportionally more idle per
submit. And the head's attenuation **saturates**: 1.5, 3 and 10 ms of idle all
cost the same 3.37–3.39, and only a 30 ms gap (longer than a whole token at
mask 7) pushes it to 4.84. A 2.7 ms submit ramps its own clocks; a 0.2–0.36 ms
one does not. The predictions carried into the gates are therefore
**`qsa-proj` 9.577 (bracket 8.90–10.85)** and **`lm-head` 3.368–3.392**.

The replay's gap is IDLE where the engine's is partly dev0 running expert
groups, so this is still the pessimistic end — and the engine again came in
**below** it, on both sets.

### Steps 2 and 3 in the engine — the oracle, at every mask and both prompts

Step 2 is `q38_attention`'s two projection calls wrapped exactly as DeltaNet's
were: submit A = `{q, k, v, idx_qk}` all `src = −1`, submit B = `o`, with the
CPU index and attention stages between them. Step 3 is `step`'s single
`q38_weight_matmul` on `m->lm_head`. The upload side needed nothing: the QSA
and head entries were already in `q38vk_dense_reserve` from step 0.

**One accounting fix the head forced.** `q38vk_dense_multi` added its elapsed
time to `dense-matmul` unconditionally, but the head's CPU path is
`q38_weight_matmul` and has **never** been inside that bucket (89.7 = `dn-proj`
52.9 + `qsa-proj` 15.9 + the four `gr-*` + `router`; `lm-head` 15.8 sits next to
it, not in it). Charging the submit there would make `dense-matmul` mean one
thing with the knob off and another with it on — the one property the A/B
depends on. The function is now `q38vk_dense_multi_ex(..., charge_dense)` with
`charge_dense = 0` for exactly one caller, the head; `vk-dense` still counts it.

| leg | mask 2 | mask 3 | mask 4 | mask 7 | bar |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| short greedy 128 | identical | identical | identical | identical | identical |
| short `teacher_forcing` | **30/30** | **30/30** | **30/30** | **30/30** | identical |
| short last-token relL2 | **1.9894e−06** | **2.0758e−06** | **2.0093e−06** | **1.7475e−06** | **≤ 1e−5** |
| short cosine (9 dp) | 1.000000000 | 1.000000000 | 1.000000000 | 1.000000000 | 1.000000000 |
| short max-abs (reported) | 2.6703e−05 | 3.0041e−05 | 2.8133e−05 | 2.3127e−05 | — |
| short argmax | 328 = 328 | 328 = 328 | 328 = 328 | **328 = 328** | unchanged |
| long greedy / `teacher_forcing` | identical / **1200/1200** | identical / **1200/1200** | identical / **1200/1200** | identical / **1200/1200** | identical |
| long relL2 / cosine / argmax | 4.2018e−07 / 1.000000000 / 248046 | 4.1945e−07 / 1.000000000 / 248046 | 4.2018e−07 / 1.000000000 / 248046 | 4.1679e−07 / 1.000000000 / 248046 | ≤ 1e−5 |

**Knob off, against the a19b938 pristine** (merge criterion 3): last-token
logits **BIT-IDENTICAL, 993 280 bytes**, relL2 0.0000e+00, greedy identical,
`teacher_forcing` identical 30/30 and 1200/1200, on **both** prompts.

The head's own leg, which the spec asked to be stated separately because the
head is the one tensor whose reassociation lands directly on the logits: **the
argmax at the last position is unchanged on both prompts at mask 4 and mask 7**
(328 and 248046).

### A correction to step 1's reading of the long-prompt number, found here

The long runs use `N_NEW=1`, and `print_gen` captures `DUMP` at `s == 0` — which
is the **prefill's** logit row, the same row `q38_tf_emit` writes to
`Q38_TF_DUMP`. `md5sum` confirms it: within every long run the two dumps are the
same bytes. So the long prompt's "last-token relL2" is a number about the
**prefill**, and prefill is CPU in both arms (`S != 1` refuses every dispatch).
It is nonzero anyway, and the reason is measured, not guessed:

| long run | mask | tier preloaded | prefill logits |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `b2-lR2`, `l-R2` | off | 14 673 | **byte-identical to each other** |
| `l-R3` (step 1) | 1 | 13 827 | **byte-identical to `l-R5`** |
| `l-R5` | 3 | 13 577 | **byte-identical to `l-R3`** |
| `l-R4` | 2 | 14 423 | differs from all of the above |

Mask 1 and mask 3 evict 846 and 1 096 experts and produce **the same prefill
bytes**; mask 2 evicts 250 and produces different ones. That is not a prefill
dispatch — it is the **expert-tier eviction changing which routed experts are
served by the GPU fp8 shader and which by the CPU kernel**, i.e. exactly §QP's
R3-vs-R1 placement class (relL2 4.9e−7 long, greedy identical), and the 250
experts mask 2 drops happen to be on this prompt's routed path while the extra
250 that mask 3 drops on top of mask 1 are not. The **short** prompt's prefill
is bit-identical at every mask, because its routed set survives every eviction.

So: **the item's own reassociation is measured on the short prompt's generated
tokens (1.7–2.1e−06 over 128 decode steps); the long prompt measures the
eviction's placement effect (4.2e−07) with `teacher_forcing` identical over
1 200 positions.** Step 1's table reported the long number without that
distinction; it is the same number, and this is what it is a number about.

### What the arm costs on the CPU side, which the bucket arithmetic does not show

The token falls **−43.12** while the three moved buckets fall **−45.82**. The
difference is not noise and it is not in one place:

| term | Δ vs knob off | note |
|---|---:|---|
| `dn-proj` + `qsa-proj` + `lm-head` | **−45.82** | the item |
| `moe` | −5.27 | `vk-take` −8.60, `vk-issue` −2.30, `cpu-experts` **+2.77**, `shared` **+2.23**, `router` +0.60 |
| `gr-read` | **+6.35** | `gr-down` +2.82, `gr-up` +2.83, the rest +0.70 |
| `dn-conv`/`recur`/`qknorm`/`gnorm` | +1.02 | |
| `qsa-attn`/`index`/`rest` | +0.05 | |
| sum | −43.67 | against the measured −43.12 |

**The +6.35 on `gr-read` and the +2.2 on `shared` are stable**, not an outlier:
across the three repeats `gr-read` reads 27.959 / 28.208 / 28.424 at mask 7
against 21.835 / 21.858 / 22.375 knob off. They are CPU BF16 GEMV loops this
item does not touch, over weights it does not move, and they got ~28 % slower.

It does not track the eviction (mask 2 drops 250 experts and `gr-read` is flat
at +0.12; mask 3 drops 1 096 and it is +1.84), nor the submit count alone (mask
3 and mask 7 differ by one submit and by 4.5 ms of `gr-read`). What it does
track is the time the token spends *waiting on a fence*: `vk-dense` 0 → 8.5 →
4.1 → 34.5 → 38.9 against `gr-read` +0.00 → +0.12 → +0.18 → +1.84 → +6.35. The
CPU now idles 97 times a token in sub-millisecond bursts, which is the same
shape as the dev0 duty cycle §Q7 step 1 measured — **on the other processor.**
That is a hypothesis with a correlation behind it, not a finding: it is
**not** diagnosed here, it is logged as **Q14**, and the honest statement is
that ~7 ms/token of the arm's raw −45.8 comes back somewhere this item did not
look. The serving A/B is what prices the net.

`cpu-experts` +2.77 is not in that class and needs no hypothesis: 1 368 more
experts are served by the CPU, and §QP (d) priced them.

### The other engine, and it did not move

Steps 2 and 3 touch `c/qwen38_core.h` only — the shared files (`qmatmul.comp`,
`backend_vulkan.c`) are step 0's and were checked against glm53 there. Proved
with the binary rather than with the diff: `glm53` built from step 1's tip
(`90e1f21`) and from this candidate are **byte-identical**, sha256
`a8e10ecf09edc05c3049c667ffcba05beb73b30415409a40214a4ba0e1f565db` on both. The
§Q7 step-1 glm53 oracle therefore still applies without re-running it, and the
serving re-acceptance at the merge is the one the arbitration already scheduled.

### Merged, and the serving path re-accepted because glm53's shaders changed

Merged into `hot-expert-tier` as `fb8d3cd`. The arm ships **no default-path
change** — `Q38_DENSE_GPU` unset is 0 is today's binary, bit-identical — and
qwen38 is not the served engine at all. glm53 is, and its `qmatmul.spv` gained
`fmt = 9` at step 0, so CLAUDE.md's rule applies whether or not glm53's own
code path moved (it did not: the binary is byte-identical to step 1's).

Page cache handled first: Qwen evicted, GLM `cat`-warmed and `fincore`-checked,
because `rome_bench.sh` had just read 173 GiB of Qwen and a cold GLM restart
would have failed the acceptance for a reason that is not the binary.

## §EDGE0: the edge0 evaluation — the residency gap is the clamp, and routing prediction cannot touch it

**Not a roadmap item.** An evaluation of five techniques from
[edge0](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/edge0), an MLX/SSD streaming-MoE framework,
against this tree (brief: `tools/hot-expert/EDGE0-IMPROVEMENTS-2026-09.md`).
Four were screened out before any rig time; the fifth is measured here and
**REJECTED**, with the number that killed it. **No engine code was changed by
this evaluation** — the binary in service is the same one that was in service
before it (sha256 `a8e10ecf09edc05c`), and the probe is a pure environment A/B.

### The four that did not need the rig

| # | edge0 technique | verdict | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | `pin_bonus` (predicted experts get retention priority) | **already exists** | `PILOT_EVICT_GUARD` (`docs/ENVIRONMENT.md:76`), and the general question is superseded by P10 value-based eviction |
| 3 | staged fixed-slot double-buffering | **already explored / inapplicable** | see below |
| 4 | Recover-LoRA | **defer** | a training pipeline; no named int4 quality gap for GLM to fix (§G15 mapped the format landscape) |
| 5 | `MoESpec`/`RouterKind` unification | **skip** | refactor value only, no delta |

**#3 confirmed inapplicable, for a reason stronger than the expected overlap.**
The slot table does already exist (`st_map_shard_range`, 288 slots/layer over 42
sparse layers, 12096/12096 mappable, `copy=0`). But edge0's design exists to buy
"zero host sync per layer per step", and **glm53 has no such sync to remove**:
its router is computed entirely on the host in f32 (`c/glm53.c:3122-3229`,
`l->router` dots producing `chosen[]`/`weight[]`), and the GPU tier is a static
host-side registry, so there is no GPU→host readback of routing anywhere in the
decode path. What crosses to the device is activation rows plus preloaded tensor
handles, and the fence wait is already overlapped with CPU expert compute by G9
(`can_defer`, `c/glm53.c:3350`).

### #1, the prerouter, re-framed as a correctness question

The throughput framing is settled and was not re-opened
(`docs/experiments/inference-paper-test-matrix-2026-07-28.md` row M3: `PREFETCH=1`
lowered replay throughput 2.5%; the coupling table predicted almost exclusively
resident experts). The untested question was the one §G15 opened: *does
per-token routing prediction plus pinning make GLM-5.3's output consistent
across tier-residency configurations?*

**Three code facts found before any run, each of which the measurement then
confirmed:**

1. **§G15 had already isolated the mechanism, and it is not the residency set.**
   Its `EXPERTS_CPU=2` arm is a maximal residency-set change — 79% of routed
   evaluations move off the tier — with the *function* held constant, and it is
   `teacher_forcing`-identical over 42 **and** 1232 positions.
2. **glm53's GPU tier is immutable after startup.** `reg[0]` is written in
   exactly three places (`c/glm53.c:2722`, `:2761`, `:2783`), all inside
   `vk_preload_tier()`, which runs once from a frozen histogram. No runtime
   insertion, no tier eviction. Placement is `vk_reg_at(index, eid)[0] != NULL`
   (`c/glm53.c:3407`). **A per-token predictor has nothing to steer.**
3. **There is no PILOT/COUPLE machinery in glm53 to repurpose.** `PILOT`,
   `PILOT_REAL`, `PILOT_TWO`, `PILOT_K`, `COUPLE`, `COUPLE_D`,
   `PILOT_EVICT_GUARD` live in `colibri.c`/`olmoe.c`/`qwen36.c`; the count is
   **0** in `glm53.c`, `sparse_index.h`, `backend_vulkan.c` and `st.h`, and
   `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md`'s glm53 section lists none of them. The brief's
   "repurpose it" would be a port into an engine with no prediction code.

### What was run

**§G15 measured residency-dependence with the placement-*forcing* knob. It never
varied the tier itself. This does.** One binary (the in-service glm53, no
build), §G15's two prompts (43 tokens `--greedy 128 --logits 512`; the same ×30
= 1232 positions `--greedy 0`), 8 threads pinned, frozen histogram copy per run,
`GLM53_PREFIX_CKPT=0` with a private `COLI_CKPT_DIR`, GLM 100.0% page-cache
resident at the start (91.7% by the long phase). **Only `COLI_VK_EXPERTS2/3`
changes.** B and C are deliberately off the recorded baseline — CLAUDE.md
requires 1695/1695 because changing the tier changes routing, which is the
effect under test; **no run here produces or may be compared to a tok/s number.**

The engine's own `[PROF] eg=…(experts=N) cpu=…(n=K)` gives the mediating
variable — the share of routed-expert evaluations taking the **unclamped** GPU
kernel rather than the CPU's `swiglu_clamped(limit=10.0)`:

| config | `COLI_VK_EXPERTS2/3` | tier resident | decode unclamped | prefill unclamped |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| **A** | 1695 / 1695 | 1296+1695+1695 = 4686 | **79.29%** (34099/43008) | 13.04% |
| **C** | 848 / 848 | 1296+848+848 = 2992 | **63.58%** (27346/43008) | 7.84% |
| **B** | 0 / 0 (dev2/dev3 skipped) | 1296 | **45.35%** (19505/43008) | 3.13% |

A's 79.29% reproduces §G15's "~79%" independently.

### The result

| pair | what changes | short TF (42) | short cos / relL2 | long TF (1232) | long cos / relL2 | greedy text |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sA1 vs sA2 | **nothing** (null control) | **identical** | **1.000000000 / 0** | — | — | IDENTICAL |
| sB1 vs sB2 | nothing (null control, B) | **identical** | **1.000000000 / 0** | — | — | IDENTICAL |
| **A vs B** | **tier config only** | **1 of 42 differ** (at 31) | **0.998848128 / 0.04935** | **1 of 1232 differ** (at 31) | **0.993094459 / 0.1176** | **DIFFERS at char 5** |
| A vs B, repeat | — | 1 of 42, at 31 | 0.998848128 / 0.04935 | — | — | DIFFERS at char 5 |
| A vs C | tier config only | identical | 1.000000000 / 1.22e−5 | identical | 0.998614315 / 0.05531 | **DIFFERS at char 334** |
| **sA_nc vs sB_nc** | **tier config, `EXPERTS_CPU=2` both sides** | **identical** | **1.000000000 / 0** | — | — | **IDENTICAL** |

Last-token argmax is unchanged in every pair (13646 short, 81247 long). Both
headline rows are **within** the pre-committed bound (§G15's extreme: 6 of 42 /
8 of 1232, cos 0.992324 / 0.981143), as the mechanism predicts, since A-vs-B
moves a strict subset of the activations that §G15's knob moved.

**The headline, in the owner's terms: two legitimate configurations of the same
binary, the same weights and the same prompt give different answers.** Config B
is what an unset cap gives you (CLAUDE.md: "an *unset* cap does not fill the
tier, it skips dev2/dev3 entirely"), and against the standard 1695/1695 it
changes a teacher-forced prediction at both prompt lengths and rewrites the
first sentence of the reply. This is §G15's finding promoted from a knob to a
configuration.

### Why this is a REJECT of edge0 #1, and not a tuning problem

**The falsification arm is the whole verdict.** Re-run A and B under
`GLM53_EXPERTS_CPU=2` — every routed expert on the CPU with the clamp disabled,
so both configurations compute the *same function* and the tier is never
consulted — and they become **bit-identical: relL2 exactly 0, max-abs 0,
`teacher_forcing` identical, greedy text identical.** The residency set's
contribution to the divergence, with the function held constant, is **zero**.

A predictor-and-pin scheme changes the residency set. The residency set
contributes 0. There is no mechanism by which it can shrink this gap.

Three further reasons, each independently sufficient:

- **Direction.** The ladder 79.29% → 63.58% → 45.35% is the share running
  *unclamped*. Pinning more experts into VRAM raises it, i.e. moves the engine
  **further** from the checkpoint's own `swiglu_limit = 10.0`. Consistency
  toward the non-conformant function is not a correctness fix.
- **Ceiling.** A perfect prerouter is the 100%-resident limit, whose function is
  exactly what `EXPERTS_CPU=2` computes — and §G15 measured *that* against
  pristine as `teacher_forcing`-identical over 42 and 1232 positions
  (cos 0.999999996 / 0.999024). At config A a perfect pin buys nothing
  measurable.
- **Capacity.** 100% residency is 288 × 42 experts at ~14.2 MB = **171 GB**
  (`c/glm53.c:2124`) against 72 GB of VRAM, of which the tier already holds
  4686 of 12096 (38.7% by count, 79% by activation). Off by ~2.5×.

**Verdict: REJECT.** Killed by `relL2 0` on the falsification arm — the number
that says the residency set contributes nothing once the two paths agree.

**The fix this evaluation does not make.** The gap is the missing `limit` push
constant in `c/shaders/qmatmul_gate_up.comp:134` (`silu(gate)*up`, unbounded),
which is already the named open item on this engine (ROADMAP §4h by-product,
lines 877–887). This evaluation deliberately did not touch it: it is a shader
item with its own gate, not an edge0 technique.

### A methodological note, repeating §G15's

**Config C is `teacher_forcing`-identical at both lengths, cosine 1.000000000 on
the short prompt (relL2 1.2e−5) — and still writes different text**, diverging
at char 334. The greedy-text oracle alone would have called C a regression and
would have called B's char-5 divergence catastrophic; `teacher_forcing` puts
them at 0 of 42 and 1 of 42. On this prompt the model is chaotic and text read
by eye is not an oracle, exactly as §G15 found.

Q11 asked for one `collapse(2)` on `q38_gr_apply` plus the revival of §Q2's
rejected rms pragma, for **−0.4 to −0.5 ms/token**, on the stated mechanism that
"with this loop parallel the invalidation is paid eight ways instead of one, and
the rms half becomes free". **Five arms were built behind one knob and measured
in a single campaign. The best of them is −0.10 ms/token on the two buckets, on

is +0.47. Nothing ships; the knob and all five arms are deleted.** Step 0 (its
own section above) predicted the direction and most of the size before the code

Pristine = `hot-expert-tier` @ **`3713416`** (the edge0-eval merge; Q3, Q1, Q2,

`0da58e9a8b2b0fb0`; candidate sha256 `0fa156e03d557346`, built from
`perf/q11-gr-apply-writeback` @ `5a3bf65`. Same regime as §Q2/§Q1/§Q3: 3 GPUs,
tier **14673 of 21858** in every run, cap 512, 80 greedy tokens,
`datapoint.py`'s rotating prompt 1, 8 threads pinned, a fresh copy of the

### The five arms, `[OPTIME]` decode only, medians of three repeats each

`gr-apply` is a top-level bucket; `gr-rms` is nested inside `gr-read`. The
column that decides the item is their **sum**, because the two loops trade time
with each other — §Q2's own lesson, and the reason Q11's row requires them to be
judged in one binary.

| arm | gr-apply | gr-rms | **apply+rms** | gr-read | step (the token) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **pristine** (both serial) | **0.18** | **1.06** | **1.24** | 21.85 | 175.20 |
| 1: write-back parallel, own region | 0.90 | 1.06 | 1.96 (**+0.72**) | 21.89 | 175.53 |
| 2: rms parallel, own region (§Q2's rejected arm) | 0.54 | 0.82 | 1.36 (**+0.12**) | 21.64 | 174.67 |
| 3: both parallel, two regions — **the shape Q11's row describes** | 0.90 | 0.81 | 1.71 (**+0.47**) | 21.56 | 175.48 |
| 4: **FUSED** one region, both `omp for`s split over b | 0.56 | 0.58 | **1.14 (−0.10)** | 21.38 | 175.10 |
| 5: FUSED one region, write-back over (b,d) | 0.88 | 0.57 | 1.45 (**+0.21**) | 21.31 | 174.89 |

Per-run spread: `gr-rms` pristine 1.06/1.07/1.06 → arm 4 0.58/0.58/0.56;
`gr-apply` pristine 0.182/0.149/0.183 → arm 4 0.561/0.583/0.529; `gr-read`
21.83/21.85/21.99 → 21.50/21.38/21.18. **`step` 175.10/175.20/175.71 against arm
4's 174.43/175.10/175.46 — the token cannot resolve this item at all**, and the
arm with the *lowest* median token (arm 2, 174.67) has a *worse* bucket pair than
the pristine. Every bucket the item does not touch is flat at arm 4:
`attention` +0.12, `deltanet` +0.18, `moe` −0.36, `lm-head` −0.02,
`dense-matmul` +0.25, `gr-down` −0.05, `gr-up` +0.01, `gr-mix` +0.01,
`gr-inject` −0.02.

The candidate binary with the knob **unset** reproduces the pristine's buckets —
`gr-read` 21.854, `gr-apply` 0.205, `gr-rms` 1.065 — so the arms above are the
only difference between the columns.

### Why: ρ, measured directly, is the whole item

`tools/hot-expert/rome_grapplybench.c` times the region cost at the write-back's
own cadence (96 regions per token, 8 threads pinned, nothing else running):

| what | ms/token at 96 sites | per region |
|---|---:|---:|
| empty `#pragma omp parallel` | 0.433 | **4.51 µs** |
| `#pragma omp parallel for` over C=4 | 0.494 | **5.14 µs** |
| one region holding TWO `omp for`s | 0.894 | **9.31 µs** |

A second `omp for` inside an existing region therefore costs **4.17 µs** —
nearly as much as a whole new region. **Fusion saves only 0.094 ms/token**, and
the harness said so before the engine ran; the engine then measured −0.10. The
two loops are **1.24 ms/token of work over 96–97 sites = 12.8 µs/site**, against
**≥ 9.3 µs/site of unavoidable synchronisation** for the cheapest two-loop
shape. Their parallel floors are 0.05 (the write-back, eight ways) and 0.27 (the
rms, four ways at C=4): 0.32 + 0.89 = **1.21 against 1.24 today**. **That is the
ceiling of this mechanism and it is zero.** `gr-apply ≤ 0.10` is not merely
unmet, it is unreachable: one fork/join per site is 0.43 ms/token, four times
the threshold, before any work is done.

### What is true, and is new: the cost is a DECOMPOSITION MISMATCH, not "the serial writer"

§Q2 recorded that parallelising the rms makes the serial `q38_gr_apply` rise
0.18 → 0.53, and explained it as four threads pulling `hyper` into four private
L2s while one thread writes it back. **Arm 2 reproduces that number exactly
(0.54) six days and five merges later** — but arms 1 and 5 show the effect runs
in *both* directions and is not about serial-versus-parallel at all:

| who writes `hyper` | who reads it next (the rms) | gr-apply |
|---|---|---:|
| serial (1 thread) | serial (1 thread) — aligned trivially | **0.18** |
| serial | parallel over b (4 ways) — **mismatched** | 0.54 |
| parallel over (b,d) (8 ways) | serial — **mismatched** | 0.90 |
| parallel over (b,d) (8 ways) | parallel over b (4 ways), same region — **mismatched** | 0.88 |
| parallel over b (4 ways) | parallel over b (4 ways), same region — **ALIGNED** | 0.56 |

The aligned fused arm is the only parallel arm whose write-back is not inflated
by 0.35–0.7 ms/token, and what is left of its 0.56 is 0.43 of region entry plus
~0.1 of work. **The rule for this track is therefore sharper than §Q2's:** it is
not "parallelising a reader slows a serial writer", it is **"whenever the thread
that writes a buffer is not the thread that reads it next, the pair pays
0.3–0.7 ms/token at this cadence, in either direction"**. Aligning the two
decompositions removes it (0.90 → 0.56 at the same thread count, the same
region and the same arithmetic), which is the direct confirmation §Q2's
mechanism never had.

### Oracle — bit-identical, and the "by construction" claim held

| pair | last-token logits (`DUMP`, 993 280 bytes = all 248 320 floats) | greedy text |
|---|---|---|
| 32 tokens, arms 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (five pairs) | **byte-identical**, all five | identical |
| 32 tokens, candidate default path with `COLI_TIMERS=1` | **byte-identical** | identical |
| 128 tokens, arms 4 and 5 | **byte-identical** | identical |

Expert cache identical in every pair (30.8 %, hit=6940 miss=15627). Plus the
offline oracle in `rome_grapplybench.c`: 4 tokens × 97 sites, `memcmp` on
**`hyper` itself** as well as on `norm`, `mixed` and `inject`, all five arms
bit-identical. Q11's row said this was true by construction and, per Q10's "the
oracle decides, not the argument", it was checked anyway — the construction
argument survived: every `hyper` element is written by exactly one (s,b,d) with
no accumulation across iterations, and each `q38_rms0` keeps its own serial
`double` sum. All four `qwen38` C tests exit 0; both engines build clean;
`c/shaders` byte-identical on both sides (`d9c6294572481c66`), and **nothing
shared with `glm53` was touched**, so GLM-5.3 was not rebuilt and does not need
re-measuring — same scope as §Q3, §Q1 and §Q2.

### The gate

| gate leg (as written in the roadmap) | required | measured | verdict |
|---|---|---:|---|
| **bit-identical** greedy text + last-token logits | yes | byte-identical, 8 pairs, all five arms, plus the harness memcmp | **met** |
| `[OPTIME] gr-apply` | **≤ 0.10** | **0.56** best of five arms (the pristine itself is 0.18) | **NOT MET — and unreachable by any pragma: one fork/join per site is 0.43** |
| `[OPTIME] gr-rms` | **≤ 0.85** | **0.58** (arm 4) | met — but only in arms that fail the leg above |
| both legs **in the same binary** | yes | no binary meets both | **NOT MET** |
| report `gr-apply` and `gr-read` together with the token | yes | the table above, three repeats each, with the spread | **met** |
| serving A/B with its own pristine rows | yes | **not run, deliberately** — see below | n/a |
| the roadmap's expected delta | **−0.4 to −0.5 ms/token** | **−0.10 on the buckets**, token unresolvable | **NOT MET** |

**No serving A/B was run, and that is a decision rather than an omission.**
There is no candidate: the engine file is back to the pristine except for a
comment. The effect at its very best is 0.10 ms/token on a 175 ms token —
0.06 % — against a rotating row that §Q1 and §Q2 both measured drifting ±3 % on
unchanged code. A `rome_bench.sh` pair could not resolve it, and running one to
produce a number that cannot mean anything is the failure mode `MEASURING.md`
exists to prevent. The in-engine per-op table is this item's arbiter and it
refutes the item.

### What this changes for the roadmap

- **Q11 is closed as REJECTED.** The write-back and the rms both stay serial.
  The comment in `q38_gr_read` that pointed here (§Q2's "it becomes worth doing
  once `q38_gr_apply` is parallel too") is replaced by this result, so the next
  session cannot be sent back down it.
- **A new bound for Track Q, and it is general:** on this box a loop is worth
  parallelising only if it carries **more than ~10 µs of work per call site**.
  `gr-apply` (1.9 µs/site) and `gr-rms` (11 µs/site) are at or under that line;
  `gr-mix` (68 µs/site, §Q2's 4.6× win) and DeltaNet's loops (§Q1) are far above
  it. Any future row proposing a pragma should be sized against 9.3 µs/site of
  synchronisation **before** it is scheduled — the arithmetic is three lines and
  it would have priced Q11 at zero without a day of rig time.
- **The 0.33 §Q2 "left on the table" was never on the table.** §Q2's rms arm
  wins 0.24–0.33 in `gr-read` and gives it back in `gr-apply` in every
  configuration measured here; the pair is ≥ 1.36 against 1.24 whatever is done
  to the write-back. That sentence in §Q2's "what this changes for the roadmap"
  and the corresponding claim in Q11's row are **withdrawn**.
- **Not tried, and out of Q11's scope:** making the *serial* write-back cheaper
  (non-temporal stores over the 40 KB, or folding it into the op that produces
  `block`) is the only remaining way at this bucket, and it is worth 0.18
  ms/token at most. Nobody should spend a day on it.

## Q11 step 0 (2026-09-12): the write-back's arithmetic — the roadmap's shape cannot win, and the record already contained the reason

Q11 asks for one pragma on `q38_gr_apply` and the revival of §Q2's rejected rms
pragma, for **−0.4 to −0.5 ms/token**. Before building either, the same step-0
discipline §Q2 and §Q1 used: re-derive the expected delta from numbers already
in this record, and state which shapes can and cannot reach the gate.

**The two loops, as they are today (§Q2's table):** `gr-apply` **0.15–0.18**
ms/token over 96 sites (1.6–1.9 µs/site: 40 KB of `hyper` read-modify-written
plus 10 KB of `block` read, i.e. ~26 GB/s — single-thread DRAM, so `hyper` is
**not** in anybody's cache when the write-back runs), and `gr-rms` **1.07**
ms/token over 97 sites (11 µs/site = 4 columns × 2.9 µs, a dependent `double`
add chain over H=2560, latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound).

**The parallel floors.** `gr-apply` over (b,d) is eight-way: ≥ 0.02, and
realistically ~0.05 because 50 KB across 8 threads does not reach 8× of a
single thread's DRAM rate. `gr-rms` is four-way at decode (C=4, S=1): ≥ 0.27.
Together **≥ 0.29 against 1.25 today**, so the mechanism's ceiling is −0.96.

**ρ, the cost of one `omp parallel` region, is the whole item.** §Q1 measured
**5.3 µs per region in-engine** (`dn-rest` 0.11 → 0.30 over 36 regions), and
§Q2's own rejected arm re-measured it on this very loop: `gr-rms` 1.07 → 0.82
is 1.07/4 = 0.27 plus 0.55 over 97 sites = **5.7 µs/region**. Take ρ = 5.3 µs.
A new region at 96 sites costs **0.51 ms/token**. Then:

| shape | gr-apply | gr-rms | new regions | total vs 1.25 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| today (both serial) | 0.18 | 1.07 | 0 | — |
| **the roadmap's shape**: a pragma on each loop | 0.05 + ρ·96 | 0.27 + ρ·97 | **2** | 1.85 → **+0.60** |
| a pragma on `gr_apply` only | 0.05 + ρ·96 | 1.07 | 1 | 1.63 → **+0.38** |
| §Q2's rejected arm (rms only) | 0.18 | 0.27 + ρ·97 | 1 | 1.33 → **+0.08** |
| **both loops inside ONE region** | 0.05 | 0.27 | **1** | 0.83 → **−0.42** |

**So the roadmap's own expected delta is only reachable in a shape the roadmap
does not describe.** "Less one fork/join per site" is in the Q11 row, but at the
ρ this record has measured twice, one fork/join per site is 0.51 ms/token —
larger than the 0.48 the two loops can give back. Two of them is 1.02. The
naive Q11 (one `collapse(2)` on the write-back, plus §Q2's pragma revived) is
predicted here, before it is built, to be **+0.60 ms/token — a regression** —
and to miss the `gr-apply ≤ 0.10` leg outright, because `gr-apply`'s own bucket
would *include* the fork/join it pays.

**The one shape that can win** fuses the write-back into the RMS's region.
It is available because of an adjacency this record has not noted before:
**every one of the 96 `q38_gr_apply` calls is immediately followed by a
`q38_gr_read`** (`attn_gr` read → attention → apply → `mlp_gr` read → moe →
apply → the next layer's `attn_gr` read; only layer 0's first read has no apply
before it). Apply writes all of `hyper`; the rms then reads all of `hyper`. One
`omp parallel` with two `omp for`s spends ρ once instead of twice, and if both
`omp for`s are split **over `b` with the same static schedule**, thread `b`
reads back the 10 KB it has just written — in its own L1 — so the rms's 40 KB
DRAM read disappears as well. That is also the direct test of §Q2's stated
mechanism: if the 0.18 → 0.53 transfer really is cross-CCX invalidation of
lines four threads pulled in, aligning the two decompositions removes it by
construction.

**Predicted, before the measurement: −0.35 to −0.45 ms/token for the fused
shape and +0.3 to +0.6 for the roadmap's shape.** Both are measured below; if
the fused shape does not deliver, Q11 is rejected on ρ and the two serial loops
stay. What is NOT predicted here is whether ρ is really 5.3 µs when the region
is entered 96 times from a cold-ish thread pool — the microbenchmark measures ρ
directly (an empty region at the same cadence) so that the verdict does not
rest on a constant taken from another item's bucket.

## Q10 step 0 (2026-09-12): the DeltaNet recurrence measured — the cost is the loop ORDER, not the traffic; the item's two numerics claims are both wrong, and the gate re-derived from the measurement BEFORE the candidate was built

The step-0 rule from §Q1's arbitration, applied to the row that arbitration
created. Nothing in the engine is changed by this section: it is the isolated
measurement, the numerics verification, and the threshold this item's
candidate is then judged against. The candidate is §Q10 below.

The roadmap's Q10 row proposes two foldings of the 48-head recurrence
(`dn-recur`, **9.19 ms/token** per §Q1 step 0, 4.8% of the token) and offers
two competing readings of why the loop costs what it does: a **bandwidth**
reading (six traversals of a 64 KB state per head, "680 MB/token at 74 GB/s")
and a **latency** reading, added at §Q1's arbitration (the state fits the
512 KB L2, so the real cost is the two `d`-inner strided reductions). The row
says step 0 decides which, and that the gate is then derived from the result
rather than from the row's "−2.5 ms/token".

### The harness

`tools/hot-expert/rome_dnbench.c`, **extended, not replaced** — `rome_dnbench
q1` still prints §Q1's rows unchanged. Part 2 adds the recurrence copied
character for character out of `q38_deltanet`'s `omp for` over `h<VH`,
parallel over heads the same way, at the engine's real shapes (VH 48,
KD/VD 128, 36 layers), built with the engine's own flags (`-O3 -march=native
-fopenmp -pthread`, no `-std=`, so `-ffp-contract=fast` is in force in both
and the contraction the oracle sees is the engine's). 8 threads pinned, rig
lock held, gateway down, restarted on every exit path. Two full repeats
(`~/bench/q10_step0.log`, `~/bench/q10_step0b.log`).

**The oracle is stricter than this track's usual one, on purpose:** the
recurrent state persists across tokens, so a wrong reassociation can leave one
token's `core` output intact and drift the state. Every variant runs from an
identical cloned state for **36 layers × 64 consecutive tokens** and is
`memcmp`ed at **every** token against the base on the `core` output *and* on
all 36 layers' full 3.146 MB state — **1 811 939 328 state elements** per
variant.

### Both of the item's numerics claims are false, and the assembly says why

The row asserts that (a) is bit-identical because "the addend of an FMA is
never contracted", and that the two reductions are "unvectorised across
`value`". Neither holds at the engine's flags. gcc 15.2 compiles the **base's**
two reductions by **outer-loop vectorisation** — 8 `value`s at a time with `d`
inner and a 512 B stride — and emits them as **vmulps + vaddps, not
contracted**:

```
.L4:    vbroadcastss (%rdx),%ymm0
        vmulps  -512(%rax),%ymm0,%ymm0
        vaddps  %ymm0,%ymm2,%ymm2
```

while it **does** contract the rank-1 update (`vfmadd213ps` at `.L10`). So
bit-identity needs the opposite of what the item assumes, in both places.
Measured, against the base over 36 × 64:

| variant | oracle | differing state elements (of 1 811 939 328) | max abs |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| (a), spelled `s*alpha + kh[d]*delta[v]` | **DIFFER** | 480 790 578 | 4.77e−07 |
| (a), spelled `fmaf(kh[d],delta[v],s*alpha)` | **BIT-IDENTICAL** | 0 | 0 |
| (a)+(b), plain `+` | **DIFFER** | 598 374 163 | 5.96e−07 |
| (a)+(b), `fmaf` only | **DIFFER** | 208 336 749 | 5.96e−07 |
| diagnostic: (b) on `previous` only | **DIFFER** | 208 336 749 | 5.96e−07 |
| diagnostic: (b) on `current` only | **DIFFER** | **0 state**, 134 009 core | 4.77e−07 |
| **(a)+(b), `fmaf` + `-ffp-contract=off`** | **BIT-IDENTICAL** | 0 | 0 |
| **(b) only, decay pass kept (control)** | **BIT-IDENTICAL** | 0 | 0 |

The two diagnostics localise it statement by statement: (b) on `current` alone
changes **no state element at all** and only the output — `current` is the one
reduction that does not write back — while (b) on `previous` alone changes
208 336 749 state elements, because `previous` feeds `delta` feeds the state.
Both are the same cause: a `d`-outer/`value`-inner `acc[v] += x*y` is a
textbook vectorisable statement and gcc contracts it, where the base's
strided outer-loop-vectorised form is not contracted.

**The shipped spelling therefore states the contraction explicitly in both
directions**: `fmaf()` where the base fuses, and `#pragma GCC optimize
("fp-contract=off")` around the function where it does not. Probed on the rig
before it was used: under that pragma the reductions stay vmulps+vaddps **and**
`fmaf` still emits a vectorised `vfmadd`.

### Bandwidth or latency: the measurement, in three cache regimes

ms/token over 36 layers, two passes per regime per campaign, two campaigns.
`l2` is one layer's state re-used (3.146 MB; 8 threads × 6 heads × 64 KB =
384 KB per core, inside this part's 512 KB L2); `l3` is the engine's own 36
layers (113 MB, inside the 128 MB L3); `dram` is 288 layers (885 MB, past L3).

| variant | traffic | l2 | l3 | dram |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| base (4 passes) | 6 units | 4.99 / 4.97 / 4.99 / 4.97 | 5.46 / 5.49 / 5.93 / 5.45 | 7.20 / 7.22 / 6.45 / 6.46 |
| (a) alone, `fmaf` | 4 units | 4.87 / 4.87 / 4.86 / 4.91 | 6.33 / 5.59 / 5.89 / 5.87 | 6.43 / 6.64 / 7.09 / 6.61 |
| **(a)+(b), contract-off** | **3 units** | **0.705 / 0.701 / 0.705 / 0.704** | **1.50 / 1.10 / 1.09 / 1.59** | **2.60 / 2.62 / 2.44 / 2.70** |
| (b) only, decay kept (control) | 5 units | 0.784 / 0.784 | 1.11 / 1.48 | 2.51 / 2.53 |

| variant | l2 mean | l3 mean | dram mean | Δ vs base |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| base | 4.98 | 5.58 | 6.83 | — |
| (a) alone | 4.88 | 5.92 | 6.69 | **−0.09 / +0.34 / −0.14** |
| **(a)+(b)** | **0.704** | **1.32** | **2.59** | **−4.28 / −4.26 / −4.24** |
| (b) only, control | 0.784 | 1.29 | 2.52 | −4.20 / −4.29 / −4.31 |

**The answer is LATENCY, and the evidence is stronger than "the regimes are
close" — it is that the two mechanisms separate cleanly:**

- **(a) removes a full third of the traffic (6 → 4 units) and is worth
  nothing**, in any regime: −0.09 L2, +0.34 L3, −0.14 DRAM, all inside this
  harness's own repeat spread. That is the bandwidth reading, tested directly,
  and it fails. **The roadmap's −2.5 ms/token was the size of this effect, and
  this effect is zero.**
- **(b) is worth −4.2 to −4.3 in EVERY regime**, and the number is the same
  whether the state sits in L2, in L3, or in DRAM. A bandwidth saving scales
  with where the data is; a latency saving does not.
- The **control settles it**: (b)'s loop order with the decay pass *kept* —
  5 traffic units, not 3 — measures the same as (a)+(b) to within 0.08. The
  saving is entirely the loop order and not at all the traffic.

**But the roadmap's stated latency mechanism is also wrong, and the record
should not carry it forward.** The row says the reductions are "unvectorised
across `value`"; the assembly above shows gcc had **already** outer-loop
vectorised both of them. What (b) actually fixes is ILP and access order: the
base runs **one** ymm accumulator down a 128-long dependent `vaddps` chain
with a 512 B stride between loads; `d`-outer/`value`-inner runs **16
independent** accumulators over unit-stride loads, which saturates this part's
two FMA pipes instead of idling on a 3-cycle dependency.

### `perf stat`

Deferred to the candidate section below: the rig lock was taken by the Q11
chain between the two step-0 campaigns, and the cycles-vs-bytes counters are
reported there against the same two kernels. The three-regime table above
already answers the question the counters were asked to answer, by a more
direct route: a bandwidth bound cannot produce an identical saving in L2 and
in DRAM.

### The gate, re-derived from the measurement — written here BEFORE the candidate exists

The roadmap's `−2.5 ms/token` is the size of folding (a), which step 0 measured
at zero, so it is not the number to build against. Step 0's own two readings of
what the engine will show:

- **additive** (the engine's 9.19 is the isolated 6.83 plus a fixed overhead —
  the dense stream's eviction, the shared region's barriers): 9.19 − 4.25 =
  **4.94**, i.e. −4.25.
- **multiplicative** (the overhead scales with the kernel): 9.19 × (2.59/6.83)
  = **3.48**, i.e. −5.71.

**The floor is set at the more conservative of the two**, per §Q1's
arbitration's own rule that the floor must sit *below* what the mechanism's
evidence predicts, so the item cannot pass on the floor and fail on its own
evidence. Note this is **not** the track's usual "at least half": half of 9.19
is 4.60, which is *stricter* than the conservative prediction of 4.94, and
adopting it would be the §Q1/§Q2/§Q3 mistake a fourth time — a threshold set
above the mechanism's own evidence before a line was written.

## Q10 (2026-09-12): the DeltaNet recurrence's loop order — bit-identical, `dn-recur` **9.169 → 1.974 (−7.195, 4.6×)** and the token **−8.50**; every gate leg met, and the in-engine result BEAT step 0's own conservative prediction by 69%

The candidate for the gate written in §Q10 step 0 above. One region in
`c/qwen38_core.h`; no shader, no other engine, no new allocation.

### What shipped

`q38_deltanet`'s per-head recurrence becomes two `noinline` functions and a
one-time self-check:

- `q38_dn_recur_base` — the loop exactly as Q1 left it, moved out of the
  `omp for` unchanged. It is the fallback and it is what
  **`Q38_DN_RECUR_FOLD=0`** selects.
- `q38_dn_recur_fold` — (a) the decay pass dropped and `fl(s*alpha)` recomputed
  on the fly, (b) `d` outer and `value` inner in both reductions. 6 traffic
  units → 3, and both reductions become unit-stride with 16 independent vector
  accumulators instead of one down a 128-long dependent chain.
- `q38_dn_fold_ok` — runs both forms once per process on a fixed 64 KB state at
  four (alpha, beta) pairs and `memcmp`s the whole state and the output; on any
  difference the engine uses the base loop and says so under `Q38_VERBOSE`.

**Why `noinline`, and it is a correctness argument rather than a style one:**
the self-check is only sound if it exercises the same machine code the engine
runs, and an inlined copy inside the `omp for` could be vectorised differently
from the out-of-line one the check calls. One body, both call sites. Measured
cost of the 1 728 calls/token it adds: **`dn-recur` 9.169 → 9.161 and the step
171.914 → 171.616 with the knob off** — nothing, and that is the knob-OFF
column below rather than an assertion.

`#pragma GCC optimize ("fp-contract=off")` and the folded path are behind
`#if defined(__GNUC__) && !defined(__clang__)`; any other compiler builds the
base path only and the call site compiles the `if` out.

### `perf stat`, the leg step 0 deferred — and it says the same thing from the counters

One kernel per run (`Q10_ONLY`/`Q10_REG`/`Q10_NOORACLE`), 8 threads, gateway
down.

| | cycles | instructions | IPC | cache-references | cache-misses |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| base, L2 regime | 3.830e9 | 6.253e9 | 1.63 | 1.300e9 | 3.09e6 |
| **fold, L2 regime** | **0.881e9** | **1.274e9** | 1.45 | **0.118e9** | 2.64e6 |
| base, DRAM regime | 27.377e9 | 32.815e9 | 1.20 | 4.482e9 | 29.5e6 |
| **fold, DRAM regime** | **12.298e9** | **7.938e9** | **0.65** | **0.748e9** | **108.5e6** |

The base **retires 4.1–4.9× more instructions** and issues **6–11× more cache
references** for the same arithmetic. Past L3 the base runs at **IPC 1.20** —
it is not stalled on memory, it is executing a very large number of
instructions — while the fold runs at **IPC 0.65 with 3.7× MORE cache misses
and is still 2.2× faster**. The candidate is the memory-bound one; the thing it
replaced was not. That is the bandwidth-vs-latency question answered a second
way, from counters rather than from cache regimes, and the two agree.

### Attenuation runs in OPPOSITE directions for the two forms of the same loop — and that is why step 0 under-predicted by 69%

Step 0's two predictions were `dn-recur` at 4.94 (additive) and 3.48
(multiplicative). It measured **1.974**. The item is not under-delivering
against its evidence; it is over-delivering, and the reason is worth carrying
forward because §Q1 and §Q2 already disagreed about it.

| | isolated (step 0) | in engine | engine / isolated |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| base, vs the DRAM regime | 6.83 | 9.169 | **1.34× (engine WORSE)** |
| fold, vs the DRAM regime | 2.59 | 1.974 | **0.76× (engine BETTER)** |
| fold, vs the L3 regime | 1.32 | 1.974 | 1.50× |
| the saving | −4.25 | **−7.195** | **1.69×** |

§Q1 found in-engine attenuation **inverse** on its serial scalar loops and
guessed it was about running beside seven spinning libgomp threads; §Q2 found
the opposite on its loops and concluded "inverse attenuation is a property of
Q1's loops and not a rule". Q10 says what the property actually is, because it
has **both directions inside one item, on one loop, at one call site**: the
attenuation tracks **how well the access pattern survives a cold cache and a
cold TLB**, not whether the loop is serial or parallel and not how many threads
are spinning. The base's 512 B-strided, single-accumulator walk is hurt *more*
in the engine, where 6.81 GB/token of dense weights have evicted the state and
the hardware prefetcher cannot follow it; the fold's unit-stride walk is hurt
*less* than in a synthetic pool, because it prefetches. **An isolated harness
therefore understates a loop-order fix and can overstate a traffic fix** — the
opposite of the direction a session would assume.

Practical rule for the rest of this track, and the thing to take from Q10 more
than the milliseconds: **for a latency-bound loop, size the win from the
in-engine bucket and the isolated RATIO, not the isolated absolute delta.**
Here the isolated ratio in the DRAM regime (2.64×) would still have
under-predicted (3.48 vs 1.974), and the L2 ratio (7.07×) would have
over-predicted (1.30). The honest statement is that the isolated harness
bracketed the answer (0.70–2.59 isolated against 1.974 in engine) and no single
isolated row predicted it. **The gate was set from the conservative end, which
is why it was met rather than argued about.**

- **`glm53` was not re-measured, and it is PROVED untouched rather than argued
  untouched.** `qwen38_core.h` is included by `qwen38.c` and the qwen38 tests
  only (`grep` in the Makefile and the sources); no shader, no `quant.h`, no
  `st.h`, no `backend_vulkan.c` changed. It was then built anyway from the
  merged tree and the binary is **byte-identical** to one built from `3713416`:
  both `a8e10ecf09edc05c`. A sha256 is a better answer than a dependency
  argument, and it costs one build.
- **The merge with `hot-expert-tier` (Q11 landed mid-campaign) owes no
  re-measurement, and that is also a sha256 rather than a claim.** Q11 rejected
  its change and shipped only a comment in `q38_gr_read`; `qwen38-vk` built from
  the merged tree is **byte-identical** to the binary every number above was
  taken on, `5a9a24953b33f509`.
- **`accept_live.sh` / `accept_ui.sh` were not run.** They gate the *served*
  binary, and the served binary is `glm53`, which this item does not touch.
  The gateway was stopped and restarted by each measurement chain and came back

- **`tests/test_qwen38_native_weights` FAILS, and it fails identically on the

### Rejected and deleted, with the measurement that rejected it

**Folding (a) on its own — the folding the roadmap sized this entire item on.**
Removing a full third of the state traffic (6 → 4 units) measures
**−0.09 / +0.34 / −0.14 ms/token** in the L2 / L3 / DRAM regimes: zero in all
three, and in the engine's own regime the sign is against it. It survives in
the shipped kernel only because the (b) loop order needs the on-the-fly
`fl(s*alpha)` anyway; a control with (b)'s order and the decay pass **kept**
(5 traffic units) measures within 0.08 of the shipped form, so **nothing in
this item's result is attributable to traffic.** It is not left in the tree as
a knob.

**The two obvious spellings of both foldings**, deleted with the element counts
that rejected them (§Q10 step 0's table): plain `s*alpha + kh[d]*delta[v]`
(480 790 578 of 1 811 939 328 state elements differ) and a d-outer
`acc[v] += x*y` without `-ffp-contract=off` (208 336 749).

### Reproducing it
