## Q13 step 0 (2026-09-12): which card is dev0, and what it idles at — the device map settled three ways, the measurement itself BLOCKED on the owner's sudo

Q13's gate: *"**bit-identical** (a DPM level or an empty dispatch changes no
arithmetic); `[OPTIME] dn-proj`, `vk-dense`, `vk-take` and the token, three
fresh-process repeats; idle power draw reported beside it; serving A/B with its
own pristine rows"*. Expected from §Q7's duty-cycle table: if the 1.37×
in-engine attenuation is dev0 de-clocking in the sub-millisecond gaps, forcing
`power_dpm_force_performance_level=high` moves `dn-proj` from 26.98 toward the
18.6–19.6 back-to-back figure (**−5 to −10 ms/token**); if it does not move,
the attenuation is not clocks and §Q7 steps 2–3's replayed predictions stand.
**Nothing was measured under a forced level — that write needs root and is the
owner's.** What this session establishes is the thing the measurement cannot be
taken without, and which nothing in the record had: **which of the three
identical cards `dev0` actually is.**

### dev0 is `0000:83:00.0` = `/sys/class/drm/card1`, and the card numbers are scrambled

The engine prints only `Radeon RX 7900 XTX (RADV NAVI31)` for all three
(`[VK] ready:`, `[VK] dev2 ready:`, `[VK] dev3 ready:`) and all three report PCI
device id `1002:744c`, so neither the log nor `lspci` alone disambiguates. The
DRM card numbers do not follow the bus order and the render nodes follow neither:

| PCI | `/sys/class/drm` | render node | Vulkan enum index | **engine role** |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| `0000:83:00.0` | **card1** | renderD128 | **0** | **dev0** (dense, KDA, 1248 experts) |
| `0000:48:00.0` | card2 | renderD130 | 1 | dev2 (`auto`, 1695 experts) |
| `0000:86:00.0` | card0 | renderD129 | 2 | dev3 (`auto`, 1695 experts) |

Three independent lines, each of which alone would be a guess:

1. **The engine's selection rule replayed against `VK_EXT_pci_bus_info`.**
   `coli_vk_init()` ranks discrete 4 / integrated 3 / virtual 2 / other 1 / CPU 0
   and keeps the best with a strict `>`, so three tied discrete GPUs leave
   enumeration index 0 selected; `coli_vk_init_dev2(-1)` and `_dev3(-1)` then take
   the next indices, skipping `G.phys` and `G2.phys`. A probe that creates an
   instance, enumerates, and applies exactly those three loops (no logical device,
   no allocation) prints `dev0 = enum[0] pci=0000:83:00.0`, `dev2 = enum[1]
   0000:48:00.0`, `dev3 = enum[2] 0000:86:00.0`. `vulkaninfo`'s own GPU0/1/2
   sections agree (`pciBus` 131 / 72 / 134 = 0x83 / 0x48 / 0x86), and no
   `MESA_VK_DEVICE_SELECT`, `DRI_PRIME` or `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` is set in
   `~/start_glm53.sh`, `~/bench/*.sh` or the running engine's `environ`, so the
   loader order is the same in both processes.
2. **The live gateway's VRAM ledger**, per `drm-pdev` in `/proc/<glm53>/fdinfo/*`
   and `mem_info_vram_used`: `83:00.0` holds **22.85 GB** while `48:00.0` and
   `86:00.0` hold **24.19 GB each, to the byte**. The two equal ones are the two
   expert-only tiers at `COLI_VK_EXPERTS2=EXPERTS3=1695`; the odd one is dev0,
   and its content checks out — 3.78 GB dense (`551 matrici`) + 624 MB KDA pool +
   1248 heat-ranked experts at the ~14.3 MB/expert the tier rows imply.
3. **`coli_vk_matmul_multi()` — the only dense dispatch path, and the one
   `Q38_DENSE_GPU` uses — touches `G` (dev0) exclusively**, so Q7's `dn-proj`
   submits and the 26.98 they cost are on `0000:83:00.0` and nowhere else.

An apparent fourth line **disagrees and is a trap**: the engine's six `/dev/dri`
fds open in the order `48:00.0`, `86:00.0`, `83:00.0` (fds 132–137, DRM
client-ids 719243/44/45, two dup'd fds per device). That is RADV's internal DRM
scan order, **not** the Vulkan enumeration order — the probe above reproduces the
identical fd pattern in its own process while enumerating `83, 48, 86`. Read the
fd order as the device order and you force the wrong card.

### What dev0 idles at today, `auto`, model resident, gateway up but idle

Read without sudo from `/sys/bus/pci/devices/<pci>/hwmon/hwmon*/` (`power1_average`,
`freq1_input` = sclk, `freq2_input` = mclk) and `gpu_busy_percent`:

| | dev0 `83:00.0` | dev2 `48:00.0` | dev3 `86:00.0` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `power_dpm_force_performance_level` | auto | auto | auto |
| idle power (`power1_average`) | **6–7 W** | 10 W | 13 W |
| idle sclk | **0 MHz** | 0 MHz | 0 MHz |
| idle mclk | **96 MHz** | 96 MHz | 96 MHz |
| `gpu_busy_percent` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| sclk DPM levels | 500 / **2371** MHz | 500 / 2371 | 500 / **2431** |
| mclk DPM levels | 96 / 456 / 772 / **1249** MHz | same | same |
| power cap | 303 W | 303 W | 315 W |
| temp | 35 °C | 39 °C | 34 °C |

**This is the mechanism Q13 suspects, quantified for the first time:** at `auto`
and idle dev0's gfx clock reads **0** and its memory clock sits at **96 of
1249 MHz — 7.7 %**. A GEMV dispatch is memory-bound (§Q7 step 0 measured the head
at 465 GB/s back-to-back), so the mclk ramp, not sclk, is the likely carrier of
the 1.37×; that also fits the non-monotonicity at 3.0 ms, which a ramp with
hysteresis produces and a throughput limit does not. It is a hypothesis with a
measured idle state behind it, not a finding: only the forced-level A/B decides.
Note the third card is a slightly different bin (2431 MHz, 315 W) — dev0 and dev2
are not, so nothing here is comparing across bins.

### The lever, and what it costs the owner

**`0000:83:00.0` is also the display card** — `card1-HDMI-A-2` is the one
`connected` connector on the box and `/sys/class/graphics/fb0` hangs off
`…/0000:83:00.0` (the kernel console framebuffer; no X or Wayland runs). dev0 is
therefore the card that carries both the dense dispatches and the console, which
is a reason to hand the level back to `auto` promptly rather than leave it, and a
thing to say out loud before anyone concludes "it is only a compute card". The
other two cards' levels are untouched by the step. The set/revert pair is

```
echo high | sudo tee /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:83:00.0/power_dpm_force_performance_level
echo auto | sudo tee /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:83:00.0/power_dpm_force_performance_level
```

and the level survives nothing — it resets to `auto` on module reload or reboot,
so a forgotten `high` is bounded by the next boot but **not** by anything shorter.
`high` pins both sclk and mclk at their top DPM level continuously: the idle draw
above (6–7 W) is what it replaces, and on a box that serves 24/7 the idle-watt
cost is the owner's call, not this item's. **A narrower variant exists and is
worth running if `high` moves the number**: `manual` unlocks `pp_dpm_sclk` /
`pp_dpm_mclk` masks, so `echo manual | sudo tee …force_performance_level` then
`echo 3 | sudo tee …/pp_dpm_mclk` forces the memory clock alone (1249 MHz) and
leaves sclk free — it isolates the mclk hypothesis and costs a fraction of the
idle watts. `profile_peak` is the fallback if `high` is rejected with EINVAL.

### The harness, ready to fire

`tools/hot-expert/q13_probe.sh` (runnable copy `~/bench/q13_probe.sh`, byte-identical)
takes the rig lock, stops the gateway only if it is the thing that stopped it
(`q7_lib.sh`), refuses on a dirty tree — Q13 is zero-code and measures the
shipped binary, so nothing is rebuilt — evicts GLM, warms Qwen and asserts
131/131 shards 100 % resident, and then for **each** level runs a 30 s no-engine
idle sample plus **three fresh-process repeats at `Q38_DENSE_GPU=1` and three at
`Q38_DENSE_GPU=7`** (mask 1 is the roadmap's "step-1 triple", mask 7 is the arm
that actually ships, where `vk-dense` is 39 ms/token and Q14's `gr-read`
inflation sits). It **never writes the DPM file**: it prints the `sudo` line and
polls the sysfs value until it reads `high`, then again until it reads `auto`,
with a timeout that refuses rather than measures. Clocks and power are sampled at
2 Hz through the runs by a single Python process — a shell sampler at 4 Hz forks
~120 processes a second and would steal from the eight pinned engine threads.
The oracle is free: every timed run already dumps `Q38_TF_DUMP` and `DUMP`, so
`auto` vs `high` is compared by sha256 at both masks, three repeats each — a DPM
level must be **bit-identical** or the finding is a hardware fault, not a win.
Cost ~12 min of engine time per level plus the warm; the gateway is down for the
duration. The serving A/B the gate also asks for is stage 2 and only if step 0
moves: `tools/rome_bench.sh qwen38-vk` two-and-two with the level flipped between
pairs, which takes its own lock and cannot run inside the probe's.

### Reproducing the device map

`tools/hot-expert/q13_devmap.c` — `cc -O0 -o /tmp/q13_devmap tools/hot-expert/q13_devmap.c -lvulkan && /tmp/q13_devmap`.
It creates an instance, enumerates, replays `coli_vk_init` / `_dev2(-1)` /
`_dev3(-1)`'s three selection loops verbatim, prints each enumeration index's PCI
address via `VK_EXT_pci_bus_info`, and dumps its own `/dev/dri` fd order next to
it so the fd-order trap above is visible in one run. It creates no logical device
and allocates nothing, so it is safe to run beside the live gateway (it was).
Cross-check without Vulkan: `grep PCI_SLOT_NAME /sys/class/drm/card*/device/uevent`,
and `grep -E 'drm-pdev|drm-memory-vram' /proc/$(pgrep -x glm53)/fdinfo/*` for the
VRAM ledger line of evidence.

### Verdict: CLOCKS, on the roadmap's own test, with high confidence

The row's rule was *"if `dn-proj` moves toward 19.6 the attenuation is clocks …
if it does not move, the attenuation is something else"*. It moves **20.030 →
17.295** at mask 1 and **22.304 → 18.843** at mask 7 — past 19.6 in both cases —
on a single changed variable, with **no overlap between the two levels' repeats
on any moved bucket** and a bit-identical oracle. The expected delta was **−5 to
−10 ms/token**: the arm that ships gives **−8.281**, inside it; mask 1 alone
gives −4.302, just under it.

**But the size is less than half what the cross-binary reading claimed, and the
difference is Q10 — which is a finding of its own.** The `auto` baseline on this
binary is `dn-proj` **20.030** (mask 1) and **22.304** (mask 7), not the 26.979 /
27.172 the record carries from the pre-Q10 binary. So **Q10 removed ~6.9 ms/token
(mask 1) and ~4.9 (mask 7) of `dn-proj` by itself**, purely by shortening the
CPU work between submit A and submit B (`dn-recur` 9.169 → 1.974, i.e. the A→B
gap 0.26 → 0.055 ms/layer). Q10's own gate reported `dn-proj` flat (−0.017) and
was right — **with the knob OFF, where `dn-proj` is the CPU kernel**. Nobody had
measured `dn-proj` at `Q38_DENSE_GPU=1` on a post-Q10 binary until now.

Two corrections to the record follow from that, and both are the replay's:

- **§Q7's duty-cycle replay under-prices the A→B gap by about 8×.** It measured
  18.61 back-to-back against 19.01–19.48 at 0.26/0.00 — i.e. 0.4–0.9 ms/token
  for that gap — and removing 78 % of it in the engine was worth ~4.9–6.9.
  The replay's busy-wait is not the engine's CPU work: the engine's OpenMP
  regions and their wind-down are what the device sees, and a spin loop on one
  core is not the same idle.
- **`bench_q7_dutycycle`'s "back-to-back control" is not a floor.** At `high` the
  engine reaches 17.295 against that control's 18.61, because the control was
  itself measured at `auto`. The true unattenuated figure for this dispatch shape
  is **≤ 17.3**, the in-engine attenuation at `auto` after Q10 is **20.030 /
  17.295 = 1.158×**, not §Q7's 1.37×, and most of that 1.37× was the long gap
  Q10 has since removed rather than the clocks.

**What this does NOT say.** It does not say the DPM level should be set. The gate
has one leg left — the serving A/B with its own pristine rows — and that leg is
worth taking only after a policy decision that is not this item's: **+69 W of
idle draw on one card, permanently, ~600 kWh/year, on the card that also carries
the console, to buy −8.3 ms/token on an engine that is not the one being
served.** `glm53`, which is served, also runs its dense and KDA work on dev0 and
was not measured here. The cheaper variant is now clearly indicated rather than
guessed: idle power is almost entirely the memory clock (96 → 1249 MHz is the
only thing that changed at idle, sclk reads 0 in both), so
`power_dpm_force_performance_level=manual` plus `pp_dpm_mclk=3` should recover
most of the −8.3 at a fraction of the watts — one more sudo pair and one more
15-minute run of the same harness.

**The other lever the row names — the keepalive dispatch — is NOT built here**
and its ceiling is now measured: **8.3 ms/token at mask 7**, less whatever the
keepalive itself costs in the gap, in an engine whose gap §Q3 showed is unevenly
distributed across layers. That is an Opus item and a separate pass.

**Q14, whose sequencing behind this one assumed they might be one mechanism:
supported in kind, bounded in size, and now with a discriminator.** `gr-read`
falls **26.993 → 26.067 (−0.926)** at mask 7 when only a GPU's DPM level
changes — real, no overlap between the levels' repeats — but at mask 1 it is
**flat (+0.104, repeats overlapping)**. The one place it moves is the one where
`vk-dense` is large (33.8 → 28.5), which is exactly §Q14's own correlation with
fence-wait time rather than with submit count or eviction. So a GPU power state
can move a CPU bucket through the fence, but it accounts for **0.93 of Q14's
+6.35**; the remaining ~5.4 is Q14's to explain, and the fence spin /
`OMP_WAIT_POLICY` / governor hypotheses stand.

### The narrow variant, `manual` + `pp_dpm_mclk=3` (2026-09-12 16:49–16:55 UTC) — the memory-clock hypothesis is REFUTED: it takes 93 % of the idle-power cost and returns at most 12 % of the gain

away.

**What this says, and it is a clean negative.** The narrow variant is **strictly
dominated**: it pays **93 % of `high`'s idle-power cost** (+64 W of +69 W) and
returns **at most 12 % of its gain on any bucket and nothing distinguishable on
the token** — the token's repeat ranges overlap at both masks, so the −0.39 is
inside the harness's own spread and is not a result. Only the dispatch-local
buckets (`dn-proj`, `vk-dense`) separate cleanly, and they move ~0.33 ms/token
against `high`'s 2.7–5.3. `lm-head` even moves the wrong way.

**So the carrier is the core clock, not the memory clock, and the item's own
hypothesis was wrong.** §Q13's reasoning ("a GEMV is memory-bound, so the mclk
ramp is the likely carrier") was a plausible inference from a memory-bound
kernel and it does not survive the measurement: pinning mclk at its top level
for the whole run, including the idle gaps, buys ~0.33 ms/token, while `high` —
which additionally holds the *core* clock's DPM level up — buys 2.7–8.3. The
gap is where the cost sits, and what recovers in the gap is the shader
processors' ramp, not the memory interface's. (Consistent with the traces: sclk
reads 0 at idle and at the sampler's median in **every** state, but its observed
maximum during decode is 1912–2208 MHz at `high` against 1466–2111 at `manual`
and 1485–3098 at `auto` — the gfx clock is gating in all three and `high` is
simply ramping it back faster.)

**Two consequences.**

1. **Neither DPM variant is worth shipping as a rig default on these numbers.**
   `high` buys −8.281 ms/token on an engine that is not served, for +69 W
   permanently on the card that carries the console; the narrow variant buys
   nothing measurable for +64 W. The "cheaper variant" escape route this record
   proposed is closed.
2. **It strengthens the keepalive dispatch, which is now the only live lever.**
   A keepalive is work submitted into the gap — it holds the *core* busy, which
   is precisely the clock this measurement identifies as the carrier, and it
   costs no idle watts when the engine is not running. Its ceiling remains the
   −8.281 measured at `high`, less whatever it costs in the gap. It is still not
   built here.

**The one discriminator not yet run**, if anyone wants the mechanism nailed
rather than inferred: `manual` + `pp_dpm_sclk` forced to level 2 (2371 MHz) with
mclk left free — the complement of this leg. If it reproduces most of `high`'s
−8.281 the attribution is settled and its own idle cost is measured at the same
time. One `sudo` pair and one 15-minute run of the same harness
(`Q13_ORDER=manual Q13_CMP="auto manual"`, after clearing this leg's outputs or
renaming the tag).

## Q14 step 0 (2026-09-12): the CPU-side twin of Q13 — **the item's own hypothesis is REFUTED. The OpenMP wait policy has ZERO headroom (both legs null, with a positive control that moves the same buckets by +16.7), and the cores are at the boost ceiling throughout decode at every mask. The ~5.4 ms/token is not a CPU idle-ramp; it is a 21–23 % loss of achieved DRAM bandwidth on loops that did not change.**

Q14's gate: *"knob off bit-identical; the `gr-read` / `shared` / `cpu-experts`
triple before and after at mask 7, three repeats; the token and the
warm-identical row"*, with step 0 quoted as *"re-run the mask 3 / mask 7
`[OPTIME]` pair with `OMP_WAIT_POLICY=active` and `GOMP_SPINCOUNT=infinite`,
then with the fence spin lengthened"*. Expected: **~7 ms/token recoverable**
(~5 % of the post-Q7 token) *"if it is the wait policy"*, possibly a one-line
env default.

**It is not the wait policy, and it is not an idle ramp of any kind.** Both
legs are null to within a tenth of a millisecond, and the null is bounded from
below by a positive control that the item did not ask for and that the finding
cannot stand without.

### The third leg needs no code: the fence spin is already a knob

The roadmap row asks for *"the fence spin lengthened"* as a throwaway build-time
change. It is not one. `vk_fence_wait()` in `c/backend_vulkan.c` has read
`COLI_VK_SPIN_US` (default **300**) since it was written — it spins on
`vkGetFenceStatus` for that budget and then falls back to `vkWaitForFences`, and
`COLI_VK_SPIN_US=0` restores the pure blocking wait. So all three of Q14's legs
are pure environment, and none of them needs a rebuild, ever. That is recorded
here so the next session does not patch a constant that is already a knob.

### The harness

`tools/hot-expert/q14_probe.sh` (runnable copy `~/bench/q14_probe.sh`), which is
`q13_probe.sh` with the variable changed from a root-owned sysfs level to a set
of environment variables — so, unlike Q13, the legs can be **interleaved by
round** (r1: every variant; then r2; then r3) and drift over the campaign hits
every variant equally. Same rig lock, same gateway rule (`q7_lib.sh`: restart
only what this chain stopped), same refusal on a dirty tree, same GLM-out /
Qwen-in eviction with a 131/131 100 %-resident assertion, same prompt, same
frozen histogram per run (`COLI_USAGE=/tmp/q14_hist.bin`, copied fresh — Qwen
rewrites it at exit, §MEASURING), `OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 OMP_PLACES=cores
OMP_PROC_BIND=close`, three fresh processes per cell, `Q38_TF_DUMP` + `DUMP`
sha256-compared across variants for the oracle. It **asserts the binary's
sha256 is Q13's** (`5a9a24953b33f509`, tree `a934285`, i.e. the tip WITH Q10 —
`~/src/colibri/c/qwen38-vk` is still the Q10 pristine `0da58e9a` and would
measure the wrong engine) and **refuses unless all three cards read `auto`**,
so the rows are comparable to §Q13's paired `auto` leg by construction.

Two things it samples that Q13 did not, because this item is about the other
processor: **per-core `scaling_cur_freq` at 2 Hz** (one Python process, never a
shell loop — q13_probe.sh's rule) and the **`cpuidle` entry/residency counters**,
delta'd across each run. The frequency sampler crashed on its path parser for
the whole of campaign 1 (a `split("/cpu")` that also splits `system/cpu`); it
was fixed and campaign 2 re-took the base rows with it working. Campaign 1's
`[OPTIME]` numbers are unaffected — the sampler is a separate process that died
in its first second, which if anything left campaign 1 marginally *quieter* than
Q13's runs.

Cost: **50–54 s per run**, ~14 min for campaign 1 (15 runs) and ~8 min for
campaign 2 (8 runs), plus the Qwen warm each time; the gateway was down for each
and restarted by the chain (`curl /v1/models` after, and the owner's service
came back both times).

did reach it, and the same axis has **16.7 ms/token of authority over `gr-read`
alone** in the other direction (2 repeats, campaign 2, mask 7):

Three things follow, and the third is the item.

1. **The instrument works.** `passive` (park at every barrier) costs +36.08
   ms/token and it lands *precisely* in Q14's buckets: `gr-read`, `shared`,
   `cpu-experts`, `router`, `gr-mix` — every CPU BF16/OpenMP bucket — while
   **every GPU bucket is flat** (`vk-dense` +0.075, `dn-proj` +0.191,
   `qsa-proj` −0.097, `lm-head` −0.016). `vk-take` falls 3.10 because the CPU
   arrives at the expert results later, so less of the wait is left — the
   engine's own counters are internally consistent under a 30 % perturbation.
   This also re-confirms §RP1's −7.5 % for `passive` and prices it far higher
   in the post-Q7 configuration.
2. **The default already sits at the fast end of this axis.** Between "park
   after libgomp's default 300 000 spins" and "never park" there is **0.09
   ms/token**; between the default and "park immediately" there is **16.68**.
   The engine's inter-region gaps are therefore already shorter than the
   default spin — the workers are not parking, so there is no wake to remove.
3. **The mechanism named in Q14's row cannot be the wake/ramp of OpenMP
   workers**, because forcing them never to sleep is worth nothing while
   letting them always sleep is worth 16.7 in the same bucket.

### And the cores never leave the boost ceiling — the idle-ramp family is refuted directly, not only by the null

2 Hz sampling of every CPU's `scaling_cur_freq`. The decode window is the last
8 s of each run (the run is 50 s, of which ~28 s is the expert preload, so the
whole-run medians below are preload-dominated and are given only for scale).
`schedutil` + `acpi-cpufreq`, min 2 500 MHz, max 3 700 (+boost to ~3 901):

| run | median of the 8 fastest cores, **decode window** | whole run | median across all 16 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| no engine, 30 s idle | **2 500.0** | 2 500.0 | 2 462 |
| `base` mask 0 (×2) | **3 895.7 / 3 896.5** | 2 684 / 2 736 | 3 476 / 3 371 |
| `base` mask 3 (×2) | **3 895.5 / 3 896.9** | 2 679 / 2 739 | 3 415 / 3 543 |
| `base` mask 7 (×2) | **3 896.9 / 3 899.6** | 2 675 / 2 888 | 3 457 / 3 460 |
| `passive` mask 7 (×2) | **3 324.1 / 3 410.6** | 2 850 / 2 825 | 2 898 / 2 997 |

**At mask 0, mask 3 and mask 7 alike the working cores sit within 5 MHz of the
3 901 MHz ceiling for the whole decode window** — there is no de-clocking to
ramp back from, and mask 7 is not distinguishable from the mask where the CPU
does *all* the dense work. `passive` is the one row that drops (−500 MHz), which
is again the control: the sampler resolves the effect when the effect exists.
(2 Hz reads the governor's set point, so it would catch a *sustained* de-clock
and not an individual 300 us dip — but a dip that never changes the set point
cannot cost 5.7 ms/token spread proportionally over 96 sites, and the `active`
leg, which removes the idleness itself, is null.)

The `cpuidle` counters say the same thing from the other side (entries/s summed

token — has the FEWEST C1 entries of any engine run**, and C2 (400 us exit
latency, 800 us target residency) is flat across all of them at ~1 900–2 000/s,
i.e. the idle SMT siblings, unchanged by the mask.

knob-off row. Here is the same comparison on the post-Q10 binary in one session
(campaign 1, three repeats, medians; campaign 2's two-repeat rows agree within
0.3 everywhere):

| bucket | mask 0 | mask 3 | mask 7 | m7 − m0 | ratio m7/m0 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| `vk-dense` | 0.000 | 32.432 | 36.524 | | |
| experts preloaded | **14 673** | **13 577** | **13 305** | −1 368 | |
| **`gr-read`** | **21.709** | **23.133** | **27.386** | **+5.677** | **1.261** |
| `gr-down` | 9.050 | 9.642 | 11.556 | +2.506 | 1.277 |
| `gr-up` | 8.504 | 9.182 | 11.078 | +2.574 | 1.303 |
| `gr-rms` | 1.066 | 1.077 | 1.127 | +0.061 | **1.057** |
| `gr-mix` | 1.447 | 1.528 | 1.630 | +0.183 | **1.126** |
| **`shared`** | **7.216** | **7.878** | **9.514** | **+2.298** | **1.318** |
| `router` | 2.701 | 2.827 | 3.203 | +0.502 | 1.186 |

Four things this says that the §Q7 reading could not:

- **The anomaly reproduces on the post-Q10 binary**: `gr-read` +5.68 and
  `shared` +2.30 against §Q7's +6.35 and +2.23. It is not an artefact of the
  binary, the session or the histogram.
- **It is proportional to each bucket's work, not a fixed cost per OpenMP
  region.** Over 96 gated-residual sites, `gr-down` pays +26 us per site and
  `gr-mix` +1.9 us per site — 13× apart, for loops that run **the same number of
  times in the same regions**. A per-region wake, futex or barrier cost would be
  equal in absolute ms; it is equal in *percent* instead (1.26–1.32 on the
  memory-bound GEMVs, 1.06 on `gr-rms`, the one loop that is serial and
  L1-resident). **Whatever this is, it slows the execution of unchanged code by
  a fraction, it does not add a constant.**
- **Read as bandwidth it is a clean 21–23 % loss.** `gr-down` and `gr-up` each
  stream 96 × 10 240 × 320 × 2 B = **629 MB/token** (§Q-PROFILE's own shape).
  That is **69.5 → 65.2 → 54.4 GB/s** achieved on `gr-down` at masks 0 / 3 / 7,
  and **74.0 → 68.5 → 56.8** on `gr-up`. The same loop, the same weights, the
  same eight cores at the same 3.9 GHz, moving 22 % less DRAM per second when
  the dense stream is on dev0.
- **Neither eviction nor submit count survives, now with this binary's own
  numbers.** Mask 0 → mask 3 evicts **1 096** experts and costs `gr-read` +1.42;
  mask 3 → mask 7 evicts **272** and costs **+4.25**. Mask 3 → mask 7 adds
  **one** submit per token (the head) and 4.09 ms of `vk-dense`. Whatever the
  carrier is, it steps hard at the m3 → m7 boundary, which is exactly where a
  1.27 GB BF16 weight matrix stops being read by the CPU every token and the
  token's last op becomes a device submit.

### Verdict, and what the item is now

**Q14's stated hypothesis — "the CPU idles in sub-millisecond bursts between
OpenMP regions and pays a ramp on each, which is Q13's shape on the other
processor" — is REFUTED.** Three independent measurements say so: the two legs
are null (±0.13 on the gate's triple), the positive control proves the axis has
16.7 ms/token of authority that the default is already collecting, and the cores
are pinned at the boost ceiling through the entire decode window at every mask
while entering *fewer* C-states at mask 7 than at mask 0. The expected **~7
ms/token recoverable** from a wait-policy default is **0**, and there is no
one-line env default to ship. **Q13's mechanism does not have a CPU twin here.**

The ~5.4 ms/token §Q13 left for this item is still unexplained, and step 0 has
sharpened what it is: **not a latency, a throughput loss — a ~22 % reduction in
the DRAM bandwidth the CPU's BF16 GEMVs achieve, present only when the dense
stream runs on dev0, stepping at the m3 → m7 boundary.** The two candidates the
data now points at, neither of which this session ran:

1. **Memory-side interference** — dev0's DMA and the amdgpu driver's per-submit
   kernel work contending for DRAM / IF bandwidth with eight cores that are
   already bandwidth-bound. It predicts exactly the observed shape: proportional
   on memory-bound loops (1.26–1.32), nearly absent on the L1-resident serial
   one (1.06).
2. **Stolen cycles on the SMT siblings** — the driver's threads, kworkers and
   the fence interrupt landing on the sibling of a core running a GEMV, which is
   also proportional and also invisible to `scaling_cur_freq`.

**One 15-minute zero-code measurement separates them** and is the recommended
next step: `perf stat -e cycles,instructions,task-clock,cache-misses` (plus
`stalled-cycles-backend` if the PMU allows it) on the same mask 3 / mask 7 pair.
If the engine's own threads retire the same instructions in the same *cycles*
but over more wall time, it is stolen time; if the cycles rise with backend
stalls, it is memory. **Neither is a Q13 twin and neither is fixed by a knob**,
which is why this is reported rather than tuned.

### What was NOT run, and why

- **Leg 3 (the fence spin, `COLI_VK_SPIN_US` 0 / 3000) was not run.** The
  campaign's own stop rule was written before it started: escalate only if legs
  1 and 2 show a signal. They show none, and the fence spin is a property of the
  *waiting* thread, which the frequency and `cpuidle` evidence now says is not
  where the cost is. The knob exists and needs no code whenever someone wants
  it; `q14_probe.sh` already carries `spin0` / `spin3000` / `spininf` /
  `actspin` as variant names.
- **No serving A/B (`rome_bench.sh`) and no warm-identical row.** The gate asks
  for one *alongside a change*; there is no change. Running `datapoint.py` to
  price a 0.09 ms/token difference in a harness whose rotating median has a
  wider spread would produce a number with no content. The gate's other legs —
  defaults reproduce, the triple at mask 7 with three repeats, the token, the
  bit-identical oracle — are all met above.
- **Nothing is merged and nothing is shipped.** No knob was added, no default
  changed, no file in `c/` touched. The only artefact is the harness.

### Reproducing it

```
scp tools/hot-expert/q14_probe.sh rome:~/bench/           # never over a running script
ssh rome 'Q14_VARIANTS="base active actinf" Q14_MASKS="7" Q14_BASE_MASKS="0 3" \
          Q14_REPEATS=3 setsid nohup ~/bench/q14_probe.sh > ~/bench/q14_c1.log 2>&1 &'
ssh rome 'Q14_VARIANTS="base passive" Q14_MASKS="7" Q14_BASE_MASKS="0 3" \
          Q14_REPEATS=2 Q14_TAG=c2 setsid nohup ~/bench/q14_probe.sh > ~/bench/q14_c2.log 2>&1 &'
```

### FRANKEN-H0d (2026-09-16): user-local ROCm 10.0.0 (TheRock stable wheels) lifts H0's forward-fails blocker entirely — hipFire now completes requests on this box

**The recipe.** `python3 -m venv ~/venvs/rocm && ~/venvs/rocm/bin/pip install -U
pip`, then, following TheRock's current `RELEASES.md` (its naming has moved
on from the "ROCm 7 gfx110X-dgpu nightly index" shape this item was briefed
against — the per-family `gfx110X-all` nightly index at
`rocm.nightlies.amd.com` is now legacy/frozen, and multi-arch per-target
packages are the live scheme): `pip install --index-url
https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-next/
"rocm[libraries,devel,device-gfx1100]"` installed **rocm 10.0.0** (stable
channel, not nightly — nightly on the same day was `10.1.0a20260823`;
10.0.0 is the numbered release TheRock currently ships for gfx1100).
`rocm-sdk init` expands the devel package; `rocm-sdk path --root` resolves
to `~/venvs/rocm/lib/python3.14/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel`. `rocm-sdk
test` (venv `bin/` on `PATH`) is 27/27 OK. Verified: `rocminfo` lists three
gfx1100; `lib/llvm/bin/clang++ --version` = AMD clang 23.0.0git
(`ROCm/llvm-project.git 8f497e09`); `find <root> -name ockl.bc` finds it
under `lib/llvm/amdgcn/bitcode/`; `ldd lib/llvm/bin/ld.lld` has **no**
libxml2 dependency at all (the 6.2 shim is gone by construction, not by
workaround). System ROCm 6.2.0 at `/opt/rocm-6.2.0` was not touched.

**The box's GCC-16 problem is NOT a ROCm-6.2 property — it reproduces
identically against this venv's own clang.** A device-only `<cmath>`-using
HIP kernel (`--cuda-device-only`) with neither `CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH` nor
`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` set fails the same way as under 6.2: clang's GCC-install
autodetection picks the newest GCC (16, headerless — no `libstdc++-16-dev`
on this box) regardless of which ROCm clang is doing the picking.
`CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH=/usr/include/c++/15:/usr/include/x86_64-linux-gnu/c++/15`
fixes it, confirmed with **no** `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` needed for that compile
(the ld.lld/libxml2 half of the 6.2 workaround is gone, as above). A full
host-linked executable additionally needs the GCC toolchain for

## FRANKEN-M0 (2026-09-15, amended 2026-09-16): rccl-tests still has no binary — the `rocm-device-libs` blocker is LIFTED, but two further blockers surfaced behind it

**2026-09-16 06:30 UTC update.** With `rocm-device-libs` installed (62 files
under `/opt/rocm-6.2.0/amdgcn/bitcode/`, `oclc_*` included), the "cannot find
ROCm device library" error described below is gone. Rebuilding surfaced the
**same GCC-16/`libstdc++-16-dev` gap H0 hits** (`§FRANKEN-H0`'s 2026-09-16
update): `amdclang++`'s HIP device compiles now fail on `fatal error:
'cmath' file not found` / `'hip/hip_runtime.h' file not found` because clang
auto-selects GCC 16 (no matching dev headers) over the working GCC 15. Unlike
hipFire, a session *can* control this build's compiler invocation: pointing
`HIPCC` at a one-line wrapper script (`exec amdclang++
--gcc-install-dir=/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/15 "$@"`, `~/amdclang_wrap.sh`,
no sudo, no system file touched — passing `--gcc-install-dir` via `CXXFLAGS`/
`HIPCUFLAGS` on the `make` command line does NOT work, because GNU Make
blocks the Makefile's own `+=` lines from extending a command-line-overridden
variable, silently dropping the real include/offload-arch flags those `+=`
lines were supposed to add) gets past both the device-library and the
GCC-16 errors. **A third, distinct blocker was then hit**: ROCm's bundled
`ld.lld` fails linking every device object —
`/opt/rocm-6.2.0/lib/llvm/bin/lld: error while loading shared libraries:
libxml2.so.2: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory`.
This box has only `libxml2.so.16` (package `libxml2-16` 2.15.2, Ubuntu's
soname-versioned naming); `apt-cache policy libxml2` shows no `libxml2`
(the old `.so.2`-providing package) available in this box's configured repos
at all, and no `.so.2` copy exists anywhere under `/home/ronald` either.
**M0 is still a named blocker: owner action is now `libstdc++-16-dev` (per
H0) and a `libxml2.so.2`-compatible package or shim for `ld.lld`** — neither
is a session-side fix (both are system library additions, and the second
may need a non-default repo since the box's own apt cache does not carry
it). `~/src/rccl-tests/build/all_reduce_perf` still does not exist; M0's
`-g 3`/`-g 2` numbers remain unobtainable tonight.

**2026-09-16 06:55 UTC update: M0 has a real result.** Both remaining
blockers cleared without a package (same recipe as `§FRANKEN-H0`'s second
update): `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$HOME/compat/lib` (the `libxml2.so.2 ->
libxml2.so.16` symlink) lets `ld.lld` run — device *and* host links both
succeed with only the benign "no version information available" warning —
and `HIPCC=~/amdclang_wrap.sh` (`--gcc-install-dir=.../gcc/15`) still covers

link's `-lstdc++` (plain `CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH` alone fixes header search but

### FRANKEN-M0c (2026-09-16): rccl-tests rebuilt against the venv ROCm 10.0.0 — the P2P transport setup failure is GONE, real GPU-to-GPU collectives run, and the small-message latency clears the plan's 33 µs TP3 bar

**Confirms FRANKEN-H0d's `rocm_p2p_probe` result at the level that matters —
an actual collective, not a lone allocation.** `rccl-tests` rebuilt against
`~/venvs/rocm` (root `_rocm_sdk_devel`, same venv as H0d) into
`~/src/rccl-tests/build-rocm10`: `CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH` (as in H0d) covers the
GCC-16-headerless header search for every device compile; the final host
link additionally needs `-lstdc++` resolved, which `CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH` does
not supply (same gap the P2P probe hit) — a wrapper
(`~/amdclang_wrap_rocm10.sh`, `exec <venv root>/bin/amdclang++
--gcc-install-dir=/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/15 "$@"`, no sudo, no system
file touched) set as `HIPCC` on the `make` command line covers it, same
pattern as the existing `~/amdclang_wrap.sh` for system ROCm 6.2. One new
wrinkle, not seen on the 6.2 build: `verifiable.mk` lists the *un-hipified*
source header (`../verifiable/verifiable.h`) as `common.o`'s prerequisite
rather than the hipified copy under `$(HIPIFY_DIR)`, so a genuinely clean
`BUILDDIR` races `common.o`'s compile ahead of the hipify-copy rule and
fails `#include "verifiable.h"` — the 6.2 build never hit this because its
`BUILDDIR` already had a stale hipified copy on disk from an earlier
completed build. Worked around by requesting the three verifiable hipify
targets (`verifiable.h`, `verifiable.cu.cpp`, `rccl_float8.h`) explicitly
before the main build; no Makefile edit. `rccl[libraries]` already bundles
RCCL (`librccl.so`, headers, cmake config) — no separate RCCL install
needed.

**`m0c_chain.sh`, one lock window (08:27:17–08:31:14 UTC, ~4 min, well
under the 15-min budget), `~/bench/m0c_out/m0c_09160827_*`: `all_reduce_perf
-b 8 -e 128M -f 2 -g 3` and `-g 2` run P2P ENABLED (no
`NCCL_P2P_DISABLE`) — both `rc=0`, both a real collective.** The
`hipIpcGetMemHandle failed: invalid argument` blocker from the 06:55 UTC
entry above is gone: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` now prints `Channel 00/0 : 1[86000]

Small-message latency (µs, out-of-place / in-place columns) and 128 MB bus
bandwidth (GB/s, algbw / busbw), against M0b's host-staged (`NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1`,
system ROCm 6.2) numbers for `-g 3`:

| size | M0b host-staged (g3) | M0c P2P/direct (g3) | M0c P2P/direct (g2) |

(RCCL's own end-of-run "Avg bus bandwidth" line — 6.11 GB/s g3, 6.43 GB/s
g2 — averages across every size including the latency-bound small ones and
is not comparable to the 128 MB point figures above; both are in the raw
logs.)

**Verdict against §5's arithmetic.** The per-token collective is the 35B's
hidden state, 2048 × fp16 = 4 KB, once per attention and once per MLP per
layer — 80 collectives/token — and TP3 breaks even only if `4/3 + 80·L <
4 ms`, i.e. **L < 33 µs**. M0c's measured L at 4 KB on `-g 3` is **25.08–
25.70 µs — under the 33 µs bar**, where M0b's host-staged 34.6 µs at 4 KB
was *over* it (the path §5 called "the whole question" was answered "no"
under the fallback transport). This does not by itself clear TP3 for
execution: §5 also names 3 as "an awkward TP degree" (head/expert counts
rarely divide by 3) and gates any pursuit on the ladder as a measured item
in its own right, not on M0's number alone — but the one-line precondition
in §5 ("TP3 for decode of a one-card model is not pursued unless M0
returns L well under 33 µs") is now met, where it was unreachable under
system ROCm 6.2 (no collective ever ran) and would have failed it under
the host-staged fallback (34.6 µs > 33 µs). A `perf/franken-m0b`-style
scoped follow-up, not part of this item, is the next real step if TP3 is
pursued.

VRAM: card0 rose to 141 MB during the `-g 3` run (well under the chain's
1 GiB assert, higher than the ~36 MB idle floor — RCCL's comm-setup
residue, same pattern noted in the 06:55 UTC entry), card1/card2
unaffected; `accept_live.sh` PASSED, gateway back in service
(`a8e10ecf09edc05c`, `/v1/models=200`) before the lock was released.

### 2026-09-15 finding (history — the `rocm-device-libs` part is lifted)

**Outcome: named blocker, not "does not run."** The plan's M0 outcomes
anticipated a *runtime* "does not run" (hostcall, atomics, KFD access); what
was hit instead is a *build-time* one, and it turned out to be the identical
cause that blocks hipFire's request-time JIT above, discovered independently
before the two were connected. `git clone` of `ROCm/rccl-tests` and its
Makefile (still Make, not CMake, as of this clone) built cleanly modulo two
problems on this box's `/opt/rocm-6.2.0`:

1. `hipify-perl` is missing from `/opt/rocm-6.2.0/bin` entirely (`find` over
   the whole ROCm tree turns up nothing named `hipify*`). Worked around
   without sudo or any system change: fetched the script directly from
   `ROCm/HIPIFY` upstream (`bin/hipify-perl`, MIT-licensed, unmodified) to
   `~/hipify-perl` and overrode the Makefile's `HIPIFY_PL_EXE` on the `make`
   command line (a `=`-assigned Makefile variable, overridable from the
   command line per GNU Make's precedence rules). This got every `.cu` test
   source hipified.
2. **`amdclang++` cannot compile any HIP device code at all**: every
   compile of a `.cu.cpp`/`.cc` file containing device code fails with
   `clang++: error: cannot find ROCm device library; provide its path via
   '--rocm-path' or '--rocm-device-lib-path', or pass '-nogpulib' to build
   without ROCm device library`, e.g.:
   ```
   /opt/rocm-6.2.0/bin/amdclang++ -std=c++14 -I/opt/rocm-6.2.0/include \
     -I/opt/rocm-6.2.0/include/hip -x hip -D__HIP_PLATFORM_AMD__ -D__HIPCC__ \
     --offload-arch=gfx1100 [... other arches ...] -O3 -I. -c \
     -o build/all_reduce.o build/hipify/all_reduce.cu.cpp
   clang++: error: cannot find ROCm device library; provide its path via
   '--rocm-path' or '--rocm-device-lib-path', or pass '-nogpulib' to build
   without ROCm device library
   ```
   Confirmed root cause: `dpkg -l | grep -i rocm` shows `rocm-llvm`
   (18.0.0.24292.60200), `hsa-rocr`, `rccl`/`rccl-dev` (the *library*, not
   the compiler's device-libs), `rocblas`, `rocfft`, etc. — but **no
   `rocm-device-libs` package**, and no `oclc_*.bc` file exists anywhere
   under `/opt/rocm-6.2.0` by filesystem search. `/opt/rocm-6.2.0/bin` is
   root-owned (`drwxr-xr-x root root`) and confirmed not writable without
   sudo (`touch` there fails with `Permission denied`; `sudo -n true` fails
   with "interactive authentication is required" — no passwordless sudo
   exists to fall back on). Also tried and also refused, twice: a
   `micromamba` ROCm venv's Triton backend directory and three
   `~/.cache/uv/archive-v0/*/triton/backends/amd/lib/` copies, via both
   `--rocm-device-lib-path=<dir>` and `HIP_DEVICE_LIB_PATH=<dir>` — every one
   of these carries only `ockl.bc`/`ocml.bc` (one also has `asanrtl.bc`),
   never the `oclc_isa_version_*` / `oclc_wavefrontsize64_*` / etc. control
   bitcode clang's HIP frontend also requires, and `amdclang++` gives the
   identical "cannot find ROCm device library" error against each.

`rccl-tests` therefore has no binary (`~/src/rccl-tests/build/` contains only

### FRANKEN-M0b (2026-09-16): the P2P failure is per-device, not per-pair — and host-staged all-reduce clears the 33 us bar only under ~3 KB

**M0's `hipIpcGetMemHandle failed: invalid argument`** left two open questions:
whether the fault is specific to a device pair (a routing/IOMMU problem) or
generic to the API on this box, and whether RCCL can run at all here once
the P2P transport is bypassed. Both are answered now, no owner action, no
system change, one 15-minute rig-lock window.

**Probe (`tools/hot-expert/rocm_p2p_probe.cpp`, no lock — ran alongside the
live gateway, `~/bench/m0b_probe.txt`).** `hipDeviceCanAccessPeer` is `1` for
all six ordered pairs among the three devices, and all three report
`ConcurrentManagedAccess=1`, `VirtualMemoryManagementSupported=1` (PCI bus
IDs 131/134/72 decimal = `0000:83`/`0000:86`/`0000:48`, matching the known
device map). **`hipIpcGetMemHandle` on a lone 1 MB allocation — no peer, no
pair, one device at a time — fails identically on all three**: `invalid
argument`, the same error M0 saw inside RCCL's pairwise setup. This rules
out a pairing- or routing-specific cause (bad peer mapping, one bad
riser/slot): the API itself is refusing on this box regardless of whether a
second device is involved. `/proc/cmdline` confirms `iommu=pt` is absent
(no `iommu=` token at all); `pcie_p2p` is `Y` (module param enabled, which
is consistent with `hipDeviceCanAccessPeer` succeeding — that check does not
call `hipIpcGetMemHandle`). Kernel is `7.0.0-29-generic` (from the RCCL log
in the run below) on this Ubuntu 26.04 box, against a ROCm 6.2.0 userspace
built for 24.04 — the same generation mismatch already named in `§FRANKEN-H0`
for hipFire's unexplained forward failure.

**Chain (`tools/hot-expert/m0b_chain.sh` via `run_chain.sh`, rig lock
07:22:52–07:26:51 UTC, 4 min total, `accept_live.sh` PASS on exit, binary
back in service unchanged `a8e10ecf09ed`).** `all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 128M
-f 2 -g3` and `-g2` with `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1`: **both ran to completion,
rc=0, no `NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=1` fallback needed.** Transport line: `Channel
00 : 0[83000] -> 1[86000] via SHM/direct/direct` (host-staged shared memory,
not sockets, not device P2P). Full tables in
`~/bench/m0b_out/m0b_09160722_g{3,2}_p2pdis.log`.

| size | g3 (TP3) time out/in (us) | g2 time out/in (us) |
|---|---|---|
| 8 B | 30.82 / 31.05 | 26.54 / 26.54 |
| 1 KB | 26.90 / 26.48 | 22.33 / 22.65 |
| 2 KB | 27.89 / 28.42 | 23.42 / 23.23 |
| 4 KB | 34.56 / 34.08 | 28.04 / 27.53 |
| 8 KB | 43.59 / 43.42 | 27.31 / 26.77 |
| 16 KB | 54.76 / 54.47 | 40.01 / 39.50 |
| 64 KB | 61.17 / 61.67 | 44.58 / 43.43 |
| 128 MB busbw | 7.91 / 7.29 GB/s | 7.09 / 6.16 GB/s |
| avg bus bandwidth | 2.84 GB/s | 2.46 GB/s |

**L against the 33 us bar (§5: TP3 breaks even only if `4/3 + 80*L < 4 ms`,
i.e. `L < 33.33 us`), using g3 (the actual TP3 configuration):**

- 8 B, `L=31 us`: `80*0.031 + 4/3 = 2.48 + 1.333 = 3.813 ms < 4 ms` — passes,
  4.7% margin. This is the pure per-collective floor (near-empty payload),
  not a token's real activation size.
- 2 KB, `L=27.89-28.42 us`: `80*0.0281 + 1.333 = 2.25 + 1.333 = 3.58 ms
  < 4 ms` — passes, 10.4% margin. **This is the last size under the bar.**
- 4 KB, `L=34.08-34.56 us`: `80*0.0343 + 1.333 = 2.75 + 1.333 = 4.08 ms
  > 4 ms` — fails, 2.1% over. **This is the first size over the bar.** The
  crossover on g3 sits between 2 KB and 4 KB.
- 64 KB, `L=61.17-61.67 us`: `80*0.0614 + 1.333 = 4.92 + 1.333 = 6.25 ms
  > 4 ms` — fails by 56%.

A TP3 decode all-reduce carries one layer's hidden-state activation per
collective (order of the model's hidden width in elements, times 2 or 4
bytes) — for a 35B-class model that is very likely several KB to tens of KB,
i.e. on or past the 4 KB point where this measured path already misses the
bar, not down at the 8 B/1 KB floor where it clears it. **Verdict: on the
evidence measured tonight, host-staged TP3 decode does not clear the 33 us
bar at realistic per-layer message sizes on this box** — it clears only in
the sub-~3 KB range, and every result here is the *host-staged fallback*,
not the true device-to-device P2P path the plan's arithmetic was written
against (that path still does not exist on this box per M0/this item's
probe).

**Remaining owner-side levers, not run, and what tonight's evidence says
about each:**

- **Kernel `iommu=pt`.** Confirmed absent from `/proc/cmdline`, and it is
  the RCCL log's own named suspect. But the probe's failure is **per-device,
  not per-pair** — a lone allocation with no second device involved fails
  identically — and `iommu=pt` specifically governs IOMMU-mediated
  cross-device DMA remapping for peer transfers. A fault that doesn't need a
  peer to reproduce is evidence *against* this being sufficient by itself,
  though it is cheap and still worth trying since RCCL flags it explicitly.
- **A custom RCCL build without the hostcall/IPC requirement.** Now
  redundant: `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` on the *existing* build already gets a
  working host-staged (SHM) transport tonight, which is what such a build
  would have bought. Not worth pursuing on this evidence.
- **BIOS Above-4G/ReBAR.** Untested directly (no BIOS access this session),
  but the failure signature argues against it as the primary cause:
  `hipIpcGetMemHandle` fails immediately with a generic `invalid argument`
  on the handle-creation call itself, identically on all three cards, not
  with an access-range or mapping fault during actual use — the signature
  one would expect from insufficient BAR size. The more likely explanation
  given all the evidence so far (per-device failure, `§FRANKEN-H0`'s
  parallel unexplained hipFire forward failure, and this box's very new
  `7.0.0-29` kernel under a ROCm 6.2.0 userspace built for 24.04) is a
  ROCm-userspace/kernel version mismatch in the KFD/DMA-BUF IPC path, not a
  BIOS setting — inference, not confirmed; nothing here tests it directly.

## P13 (2026-09-16): the `COLI_KDA_GPU=2` bisect — **RETRACTED as
"intermittent"; root-caused as a stale shader build artifact in
`colibri-x2`'s test harness, not a defect in any engine commit**

**Correction, same day, after the "12/12 IDENTICAL, likely a race"
conclusion below was reported.** The coordinator's field-by-field diff
request found the actual cause. Every one of X2's three reproductions
(`x2_iso_chain.sh`'s `p_gpu2`, `x2_regime_chain.sh`'s `qB`, and the G12
row in `x2_chain.sh`) set `COLI_VK_SHADERS` to `~/src/colibri-x2/c/shaders`
— including when running the **pristine** binary. This bisect always used
a binary's own matching shaders dir and never reproduced. **X,P,P,X on the
pristine binary, `COLI_KDA_GPU=2`, `--greedy 0`, interleaved
(`p13_shader_ab.sh`):**

| pair | result |
|---|---|
| X1 vs X2 (both `colibri-x2` shaders) | IDENTICAL — both the degenerate 154822 line |
| P1 vs P2 (both `colibri`'s own shaders) | IDENTICAL — both the coherent line |
| X1 vs P1, X2 vs P2 (cross) | DIFFERS, both directions |

Deterministic, not probabilistic: 2/2 and 2/2, no overlap. **Root cause:**
`kda_step.comp`'s `conv_channel()` gained a third parameter (`uint qbase`)
in `75ec4bb` (P5.2). `x2_chain.sh` builds a second reference binary by
detouring through the pre-`75ec4bb` commit `be95eb5` (`git checkout
--detach be95eb5 && patch -p1 < .../x2_dump.patch && make -C c glm53
VK=1`) — that `make` rebuilds **every** `.spv`, including `kda_step.spv`,
from `be95eb5`'s two-parameter shader source. The script then restores
only the one tracked file it patched (`git checkout -q -- c/glm53.c`) and
switches HEAD back to the branch; `git checkout <branch>` does not touch
gitignored build artifacts, so the orphaned two-parameter `kda_step.spv`
was left sitting in `colibri-x2/c/shaders/` — confirmed by disassembly
(`spirv-dis`): the stale `.spv` exports `conv_channel(i1;i1;` (2 params,
Bound 486); a fresh compile of the CURRENT `kda_step.comp` (run twice,
moments apart, byte-identical both times — ruling out a toolchain or
non-determinism explanation) gives `conv_channel(i1;i1;u1;` (3 params,
Bound 538), matching `colibri`'s own shader exactly. Feeding the current
(post-`75ec4bb`) pristine binary a pre-`75ec4bb` shader missing a
parameter is a host/shader ABI mismatch — degenerate output is the
expected shape of that failure, not a race.

**Production was never exposed to this**: `~/start_glm53.sh` hardcodes
`COLI_VK_SHADERS="$HOME/src/colibri/c/shaders"` — always the matching,
correctly-built directory. **No culprit commit exists to name because
there is no code-level defect in the `dd8fc3c..HEAD` range**; `75ec4bb`
is not at fault for changing the shader interface (that is ordinary
development), the fault is `x2_chain.sh`'s detour build not restoring or
invalidating the shader artifacts it rebuilds from an old commit. P13 is
CLOSED: not a regression, a test-harness bug. Recommended (not done
here, out of this item's scope): make `x2_chain.sh`'s G14-detour build in
a throwaway worktree instead of mutating `colibri-x2`'s own working tree,
or `rm -f c/shaders/*.spv` before switching back to the branch so `make`
is forced to rebuild them from the restored source next time they are
used.

Built each of the four suspects plus the G12-landing anchor in dedicated

**A bug in the first version of `p13_chain.sh` caused a real ~28-minute
outage of the owner's live gateway (15:11–15:39 UTC), unrelated to the
bisect question itself and already fixed** (commit `4f1c477` on this

running, which it always is (the gateway's own engine) — so the very
first window exited 1 *before* `stop_gateway` ran, and `on_exit`'s
unconditional `pkill -9 -x glm53` killed the gateway's own engine child
directly instead of a test run's, leaving `openai_server.py`'s dispatcher
permanently stuck ("colibri engine dispatcher stopped", 500 on
`/v1/chat/completions`) while `/v1/models` kept answering 200 and hid it.
Recovered by hand: killed the stuck process group, cleared the stale
`~/bench/.rig.lock`, restarted via the documented procedure. Verified
recovery with a real chat completion and `accept_live.sh` (full) PASS
before resuming. Fixed by dropping `glm53` from that preflight list —
`stop_gateway` is the only thing allowed to kill it, and only together
with the wrapper.

sanity anchors the item specified (G12-landing sha, expected IDENTICAL:

| P2.1/P2.4 | `63a1b31f8053054c` | `23ed436` | IDENTICAL |
| P2.1 | `6264d23e0ff5e0d4` | `0b75c42` | IDENTICAL |
| P6b | `9be877a737f5ff18` | `7b70112` | IDENTICAL |
| P5.2 | `80ec2ad693fe04bd` | `75ec4bb` | IDENTICAL |

**12 runs, 0 DIFFERS.** Every `gate_compare` reported IDENTICAL with 1

**Methodology cross-check, to rule out an environment drift instead of a
real non-repro:** the packet is byte-identical across `colibri`,
`colibri-p13` and `colibri-x2` (`sha256 ef569aa0…` in all three); the KDA
shader *sources* are byte-identical between `colibri` and `colibri-x2`
(only the compiled `.spv` differs, an unreproducible `glslc` build
artifact, not a semantic change); every run here and X2's own
`p_gpu2.err` report the identical expert preload (1288 heat-ranked
experts resident) and the identical KDA slot pool (1 × 156 MB, the CLI's
single-slot allocation) — nothing measurable differs between this
session's conditions and X2's.

**Conclusion: the defect is real (§X2 has concrete evidence: a decoded
"# 3.1.1.1.1.1…" and a teacher_forcing line 92/564 positions = token
154822) but is not a deterministic function of (binary, prompt), and a
single-sample-per-commit bisect cannot localize it.** X2's own binary and
packet reproduced the defect once and produced the correct output seven
times right after, here, under verified-matching conditions — an observed
rate around 1-in-8 on that one binary, not "broken" or "fixed" in any
binary sense. A commit reporting IDENTICAL under this method is not
evidence of innocence; a commit that happened to report DIFFERS would not
have been evidence of guilt either. **No culprit commit is named — doing
so from these results would not be supportable.**

This fits exactly the mechanism §X2 already proposed and did not resolve:
"(ii) the teacher_forcing readout races the GPU (reads the logits buffer
before the chained command buffer's fence signals)". The single-submit
KDA chain that hypothesis implicates was fixed in kind at G12's own
landing (stage 2b/2c, `1a831b4`/`dd8fc3c`) and every commit tested here
only adds more batching on top of the same submit-then-read-back shape —
consistent with a host/device race present since G12 itself, gated by
scheduling timing rather than by which commit is running, and rare enough
that G12's own 1260-position gate and four of five bisect points here
(6 of 6 non-repeated candidates, 12 of 12 total) never observed it.

**Next (Opus, not this item's scope): confirm hypothesis (ii) directly**
— a fence-wait assertion or timing instrumentation around the CLI's
`teacher_forcing` readout relative to the KDA chain's command-buffer
submission, or a repeated-sampling bisect (N >= 10-20 per candidate) if a
commit-level answer is still wanted once a trigger is known. Until then,
CLAUDE.md's existing rule stands: every CLI oracle on `glm53` runs at
`COLI_KDA_GPU=0`.

## X1 (2026-09-16): retained Vulkan command buffers — **REJECTED on measurement, and the projection it was built on is refuted by a direct number.** The per-token descriptor writes + command re-record that this graft removes cost **1.1–3.7 µs (median 2.8) per submit**, against a driver submit of **22–25 µs** and a GPU wait of **135–1568 µs**. That bounds the whole mechanism at **≈0.27 ms/token on qwen38-vk (97 submits) and ≈0.13 on glm53 (34)**, against a projected **−3 to −8 ms/token**: a factor of 12–30 out, and roughly 20× below this box's own run-to-run spread. On qwen38-vk every oracle is bit-identical; on glm53 only the `tworeq` 4-slot text identity stands (the CLI logit legs are void — §X2's defect, garbage on both sides). The serving A/B is NO VERDICT on the headline on both engines (one column separates, at +0.2 %, exactly the size the ceiling predicts). The mechanism is **not merged**: the branch is the negative result, this section is what lands, and the `VK_PROF` phase split that measured it is the part worth keeping.

Graft X1 of `tools/hot-expert/FRANKEN-ENGINE-PLAN-2026-09-15.md` §4, on
`perf/x1-retained-cmdbuf`. Pristine = a build of the branch point `116d2f5`,
which comes out **byte-identical to the glm53 in service** (`a8e10ecf09edc05c`)
and to the rig tree's `qwen38-vk` (`d05b09adfe27b603`), so "the pristine" and
"the binary the owner is served by" are the same file here.

### What was built

`COLI_VK_RETAIN_CB=1` (off by default) gave `coli_vk_matmul_multi` (Q7's dense
stream on qwen38-vk; GLM's batched projections) and `coli_vk_kda_layer` (G12's
whole-KDA-layer chain on glm53) a table of retained recordings, keyed by the
exact signature of the recording — the resident tensor pointers, the shapes, the
chaining, the y layout, the (layer, slot) of the KDA state, the push-constant
floats. A hit skips `vkUpdateDescriptorSets` and the reset/begin/record/end and
submits the previous token's command buffer verbatim. Each entry owns its own
descriptor sets and command buffer, so nothing shares `G.cmd`/`G.dset` with the
dynamic path. A scratch realloc bumps a generation counter and drops the whole
table, because a retained recording names `VkBuffer` handles that the realloc
destroys — and the driver may hand the same numeric handle back.

The MoE expert groups were deliberately left dynamic: their expert set and row
counts change every token, so every recording would be a miss. That is also
where §Q7's `vk-issue` 13.8 + `vk-take` 4.8 ms/token live, which matters below.

### Step 0, the isolated microbenchmark (`rome_vkbench <spv> x1`)

The same sites, knob off and on, interleaved **inside one process** (A,B,B,A per
outer repeat, five outer repeats, median of medians), at the engine's own shapes
and at the engine's own inter-submit gaps — the form §Q7's arbitration made
mandatory for a step-0 GPU prediction. `copies` distinct tensor sets rotate so
the weights stream from VRAM, and the pool size is printed (252–2543 MB, all
above the 96 MB Infinity Cache). Retention is proved non-vacuous by the hit /
miss counters printed on every line.

| site (×per token) | gap replayed | OFF ms/site | ON ms/site | Δ ms/token, three passes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| deltanet-A, 4 tensors (×36) | 0.26 | 0.3388 / 0.3413 / 0.3411 | 0.3392 / 0.3400 / 0.3397 | +0.017 / −0.049 / −0.051 |
| deltanet-B, 1 tensor (×36) | 1.50 | 0.3170 / 0.3063 / 0.3012 | 0.3196 / 0.3006 / 0.3047 | +0.093 / −0.204 / +0.125 |
| qsa-A, 4 tensors (×12) | 0.30 | 0.4746 / 0.4748 / 0.4740 | 0.4755 / 0.4735 / 0.4738 | +0.010 / −0.015 / −0.003 |
| qsa-B, 1 tensor (×12) | 1.50 | 0.3049 / 0.3072 / 0.2993 | 0.3239 / 0.3224 / 0.3232 | +0.229 / +0.182 / +0.286 |
| lm-head, 1 tensor (×1) | 1.50 | 2.4949 / 2.4113 / 2.3843 | 2.4977 / 2.3913 / 2.4020 | +0.003 / −0.020 / +0.018 |
| kda-proj8, 8 tensors (×34) | 0.00 | 0.9570 / 0.9563 / 0.9559 | 0.9529 / 0.9550 / 0.9535 | −0.140 / −0.044 / −0.081 |

Summed over the five qwen38-vk sites at their own gaps the three passes give
**+0.352 / −0.106 / +0.375 ms/token**: not a small win, a sign that does not
even hold across repeats. The A/B at this level is measuring the box, not the
change.

### The phase split, which is the item's whole answer

`VK_PROF=1` now splits both retained paths into *our* work (descriptor writes +
recording), the driver's `vkQueueSubmit`, and the fence wait, in windows of 256
calls so a line belongs to one shape rather than to a run's mixture:

```
[VK_PROF mm] n=256  | desc+record 1.81 us/call (136 of 256 recorded) | submit 23.45 | wait  206.88 us
[VK_PROF mm] n=768  | desc+record 0.79 us/call (124 of 256 recorded) | submit 22.09 | wait  326.64 us
[VK_PROF mm] n=1536 | desc+record 0.50 us/call (120 of 256 recorded) | submit 21.80 | wait  272.44 us
[VK_PROF mm] n=2304 | desc+record 1.91 us/call (134 of 256 recorded) | submit 24.34 | wait  276.10 us
[VK_PROF mm] n=3072 | desc+record 1.44 us/call (132 of 256 recorded) | submit 23.43 | wait  918.99 us
```

Each window is ~half retained and ~half recorded, so per RECORDED call the twelve
windows give **1.07, 1.63, 1.71, 1.98, 2.16, 2.76, 2.79, 2.97, 3.16, 3.39, 3.41,
3.65 µs — median 2.8**. That is everything a retained command buffer can remove,
measured rather than assumed, and it is **0.9–1.5 % of the 22–25 µs submit and
0.2–2 % of a 135–1568 µs round trip**.

**The arithmetic the projection needed.** −3 ms/token over qwen38-vk's 97
submits is 31 µs per submit; −8 ms/token is 82 µs. The measured quantity is 2.8.
The plan took its −3..−8 from `vk-issue` 13.8 + `vk-take` 4.8 ms/token and read
those as "the CPU-side re-record and validation". They are not: they are the
**expert group's** buckets — the path X1 deliberately leaves dynamic — and even
there the record is a small part of a bucket that is mostly submit and GPU wait.

### Oracles — bit-identical, which is this item's bar

qwen38-vk, short prompt 128 greedy tokens, `Q38_DENSE_GPU=7` (the only regime in
which this engine has retained sites at all), against the `116d2f5` pristine:

| leg | knob off | knob on |
|---|---|---|
| last-token logits (993 280 B) | **BIT-IDENTICAL** | **BIT-IDENTICAL** |
| `teacher_forcing` | **BIT-IDENTICAL** | **BIT-IDENTICAL** |
| greedy text, 128 tokens | **IDENTICAL** | **IDENTICAL** |
| default path, mask 0 | — | **BIT-IDENTICAL** |
| long prompt (40×), mask 7 | — | **BIT-IDENTICAL** |
| `tworeq.py TWOREQ_ARCH=qwen38`, 3 requests in one engine | — | **IDENTICAL across 3 requests** |

### The in-engine `[OPTIME]` A/B, and why it cannot be used for this item

Three fresh-process repeats a side, alternating off,on,off,on,off,on, medians of
the decode bank at mask 7:

| bucket | knob off | knob on | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **step (the token)** | 120.214 | 115.506 | **−4.71** |
| the five retained sites (`dn-proj`+`qsa-proj`+`lm-head`+`vk-issue`+`vk-take`) | 59.657 | 59.117 | −0.54 |
| buckets X1 CANNOT touch (`gr-read`, `shared`, `router`, `dn-recur`, `dn-conv`, `cpu-experts`, `qsa-attn`) | 56.869 | 52.777 | **−4.09** |

**87 % of the apparent −4.71 sits in buckets the change does not touch**, and
every one of them moved the same way by the same few percent. That is a session
drift, not an effect: alternating A,B,A,B puts every B run immediately after an
A run, so a monotone warm-up biases B, which is exactly what `gate_lib.sh`'s
A,B,B,A rule exists to cancel. Reported here rather than tuned away, and **not**
quoted as X1's delta; the phase split above is the number.

### What this says about the plan's branch 3, and what the real lever is

§3 of the plan puts a **≤ 28 tok/s ceiling** on a Colibri-native VRAM-resident
40-layer path, from "40 layers × ≥ 3 submits per layer × ≥ 0.30 ms per gap ≥ 36
ms/token of submit gaps alone", and makes X1 a **precondition** of V1 for that
reason, with the falsifier "X1 lands below 2× on the submit buckets".

**The falsifier fires, at 1.00×, and the reason is worth more than the verdict.**
The 0.30 ms gap is not overhead: §Q7 measured it as the engine's own CPU work
between submits (`qsa-attn` 3.46 + `qsa-index` 0.13 over 12 layers). Of a
0.30–1.50 ms gap, **2.8 µs is our recording** — 0.2–0.9 %. Retained command
buffers cannot remove that ceiling because the ceiling is not made of recording.
On the measured split it is made of, in order: the GPU wait (135–1568 µs), real
CPU work between submits, and **22–25 µs of driver `vkQueueSubmit` per submit**
— 120 submits/token at 3 per layer is **2.8 ms/token of pure submit cost**
before any compute or any gap.

So the lever on a 40-layer resident path is **fewer submits**, which is what this
fork's landed items already do (P2 batching the dense prefill stages, G12 folding
a KDA layer into one submit, Q3 absorbing the shared expert into the gap, Q7
batching the dense stream) — not cheaper recording of the same number of them.
V1's step 2 does not need X1, and it does not get relief from it.

### Serving A/B, `rome_bench.sh qwen38-vk`, interleaved A,B,B,A

Both arms are the same candidate binary at `Q38_DENSE_GPU=7`; only
`COLI_VK_RETAIN_CB` differs. The harness's own eviction, warm and residency
assertions; the tier came up at 13 305 experts on every run. Retention is proved
live by the engine's own line — **`[RCB] retained command buffers ON: 96
site(s) recorded`**, i.e. the 36×2 + 12×2 + 1 = 97 dense submits per token this
engine has at mask 7, found empirically rather than assumed.

| run | rotating median | warm-identical | cold |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `x1m7-off-run1` | 5.70 | 8.28 | 4.29 |
| `x1m7-on-run1` | 5.82 | 8.30 | 4.37 |
| `x1m7-on-run2` | 6.29 | 8.31 | 4.29 |
| `x1m7-off-run2` | 6.06 | 8.24 | 4.28 |

`gate_ab_verdict`, verbatim:

| column | verdict |
|---|---|
| rotating median (the headline) | A=5.880 [5.700–6.060] B=6.055 [5.820–6.290] — **OVERLAPPING, NO VERDICT** (+3.0 % on means, which is the box's own spread) |
| warm-identical | A=8.260 [8.240–8.280] B=8.305 [8.300–8.310] — **SEPARATED, +0.5 % on means, +0.2 % conservative** |
| cold | A=4.285 [4.280–4.290] B=4.330 [4.290–4.370] — **OVERLAPPING, NO VERDICT** |

The one column that separates puts the change at **+0.2 % conservative**, i.e.
8.26 → 8.305 tok/s = 121.1 → 120.4 ms/token, **−0.7 ms/token**. The phase split
predicts 97 × 2.8 µs = **−0.27**. Same sign, same order, and both are far under
the rotating column's own 3–5 % spread — which is why the headline cannot see it
and never could. **This is a consistency check on the ceiling, not a win**: a
0.2 % conservative figure from two single-request samples per arm is not a reason
to carry a descriptor/command-buffer cache in a file both engines build.

### The same split IN THE ENGINE, which is where the microbenchmark could have been wrong

qwen38-vk, mask 7, knob **off** so every window is 256-of-256 recorded, `VK_PROF=1`:

```
[VK_PROF mm] n=1536 | desc+record 3.08 us/call (256 of 256 recorded) | submit 27.08 | wait 330.92 us
[VK_PROF mm] n=2048 | desc+record 2.65 us/call (256 of 256 recorded) | submit 25.33 | wait 346.38 us
[VK_PROF mm] n=2560 | desc+record 2.62 us/call (256 of 256 recorded) | submit 25.40 | wait 343.01 us
[VK_PROF mm] n=2816 | desc+record 2.60 us/call (256 of 256 recorded) | submit 25.41 | wait 347.89 us
```

**2.54–3.08 µs in the engine against 2.8 median in the microbenchmark.** The
usual failure ("fast in L3, slow in the engine") does not happen here, and the
one hypothesis that could have saved the projection — that a busy CPU with cold
caches records ten times slower — is measured false.

**And the bucket the projection was actually taken from.** The expert group's own
`[VK_PROF]` line, same run, per group submit:

```
[VK_PROF] memcpy_x 0.009 | desc 0.006 | record 0.003 | issue->take 0.504 | memcpy_y 0.005 ms
[VK_PROF] memcpy_x 0.009 | desc 0.006 | record 0.003 | issue->take 0.472 | memcpy_y 0.005 ms
```

Descriptor writes **6 µs** plus recording **3 µs** — for a group that binds up to
64 experts and records 128 dispatches — against **472–504 µs** of issue→take.
So `vk-issue` + `vk-take` are **1.8 % recording and 98 % submit, GPU and
readback**. Even a hypothetical retained expert group (impossible: the expert set
changes every token) would be worth 9 µs a group.

### glm53 — the logit oracle is VOID, and what is left standing

The KDA chain (`COLI_KDA_GPU=2`) is the retained site on this engine. The legs
that were run, and what each is worth:

| leg | result | worth |
|---|---|---|
| `g-off` / `g-on` (`prefill_profile.sh`, `COLI_KDA_GPU=2`), `teacher_forcing` and `last_logits` vs the `116d2f5` pristine | IDENTICAL / IDENTICAL, 782 positions and 154 881 logits a side | **VOID — see below** |
| `g-on-c0` (knob on, `COLI_KDA_GPU=0`, the CPU recurrence) | **IDENTICAL** / **IDENTICAL** | valid, but no retained site fires on this path either |
| `tworeq.py TWOREQ_SLOTS=4`, knob **off** and knob **on** | **IDENTICAL across 4 requests** in both, and the two runs' generated text is **byte-identical to each other** | **the only serving-path evidence for glm53** |

**Two independent reasons the `prefill_profile.sh` legs prove nothing here.**

1. They print no `[RCB]` line: in that CLI mode the engine takes neither retained
   path, so even a valid comparison would be an oracle on the BINARY and not on
   the retained path.
2. **The comparison itself is void.** §X2 established the same night that the
   CLI `--prompt` path under `COLI_KDA_GPU=2` **generates garbage on the pristine
   serving binary** — `teacher_forcing` and the text both degenerate — while the
   served path and the CPU path are fine. Both sides of these legs were taken
   through that path, so this table compared garbage with garbage and its
   IDENTICAL verdicts carry no information about numerics.

So for glm53 the standing evidence that the retained path does not change the
output is **`tworeq.py` at 4 slots, knob off vs knob on, byte-identical generated
text across 4 requests in a persistent engine** — the regime the retained path
actually fires in (the four `rome_bench` runs below print `[RCB] retained command
buffers ON: 32 site(s) recorded`). There is **no glm53 logit-level oracle** for
this item. Closing that would be one `x1_probe.sh profg` invocation (~25 min
under the lock, and it would have to avoid the §X2 path); it was **not run**, by
decision, because the item is rejected on its measured size and a logit oracle
would not change that verdict.

### Serving A/B, `rome_bench.sh glm53`, interleaved A,B,B,A, `COLI_KDA_GPU=2`

| run | rotating median | warm-identical | cold |

### The verdict

| leg | required | measured | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| bit-identical, qwen38-vk, both knob positions | identical | logits, `teacher_forcing`, greedy text, `tworeq` all identical | **MET** |
| bit-identical, glm53 | identical | `tworeq` at 4 slots byte-identical across the knob, in the regime where `[RCB]` fires; the `prefill_profile.sh` logit legs are **VOID** (§X2's CLI-at-`COLI_KDA_GPU=2` defect, garbage on both sides) | **NOT ESTABLISHED at the logit level; text-identical in the regime that matters** |
| A,B,B,A both engines through `gate_ab_verdict` | a verdict | qwen38-vk rotating **NO VERDICT**, warm-identical **+0.2 % conservative**; glm53 **NO VERDICT** on all three | **the change does not separate** |
| the projected −3 to −8 ms/token | −3 to −8 | ceiling **−0.27** (qwen38-vk), **≈−0.12** (glm53) | **NOT MET, by a factor of 12–30** |

**Rejected, and not merged.** The mechanism is ~200 lines in a file both engines
build, for an effect two orders of magnitude under the harness's resolution.
`perf/x1-retained-cmdbuf` stays unmerged as the negative result; this section is
what lands. The part worth re-taking on its own someday is the `VK_PROF` phase
split, because the number it produces — *what fraction of a Vulkan submit on this
box is our own CPU work* — is what every future submit-batching item needs, and
nothing in the tree reported it before.

### Reproducing it

Everything named here lives on the unmerged branch `perf/x1-retained-cmdbuf`
(tip `3bcea49` for the code, the docs commit on top): the table, the knob, the
`VK_PROF` phase split, `rome_vkbench <spv> x1` and `x1_probe.sh`. Check it out to
re-run any of it:

```
git checkout perf/x1-retained-cmdbuf && make -C c qwen38 qwen38-vk glm53 VK=1
ssh rome 'setsid nohup bash ~/src/colibri-x1/tools/hot-expert/x1_probe.sh prof >> ~/bench/x1_prof.log 2>&1 &'
```

## V1 (2026-09-16): a Vulkan expert tier for `qwen36`

FRANKEN-ENGINE-PLAN-2026-09-15.md §2.6, item V1. Branch
`perf/v1-qwen36-vk-tier`; design `tools/hot-expert/V1-STEP0-2026-09-16.md`.
Rig clone `~/src/colibri-v1`, chain `tools/hot-expert/v1_step1_chain.sh`
through `run_chain.sh`, logs `~/bench/v1_step1.log` and `~/bench/v1_step1_out/`.

### V1 step 1 — `qwen36-vk` builds, the tier is compiled in and OFF, and with it off the binary is bit-identical to the CPU engine. GATE PASS.

`make -C c qwen36-vk VK=1` is the `qwen38-vk` shape: a **separate** binary
(`-DQ36_VK_TIER`), so `make qwen36` is untouched and still links no Vulkan
(verified in the chain: `ldd | grep -c vulkan` = 1 and 0). `qwen36_tier.h`'s
guard widens to `COLI_CUDA || Q36_VK_TIER`; the Vulkan implementation of the
same `qt_*` contract is a new file, `c/qwen36_tier_vk.c`, so `qwen36_tier.c`
(the CUDA tier and its seven tests) is not edited at all. The tier is OFF
unless `Q36_VULKAN=1`, and with it unset `qt_init` returns before
`coli_vk_init`, so the tier-off arm opens no Vulkan device.

Run `v1s109160748`, 2026-09-16 07:48–07:56 UTC. Container
`/home/ronald/models/qwen36_i4_gs64`, page-cache residency **100.0 %**,
`OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 OMP_PLACES=cores OMP_PROC_BIND=close`, cache/layer 256
(every expert in RAM, as arm C). Binaries: `~/bench/qwen36.v1cpu`
sha256 `168023797188f8e8` (`make qwen36`, no VK), `~/bench/qwen36-vk.v1`
sha256 `1692120ced60a8f0` (`make qwen36-vk VK=1`). VRAM on all three cards
< 40 MB before the runs.

| leg | prompt | result |
|---|---|---|
| `teacher_forcing` (per-position argmax over the whole prefill) | packet, 625 positions | **IDENTICAL** |
| | short, 22 positions | **IDENTICAL** |
| | short at `N_NEW=1`, 22 positions | **IDENTICAL** |
| last-token logits, `cmp` (not a cosine — the claim is bit-identity) | packet / short / short-1 | **IDENTICAL**, 993 280 B each |
| greedy text (the decoded tokens on stdout) | packet, 8 tokens | **IDENTICAL** |
| | short, 16 tokens (64 non-space chars) | **IDENTICAL** |
| whole per-position logit dump, `cmp` | packet | **IDENTICAL**, 620 800 016 B |
| | short / short-1 | **IDENTICAL**, 21 852 176 B |
| `majflt` per run | all six runs | **0** |
