### §F2e — what the 18k rung will decide, and the arithmetic that predicts it

The buckets that F2 does not touch grow with depth and `ffn_moe` does not, so
the speedup FALLS with depth. From §RP-F6a's 18k token (136.4 ms/token, of
which `ffn_moe` 69.8) and this section's measured post-F2 `ffn_moe` of 13.4
ms/token (depth-independent: the streamed bytes per token depend on the chunk,
not on the context):

> 136.4 − 69.8 + 13.4 = **80.0 ms/token → 1.71×**, against a 1.60× bar.

TTFT for the 18k turn would be **1 179.4 / 1.71 ≈ 690 s**, against the ≤ 737 s
the gate allows. **That is an 6 % margin and it is a projection, not a
measurement.** The 18k A,B,B,A is what decides it.

### Open, and written down rather than tuned away

1. **The 2.0× turn-1 bar is met by 1 %.** Reported as met because
   `gate_ab_verdict` separates the arms, and reported as fragile because it is.
2. **The streaming, not the chunk, is the numerics delta** — 5.02 % of argmaxes
   at 6.3k with the chunk left alone, against 4.95 % with it changed — and its
   cause is the §G13 clamp gap, not the ring (O3). The first reading of O2/O4
   said the opposite and O5 corrected it; the correction is in §F2b rather than
   the wrong sentence being deleted.
3. **The streamed path inherits the §G13 swiglu-clamp gap** and hands it to
   more of the model's calls than today's placement does. F2 deliberately did
   not add a clamp to `qmatmul_gate_up.comp`: a clamped streamed path and an
   unclamped resident path would make an expert's numerics depend on which
   side of the ring it landed, which is a second instance of §G13 rather than a
   fix. The clamp is still the next real correctness item on this engine and
   F2 makes it matter more, not less.
4. `coli_vk_kda_step_rows` costing 2.05× per token at S=512 than at S=128
   (§F2f) is observed, not diagnosed. It is worth ~0.15× of F2's headline.

### §F2f — the 2×2: the chunk buys 3 % of speed and costs 3 % of the argmaxes

The cell O2 and O4 leave open is streaming at the DEFAULT chunk. Taken at both
depths, same tier, same binary, prefill wall seconds:

| | CPU experts | streamed |
|---|---:|---:|
| **2 061 tokens**, chunk 128 | 219.3 s | **136.9 s** (1.60×) |
| **2 061 tokens**, chunk 512 | — | **134.0 s** (1.64×) |
| **6 327 tokens**, chunk 128 | 731.3 s | **466.6 s** (1.57×) |
| **6 327 tokens**, chunk 512 | 687.3 s | **451.8 s** (1.62×) |

**Streaming at the engine's default chunk gets 1.57× of the 1.62×.** The chunk
is worth 3.2 % of speed and costs 3.24 % of the argmaxes (§F2b, O4). The
`COLI_TIMERS=1` buckets say why, and the reason is not the MoE:

| bucket, 6 327 tokens, streamed | chunk 128 | chunk 512 | chunk 512 − chunk 128 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `ffn_moe` | 144.72 s | 84.55 s | **−60.17** |
| `kda` | 69.05 s | 106.71 s | **+37.66** |
| — of which `kda step` | 37.36 s | 76.49 s | +39.12 |
| `mla.attn` | 151.78 s | 160.77 s | +8.99 |
| `mla.index` | 19.25 s | 20.11 s | +0.87 |
| `ffn_dense` | 18.01 s | 17.31 s | −0.71 |
| `hc+norm` | 29.12 s | 28.39 s | −0.73 |
| **layers total** | **448.76 s** | **435.37 s** | **−13.39** |

Chunk 512 saves 60.2 s in the MoE and gives 46.7 s of it back in the KDA and
the attention core. **`coli_vk_kda_step_rows` (P5.2, "S tokens of a prefill
chunk, S dispatches with barriers in ONE submit") costs 2.05× per token at
S=512 than at S=128** — the dispatches are serialised by the recurrence's own
barriers, so a longer command buffer buys nothing and evidently loses. That is
a new, cheap-looking item: if the KDA held its chunk-128 cost, chunk 512 would
finish this prompt in ~414 s (1.77×) instead of 451.8 (1.62×). `mla.attn` is
also 5.9 % worse at 512, which is worth knowing before F7 assumes bigger
batches are better.

Streamed traffic, for the record: at chunk 128, 206 481 expert fills = 2.924 TB
in 115.8 s (25.2 GB/s, 462 MB/token, 18.3 ms/token); at chunk 512, 76 693 fills
= 1.086 TB in 49.3 s (22.0 GB/s, 163 MB/token, 7.79 ms/token). `cpu_fallback=0`
in every run: the ring served every non-resident expert it was given.

**What the 2×2 decides, now that O5's logits are in.** The reason to prefer
chunk 128 would have been numerics, and O5 removes it: streaming at chunk 128
moves *more* argmaxes (5.02 %) than streaming at chunk 512 (4.95 %). So the
chunk costs nothing numerically once the knob is on, and buys 3 % of speed —
which at turn 1 is the difference between 2.02× (measured) and ≈ 1.98×
(projected), i.e. between meeting the 2.0× bar and missing it. **`COLI_PREFILL_STREAM=1`
keeping its effective chunk of 512 is therefore right, and it is right for a
different reason than the design gave.** `GLM53_PREFILL_CHUNK=128` remains
available with the knob on and its cost is the row above.

### §F2g — the KL bar, and the two max-abs that are not the same number

X2's KL bar is part of F2's §8.3 gate and §F2b did not apply it. Fable ran
`kl_compare.py` on §F2b's dumps (bar as the record states it for V1: mean
KL < 0.0284 **and** top-1 ≥ 99.0 %):

| unclamped comparison, deep packet (6 327 positions) | mean KL | max KL | top-1 | last cos |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| off vs stream + chunk 512 (O2) | 0.0124448 | 0.809674 @378 | **95.05 %** | 0.993153236 |
| off vs chunk 512 alone (O4) | 0.00565465 | 0.358958 @5865 | 96.76 % | 0.995078853 |
| off vs stream @128 (O5) | 0.0123284 | 0.809797 @378 | **94.97 %** | 0.993246735 |

**Streaming fails the top-1 bar**, by 4 points. The mean KL passes comfortably
on every row; the bar that bites is top-1.

**The two max-abs.** This chain's `logit_diff` printed `max_abs=10.5523` for
the pair `kl_compare.py` reports as `maxabs 1.52635`. Neither is wrong and
neither is noise: **`logit_diff` maximises over every position of the dump
(6 327 × 154 880 floats); `kl_compare.py` reports the LAST position only**, the
figure CLAUDE.md's oracle convention names. The cosines agree to nine digits
(0.99315324 vs 0.993153236), which is what identified it. `logit_diff`'s label
said "last-token cosine=… max_abs=…", which reads as though both were the last
token's; it now says `max_abs(all positions)`.

### §F2h — step 2a: the swiglu clamp on the routed-expert GPU kernels

The consequence of §F2g is not that F2's ring is wrong — §F2b's O3 proved the
kernel — but that F2 hands ~11 % more of the model's routed calls to a kernel
that has been missing GLM-5.3's clamp since §G13. So the clamp is fixed first.

**What was reproduced, and from where.** `c/glm53.c`'s `swiglu_clamped` and the
two fused copies inside `mlp3_cpu`:

```
g = gate > limit ? limit : gate                        one-sided, ceiling only
u = up < -limit ? -limit : (up > limit ? limit : up)   two-sided
out = (g / (1 + exp(-g))) * u                          siluf_(g) * u
```

transcribed into `qmatmul_gate_up.comp` and `qmatmul_gate_up_tile.comp` with
the same ternaries (`min`/`clamp` would agree on every finite input and are not
what the CPU executes). `limit` is a seventh push constant that exists only in
the clamped variant.

**Why "off" is a fact and not a promise.** The clamped kernels are a SECOND
SPIR-V module — the same `.comp` compiled a second time with `-DSWIGLU_CLAMP`
— on a SECOND pipeline layout (28 push-constant bytes instead of 24). Nothing
is loaded, built or bound until `coli_vk_set_swiglu_limit()` is given a
positive limit. Three consequences, all checked rather than argued:

* the unclamped `.spv` files are **byte-identical** to the ones in the served
  tree (`cmp`: `qmatmul_gate_up.spv`, `qmatmul_gate_up_tile.spv`, `qmatmul.spv`,
  `qmatmul_tile.spv` — all four);
* the expert-group path pushes `sizeof(struct PC)` = 24 bytes out of a `PCL`
  whose first six fields are `PC`'s, in `PC`'s order, so the recorded command
  buffer is the one it always was;
* **`qwen38-vk` is therefore literally unchanged, not merely unaffected.** It
  drives the very same expert-group path and never sets a limit, so it binds
  the same pipeline, the same layout and the same bytes, and loads the same
  SPIR-V. No qwen38-vk oracle run is owed and none was taken; the evidence for
  that claim is the four `cmp` results and the 24-byte push above.

**The kernel was checked before the model was loaded** — a model-free line in
`tools/hot-expert/f2_ring_probe.c` (`F2_CLAMP_CHECK=1`), one minute, gateway
up, no oracle window spent:

| pipeline | non-finite | max·y(unclamped) − y(limit 1e30)· | max·y(unclamped) − y(limit 10)· | max·y· | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| per-row | 0/4 096 | **0** | 2 204.05 | 3 358.25 | PASS |
| tiled | 0/32 768 | **0** | 2 345.96 | 3 646.01 | PASS |

The huge limit reproduces the unclamped kernel exactly (so the second module,
its layout, its seventh push constant and the descriptor binding are all
right); the model's real limit of 10 changes the result substantially (so the
knob is not a no-op). Its first run printed all-zero differences and a `PASS`
would have been meaningless: the probe had been feeding the shaders raw shard
bytes as *scale* planes, the kernel returned NaN, and every `|difference|`
compares false. The check now uses synthetic scales and refuses a non-finite
or all-zero result.

**Cost:** none measurable. Deep packet, clamp off 689.2 s, clamp on 691.5 s
(+0.3 %); shallow 219.5 → 220.0 s.

### §F2i — what the clamp is worth, and F2's KL gate with it on

All at the served tier, frozen histogram, one binary, `GLM53_PREFIX_CKPT=0`,
chain tag `f209191129`, rc=0, `accept_live` PASS.

**O1′ (hard gate, re-proven on the new binary):** `COLI_PREFILL_STREAM` and
`GLM53_VK_SWIGLU_CLAMP` both unset → `GLM53_LOGIT_DUMP_ALL` **bit-identical**
to the served pristine's dumps at 6 327 **and** 2 061 tokens (`cmp`). Every
reuse below rests on that.

**The clamp's own value**, same prompt, same reference (the CLAMPED all-CPU
path, `GLM53_EXPERTS_CPU=1`), so the only thing that moves is whether the GPU
clamps:

| | mean KL | top-1 |
|---|---:|---:|
| **before** — today's engine, unclamped GPU + clamped CPU | 0.0232556 | **91.95 %** (1 895/2 061) |
| **after** — clamped GPU + clamped CPU (= C1) | **0.00142941** | **98.84 %** (2 037/2 061) |

16× on mean KL, and the placement-dependence §G13 named falls from 8.05 % of
argmaxes to 1.16 %. The residual 1.16 % is float summation order between the
AVX2 row kernel and the subgroup reduction and no clamp can remove it.

**C1 fails the 99 % top-1 bar at 98.84 %, and the bar is the wrong shape for
it.** C1's two sides differ in the placement of ~89 % of the routed calls (the
tier-resident ones, GPU vs CPU); O3's two sides differed in the placement of
100 % vs 100 % and agreed on 2 061/2 061. Worth stating plainly: **the SERVED
engine fails that same bar against that same reference, at 91.95 %** — so a
line that compares a mixed placement against an all-CPU one cannot gate
anything. C2 is the like-for-like line and it is F2's gate.

**C2 — F2's KL gate. Clamp on BOTH sides; streaming on vs off, chunk
unchanged. This is exactly and only what F2 does:**

| | mean KL | max KL | top-1 | last cos | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **C2** clamp+stream@128 vs clamp, deep | **3.48383e-05** | 0.0218217 @1690 | **99.89 %** (6 320/6 327) | 0.999998894 | **MEETS THE BAR** |
| C3 clamp+stream@512 vs @128, deep | 0.000367965 | 0.0718822 @4601 | 99.68 % (6 307/6 327) | 0.999949278 | (reported; would also meet) |

Against §F2g's unclamped O5 (mean KL 0.0123284, top-1 94.97 %) the clamp takes
streaming's KL down **354×** and its top-1 from 94.97 % to 99.89 %. The clamp
was the whole of F2's numerics problem, which is what O3 predicted.

**What shipping actually changes, measured against the served binary** (deep,
6 327 positions):

| candidate vs served pristine | mean KL | top-1 |
|---|---:|---:|
| clamp alone | 0.017019 | 93.49 % |
| clamp + stream @128 | 0.0170341 | 93.54 % |
| clamp + stream @512 | 0.016991 | 93.52 % |

**The three are the same number.** Once the clamp is on, streaming and the
chunk add nothing on top of it — stream@128 is even a hair closer to the
pristine than the clamp alone. So the change a user would see is the clamp,
and the clamp is a fix: it moves the GPU toward the CPU path, which is the
definition GLM-5.3 ships. The pristine is the side that disagrees.

### §F2j — step 2c: streaming no longer changes the chunk, and what the chunk is worth

`COLI_PREFILL_STREAM=1` used to raise the effective prefill chunk to 512.
That conflated a placement change with a batching change that predates it in
one env var; it does not any more (`forward_prefill`: the default is 128
whatever the streaming knob says, and `GLM53_PREFILL_CHUNK` is the only thing
that moves it).

**The four cells, ONE chain, ONE binary, back to back, deep packet:**

| | prefill wall | vs off |
|---|---:|---:|
| clamp off, stream off, chunk 128 | 689.2 s | 1.00× |
| clamp on, stream off, chunk 128 | 691.5 s | 1.00× |
| clamp on, **stream on, chunk 128** | **509.6 s** | **1.36×** |
| clamp on, **stream on, chunk 512** | **453.7 s** | **1.52×** |

So chunk 512 is worth **509.6/453.7 = 1.12×** on top of streaming.

**§F2f's "the chunk is worth 3 %" is withdrawn.** That figure compared 466.6 s
from one chain against 451.8 s from another, and this session measured the
run-to-run spread on this exact quantity: two knob-off deep runs whose outputs
are `cmp`-identical took **731.3 s and 689.2 s — 6.1 % apart**. A 3 % figure
taken across chains is inside that; a 12 % figure taken back to back within one
chain is not, but it is still one pair. The honest statement is **the chunk is
worth somewhere between 3 % and 12 % and only the A,B,B,A ladder can pin it.**

**Recommendation, against the prior "serve at 128".** Serve at **512**, and the
reason is not numerics:

* numerics no longer argue for 128. C3 says the chunk costs mean KL 3.7e-04
  and 0.32 % of top-1 on top of clamp+streaming, and §F2i's "vs served
  pristine" rows are identical at 128 and 512 to two decimal places. The 3.24 %
  of argmaxes §F2b attributed to the chunk was measured without the clamp,
  where everything was noisy;
* speed does. Turn 1's 2.0× bar was met at 2.02× with chunk 512 (§F2d) — by
  1 %. Chunk 128 is 12 % slower on the best-controlled pair available, which
  puts turn 1 at ≈1.8× and misses the gate outright;
* and 128 is one env var away for anyone who wants it, with its cost now on
  the record.

If the ladder contradicts this, the ladder wins; it is the instrument, and the
recommendation above rests on single CLI pairs.

### §F2k — why chunk size changes numerics at all (bounded reading, 30 min, no rig)

Two hypotheses killed, one left standing, one experiment named.

**Killed: the indexer.** `coli_sparse_index_select_range` is called once per
chunk with `sequence = seen` = the chunk's END, which looked like a chunk
dependence in the pool partition (`pools = (sequence + pool - 1)/pool`,
`complete[p] = start + pool <= sequence`). It is not. The per-query filter is
`if (!complete[p] || last > q)` with `last = first + (p+1)*pool - 1`: any pool
that passes `last <= q` has `start + pool <= q + 1 <= sequence`, so
`complete[p]` is *implied* and contributes nothing. The tail is built from
`visible`, counted over `[first, q]`. **Every input to the selection is the
query's own position; the selected set is chunk-independent.**

**Killed: the tile threshold.** `vk_tile_ok4` picks the TILED gate_up/down
pipeline for an expert with more than one row and the PER-ROW one for a single
row, keyed on `rows[c]` — and a chunk of 128 gives a cold expert 1 row where a
chunk of 512 gives it 2–6, so the chunk silently switches kernels for the same
(token, expert) pair. Measured directly in `f2_ring_probe.c`: the same expert,
the same row 0 input, through the per-row pipeline and through the tiled one —
`max|y_tiled_row0 − y_perrow_row0| = 0` exactly, on outputs of magnitude 3 646.
**The two kernels agree bit for bit; the threshold is not a numerics change.**

**Standing: the accumulation order into `out[]`.** `union_ids` is built in
first-appearance order over the whole chunk (`c/glm53.c`), so for a token that
is not in the first chunk the order in which its 8 routed contributions are
added depends on which tokens precede it *within its chunk*. Both accumulation
loops inherit it. This is chunk-dependent by construction and is the only
mechanism left that is proven to exist.

**Not examined, and named so nobody assumes it was:** the MLA absorb kernel's
reduction shape, which depends on both `S` (chunk rows) and `T` (chunk end);
and the DOWN projection's own tile threshold (`qmatmul.comp` vs
`qmatmul_tile.comp`), which the probe did not compare.

**The decisive experiment, not run (two CLI runs, ~25 min of gateway):**
chunk 128 vs 512 with `COLI_VK_TILE=0`, which removes every tile threshold at
once. If the two become bit-identical the remaining cause is the tiled down
projection; if they do not, it is the accumulation order or the attention core.
`GLM53_DUMP_INDEX=1` diffed at the two chunks would confirm the indexer
reading empirically — the engine already carries that dump for exactly this
question ("il primo posto da guardare quando il motore diverge solo su certe
lunghezze").

## §F1-STEP0 (2026-09-19): the eg/cpu overlap split — CPU misses are decode's critical path, ceiling −54 ms/token (+29 %) at 18k; the realistic number is unmeasured

`FRANKEN-ENGINE-PLAN-2026-09-15.md` §8.3 item **F1**, step 0 (rev 19's order:
"F1 step 0 (the eg/cpu overlap split) → F1 → F7 → F5"). c/glm53.c's
`ffn_layer` already overlaps the deferred-CPU (non-resident) expert compute
with the resident groups' GPU fence wait (the G9 gap), so `[PROF] eg=`
CONTAINS that CPU time and the earlier profile could not say whether the CPU
misses are on decode's critical path (§RP-F6a: "the two run concurrently and
this profile cannot say how much of `ffn_moe` a vanished CPU path would
return"). This step adds three accumulators inside the SAME window, changing
nothing that is computed: `issue` (the three
`coli_vk_expert_group_issue/issue2/issue3` calls' own wall time), `cpu_in`
(the deferred-CPU call's own contribution to `g_t_cpu`, isolated by reading
it before/after just that call) and `take` (the fence waits left AFTER the
CPU work is already done), plus `windows`/`cpu0_windows`/`take_cpu0` (the
GPU-alone reference: `take` in the windows with zero deferred CPU experts).

Branch `perf/f1-step0-eg-cpu-split`, built in `~/src/colibri-f1s0`, candidate
`e8f8ca3208c9047a` — **timers only, never put in service.** Chain
`f1_step0_chain.sh`, tag `f1s009191720`, rc=0. Phase 1 (oracle): candidate vs
the served pristine `~/bench/glm53.f2` (sha `5c01246cdea888dc`), same serving
env on both sides (`COLI_KDA_GPU=2 GLM53_VK_SWIGLU_CLAMP=1
COLI_PREFILL_STREAM=1 GLM53_PREFILL_CHUNK=512`), `teacher_forcing`
**IDENTICAL**. Phase 2: one ladder arm (no A/B — the oracle already proved
candidate and pristine compute identically), same steps as §F2-LADDER
(1024,1024,2048,4096,8192; gen=128). `accept_live` PASS after the chain, the
served pristine `5c01246cdea888dc` back in place.

### The reading (Fable's, arithmetic checked here and it holds exactly)

At req 8: issue 0.329 s / 3 354 windows = 0.098 ms/window; cpu_in 5.860 s /
3 354 = 1.747 ms/window; take 0.107 s / 3 354 = 0.032 ms/window; take_cpu0
0.041 s / 85 = 0.482 ms/window — the true, unmasked GPU dispatch+compute cost
for one window, since a `cpu0` window calls `take` immediately after `issue`
with nothing to fill the gap. `[PROF] cpu=…(n=10467)`: 10 467 CPU-computed
(token, expert) pairs / 3 354 windows = 3.121 experts/window, 1.747 / 3.121 =
0.560 ms/expert. `cpu_in`/forward: 5.860 s / 80 forwards = 73.3 ms/forward
against a mean forward of 19.474 s / 80 = 243.4 ms/forward — **30.1 %** of the
forward (req 7: 5.203 s / 65 = 80.0 ms of 258.6 ms/forward, 30.9 %). Every one
of these figures matches what was reported before this section was written.

**`take ≈ 0` while `cpu_in ≫ take_cpu0` is the finding, and the reason `take`
collapses is mechanical, not incidental.** In the 97.5 % of windows with a
deferred CPU expert (3 269 of 3 354), the CPU work runs in the G9 gap and,
because it takes far longer (1.747 ms of compute) than the GPU alone needs
(0.482 ms), the GPU fence is already signalled by the time `take` is called —
so `take` reports almost nothing (0.032 ms, blended with the small tail of
windows where it still legitimately waits a little). In the 2.5 % of windows
with nothing deferred (`cpu0_windows`), `take` cannot be masked by anything
and reports the real number, 0.482 ms. **The GPUs are always finished before
the CPU experts: the CPU-computed non-resident experts, not the GPU fence
wait, are decode's critical path in `ffn_moe`.**

Ceiling for F1 (misses free, GPU windows still pay their own 0.48 ms/window):
(`cpu_in` + `take` − `take_cpu0`) × 42 MoE layers/forward = (1.747 + 0.032 −
0.480) × 42 = **54.6 ms/token** — req 8's 243.4 ms/forward would fall to
≈ 188.8 ms/forward, **+29 % decode throughput at 18k.** This is above the
plan's "≤ 45 ms/token" guess for F1: **confirmed in kind, revised upward in
size.**

**This ceiling is not free, and is not this section's number.** An on-demand
streamed miss at batch 1 still has to fill (from host RAM, page-cache or a
ring), submit and compute on a GPU, then read back — 3.12 experts × 14.16 MB
per window is real bandwidth and real per-wave overhead the CPU path does not
pay in this shape. If that comes to ~1.0–1.2 ms/window the gain is still
~25–30 ms/token (~+12 %); at or above today's ~1.75 ms/window CPU cost F1 has
nothing to gain. **That number is unmeasured; it is the falsifier probe
(task B, below), to be run before any F1 engine work.**

**Depth:** `cpu_in`/window is roughly flat across the whole ladder — 1.60 to
2.14 ms/window from ctx 1 287 to 18 669, with no clear trend against depth
(the ~11 % non-resident share does not depend on context length) — but
because the OTHER buckets (`mla.attn`, `mla.index`, `kda`) grow sharply with
depth, `cpu_in`'s SHARE of the forward is much larger at shallow depth than
the 30 % measured here at 18k. F1's ceiling is likely a bigger *percentage*
win at shallow depth even though the CPU cost itself is not growing there.

chain and tag, F2's own 18k ladder gate, read-only, no rig lock held). Turn 4

reused=5239, hit_pct=100.0, majflt=0` in every arm's jsonl row, and preload
residency is identical too (`preload dev2: 1695`, `dev3: 1695`, `dev0:
1248` in all four engine logs) — neither the prompt's new-token count nor the
tier/usage state differed between arms; that is not the explanation for the
turn's decode separating against streaming by 4.5 % (4.528 → 4.316 tok/s,
record §F2-LADDER). That separation is only a ~1.4 s total difference over

a 0.87 s swing; `ffn_moe`: A1 295.744 s vs A2 294.789 s, a 0.95 s swing) — so
no bucket in this table can be credibly assigned to the decode tail's
~10 ms/token move. **Not explained by the logs**: the per-request granularity
available here is a whole ladder-turn window, not a decode-only slice — the
resolution gap this section's eg/cpu split exists to close, on a
decode-only request, once one is profiled with it.

## §F1-PROBE (2026-09-19): batch-1 streamed misses are SLOWER than the CPU path -- F1 as designed is REJECTED

Chain `f1_probe_chain.sh` (Fable launched it; rc=0, gateway down ~5 min, `accept_live` PASS, in service `5c01246cdea888dc` after it; log `~/bench/f1_probe.log`). `f2_ring_probe` with `F1_DECODE_PROBE=1`: per window k random page-cache-resident experts, 8-thread fill into the host-RAM ring, S = 1 row, wall latency from "routing known" to "outputs on host", 2 000 windows per point. Reference: the CPU path today costs **1.747 ms per window at 3.12 experts** (§F1-STEP0).

| split | k | total median (ms) | p90 | mean | fill | submit | compute+readback |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| round-robin, 3 cards | 1 | 1.872 | 2.579 | 4.711 | 1.151 | 0.043 | 0.675 |
| round-robin | 2 | 2.109 | 31.470 | 6.720 | 1.346 | 0.083 | 0.664 |
| round-robin | 3 | **2.699** | 32.477 | 7.062 | 1.647 | 0.124 | 0.910 |
| round-robin | 4 | 3.230 | 31.991 | 7.036 | 1.686 | 0.127 | 1.405 |
| round-robin | 6 | 3.652 | 5.235 | 6.726 | 1.799 | 0.135 | 1.709 |
| all on dev2 | 1 | 1.549 | 1.768 | 1.970 | 0.845 | 0.037 | 0.667 |
| all on dev2 | 2 | 2.151 | 2.793 | 2.902 | 0.934 | 0.039 | 1.173 |
| all on dev2 | 3 | **3.296** | 3.428 | 3.518 | 1.575 | 0.045 | 1.682 |
| all on dev2 | 4 | 3.838 | 4.016 | 4.311 | 1.612 | 0.045 | 2.183 |
| all on dev2 | 6 | 4.972 | 5.412 | 5.436 | 1.729 | 0.051 | 3.190 |

Fits: round-robin `1.497 + 0.380*k` ms, dev2 `0.925 + 0.699*k` ms. **At the decode's own k = 3 the streamed window is 2.70 ms (median; 7.1 mean, with a 30 ms tail on the shared-link cards) against 1.747 ms on the CPU: 1.5x SLOWER, and slower at every k including k = 1.** The cost is structural, not tunable: at one row per expert the GPU still has to pull the expert's whole 14.16 MB across PCIe to use one row of it (0.67 ms per expert on a card), and the fill that precedes it costs another ~1 ms of fixed handshake; in prefill the same bytes are amortised over hundreds of rows, which is why F2 works and this does not. **Decision (Fable): F1 "streamed decode misses" is rejected.** A hybrid (one miss to dev2 while the CPU does the other two) bounds at ~0.2 ms per window = ~8 ms/token = ~3 %, not worth an engine change. The 54.6 ms/token that §F1-STEP0 put on the critical path is still there and still the largest decode bucket; what can reach it is fewer misses or a faster CPU miss (3.12 experts x 14.16 MB in 1.747 ms is ~25 GB/s of weight reads, far under this box's memory bandwidth, so the int4 batch-1 kernel or its threading across the three experts of a window is worth one look -- a Sonnet-sized profiling item, opened as F8, not started). Order now: **F7 design (batched MLA attention core in prefill) -> F7 -> F5; F8 look when the rig is idle; F3 when a model is named.**

`FRANKEN-ENGINE-PLAN-2026-09-15.md` §8.3 item **F7**, design note
`tools/hot-expert/F7-MLA-ATTN-GPU-DESIGN-2026-09-19.md`. Branch
`perf/f7-mla-attn-gpu` (`b538764`), knob **`GLM53_MLA_ATTN_GPU=1`**, off by
default, prefill only (`tokens > 1`), sub-batch `GLM53_MLA_ATTN_SB` (default
128 rows per submit). Pristine `~/bench/glm53.f2` (`5c01246cdea888dc`), the
binary in service. Chains `f7*` in `~/bench/f7_out`, logs `~/bench/f7_probe.log`
and `~/bench/f7_oracle.log`.

**The whole of `_tm2` moves**: score, softmax, weighted pool and the `kvb_v`
value rows become four dispatches on dev0 (`c/shaders/mla_attn_score.comp`,
`_softmax`, `_pool`, `_vproj`, one 8-binding layout), and the o-projection
behind it becomes one `mv_rows_s` submit for the chunk instead of 512 `mv`
submits. The CPU nest is untouched and is the fallback on any Vulkan failure.
The four existing GPU-path `.spv` files and the seven other shaders are
**byte-identical** to the served tree's (`cmp` against `~/src/colibri/c/shaders`;
four new files, nothing changed), so `qwen38-vk` is untouched; all three
engines build.

### Where the latents live, and what it costs in VRAM

Rejected: the decode path's persistent per-layer device mirror
(`coli_vk_kv_ensure`/`coli_vk_kv_row`, which `colibri.c` uses and which is
already skipped when DSA is on). It is 0.41 GB at 18k and 1.47 GB at the
65 536 cap, **per sequence**, times four KV slots. dev0 has **1 447 MiB free
while serving** (card0, measured 2026-09-19 18:30 UTC). Chosen: one shared set
of scratches re-filled per (layer, chunk) call -- nothing per layer, nothing
per slot, and no invalidation to get wrong on a checkpoint restore or a
cancelled prefill. **140 MB of dev0 at 18 439 positions, 236 MB at 65 536**, at
SB = 128. The expert tier caps do not move.

### The contradiction, and why it was not tuned away

The design expected the reordering to be small enough for the bar. It is not,
and it gets worse with depth (98.34 % at 3 013 positions, 97.14 % at 9 115).
**This is the case the plan reserves for a Fable review, so it is written down
rather than tuned.** What the evidence says about the cause:

* It is **not a kernel defect.** The probe's scalar-reference diff is 1.2e-09
  on context values of 2.3e-03 (5e-07 relative) -- gather, dequant, the int4-g64
  scale planes, the head/latent layouts and the softmax structure are all right.
  The first disagreement is at **position 1420 in BOTH packets**, i.e. the same
  deterministic, prompt-driven divergence, not noise.
* It is **score-pass reassociation, and the CPU is the less accurate side.**
  The CPU's `glm_lane_dots` uses the `MLA_MULADD` barrier -- product rounded,
  then added -- sequentially over L = 512, so its own error is about
  512*eps*sum|terms|; with 512 terms that is ~5e-04 relative to the dot. The
  GPU's 32-wide K-tiled `fma` is roughly an order of magnitude tighter. The two
  therefore differ by ~5e-04 on each score before `exp`, which perturbs every
  attention weight by ~0.05 %, in 11 layers, under 45 layers of amplification.
  **Making the GPU more accurate moves it further from the reference, not
  closer**: the bar is measured against a reference whose own fp32 error is the
  dominant term.
* **Size check against the record.** F2's C2 (stream on vs off, both GPU, only
  the ~11 % non-resident experts reassociated) was mean KL 3.48e-05 / top-1
  99.89 %. F2 step 2's placement change against the clamped all-CPU reference
  was mean KL 0.00143 / top-1 98.84 %, and that one shipped. F7 at
  0.00279-0.00538 / 97.14-98.34 % is the largest of the three and the first to
  miss the bar.

**What a review has to decide**, and neither half is this item's to take:
whether a prefill-only kernel that moves top-1 by ~3 % on the *reference's own*
fp32 noise is acceptable at 1.42x, or whether the score pass needs a
higher-precision accumulation **on both sides** (which changes the served
binary's numerics and is a different item). A cheap next measurement that would
settle the attribution is a probe variant with realistic magnitudes -- scores of
O(1-10) rather than the current O(1e-3) -- bounding the score-pass difference
against `glm_lane_dots` directly instead of inferring it.

### The A,B,B,A ladder was deliberately NOT run

The item is blocked on a hard numerics bar, and the serving-regime ladder costs
~45 min of the owner's gateway. The two CLI arms above are a better speed
measurement than the short rung would have been (one binary, identical prompts,
both knob states, deterministic, 9 115 and 3 013 tokens); and decode cannot move
because the knob is unreachable at `tokens == 1`. The full-ladder command is in
the hand-off, ready to launch if the review reopens the item.

### §F7 round 2 (2026-09-20, after Fable's float64 arbitration): the "CPU is the less accurate side" reading above is REFUTED, and so is every defect hypothesis. No defect found; the bar as written cannot be met by a reordered kernel.

**The correction, next to the wrong reading rather than instead of it.** The
paragraph above argues the GPU-vs-CPU gap is "score-pass reassociation in which
the CPU is the LESS accurate side". **That is wrong.** Fable added a float64
reference arm (`GLM53_MLA_ATTN_REF64=1`, `a18847a`: the same score/softmax/pool
nest in `double`, same slots, same order, cast to float only before the
untouched `mv_rows`/`mv` projections) and measured:

| comparison | positions | mean KL | top-1 | first disagreement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| R1 `ref64 \|\| off` shallow | 3 013 | **1.67966e-05** | **100.00 %** | — |
| R2 `ref64 \|\| gpu` shallow | 3 013 | 0.00278644 | 98.34 % | 1 420 |
| R1 `ref64 \|\| off` deep | 9 115 | 0.00320565 | 98.37 % | 3 157 |
| R2 `ref64 \|\| gpu` deep | 9 115 | 0.0055081 | 96.98 % | 1 420 |

The CPU fp32 path **is** the exact arithmetic to 1.7e-05 / 100 % on the shallow
packet. Two things follow that the earlier reading missed: the GPU is ~160x
further from float64 than the CPU is *at shallow*, and at depth even pure fp32
rounding costs 1.6 pt of top-1 (R1 deep) — the sparse selection amplifies, so a
GPU kernel's bar has to be set relative to R1, not in absolute terms.

**Every defect hypothesis was then eliminated by measurement, not by argument.**

| hypothesis | test | result |
|---|---|---|
| the four attention shaders | `f7_attn_probe` **replay** of real engine chunks (`GLM53_MLA_ATTN_DUMP`): real absorbed queries, real latents, real per-row `selected`, real `kvb_v`, vs a float64 core, **all 512 rows x 64 heads x 11 DSA layers**, dense (base 1024, seen 1536) AND sparse (base 2560, seen 3013, used 2049) | **clean.** GPU-vs-CPU ≤ 2.0e-06 relative, p99 ≤ 1.2e-06; GPU-vs-float64 / CPU-vs-float64 ratio **0.80–1.27** across all 11 layers. Per-row causal `used[t] == base+t+1` verified |
| batched o-projection taking P4's tiled kernel | forced the per-row pipeline (`coli_vk_tile_suspend`), re-ran | logits **identical to 6 digits** — the tiled and per-row fmt-4 kernels walk `wi = lane; wi < words; wi += sgsize` and `subgroupAdd` identically, so they are bit-identical per row. Change REVERTED (it cost 21 % on the shallow arm and bought nothing) |
| batched o-projection silently falling back to the CPU int4 kernel (`coli_vk_matmul` returns 0 if its 33.5 MB scratch reserve fails) | explicit call + one-shot warning | never fired: `no (it stayed on the GPU)` |
| the o-projection at all | R4 `gpu \|\| gpu, o per row` (`GLM53_MLA_ATTN_O_PERROW=1`) | **mean KL 0, top-1 100.00 %, maxabs 0** — bit-identical |
| the sub-batch loop / device scratch reuse | R6 `gpu sb=512 \|\| gpu sb=128` | **mean KL 0, top-1 100.00 %, maxabs 0** — bit-identical |
| run-to-run nondeterminism | `off` (19:18) vs `ref64` (20:16), separate runs | agree to 1.7e-05 — noise floor is far below the gap |
| expert placement / streaming differing between arms | startup and `[STREAM]` lines | identical tier (1 296 / 1 695 / 1 695), `cpu_fallback=0` |
| the arms using different packets | md5 of all six `*_shallow_packet.txt` | identical |

**Where the divergence actually is.** A per-position KL profile of the shallow
packet (`tools/hot-expert/f7_klprofile.py`) shows R1 and R2 agreeing to five significant figures
through position 1 259 and R2 then stepping 300x:

| positions | R1 mean KL | R2 mean KL | R2 top-1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0–755 | ~1e-10 | ~1e-10 | 100 % |
| 756–1 259 | 7.0e-06 / 3.9e-05 | 7.0e-06 / 3.9e-05 | 100 % |
| 1 260–1 511 | 7.4e-06 | **0.0022** | 98.02 % |
| 1 512–3 012 | 1.2e-06 … 8.8e-05 | 0.0035 … 0.0060 | 95.6–98.8 % |

At 16-position resolution the onset is **position 1 392** — row 368 of the
512-row chunk at base 1 024, which is not a sub-batch boundary, not a regime
boundary and not a `used` threshold.

**The in-situ dump settles it.** The dump was moved above the GPU early-return
so the KNOB-ON run writes its own `context` for the same chunk, and
`tools/hot-expert/f7_ctxdiff.py` diffs the two runs' contexts per row — which a
replay of the CPU run's inputs cannot do. Per DSA layer of chunk base=1 024,
over all 512 rows:

| DSA layer | p50 | p90 | p99 | max |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 2.92e-07 | 4.05e-07 | 6.17e-07 | 9.43e-07 |
| 1 | 1.03e-06 | 1.78e-06 | 2.59e-06 | 4.68e-06 |
| 2 | **2.04e-06** | 2.99e-04 | 3.45e-03 | 1.58e-02 |
| 3 | 2.70e-06 | 5.97e-04 | 4.54e-03 | 6.16e-02 |
| 5 | 3.83e-06 | 3.48e-02 | 1.23e-01 | 2.07e-01 |
| 10 | 6.18e-06 | 6.89e-02 | 1.26e-01 | 2.36e-01 |

**The median never leaves fp32 level** — 2.9e-07 → 6.2e-06 over eleven DSA
layers, a gentle ~2x per layer. The max jumps 3 400x between layers 1 and 2 and
the p90/p99 follow: the divergence lives entirely in a growing MINORITY of
(row, head) pairs whose softmax is near-degenerate, where a 1e-6 perturbation
flips which slot dominates. That is the same population Fable's own flip-margin
analysis found on the logits (its script lives on the rig, not in this repo) (median ref P(top1) 0.16–0.19, median gap
0.007 shallow / 0.016 deep).

**Conclusion, and why it is not the earlier argument again.** The earlier
reading was an inference from first principles and was wrong. This one is a
measurement: every component of the GPU path is at or better than fp32 parity
with the CPU, in situ, per row, per head, per layer, in both selection regimes,
and the two remaining candidates (the o-projection and the sub-batching) are
provably bit-identical. **No defect exists to fix.**

What remains is a property of the comparison, and it is worth stating plainly:
`ref64 || off` changes only PRECISION (identical summation order, more bits), so
it preserves the ordering of two nearly-equal scores almost perfectly — hence
100 % top-1 at shallow. `ref64 || gpu` changes the summation ORDER, which
perturbs near-ties in random directions at the same RMS error. **A reordered
kernel therefore cannot reach the 99.9 % top-1 that a precision-only reference
change reaches, at any accuracy**; the shallow arm of the proposed acceptance
bar is unmeetable by construction, not by this kernel's fault. The deep arm is
the meaningful one and F7 is close to it already: R2/R1 at depth is
0.0055/0.0032 = **1.7x on mean KL and −1.4 pt on top-1**, against an allowance
of 1.2x and −0.3 pt.

**Speed, current code (the tile-suspend experiment reverted):**

| packet | tokens | knob off | knob on | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| deep | 9 115 | 678.8 s | 479.0 s | **1.417x** |
| shallow | 3 013 | 206.5 s | 131.7 s (sb 128) / 130.1 s (sb 512) | **1.57–1.59x** |

`GLM53_MLA_ATTN_SB=512` is bit-identical to 128 (R6) and slightly cheaper (66
submits instead of 264, GPU 2.445 s against 3.160 s on the shallow arm); it is
not made the default here because no gate has been run on it.

**Open, for Fable:** whether to accept F7 against a depth-relative bar (and what
that bar is), or to require a bit-identical kernel — which means the CPU's
summation order on the GPU, i.e. no tiling, i.e. no F7.

## §F7-VERDICT (2026-09-20): the jitter arm settles the numerics, the full 18k ladder passes, F7 in service

**The numerics, arbitrated (Fable).** Round 1 missed top-1 >= 99 % against the CPU path and argued the CPU was the less accurate side; the float64 reference (`GLM53_MLA_ATTN_REF64=1`) refuted that (`ref64||off` KL 1.68e-05 / 100 % shallow, `ref64||gpu` 0.00279 / 98.34 %). Round 2 found no kernel defect (replay of real dumped inputs at fp32 parity; o-projection and sub-batch variants bit-identical). What remained unexplained was a 160x gap between two fp32-level differences. **`GLM53_MLA_ATTN_JITTER=6e-7`** (oracle only: the CPU core's context multiplied by `1 + eps*r`, r a deterministic hash in [-1,1]; eps chosen so the median |perturbation| equals the GPU kernel's measured layer-1 median row error, 2.9e-07) closes it, shallow packet, 3 013 positions:

| pair | mean KL | top-1 | first disagreement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `ref64 \|\| off` (same order, more bits) | 1.68e-05 | 100.00 % | - |
| `ref64 \|\| gpu` | 0.00279 | 98.34 % | 1420 |
| **`ref64 \|\| jit6e7`** (CPU path + fp32-sized noise) | **0.00263** | **98.17 %** | **1420** |
| `off \|\| jit6e7` | 0.00265 | 98.17 % | 1420 |

**A random fp32-rounding-sized perturbation of the attention core moves this model exactly as far as the GPU kernel does, and starts at the same position.** The float64 arm is close to the CPU path only because the same summation order gives correlated rounding; it is not a yardstick for a reordered kernel. Flipped positions are unsure ones (`~/bench/flip_margin.py`: median reference P(top1) 0.16-0.19, median lead 0.007 shallow / 0.016 deep, no flip above a 0.15 lead). **Decision: F7's numerics are accepted; for a reordered attention kernel on this model the bar is "moves no further than the eps = 6e-7 jitter arm", and top-1 >= 99 % against a reference is withdrawn for this class of change** (at depth even `ref64||off` is 98.37 %). Mean KL stays 5-10x under the 0.0284 bar. O1 (knob off == pristine, bit-identical) holds.

**The ladder** (chain tag `f709200252`, Fable launched it, rc=0, `accept_live` PASS; one binary `e87ae9399a105462`, A = knob off, B = `GLM53_MLA_ATTN_GPU=1`, service env in both, A,B,B,A, steps 1024,1024,2048,4096,8192):

| | A1 | A2 | B1 | B2 | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| TTFT turn 1 (1 287 tok), s | 68.542 | 67.816 | 50.387 | 50.624 | SEPARATED -25.4 % conservative, **1.35x** |

## §F8-STEP0 (2026-09-20): the batch-1 CPU expert's cost is a 64-deep per-group scalar reduction chain, not the FMA itself and not the memory system — fixing it (bit-identical) projects ~30% off the bucket, upper bound

`FRANKEN-ENGINE-PLAN-2026-09-15.md` item **F8**, step 0: a standalone CPU
microbenchmark, no engine change, answering where the 0.560 ms/expert of
§F1-STEP0 (3.12 non-resident experts x 0.560 ms = 1.747 ms/window, 73 ms of
a 243 ms decode token, the largest decode bucket and the one on the
critical path) goes. Branch `perf/f8-step0-cpu-expert-bench`, three rounds
of arbitration on the same branch (commits `a6c586b` -> `a5ca65e` ->
`b984e90`, same sha on the Mac and the rig's `~/src/colibri-f8`), built and
run in `~/src/colibri-f8` on the rig (`gcc -O3 -march=native -fopenmp
-pthread`), `OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 OMP_PLACES=cores OMP_PROC_BIND=close`. Real
GLM-5.3 shapes read from the rig's own `config.json`: hidden=4096,
moe_intermediate_size=2048, gs=64 -> gate/up `[O=2048,I=4096]`, down
`[O=4096,I=2048]`, 14 155 776 B/expert. `tools/hot-expert/f8_cpu_expert_bench.c`
links `c/quant.h` directly, a pool of 350 distinct experts (4.95 GB, past
the 128 MB L3) visited in fixed-seed random order, 3 000 windows, two full
passes per round (`tools/hot-expert/f8_bench_run.sh`, rig lock held,
gateway left running and untouched — `~/glm53_server.log`'s `[req]` count
unchanged across every pass, none CONTAMINATED).

### Task 1: which kernel decode actually runs, and where `GLM53_I4_FAST` reaches

Read of `c/glm53.c`, no rig needed. At nr=1 (decode), `mlp3_cpu_rows`'s
`S4 = 1 & ~3 = 0`, so every output row goes through the tail loop calling
`i4_row_sel(sim3=0, ...)` -> `coli_i4_row` — the exact kernel this bench's
baseline (`mlp3_like`) already used, bit-identical to `mlp3_cpu_rows` at
nr=1 by that function's own comment ("Row r of out is bit-identical to
mlp3_cpu on row r of x") and confirmed here (`max_abs_diff=0.0` against an
independent `matmul_i4_grouped` rebuild, both rounds). **No separate
rows-shaped baseline was needed.** Separately: `mlp3_cpu_rows_ok()`
requires `!i4_fast_on()`, so `GLM53_I4_FAST` never reaches
`cpu_expert_rows`/`mlp3_cpu_rows` at all — when set, `ffn_moe_run_deferred_cpu`'s
`mlp3_cpu_rows_ok()` check fails and it falls to the per-token `mlp3_cpu()`
loop instead, which DOES honour the flag and uses `coli_i4_row_f4`. At
tokens=1 (decode) that fallback is one call per non-resident expert per
step — structurally the same work `cpu_expert_rows` would have done, just
reached by a different branch. **`GLM53_I4_FAST` already exercises
`coli_i4_row_f4` in decode today**, via that fallback path; it is not the
gateway's default and was not designed for nr=1 specifically.

### Three arbitration rounds, same pool/windows/lock discipline

| kind | round | pass1 median ms | pass2 median ms | GB/s (p1/p2) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline, engine-shaped (ms/expert) | 1 | 0.4953–0.4968 | 0.4954–0.4977 | 28.4–28.6 |
| matmul gate/up/down alone (ms) | 1 | 0.160–0.166 | 0.161–0.169 | 28.5–29.5 |
| thread scaling T=1/2/4/8 (ms/expert) | 1 | 3.92–4.02 / 1.93 / 0.97 / 0.494–0.498 | 3.95–4.03 / 1.92–1.94 / 0.968–0.971 / 0.495–0.497 | T8: 28.4–28.6 |
| fork/join 3 teams/window (ms/window) | 1–3 | 1.4858–1.4921 | 1.4862–1.4894 | 28.5–28.6 |
| fork/join 1 team/window (ms/window) | 1–3 | 1.3213–1.3349 | 1.3274–1.3391 | 31.7–32.1 |
| expert-parallel groups 3+3+2 (ms/window) | 1 | 1.6997–1.7106 | 1.7039–1.7119 | 24.6–25.0 |
| bandwidth ceiling, 8-thread full-word touch | 1–2 | 0.5123–0.5197 | 0.5105–0.5189 | 27.2–27.7 |
| f4 (4 acc, hsum/group), 3 / 1 team (ms/window) | 2–3 | 1.3348–1.3388 / 1.3323–1.3396 | 1.3373–1.3383 / 1.3324–1.3333 | ~31.7–31.9 |
| f8 (8 acc, hsum/group), 3 / 1 team (ms/window) | 2–3 | 1.5385–1.5465 / 1.5367–1.5437 | 1.5401–1.5448 / 1.5396–1.5437 | ~27.5–27.6 (WORSE) |
| **gv (4 acc/group, vector combine, hsum once/row), 3 / 1 team (ms/window)** | 3 | **1.1897 / 1.1849** | **1.1937 / 1.1851** | **35.6–35.8** |

Bit-exactness/reassociation checks (checked before any variant is timed,
the way G11's `i4_kernel_bench.c` does it): `mlp3_like` vs. an independent
`matmul_i4_grouped` rebuild and the fused-window vs. 3x-serial baseline
both read `max_abs_diff=0.0` in every round (same `coli_i4_row` calls,
same order — restructuring which OpenMP team a `#pragma omp for` runs
under changes no summation order). Round 3's corrected metric — relative
L2 of the WHOLE expert output vs. the `coli_i4_row` baseline, after the
full 3-stage MLP including the clamped swiglu, not a per-element
max-relative-diff (round 2's own 3.0e-04–4.5e-04 was an artefact of that
metric blowing up on near-zero output dimensions, not a real discrepancy):
**f4 rel_l2 2.83e-07–2.96e-07, f8 2.80e-07–2.87e-07, gv 3.32e-07–3.36e-07**,
max_abs 5.0e-05–6.1e-05 for all three — the same order of magnitude as
record §G14's own figure for f4 (~1e-7), consistent with pure reassociation
noise, not a bug, for all three kernels.

### Reading, round by round

**Round 1** (baseline/thread-scaling/expert-parallel/bandwidth-ceiling):
baseline reproduced §F1-STEP0's 0.560 ms/expert at 0.495–0.498 ms (11–12%
lower — expected direction, no concurrent GPU dispatch, no per-token
routing lookup, a synthetic pool). Thread scaling 1->8 was near-linear
(7.94–7.96x of 8x ideal) and the fork/join fusion (one team per window
instead of three) was bit-identical and ~10% faster. Expert-parallel
(splitting the 8 physical cores into disjoint 3+3+2 groups per expert) was
slower than serial-with-8-threads at every measurement.

**Round 2** (arbitration on round 1's reading): the near-linear thread
scaling was initially read as bandwidth-bound; the alternative hypothesis
was that `coli_i4_row`'s single `__m256 acc` chained through
`_mm256_fmadd_ps` (5-cycle Zen2 FMA latency) is a latency-bound serial
reduction, exactly what record §G14 diagnosed and fixed with
`coli_i4_row_f4` (4 independent accumulators, shipped opt-in as
`GLM53_I4_FAST`, isolated 1.26–1.65x, in-engine 1.095x). Testing `f4` and a
bench-local 8-accumulator extension (`f8`, not a shipped kernel) in the
engine's own structure **refuted this as the dominant effect here**: `f4`
1-team is statistically flat against the fork/join-fixed baseline
(1.332–1.340 vs 1.321–1.337 ms/window) and `f8` is measurably WORSE
(1.537–1.545, ~16%) — once a thread already pipelines ~512 independent
rows (static schedule, 8 threads over 4096 gate+up rows), breaking one
row's internal FMA chain further buys nothing, and `f8`'s extra registers
cost more than they save. The original "bandwidth ceiling" measurement was
also flagged as a possible artefact (a single-accumulator reduction has
the same shape as the FMA-chain worry) and was rewritten to unroll 4
independent partial sums per thread before combining; the number barely
moved (27.2–27.7 GB/s both before and after), which is itself evidence
the ~28–32 GB/s figure across every variant here (matmul-alone, baseline,
f4, the ceiling touch) is a genuine, convergent hardware number for this
box at 8 threads, not an artefact of any one loop's shape.

**Round 3** (the actual mechanism): with `f4`/`f8` refuted, the remaining
suspect was the PER-GROUP tail, not the per-group SIMD body: with gs=64,
`coli_i4_row`/`coli_i4_row_f4` both reduce each group's accumulator to a
scalar via `hsum256` and then chain it into the row total with a scalar
`fmaf(hsum,sc,a)` — a 64-deep serial scalar dependency chain across the
groups of one 4096-wide row, layered on top of the (already-hidden) vector
work. `coli_i4_row_gv` ("group-vector") keeps `f4`'s own bit-trick decode
and 4-accumulator group body UNCHANGED and only changes the end-of-group
combine: the group's scaled partial sum stays a VECTOR
(`fmadd(group_sum, scale_broadcast, tot_k)`), folded into one of two
alternating running vector totals (breaking the group-to-group chain too),
with a single `hsum256` at the very end of the row. **This is the real
lever**: `gv` 1-team is 1.1849–1.1851 ms/window, **11.1–11.5% faster than
the fork/join-fixed baseline** (1.321–1.337) and **20.4–25.8% faster than
today's engine-shaped 3-team baseline** (1.486–1.492) — a materially
larger, and now correctly explained, effect than round 1's fork/join
finding alone. Reassociation is the same order as `f4`'s (rel_l2 ~3.3e-07),
i.e. no worse a change than the one already shipped as `GLM53_I4_FAST`.

### Projected saving, engine-change implication

Both levers are worth stacking: fork/join fusion (one team per window, bit-
identical) plus the `gv` combine (reassociating, ~1e-7-class, same
category as `GLM53_I4_FAST`). At `gv` 1-team = 1.185 ms/window (3
experts) scaled to the real 3.12-expert average (1.185 x 3.12/3 = 1.233
ms/window) against the in-situ reference 1.747 ms/window: **1.417x, ~514
us/window saved x 42 MoE windows/token ~= 21.6 ms/token, ~30% of the 73 ms
CPU-expert decode bucket, ~8.9% of the 243 ms token.** This is quoted as
an UPPER BOUND, not an expected delivered number: record §G14 saw its own
isolated 1.26–1.65x for `f4` attenuate to 1.095x once inside the full
engine (GPU dispatch, routing lookup, cache effects this synthetic pool
does not have), and `gv` has not yet been measured in that setting.

**Engine change implied (not made in this step):** wire `coli_i4_row_gv`'s
combine strategy into the decode-only int4 row kernel path (behind the
existing `GLM53_I4_FAST` knob, since it is the same class of change —
reassociation, not a new format), plus fuse `ffn_moe_run_deferred_cpu`'s
per-expert `#pragma omp parallel` into one team per window (bit-identical,
no knob needed for that half). Judge it exactly like F7: `teacher_forcing`
+ KL vs. knob-off, an A,B,B,A decode ladder, and (new, matching F7's own
lesson about a reordered kernel) a jitter-class arm before trusting any
argmax-agreement number at face value.

**F5/MTP stays deferred.** Its precondition was "a materially cheaper CPU
miss"; this step projects one (upper bound ~30% of the bucket) but has not
delivered it — F5 reopens only once the `gv`+fork/join change is actually
in the engine and measured in situ, not from this isolated projection.

**F8 engine step (2026-09-20, Sonnet): built, not gated.** `coli_i4_row_gv`
moved into `c/quant.h` verbatim; `GLM53_I4_FAST=2` selects it wherever `=1`
selects `coli_i4_row_f4` (`mlp3_cpu`) and, unlike `=1`, does not disable the
decode rows path — `mlp3_cpu_rows`' per-row tail alone (not the 4-row batch
kernel) routes through it. `GLM53_MOE_ONE_TEAM=1` fuses a decode window's
deferred CPU experts into one OpenMP team when every expert qualifies for
the rows path, falling back to today's per-expert loop for the whole window
otherwise. Branch `perf/f8-cpu-expert-gv`, built for all three engines and
checked with a new C test (`tests/test_glm53_f8_moe_fuse`, no model, no
Vulkan) on the rig; the gate chain (`tools/hot-expert/f8_gate_chain.sh`,
oracle + A,B,B,A decode ladder against `~/bench/glm53.f7`) is written but
not launched. No in-engine number yet — that is the next step.

## §F9a (2026-09-20): head-lane SIMD for the DSA indexer's score pass -- bit-identical on the rig, built, not gated

Rev 29 note (Fable): F9 re-scoped -- before any GPU indexer, the CPU score
pass gets the P5.1 head-lane treatment (bit-identical); the GPU version is
reconsidered only on what is left after it. This item is that treatment.
`perf/f9a-index-lanes` (`d52ba9e`, fixed `e7edac4`, bench added `57aa0fd`),
built on the rig at `~/src/colibri-f9a`, `glm53` sha256 `189fd9451c8e1c2e...`.

**The change** (`c/sparse_index.h`): port P5.1's MLA attention pattern
(`glm_transpose`/`glm_lane_dots`, `c/glm53.c`) to the indexer's per-pool
score dot. Per row, transpose the row's queries once to `qT[d][h]`
(`coli_index_transpose`), then for each pool vector compute every head's
dot at once via `coli_index_lane_dots`, heads in the AVX2 lanes (64/32/8-
wide blocks, scalar tail for the remainder), each lane summing over `d` in
ascending order with a plain multiply-then-add -- no scale folded in, no
change to the ReLU/`head_w`/`scale` accumulation over heads, which stays
the untouched scalar loop (its order is part of the score). Applied to
both call sites: `coli_sparse_index_score_row` (decode/few-rows axis,
transpose once per call, one thread per pool) and the rows-parallel branch
of `coli_sparse_index_score_select` (prefill/many-rows axis, transpose
once per row, one thread per row). `GLM53_INDEX_LANES=0` restores the
scalar dot; `GLM53_INDEX_SCALAR=1` (F6a's original single-threaded scan)
never reaches this code, so it implies lanes off regardless.

**What the scalar loop actually compiles to (the item's central check).**
`objdump -d` of this build's own `coli_sparse_index_score_row` (and a
matching standalone probe, `gcc -O3 -march=native -fopenmp`, Ubuntu gcc
15.2.0): the per-head dot is NOT a bare sequential scalar chain. GCC
vectorises the products 8-wide (`vmulps`) but adds the eight results back
into the running accumulator ONE AT A TIME, in strict ascending order
(`vaddss`), never `vfmadd` -- bit-identical to a naive `dot=0; for d:
dot+=a[d]*b[d]` with separate multiply and add. For `dim % 8` left over it
vectorises a further 4-wide block the same (non-fused) way if at least 4
remain, and finally falls to `vfmadd231ss`, ONE ELEMENT AT A TIME, for
whatever is still left -- exactly when `dim % 4 != 0`. GLM-5.3's
`index_head_dim` is 128 (`dim % 4 == 0`), always clear of this;
`coli_sparse_index_lanes_usable(dim)` guards it anyway (falls back to the
scalar dot for any other `dim`) so a future config can't silently drift.
**`#pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT OFF` does nothing on this GCC** (`warning:
ignoring '#pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT'` -- gcc has never implemented it); the
first version of this header used it for the lane kernel's own head-count
tail and a from-scratch per-head recomputation plus AddressSanitizer
caught the resulting FMA drift for a head count not a multiple of 8 (never
hit by the real model's 32 heads, but hit by the unit test's wider
coverage). Fixed with the same empty-asm-barrier trick already in use for
the AVX2 path (`COLI_IDX_MULADD`), applied to a plain scalar multiply
(`COLI_IDX_MULADD_SCALAR`); a standalone probe of the exact tail shape
went from 1 `vfmadd231ss` to 0 once applied.

**Compiler scope.** The bit-identical claim is GCC-specific by
construction (it is about what GCC emits for this exact loop, not a
portable rule). A clang cross-build of the identical source (checked on
the Mac, `clang -target x86_64-apple-macos11 -mavx2 -mfma`) was found,
while writing the unit test, to contract the reference's OWN scalar dot
into FMA in cases GCC does not -- so `coli_sparse_index_lanes_on()`
defaults on only for real GCC with AVX2/FMA (`COLI_INDEX_HEADVEC`, checked
ahead of the default so a GCC build without AVX2/FMA doesn't default on
into the unprotected-by-vectorisation scalar-only case either), same shape
as P5.1's own `COLI_MLA_HEADVEC` gate. `c/Makefile`'s `CC=gcc` is the
engine's only production compiler, so this is not a live gap on this box.

### Microbenchmark (`tools/hot-expert/f9a_index_bench.c`, real dims: heads=32, dim=128, pool=4, topk=2048, 8 threads pinned, two runs)

per-call malloc/transpose overhead is a larger share of a single row's

off and on (`memcmp`), on the same binary, same run.

### Unit test (`c/tests/test_sparse_index_topk.c`, appended after F6a's own 4 000-trial top-k suite)

3 000 `coli_sparse_index_score_row` trials (raw `scores[]` array `memcmp`,
random heads 1-40 mixing multiples of 8 and not, dim 1-24, pools 1-60, a
random causal cutoff) + 2 000 full-pipeline trials via
`coli_sparse_index_select_range` (few-rows and many-rows axes alternating,
random sequence/heads/dim/pool/topk/tail) + 10 structured cases (the dense
regime at 2 051 tokens with and without tail, an exact pool boundary, a
maximally incomplete last pool, the real model shape at a sparse sequence
length, each at both a one-row and an all-rows q-range) -- lanes forced on
vs off via a test-only hook (`coli_sparse_index_lanes_set`, since the env
var is cached once per process and a single test binary needs both arms).
Gated behind `defined(COLI_INDEX_HEADVEC) && defined(__GNUC__) &&
!defined(__clang__)`; prints `SKIPPED` and exits 0 on any other build
(the claim being tested does not hold there by design, see above).

## §F10-STEP0 (2026-09-20): where KDA's 93.3 s (24 % of the 18k turn) goes -- proj is GPU and not the villain, step's dispatch-count doubling is, the CPU recurrence is memory-bound at ~0.5 flops/byte

`FRANKEN-ENGINE-PLAN-2026-09-15.md` item **F10**, step 0: reading plus a
CPU-only microbenchmark, no engine change, no engine run, no Vulkan.
Established starting point (the served binary's own `[OPTIME req=6
ctx=18439]`, tag `f9a09201043` arm B1, not re-measured here): 382 s of
layer time, KDA 93.3 s (24 %), split `proj=40.8 s (0.134 ms/row-layer)
decay=2.9 step=33.9 (0.111 ms) norm=4.1 ko=7.5` over 305 320 rows.

### 1. What `kmv_rows` is, and why it is not the doubling

`kmv_rows` (`c/glm53.c:1181`) is `kda_layer_rows`' stage A: eight calls,
one per projection (`kq, kk, kv, kfa, kb, kga` from `x`; `kfb` from `low`;
`kgb` from `lowg`), each `S` rows at once. Default (`COLI_KDA_CPU` unset)
it calls `mv_rows_s` (`c/glm53.c:963`), which for `fmt` 1/4 and
`g_vk_ready` dispatches through `coli_vk_matmul` (`c/backend_vulkan.c:1019`)
on dev0 -- **this runs on the GPU in the served engine**, not the CPU, for
every KDA projection including `ko`. Shapes (rig `config.json`,
`linear_attn_config`): `kda_heads=64`, `kda_hd=128` -> `kda_proj=8192`,
`hidden=4096`; `kq/kk/kv/kb/kga` are `[8192,4096]`, `kfb/kgb` are
`[8192,128]`, `ko` is `[4096,8192]`, all int4-g64 (`quantize_loaded`,
columns % 64 == 0). Every one of these has `I % 8 == 0`, so
`vk_tile_ok4()` (`c/backend_vulkan.c:415`) selects the **P4c tiled
pipeline**: 8 rows per weight read (`VK_TILE_R`), dispatch
`y = VK_TILES(S) = ceil(S/8)` instead of `y = S` -- weight bandwidth is
amortised over 8 rows regardless of `S`, and the fixed submit+fence cost
(`coli_vk_matmul`'s own comment: ~0.4 ms/call) is amortised over more rows
as `S` grows. **Nothing here predicts a 2x-per-row cost at S=512 vs 128,
and the record does not show one**: §F2-LADDER's chunk-512-vs-128 A/B
(same tier, freed CPU cores in the streamed arm) found `proj`
**cheaper** at the larger chunk (60.58 -> 40.45 s), explicitly attributed
there to CPU contention from the streamed experts, not a chunk effect.
The 8 MB (S=512) vs 2 MB (S=128) upload the item's own hypothesis named is
a real memcpy into `G.x` (`coli_vk_matmul`'s `memcpy(G.x.ptr, x, xb)`,
CPU-side, before the submit) but it is linear in `S` like the GPU work
next to it, so it changes wall time, not the *per-row* rate. **Reading
answers Q1: kmv_rows/proj is not the fixable lever this item is looking
for.** Per this item's own instruction, it is not benchmarked on the CPU
here -- that would time a kernel the engine does not run there. What
would diagnose its cost precisely is a GPU-side chain reusing the
existing `VK_PROF`/`VK_EXT_calibrated_timestamps` instrumentation
(`c/backend_vulkan.c`'s dense-path phase split, already built for the
non-tiled path) at `coli_vk_matmul` called directly with these eight
shapes, `S` in {64,128,256,512}, and again with a 512-row call split into
four 128-row calls to see whether row-blocking alone changes the
per-row memcpy/submit/wait split -- described here, left to a chain
that initialises Vulkan, which this item does not do.

### 2. What bounds the recurrence step, CPU path (`coli_kda_step`, `c/delta_attention.h:85`)

Per token per head: a 3*width-channel short causal conv (SiLU, its own
OpenMP team), then a 128x128 state tile read-modify-written in two
sequential passes (decay+read, then correction+read-out) -- `heads`
independent, one `#pragma omp parallel for` over `head`, threads indexed
by `coli_kda_threads()`/`omp_get_thread_num()` into a per-thread `v_dim`
scratch slice. State per layer: `64*128*128*4 B = 4 MiB`; 34 KDA layers
(G12 spec) = **136 MiB, 6.25 % over this box's 128 MiB L3** -- the cliff
the record already named (`ROME-3x7900XTX-2026-09-04.md`, "A cliff worth
recording", 6.87 vs 12.89/12.93 ms/token, a 47 % spread at
`COLI_KDA_GPU=0`). Arithmetic intensity is low: ~8.39 M FLOPs/call (2
passes x ~4 FLOPs x 128x128x64) against `bytes_per_call = 4 x
state_bytes = 16 777 216 B` (two passes, each a read+write of the whole
[k_dim x v_dim] tile) -- **~0.5 FLOPs/byte, deep in memory-bound
territory** on hardware that needs low double digits of FLOPs/byte to be
compute-bound. This is NOT the path the serving config uses in prefill
(`COLI_KDA_GPU=2` routes stage C through `coli_vk_kda_step_rows` whenever
it succeeds); it is what runs at `COLI_KDA_GPU=0` and as the fallback,
and it is the kernel a CPU-side redesign would start from.

### 3. Microbenchmark: `tools/hot-expert/f10_kda_bench.c` -- CPU only, links `c/delta_attention.h` directly

No engine, no Vulkan, no model weights: synthetic fixed-seed inputs at the
real shapes (`heads=64, k_dim=v_dim=128, kernel=4`), output checked for
finiteness plus a checksum against dead-code elimination. Two modes:
`single` (one layer's 4 MiB state reused across `N=2048` tokens -- the
best case, no inter-layer eviction) and `multilayer` (34 layers' 136 MiB
walked in layer order per token, `N=64` tokens x 34 layers = 2 176 calls
-- the real forward-pass traffic pattern). Thread scaling via
`omp_set_num_threads()`, 1/2/4/8. Per this item's own instruction, part
3(a) (the eight projections) is NOT run here -- see §1: they are GPU work
in the served engine, and timing them on the CPU would not be timing the
code that runs.

Built and run on the rig (`gcc -O3 -march=native -fopenmp -pthread`,
`~/src/colibri-f10` at `c6325e8`), `OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 OMP_PLACES=cores
OMP_PROC_BIND=close` for the env wrapper (the bench itself sets thread
count per row), rig lock held (`f10_bench_step0`), gateway left running
and untouched (`~/glm53_server.log` `[req]` count 16 before and after,
both passes, neither CONTAMINATED). Two passes, same seed offsets:

| mode | threads | ms/token (pass1 / pass2) | GB/s (pass1 / pass2) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| single (4 MiB, resident) | 1 | 0.923 / 0.924 | 18.17 / 18.16 |
| single | 2 | 0.586 / 0.585 | 28.61 / 28.70 |
| single | 4 | 0.403 / 0.393 | 41.66 / 42.70 |
| single | 8 | 0.299 / 0.305 | 56.03 / 55.04 |
| multilayer (136 MiB, 34 layers/token) | 1 | 38.45 / 38.52 | 14.83 / 14.81 |
| multilayer | 2 | 27.96 / 29.12 | 20.40 / 19.59 |
| multilayer | 4 | 22.23 / 25.18 | 25.66 / 22.65 |
| multilayer | 8 | **18.16 / 11.36** | 31.41 / 50.23 |

`single` is deterministic to 3 significant figures across passes and
scales sub-linearly with threads (3.08x at 8x threads: parallel overhead
plus L2/L3 bandwidth sharing across cores' head slices, not the OpenMP
fork/join alone -- two `parallel for` regions per call, 2 048 calls per
row). `multilayer` at 8 threads reproduces the record's cache-cliff
bimodality **independently, in a synthetic bench that never touches the
engine**: an 8.4 s / 38 % spread between two otherwise-identical passes,
same shape as the previously-documented 47 % spread in the live engine at
`COLI_KDA_GPU=0` -- both are the 136 MiB-vs-128-MiB-L3 cliff, and which
side of it a run lands on varies with physical page placement, not with
anything this bench or the engine controls.

### Reading (6 lines)

`proj` (kmv_rows) is GPU work in the served engine (P4c tiled, weight
reads amortised over 8 rows and over `S`) and the record's own
chunk-128-vs-512 data shows it getting *cheaper*, not doubling, at larger
S -- it is not this item's lever and needs no fix. The CPU recurrence
(`step`'s fallback/knob-off kernel) is real but memory-bound at ~0.5
FLOPs/byte, and its only known cliff (136 MiB vs 128 MiB L3) is already
removed by the serving knob (`COLI_KDA_GPU=2`) and is not bit-identically
fixable without a numerics change (bf16 state was already proposed and
rejected as exactly that). **The actual 2.05x-per-token S=512-vs-128
doubling (record §F2f, `coli_vk_kda_step_rows`, ~37.7 s of the 93.3 s KDA
bucket, ~0.15x of F2's headline) lives entirely on the GPU dispatch path
this item was told not to touch**: S sequential 64-workgroup dispatches
serialised by full `VkMemoryBarrier`s in one command buffer, "observed,
not diagnosed" per the record. Fixing it needs a GPU-side chain first
(per-dispatch/barrier timestamps, §1's proposed instrumentation extended
to `coli_vk_kda_step_rows`) to learn whether the cost is barrier drain
latency, dispatch launch overhead, or GPU clock/power-state cycling
between tiny dispatches, before any code changes -- **that diagnosis is
Opus-tier** (it is profiling-and-interpretation work on a new
instrumentation path, CLAUDE.md's own boundary), and whatever fix it
points to (more work per dispatch, fewer barriers, or a genuine
parallel-scan reformulation of the recurrence) is Opus-tier too if it
touches the shader, Sonnet-tier only if it turns out to be a pure
dispatch-count/tiling change reusing a pattern already in this file. F10
step 0's answer is therefore: **not this session's item to fix**; the
next step is the GPU diagnostic chain, not a kernel change.
