## §F11-M0 (2026-09-22): design measurement M0 -- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS under llama.cpp fit, a 32k against a 256k window at the SAME placement: the 256k reservation alone costs 1.6x decode and 2.3x prefill at every depth from 1.5k to 19k; M0b: a step between 128k and 256k; and the 30 % on the host is the per-layer embedding table, not experts -- every expert is resident

**Question (design §4, M0).** What do RAM-resident experts cost on llama.cpp's HIP MoE path, read from a 32k and a 256k window on the same model. **The estimator answered half of it before the run: fit places the SAME tensors at both windows**, so the two arms differ only in what is reserved for the window, not in how many experts are on the host.

**Chain.** `~/bench/f11_fit.sh` (waits for GLM serving and a free lock, then `F11_ONLY=Q F11_SKIP_SWEEP=1 F11_CTX=<ctx> run_chain.sh f11_ladder_chain.sh` for each window, then `accept_live`), chain at `ae00d04`. Tags `f1109220106` (32 768) and `f1109220114` (262 144), two arms of one configuration per window (a repeat, not an A/B), default ladder steps to ~19.5k, `--gen 128 --followups 2`. Both chains rc=0 (01:14:53 and 01:24:52 UTC), `accept_live` PASS at 01:27:57 after the last chain had exited, `glm53` alive. Logs `~/bench/f11_fit_{32768,262144}.log`, rows `~/bench/ctx_ladder_out/f110922{0106,0114}_Q{1,2}.jsonl`. Three earlier launches of this loop were lost to the chain (`--fit-print` given to llama-server, then an unbound variable; commits `65bab5c`, `ae00d04`) and one to the rig lock still held by a `serve_alt` restore; none produced a number.

**`llama-fit-params` (MiB; device, model, context, compute), identical model column at both windows:**

| device | model | context 32k | compute 32k | context 256k | compute 256k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ROCm0 | 21 724 | 227 | 495 | 1 536 | 2 986 |
| ROCm1 | 19 907 | 224 | 619 | 1 533 | 3 118 |
| ROCm2 | 19 590 | 221 | 844 | 1 530 | 3 118 |
| Host | 28 110 | 0 | 209 | 0 | 1 564 |

Weights on the cards 61.2 GiB, on the host 27.5 GiB (30 % of the 93.7 GB file -- see point 2 below: that is the per-layer embedding table, not experts); the 256k window adds ~1.5 GiB of q8_0 KV and ~2.5 GiB of compute buffer per card. Measured VRAM after load: 22.21 / 23.99 / 21.88 GB at 32k, 24.81 / 24.59 / 24.09 GB at 256k (of 25.77 GB per card).

**Decode and prefill per turn (Q1 / Q2 arms):**

| depth (tokens) | 32k: decode tok/s | 32k: ms per prefill token | 256k: decode tok/s | 256k: ms per prefill token | decode ratio |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---:|
| 1 460 | 25.52 / 28.95 | 1.65 / 1.35 | 16.77 / 15.17 | 2.08 / 1.83 | 1.71 |
| 2 839 | 26.83 / 28.21 | 0.78 / 0.64 | 14.12 / 14.88 | 1.01 / 0.89 | 1.90 |
| 5 451 / 5 426 | 27.35 / 27.14 | 0.77 / 0.47 | 17.30 / 15.40 | 0.85 / 0.78 | 1.67 |
| 9 989 / 9 916 | 25.97 / 26.52 | 0.43 / 0.37 | 15.21 / 14.59 | 0.81 / 0.72 | 1.76 |
| 19 488 / 19 415 | 23.46 / 23.14 | 0.39 / 0.34 | 14.72 / 14.99 | 0.89 / 0.82 | 1.57 |
| follow-ups at 19.5k (median of 3) | **23.93 / 24.56** | 0.63-0.70 s a turn | **15.05 / 14.99** | 0.73-0.89 s a turn | **1.62** |

Cold 19.5k prompt (sum of step prefills): 20.8 / 16.7 s at 32k, 35.7 / 32.4 s at 256k. The 256k numbers repeat §F11-STEP0 and §F11-DEPTH (14.4-15.2 at 18-19k) to within their spread.

**What this says.**
1. **Reserving a 256k window costs llama.cpp 1.6-1.9x in decode and 2.1-2.4x in prefill at EVERY depth, including 1.5k.** As first written this point blamed the graph; **M0d (08:09-08:22 UTC, `~/bench/f11_fit5.sh`, chain `af01221` with `-lv 4`, tag `f1109220809`, decode 14.87 / 15.00 tok/s, `accept_live` PASS after) read the cause from llama-server's own fit log:** at 256k the projected use is 26 247 MiB on ROCm0 against 24 560 total ("cannot meet free memory targets on all devices, need to use 5 141 MiB less in total"), so `common_params_fit_impl` moves the MoE tensors of FIVE layers -- 1 on ROCm0, 1 on ROCm1, 3 on ROCm2, overflow types UP/GATE -- to system memory: `CPU_Mapped model buffer size = 3 174 MiB` next to the 644 MiB token embedding and the 27 466 MiB per-layer table; ROCm0/1/2 hold 19 701 / 19 907 / 19 224 MiB of weights, 1 088 + 408 MiB of KV (the second is the sparse-attention indexer's cache), 37 MiB of recurrent state and 1 784-1 789 MiB of compute buffer each; the graph has 8 082 nodes and 22 splits. **The chain's separate `llama-fit-params` print (identical model column at every window) does not reproduce the server's decision and is not to be read as the placement.** So the step between 128k and 256k is: the 256k KV (1.5 GB) plus llama.cpp's 1.8 GB compute buffer plus its 1 GB margin displace ~5 layers of expert gate/up onto the CPU path, and those ~50 CPU expert evaluations a token cost the 26-30 ms that separate 40 ms from 66-70 ms -- **~0.5 ms per CPU-side expert evaluation**, consistent with M0c's 0.6 ms from the margin-3 072 arm. Nothing in the attention graph scales with the allocated window (the agent's read of `get_n_kv()`: used cells padded to 256). For the design: Qwen3.8 at this quant is fully resident at 256k only with a per-card working set of ~1.5 GB KV + well under 1 GB of scratch -- llama.cpp's 1.8 GB scratch and 1 GB margin are what push it over; and a CPU-side expert costs ~0.5 ms against ~0.09 ms to stream the same 2.4 MB over one card's PCIe link (28 GB/s), so the ring, not the CPU, is the right fallback (design §2 row 4).
2. **CORRECTED the same morning, from the GGUF header (pure-python read of the tensor table, no engine): the 27.5 GiB on the host is NOT experts.** `per_layer_token_embd.weight` is [160 x 320 001 536] IQ4_NL = 28.8 GB = 27.47 GiB, a hashed n-gram per-layer-input table that llama.cpp declares `LLM_TENSOR_LAYER_INPUT` (a `GET_ROWS` gather on the CPU input device, `TENSOR_READ_LAZY`, `src/models/qwen4exp.cpp:139`, `src/llama-arch.cpp:902`); it is the whole host column. **Every routed expert of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is on the cards in this configuration**, and the file's name misleads: the routed experts are IQ3_S gate/up (47 of 48 layers; 1 layer IQ4_XS) and IQ4_NL down (43 layers; 5 Q8_0), 3.44 / 4.5 bpw, per expert 2 x 2560 x 640 + 640 x 2560 = 4.9 M weights ~ 2.3-2.5 MB, 512 experts x 48 layers ~ 58-60 GB; the trunk is Q8_0 (~5 GB: attn_qkv/attn_gate, ssm_out, hc_*, shared expert, lm_head Q6_K). The first record of this section (an hour earlier) derived "~24 of 34-40 ms a token is the host read" from "30 % of the experts on the host"; that arithmetic is withdrawn -- there is no miss term in this configuration. **What llama.cpp's 24-29 tok/s therefore measures is the fully resident case:** per token ~480 expert evaluations x ~2.4 MB = ~1.15 GB of expert bytes plus ~5 GB of dense trunk read from VRAM, ~6.2 GB a token over three cards (~2 GB each at 800+ GB/s: ~2.5 ms a card, ~7.5 ms a token if the cards run in sequence) against a measured 34-40 ms -- **llama.cpp is 4-5x off the bandwidth bound with everything resident**, which is the sync/launch/kernel-efficiency gap M1 and M5 measure, not a streaming gap. The design's §1(a) miss term is zero for this model at this quant on three cards; it stays real for DeepSeek-V4-Flash (90.9 GB) and GLM-5.3 (149 GB), which do not fit.
3. The right "llama.cpp on this rig" reference for the design's target table is therefore **~25 tok/s at 32k-128k, 15 at 256k, all experts resident**, not 15 alone; §6's ">= 40 tok/s at 256k" is measured against a reference engine that pays a reservation tax the new engine is designed not to pay.

**M0b (2026-09-22 07:19-07:39 UTC, `~/bench/f11_fit3.sh`, tags in `~/bench/f11_fit_{65536,131072}.log`, both rc=0, `accept_live` PASS 07:39:09): it is a STEP between 128k and 256k, not a slope.** Same placement again (model column identical; 64k adds 411 MiB KV + 0.9-1.0 GiB compute per card, 128k adds 785 MiB + 1.6-1.7 GiB).

| window | VRAM at load, GB (card0/1/2) | decode at 19.5k, median of 3 (Q1 / Q2) | cold 19.5k prompt s (Q1 / Q2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32 768 | 22.21 / 23.99 / 21.88 | 23.93 / 24.56 | 20.8 / 16.7 |
| 65 536 | 22.80 / 24.58 / 22.46 | 23.98 / 23.86 | 23 / 18 |
| 131 072 | 24.44 / 24.59 / 22.00 | 24.11 / 24.35 | 26 / 26 |
| 262 144 | 24.81 / 24.59 / 24.09 | 15.05 / 14.99 | 35.7 / 32.4 |

24 tok/s from 32k through 128k, 15 at 256k. Note the estimator's own sum for card0 at 256k is 21 724 + 1 536 + 2 986 = 26 246 MiB against a 24 576 MiB card, i.e. **llama.cpp's fit over-commits card0 by ~1.6 GiB at 256k and still loads** (the driver evicts to GTT rather than failing), while at 128k the sum is 24 084 MiB and fits. The hypothesis is therefore VRAM over-commit evicted to GTT (host memory read over PCIe), not the window in the graph; **M0c (in flight, `~/bench/f11_fit4.sh`) re-runs 256k at fit margins 1 024 and 3 072 MiB with `mem_info_gtt_used` sampled every 20 s** -- if the 3 072 arm decodes at ~24 and GTT stays flat, the lesson is a per-card VRAM budget with real headroom (design §3.3), not an attention cost.

**M0c (07:46-08:0x UTC, `~/bench/f11_fit4.sh`, logs `~/bench/f11_fit_262144_m{1024,3072}.log`, `~/bench/f11_gtt.log`): the over-commit hypothesis is REFUTED.** Margin 1 024 repeats the step (decode at 19.5k 14.04 / 14.26 tok/s) and `mem_info_gtt_used` stays at 15 MiB on all three cards for the whole run (the ~900 MiB seen between runs is GLM's Vulkan engine); nothing is evicted. Margin 3 072 loads 22.55 / 22.63 / 22.41 GB (2.2 GB less per card, i.e. ~2 700 experts moved to the CPU) and decodes SLOWER, 12.57 / 12.97 tok/s: headroom does not remove the step, and the ~3.7 % of expert evaluations now on the CPU cost ~11 ms a token, i.e. **~0.6 ms per 2.4 MB expert on llama.cpp's CPU path (8 cores, IQ3_S/IQ4_NL) = ~4 GB/s effective**, far under the 22 GB/s RAM read and the 28-61 GB/s PCIe stream -- the number behind the design's "CPU as the last-resort device". The step between 128k and 256k is therefore inside llama.cpp: M0d (point 1 above) read it from the server's fit log -- five layers of expert gate/up moved to the CPU path.

## §M5 (2026-09-22): the launch, sync and P2P floor on gfx1100 under HIP (ROCm 7.14), and a synthetic 48-layer token that runs AT the VRAM bandwidth bound as 240 plain launches -- the design's §1(b)/(c) confirmed

**Harness.** `tools/hot-expert/m1/m5_bench.hip` (worktree `~/src/colibri-m1`, branch `m5-harness`; Sonnet-built to the brief `M1-M5-BRIEF-2026-09-22.md`, one event-device bug fixed by the orchestrator), built with hipcc in `rocm/dev-ubuntu-24.04:7.14.0-full` for gfx1100, run in that image with the cards mapped, under `run_chain.sh ~/bench/m5_chain.sh` (gateway stopped, all three cards empty at 26 MiB, restarted and `accept_live` after). Medians over 10 000 / 2 000 / 5 000 / 200 iterations after warm-up; the raw file with p10/p90 is `~/bench/m5/m5_20260922_083626.txt` (+ `.json`). The Q8_0-class kernels are deliberately plain (scalar int8x4 dot, one workgroup per row, LDS tree reduction; `__builtin_amdgcn_sdot4` does not compile for gfx1100 on this toolchain). Numerics oracle against an fp64 CPU reference of the same block formula: max abs 0.0 on both the GEMV and the MoE step.

| measurement | value |
|---|---|
| `hipLaunchKernel`, empty kernel, async back to back | **2.97 µs** per launch |
| launch + `hipStreamSynchronize` each (a blocking per-op call) | **23.8 µs** |
| the same 2 000 launches as one `hipGraph`: per node / per graph launch | 2.75 µs / 5.51 ms -- **the graph saves 7 %, no more** |
| cross-stream `hipEventRecord` + `hipStreamWaitEvent` ping-pong, one card | 31.2 µs per round trip |
| 10 KB hidden vector card->card, `hipMemcpyPeerAsync` + sync, P2P enabled (all six pairs can and do) | 28.3-32.2 µs |
| the same through pinned host memory (two synchronous copies) | 49.7-57.8 µs |
| P2P bandwidth, 64 MB: 83:00.0<->86:00.0 (the shared-link pair) / 86<->48 / 83<->48 | 19.2 / 15.8 / 23.9 GB/s |
| plain read-reduce over 2 GB on one card (the bandwidth reference) | **800 GB/s** |
| synthetic 48-layer token on one card, 3.84 GB of int8 weights: per layer one 10 240x2 560 GEMV + a 10-of-512-expert MoE step (gate+up one launch, SiLU*up, down one launch, sum) = 5 launches, 240 a token, on one stream, no host sync inside | **4.84 ms = 794 GB/s, as separate launches; 4.69 ms = 820 GB/s as one hipGraph** |

**What this says.**
1. **A whole-token command stream of plain kernels on one card runs at the memory bound.** 240 launches a token cost ~0.7 ms of CPU issue time and are hidden behind the GPU; the token takes what its bytes take. The design's §1(b) ("no per-op host round trips") and §1(c) ("pipeline by layer range, one command stream per card") are confirmed as sufficient conditions on this hardware; a hipGraph is not needed and buys 3 %.
2. **What a sync costs:** 24 µs per blocking call, 31 µs per cross-stream dependency, ~29 µs per pipeline boundary (P2P, sync included). At two boundaries and no other syncs a three-card token pays ~60 µs; Colibri's ~10 blocking calls per layer x 48 layers x 24-31 µs = 12-15 ms is where its trunk time goes (§F3-STEP2A measured 0.25-0.4 ms per call under Vulkan/RADV -- 10x worse than HIP's floor here).
3. **Projection for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, all experts resident (§F11-M0 point 2), from these numbers alone:** ~6.2 GB a token / 800 GB/s = 7.8 ms if the three layer ranges run in sequence, +0.06 ms of boundaries, +attention (M3) -> **~125 tok/s bandwidth-bound at short context**, against llama.cpp's 24-29 (34-40 ms). llama.cpp's gap is therefore NOT the launch floor: its graph has 8 082 nodes and 22 splits (M0d), the splits are host-mediated, the per-layer-embedding gather and five layers' experts (at 256k) run on the CPU, and its expert kernels at N=640 may sit under the bandwidth bound -- M1 separates the last one. Labelled projected; M1 and M3 refine it.
4. P2P between the shared-link pair (83:00.0<->86:00.0) is 19 GB/s and between the other pairs 16-24 GB/s: enough for hidden vectors (10 KB in ~30 µs), not a channel for weights. The host->device stream (28/61 GB/s, §PCIE-STREAM) remains the way to move experts.

## §M1 (2026-09-22): routed-expert kernels head to head on gfx1100, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's real expert shapes -- hipFire 452 GB/s at batch 1 and 826 (the bound) at batch 32; llama.cpp's served `mul_mat_id` path 174 / 271 GB/s

**Harness.** `tools/hot-expert/m1/m1_ggml.cpp` (llama.cpp's HIP backend through the public ggml API: two `ggml_mul_mat_id` for gate/up in the file's IQ3_S, `ggml_swiglu_split`, `ggml_mul_mat_id` down in IQ4_NL, weighted sum -- the ops `build_moe_ffn` emits for this model; 24 graph nodes) and `m1_hipfire.hip` (hipFire's `gemv_mq4g256v2_moe_gate_up_k8_indexed` + SiLU*up + `..._moe_down_k8_indexed_batched_expanded` + combine, kernel sources copied verbatim from `~/src/hipfire` @ 2774aa2 under `hipfire_src/`). One layer's 512 experts resident on one card, `ids[10]` (hipFire: `ids[8]`, its K_TOP is compiled in) on the device, 100 warm-ups, 1 000 timed iterations, host wall per whole step with a device sync (ggml) / hipEvents (hipFire). Run under `run_chain.sh ~/bench/m1_chain.sh` with the cards empty, `accept_live` PASS after; raw `~/bench/m1/m1_20260922_093336.txt`. **The first ggml run (`m1_20260922_090xxx`) printed `maxabs=0, cos=nan`: the harness reused one allocated graph for 1 100 computes and `ggml_gallocr` reclaimed the input leaves' memory after the first, so the timed graph ran on clobbered inputs; fixed with `ggml_set_output` on the inputs (commit `e1829ac`), and the oracle now refuses a zero output.** The numbers below are from the fixed run; the clobbered run's 127 µs is discarded.

| candidate | format, bytes per 10-expert step | batch 1: µs / GB/s | batch 32 (32 independent footprints): µs / GB/s | oracle vs fp32 CPU on the dequantised weights |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| llama.cpp `mul_mat_vec_q_moe` (served path) | IQ3_S gate/up 3.44 bpw + IQ4_NL down, 23.3 MB | **133.9 / 174** | 2 755 / 271 | cos 0.999962, max abs 36 on outputs of ~1e3 |
| hipFire MQ4G256V2 kernels | 4.25 bpw affine, 8 experts, down padded K 640->768 (+20 %), 22.3 MB | **49.3 / 452** | 864 / 826 | cos 1.000000, max abs 8.5e-4 |
| VRAM read bound (§M5) | | 29 µs / 800 | | |

**Candidate 3, same day (L0 step 1; `m1_native.hip`, commit `3e7c435`; raw `~/bench/m1/m1_20260922_123xxx.txt`): hipFire's kernel shape reading the experts in their NATIVE file formats -- IQ3_S gate/up and IQ4_NL down, decode ported bit-exactly from ggml (`iq3s_grid` in constant memory), K_TOP = 10 at runtime, no padding (K = 640 = 20 IQ4_NL blocks), 4 launches a step.** Batch 1: **60.5 µs for the real 23.3 MB = 385 GB/s**; batch 32: 1 542 µs = 484 GB/s; oracle cos 1.000000, max abs 7.3e-4. Against hipFire's candidate that is the same time per step (49.4 µs for 8 experts at 4.25 bpw scales to ~62 µs for 10) with 19 % fewer bytes and **no requantisation**, so the design's format question (§9.3) closes: **L0 keeps the file's IQ3_S/IQ4_NL experts as they are.** The batched path (484 vs hipFire's 822 GB/s at 32 rows) is an open optimisation for prefill, not a decode matter. A bit-exact CPU emulation of the kernel decode against `ggml_get_type_traits()->to_float` (25 600 weights, zero mismatches, a deliberately broken variant fails) is in `m1_native_emul.cpp`.

**What this says.** Per token (48 layers, decode): llama.cpp's expert kernels take ~6.4 ms, the native kernel ~2.9 ms at K_TOP 10, hipFire's ~2.4 ms at K_TOP 8 (~3.0 scaled), the bound is 1.4 ms. hipFire's wave-per-row GEMV with the top-k rank on grid.y is 2.7x llama.cpp's per byte at batch 1 and AT the bound at batch 32; llama.cpp's dedicated MoE mmvq kernel sits at 22 % of the bound on these small experts (N=640 rows, K=2 560) and 34 % at batch 32. **Design §2 row 3 is decided for the kernel shape: hipFire's,** with two ports the design must make: K_TOP as a runtime/grid parameter (Qwen3.8 uses 10), and a group-128 (or 64) variant of the format so the expert down's K=640 needs no padding. The FORMAT question (4.25 bpw affine vs IQ3_S's 3.44 bpw with a table) is a quality question, M5-quality, not a speed one: at the bound the bytes are the cost, and 3.44 bpw reads 19 % fewer bytes than 4.25.

## §L0-STEP1 (2026-09-22): the loader -- 64.9 GB of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next placed on three cards by layer range in 12.8 s, the 28.8 GB gather table in host RAM; the n-gram hash ported and cross-checked

`tools/hot-expert/franken/` (commit `673ff65`): split-GGUF reader on ggml's `gguf.h` (no libllama), the design §9.1 placement (layers 0-15 / 16-31 / 32-47 + lm_head), per-layer per-expert device pointer tables, `hipMalloc`+`hipMemcpy` upload in the file's formats, and the CPU-side PLE gather ported from `qwen4exp.cpp:969-1227` (16 hash heads, `layer_multipliers`, EOS propagation at sequence start) -- re-derived independently in Python from the GGUF's own `ple.*` arrays and identical bit for bit. `--plan` (CPU): trunk 1.76 / 1.05 / 1.57 GB, routed experts 20.09 / 19.50 / 19.92, shared 0.08 x3, hc 0.23 x3, indexer 0.01 x3 = **22.18 / 20.87 / 21.82 GB per card**, 28.80 GB host. `--upload` under `run_chain.sh ~/bench/fl_chain.sh` (cards empty): the same bytes on the cards, **load time 12.76 s** from a warm page cache; `accept_live` PASS after. With 256k KV (1.5 GB) and ≤ 0.3 GB scratch per card the fullest card sits at ~24.0 of 25.77 GB; the ranges can shift a layer off card 0 if L0's scratch needs more.

## §L0-STEP2 (2026-09-22): the one-card decode loop over layers 0-15 runs on the GPU and equals its own CPU graph bit for bit; it matches llama.cpp to the numerical floor through layer 6 and diverges beyond by ROUTING, which llama.cpp's own activation quantisation flips too; first timing 11.7 ms for 16 layers, profiled: launch-bound small kernels and a trunk GEMV at 2.7x its bytes

**What exists** (`tools/hot-expert/franken/decode/`, commits `62b134a`, `be26445`; oracle tool `oracle_dump.cpp`). The layer math is written ONCE (`decode_graph.cpp`) against a backend interface with a CPU implementation (`franken_decode_cpu`, links no HIP) and a GPU one (`franken_decode`, device 0), 35 kernels, zero spills, occupancy 16 waves/SIMD (attention 15), ported op for op from `qwen4exp.cpp` @ 39931761a and `delta-net-base.cpp`/`ops.cpp` for the fused forms. Three facts the port forced that the harnesses had wrong: (1) the UD file is not uniform -- layer 2's gate/up are IQ4_XS and layers 2 and 4's down are Q8_0, so four expert kernels; (2) **the indexer has ONE key head** (`k_proj` [2560,128]) and four rectified query heads summed, so §M3's scan charged 4x the real bytes (the depth term at 256k is ~17 MB a layer, ~22 µs at the bound, not 67 MB / 87 µs); (3) §M3's GDN step predicted from the undecayed state and stored the state transposed -- corrected in the engine (M3's timing stands as a cost model, the engine's kernel is the model's).

**Oracle.** `oracle_dump` runs llama.cpp on the CPU (no GPU, `-ngl 0`) over the ids `248044 785 10945 315 1495 374` with `cb_eval` and writes 1 256 named intermediates (`~/bench/franken/oracle/`). The engine compares every tap it computes. GPU run (`~/bench/franken/step2_gpu_20260922_151551.txt`, cards empty, 21.50 GB placed): `l_last-0` cos 0.999959, `-3` 0.999810, `-6` 0.999390, `-7` 0.998718, `-10` 0.996629, `-15` 0.989552; `ffn_moe_out` ≥ 0.9994 through layer 2, 0.997 at 3-6, then 0.90-0.97. **The GPU equals the CPU graph: `franken_decode_cpu --oracle <the GPU run's dump>` gives 534 of 534 taps cos 1.000000.** The divergence from llama.cpp is the top-10-of-512 router picking a different tenth expert at near-ties (measured: at layer 1 probabilities 0.0606 vs 0.0600), and it is the REFERENCE's quantisation that does it -- llama.cpp's CPU `mul_mat` quantises activations to the weight's `vec_dot_type` before every dot; with that arm reproduced (`--quant-act`) layer 0 is at cos 1.000000 on every tap (bit-identical only on the one tap without a matmul), and a 6e-7 jitter on our own path flips nothing through layer 15 (cos 1.000000), 4e-4 first flips at layer 7 and lands at 0.9993. So the brief's "cos ≥ 0.999 at layer 15" bar cannot be met against a reference with different rounding at every matmul, and is the wrong bar: **the L0 gate stays what design §9.5 says -- greedy text and last-token logits on real prompts -- plus routing compared as a SET per layer (the dump tool gets the expert ids, next).** The engine is the more accurate side of the pair (f32 activations); llama.cpp's HIP backend (q8_1 activations in mmvq) differs from its own CPU backend the same way -- that spread is the honest floor and is measured next.

**Timing (`step2_time_*.txt`, `--time 64 --profile`, box idle, no host sync in the body -- three were removed first: a per-QSA-layer bias upload, the PLE upload inside the layer, `--verbose`'s per-layer id read-back).** **Layers 0-15 on one card: 11.73 ms a token** (12.9 before the geometry fixes), 931 launches, 0 host syncs. Profile (device timeline, each class including the bubble ahead of it): trunk GEMVs 5.89 ms, elementwise/hyper-connection 2.00, QSA (4 layers, ctx 512) 1.17, norms 0.76, expert gate/up 0.56, expert down 0.49, combine 0.14, GDN 0.34, router 0.30, copies 0.10. **Reading:** the experts are at §M1's number (75 µs a layer); the trunk (1.76 GB on this card, 2.2 ms at the bound) is 2.7x off; and ~4 ms is small kernels -- 58 launches a layer at a device floor of ~5-8 µs each, which is what §M5's "launches are free" does NOT cover (it measured launches with enough work behind them). Per token over three cards in sequence this would be ~35 ms = llama.cpp's speed; the way down is fewer, fatter kernels and a trunk GEMV at the bytes -- step 2b, same day.

**Step 2b (commit `c0633eb`, `step2_time_20260922_155520.txt`): 16 layers on one card 11.73 -> 7.62 ms; 931 -> 389 launches; 0 host syncs; GPU still equals the CPU graph (534/534 cos 1.000000 against this run's dump).** What changed: projections that share an activation run as ONE batched GEMV over the concatenated row space with per-matrix format and epilogue (hc down+inject; GDN qkv+gate+beta+alpha; QSA q+k+v+indexer q+k; router+shared-expert gate/up/gate-inp; PLE key+value), scale/SiLU/sigmoid as GEMV epilogues, the conv+gate chain and the QK-norm/IMRoPE/gate group as one kernel each, `hc_combine` producing the next norm, and the top-k not launched when the whole context fits the 2 048 budget (llama.cpp's `ggml_top_k` is the identity there too). "<= 15 launches a layer" was the wrong target: 17 of the 58 were projections and the batch is what collapses them; it is 23 (GDN) / 26 (QSA) now. Profile: trunk GEMVs 4.40 ms, elementwise/hc 0.90, experts 0.56 + 0.50 + 0.15, GDN 0.35, QSA (4 layers) 0.31, router 0.30, norms 0.26. **Per-projection achieved bandwidth (weight bytes over device time):** GDN qkv/gate/beta/alpha 547 MB at 461 GB/s, ssm_out 497, attn_output 493, PLE 484, QSA q/k/v/indexer 434, router+shexp 245, hc_up 199, shexp_down 141, **hc_down+inject 128 GB/s (117 MB in 913 µs: 32 GEMVs of ~3.6 MB a layer, latency-bound)**. The big projections run at 55-60 % of the bound; the trunk's remaining gap is the many small matrices (hc_*, shared expert, router: ~2.2 ms for ~400 MB) that a per-layer launch cannot fill the card with. Extrapolated to three cards in sequence: ~23 ms a token (43 tok/s) at short context, against llama.cpp's 34-40; the next 2x is (a) the small-matrix GEMVs -- one launch spanning several LAYERS is impossible (dependencies), so the fix is split-K to 96 CUs x 8 waves for every matrix under ~10 MB and 16-byte loads where the AoS layout allows (a Q8_0 block pair is 68 B; loading via a 4-byte-aligned base is the open experiment), (b) the 389 launches x ~5 µs floor = ~2 ms, only recoverable by more fusion of the per-layer elementwise (0.9 + 0.26 ms) into the GEMV epilogues, (c) cross-card pipelining does NOT help a single stream (design §3.5).

## §L0-STEP3 (2026-09-22): the whole model on three cards with a 256k allocation -- greedy 12 of 16 tokens identical to llama.cpp, routing 0.92, **22.9 ms a token (43.7 tok/s)** at short context, before any issue-path work

**What runs** (`tools/hot-expert/franken/decode/`, commits `0b82a6f`, `69d669b`, `c265941`, plus `d59adcb`/`6296d5d`/`3388a2f`): layers 0-15 / 16-31 / 32-47 on the three cards, one stream each, the wide residual (`hc_count` x 2 560 f32 = 40 KB) crossing a boundary by `hipMemcpyPeerAsync` on the destination stream behind a source-stream event, no host in the loop; final mixer + Q6_K `lm_head` (248 320 rows) + a device-side two-stage argmax on the last card, one int back per token. Placement 21.50 / 20.87 / 21.82 GB of weights; QSA caches **1.208 GB per card at 262 144 cells (4 layers x 302 MB, 1 152 B/token/layer = 1 088 q8_0 K/V + 64 pooled bf16 indexer key per 4 cells)**, GDN state 40 MB; after scratch **23.08 / 22.45 / 23.40 GB used, 2.67 / 3.30 / 2.35 GB free** -- the design's §9.1 arithmetic to the byte.

**Four bugs between the build and the run, each found in one turn from the failure text:** (1) all three backends' allocations landed on the last card -- HIP's current device is process-wide state and only the constructors set it (OOM at `blk.18`, exactly 24 GB / 1.34 GB a layer); every allocating/launching entry now sets its device and placement is verified per card; (2) the indexer cache kept every raw key in f32 (8x the budget); it now keeps a running block sum + one key; (3) the batched GEMV addressed quantised rows in ELEMENTS for any format other than Q8_0 -- the Q6_K head was the first such tensor and its last rows ran 114 MB past the buffer (a page fault on the head's card); plus an 8x under-sized LDS slice in the same launcher; (4) twice, profiling events created on the wrong device (a raw `hipSetDevice` left the tracker stale; then the fix was lost in a rebase) -- the same rule §M5's harness hit.

**Oracle (llama.cpp on the CPU, temperature 0, the 6-token input `248044 785 10945 315 1495 374`):** reference `271 2064 10054 1040 488 2493 381 3322 264 33466 4299 0 25677 97 271 12189` ("It sounds like you might be having a frustrating moment! 😤 Since ..."); **the engine: identical through position 11, first mismatch at 12 (271 vs 25677)** -- twelve tokens of text the same, on a model whose router flips a near-tied tenth expert under the reference's own quantisation (§L0-STEP2). Routing set overlap per layer on same-input positions: 0.989 at layer 0, 0.83-0.97 through layer 47, mean 0.919 (the CPU path had shown 7 of 16 and 0.909; the GPU path, with f32 everywhere, is closer to the reference than the engine's own CPU arm).

**Timing (`--time 32`, medians over 32 tokens, short context, 256k allocated):** with `--dump`/`--routing` recording inside the timed loop 46.0 ms (their in-body copies stall every card ~1.8x -- never measure with them); with `--profile` 28.38 ms (dev0 12.04, dev1 7.6 + 9.8 waiting, dev2 8.6 + 15.5 waiting: the profile's own event per op costs the first card, whose work is not pre-queued while it waits); **without either: 22.88 ms a token = 43.7 tok/s.** Launches 389 / 382 / 390 per card, host syncs 0, one P2P boundary each. **Against the references: llama.cpp 34-40 ms at the same depth with a 32k-128k window and 66 ms with 256k (§F11-M0); the design's target >= 40 tok/s at 256k is crossed at short context on the first end-to-end run;** the depth ladder to 256k is the next measurement (the attention was measured to add ~2 ms, §M3). **Issue path measured (commit `95275d6`, `step3_256k_issue.txt`): 22.70 ms a token, `issue_ms` = 3.18 ms of host time to enqueue the whole token, 2.74 µs a launch over 1 161 launches = §M5's floor.** The first card was never CPU-bound; the 12 ms was the profiler's event per op (now one per class change) and two routing-log copies a layer (now written by the router kernel). The 22.7 ms is GPU time, ~7.6 ms a card, and the next 2x is the trunk's small matrices and the per-launch device floor (§L0-STEP2).

**First depth point (`step3_depth8k.txt`, 8 192 random ids fed one at a time -- there is no batched prefill yet -- then `--time 32`): 29.28 ms a token, and `issue_ms` = 21.83 ms, 18.6 µs a launch.** Host time per token grows with depth: ~1.5 ms per QSA layer at 8k, i.e. something on the issue path is O(n_kv) per layer (a per-token table or memset sized by the cache), which would be ~50 ms a layer at 256k. **Cause and fix the same evening (commit `5c516e0`):** the top-k's candidate buffers were grown on demand -- `n_kv` grows by one cell a token, so once the cache exceeded the 2 048 budget every QSA layer did `hipFree` + `hipMalloc` twice per token (48 allocator calls a token), and `hipFree` synchronises the device, so the host waited on the queued GPU work of every layer -- which is why the cost grew with depth without any host loop being O(n_kv). Reserved once at construction from `--ctx`. **Re-run at 8k depth: 23.21 ms a token (22.70 at depth 6), `issue_ms` 3.25, 2.77 µs a launch** -- the depth cost from 6 to 8 192 tokens is 0.5 ms, as §M3's attention numbers predict. The batched prefill (the depth ladder needs it: 256k fed token by token is 97 min) is in build.

## §L0-PREFILL (2026-09-22, first run): batched prefill exists -- 8 192 tokens in 61.3 s (7.48 ms a token, 134 tok/s) at chunk 256 on three cards; the chunked path is bit-identical to token-by-token on the CPU arm and on the GPU everywhere except the later QSA layers' attention (cos 0.999995-0.999999); the unified GEMM kernel cost decode 4.3 ms

**What exists** (`decode/`, commits `5baa3f3` T-wide graph + GDN over T + QSA over T, `94d9522` CLI, `53c1644` expert row-gather batching, `284ef42` PREFILL.md; the causal rule with its proof from `qwen4exp.cpp:477-623` and `llama-memory-hybrid-idx.cpp:430-458` is in `decode/PREFILL.md`): the same graph over T token-major rows, weights read once per chunk by `k_gemm_batch` (8 activation columns per weight block), the GDN conv as a history+chunk window and the recurrence walked in order with the state in registers, QSA per query row after the chunk's cache writes, a device-side sort of the T x 10 expert assignments feeding gather variants of the four expert kernels.

**Gates.** CPU arm (`franken_decode_cpu`, 6 tokens, layers 0-47): `--chunk 6`, `4` (4+2) and `5` (5+1) against a `--chunk 1` dump: 1 592 float taps at cos 1.000000 / max abs 0, the 12 top-k selections contained, the same 16 greedy ids -- bit for bit, as the proof claims. **GPU (`~/bench/pf_chain.log`, `~/bench/franken/prefill/chunk6_oracle.txt`): identical on every tap except the attention outputs of QSA layers 23-39 (cos 0.999995-0.999999, max abs 5e-4 to 1.1e-3), and the greedy ids leave the chunk-1 run at position 7** (8008 -- the CPU arm's value -- vs 3322). The T>1 GPU attention reads something the T=1 path does not (the chunk's own K/V or indexer keys from the T-wide scratch rather than the cache after the write is the suspect); being fixed to bit-exact.

**Numbers.** `--time-prefill 8192 --chunk 256`: **61.3 s, 7.48 ms a token, 133.7 tok/s** -- llama.cpp does 0.8-2.0 ms a token on this rig (§F11-STEP0/§F11-DEPTH), the design's target is <= 1 ms; a first implementation, unprofiled (the IQ3_S gather runs at occupancy 7, the QSA stage launches per row, the boundary carries T x 40 KB). **Decode with the new single kernel: 26.98 ms a token (22.70 before)** -- `k_gemm_batch` at T=1 (VGPR 135, occupancy 10) is slower than the one-column kernel it replaced; a T=1 specialisation of the same template restores it. Both fixes landed the same evening (`ab8c9cd`, `f6e6884`):

**Bisection of the chunk-6 divergence (GPU, `~/bench/franken/prefill/{b,c,d,e}.txt`):** chunk-1 against its own dump: identical (the engine is deterministic run to run); chunk-6: first differing taps in layer 1, growing with depth; chunk-6 with `--no-expert-gather`: **zero differing taps -- bit-identical**; LDS staging off on both arms: unchanged. So the entire divergence is the expert row-gather path's summation order (item 5); it is being made order-identical to the per-token expert kernels, or else stays behind a knob.

**Decode restored:** `k_gemm_batch<TILE=1>` (VGPR 58, occupancy 16) for T=1 -- **23.31 ms a token, greedy 12/16 as before**, issue 3.2 ms.

**Prefill profiled (`g.txt`, 8 192 tokens, chunk 256, per prompt token per device):** trunk GEMM 1.69-1.76 ms, experts gate/up 0.31-0.34 + down 0.18-0.22, QSA 0.19, GDN 0.017, everything else < 0.02; launches 20.7 a token; the three cards run in SEQUENCE (device 1 waits 2.5 ms, device 2 4.9 ms per token for the upstream chunk) so 2.56 + 2.43 + 2.39 = 7.4 of the 7.6 ms. Chunk 64 gives the same 7.64 ms. **Reading:** (1) the cards are idle two thirds of the time -- pipelining chunk n+1 on card 0 while chunk n runs on card 1 is legitimate for prefill (design §3.5) and worth ~3x by itself; (2) the trunk GEMM at TILE 8 reads its ~1.7 GB per device 32 times a chunk = 0.27 ms a token at the bound but takes 1.7: it is neither bandwidth- nor compute-bound, it is an inefficient first kernel (scalar int8 decode, occupancy 10) -- a proper LDS-tiled GEMM, and RDNA3's int8 dot instruction if the toolchain exposes it for gfx1100, are the next kernel item; (3) the batched experts cost 0.55 ms a token against ~6 µs at the bound, same story. Ceiling from these three: ~1 ms a token, the design's target.

**Pinned (commit `48360e7`, `~/bench/franken/prefill/gate{0,1,2}.txt`):** with the gather off by default the chunked GPU run is **bit-identical** to token-by-token (STEP2 PASS, greedy 12/16 as decode); the gate/up gather alone is also bit-identical; **the down gather alone is the whole divergence** (IQ4_NL/Q8_0 down: one kernel's summation order, being fixed). Prefill with the gather off: **7.89 ms a token** (7.61 with it) -- the experts are 0.7 of the 2.6 ms a card; the trunk GEMM (1.69 ms a token a card) and the three cards running in sequence are what matter.

## §L0-PREFILL-2 (2026-09-22): chunk pipelining across the three cards and an LDS-tiled trunk GEMM -- prefill 7.7 -> 3.0 -> 1.63 ms a token (8 192 tokens in 13.4 s), the cards 94-100 % busy; the int8-dot GEMM is reachable on gfx1100 but its numerics are wrong and it is no faster

**What changed** (commits `08fc15f`, `9f2fbf0`; `~/bench/pf_chain6.log`, `~/bench/franken/prefill/pl*.txt`, `lds*_gate.txt`). (1) Chunk n+1 starts on card 0 while chunk n runs on card 1: two residual banks per device chosen by chunk parity, a drain event recorded by the destination after the P2P copy and waited on by the source before it reuses the bank (no host call; two banks bound the run-ahead), the pinned staging ring sized to the chunk's 2.6 MB upload (it was 64 KB, so every chunk had been falling through to a blocking `hipMemcpy` that drained card 0's queue), and `step()` enqueues without waiting until the last chunk. (2) A 64x64 LDS-tiled GEMM for T>1 (weights decoded once per 64 columns instead of per 8, `ds_load_b128` inner loop; VGPR 60, LDS 17 KB, occupancy 14) behind `--gemm-lds 1`, and a variant with the activation tile quantised to int8 and RDNA3's dot instruction behind `--gemm-lds 2` -- **`__builtin_amdgcn_sudot4` compiles to `v_dot4_i32_iu8` for gfx1100** (the M5 harness had given up after `sdot4` failed); `k_gemm_batch<1>` for decode is untouched.

| arm (8 192 tokens, chunk 256, three cards) | prefill ms/token | trunk GEMM per card per token | busy fraction per card | numerics vs chunk-1 (bit-exact gate, greedy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pipeline off, batch_tile | 7.70 | 1.62 ms | -- | bit-identical, 12/16 |
| **pipeline on, batch_tile (default)** | **3.00** | 1.62 | 0.94 / 0.97 / 1.00 | **bit-identical, STEP2 PASS, 12/16** |
| pipeline on, `--gemm-lds 1` (f32 LDS tile) | **1.63** | 0.47 | 0.94 / 0.97 / 1.00 | cos 1.000000, max abs 4e-4..2e-3 on Kcur (a summation order), greedy leaves at the layer-7 near-tie (8008) |
| pipeline on, `--gemm-lds 2` (int8 dot4) | 1.65 | 0.48 | same | **wrong**: cos 0.981-0.993, max abs 0.55-0.96 -- a bug in the activation quantisation, not a rounding difference; off |

**What this says.** Prefill is at llama.cpp's rate on this rig (0.8-2.0 ms a token, §F11) and 1.6x the design's <= 1 ms target; the trunk GEMM is now 0.47 of the 1.46 ms a card per token (the bound is 0.03), the batched experts ~0.7 and the per-row QSA 0.19 are the next items. The LDS GEMM changes the summation order (the rule: behind a knob, measured -- here last-bits on the taps and a near-tie flip in the greedy sequence, the same class as llama.cpp's own CPU/GPU spread); which kernel serves is decided with the quality harness at step 4. The int8-dot path is worth fixing only if the f32 tile turns compute-bound later; at T=256 it is not.

## §L0-256K (2026-09-22): THE HEADLINE -- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next at 256k on the Franken engine: a cold 262 000-token prompt in 467 s (7.8 min, 1.78 ms a token), then **decode at 256k depth 26.1 ms a token = 38.4 tok/s**; llama.cpp on the same rig: 17 min and 6 tok/s

**Run** (`~/bench/pf_chain7.log`, `~/bench/franken/prefill/depth256k.txt`; engine at `9f2fbf0` + `48c7860`, three cards, `--ctx 262144 --chunk 256 --gemm-lds 1 --time-prefill 262000 --time 32`, gateway stopped, cards empty, `accept_live` PASS after): 1 024 chunks of 256 synthetic ids, then 32 decoded tokens at depth 262 000-262 032, medians.

| | Franken engine (2026-09-22) | llama.cpp HIP on this rig (§F11-DEPTH, fit, 256k window) | design §6 target (rev 7, projected) |
|---|---|---|---|
| cold 256k prompt | **467 s = 7.8 min** (1.78 ms/token; 1.63 at 8k -- the attention's share grows with depth) | 1 008-1 042 s = 17 min | ~5 min |
| decode at 256k depth | **26.06 ms/token = 38.4 tok/s** | 6.07-6.45 tok/s (155-165 ms) | >= 40 tok/s |
| decode at short depth | 23.3 ms = 42.9 tok/s (depth 6), 23.2 at 8k | 24-29 tok/s at <= 128k window, 15 at 256k | -- |
| host issue per token | 3.2 ms, 2.6 µs a launch | -- | -- |

**What this says.** The depth cost from 6 to 262 000 tokens is 2.8 ms a token -- §M3's measured attention floor (1.7 ms QSA + 0.6 GDN) plus the indexer's growth -- so the design's central claim holds on the real engine: attention at 256k is cheap by construction once the kernels run at the bytes, and the model is fully resident. Decode at 256k is **6.2x llama.cpp** and 4 % under the projected >= 40; the cold prompt is **2.2x llama.cpp** and 1.5x the projected 5 min. Both remaining gaps have named owners: decode's ~7.6 ms a card is the small-matrix trunk GEMVs and the ~390-launch floor (§L0-STEP2), prefill's 1.46 ms a card is the batched experts (0.7) and the per-row QSA loop (0.19) with the trunk GEMM now at 0.47 (§L0-PREFILL-2). Numerics: the served path with `--gemm-lds 1` differs from the token-by-token path in the last bits of the trunk projections (a summation order) -- to be measured with the quality harness at step 4 alongside llama.cpp's own CPU/HIP spread; the default path is bit-identical chunked or not.

**Not yet:** the gateway (step 4: the engine speaks Colibri's engine protocol, `serve_alt.sh franken`, `accept_live`, `accept_ui`), the quality measurement at the served settings, DeepSeek/GLM (L0b/L5: the streamed models).

CONTEXT_EXCEEDED and DONE-before-CANCELLED. ## §L0-QUALITY (2026-09-23): the Franken engine as served against llama.cpp's Qwen3.8 on the same 70 MMLU-Pro questions and the needle set, same reasoning, same budget -- 77.1 % vs 80.0 %, NOT DISTINGUISHABLE (McNemar p = 0.69); needles 8/8 at every depth to 200k on both, the engine 1.2-1.9x faster on them

**Run** (`tools/hot-expert/franken_quality_chain.sh`, `~/bench/franken_quality/`, 02:27-07:43 UTC, GLM restored after, `accept_live` PASS). Both arms through port 8081 with `reasoning_effort=xhigh` sent explicitly (Qwen3.8's template default; the Franken gateway serves the UI with thinking off), `--mmlu-max-tokens 16000`, the 2026-09-21 seed-fixed MMLU-Pro sample (5 per category, 70), the needle corpus at 30k / 60k / 120k / 200k. Arm 1: the Franken engine as served (`FRANKEN_GEMM_LDS=1`, three cards, 262 144 cells, one KV slot) behind Colibri's gateway -- **whose `--max-tokens 4096` cap truncated 10 long-thinking answers, all scored wrong**. Arm 2: llama-server (HIP, fit, 262 144 window) on the same GGUF, no such cap (7 answers over 16 000 tokens, scored wrong).

| | Franken engine (served) | llama.cpp |
|---|---|---|
| MMLU-Pro, 70 items | **54/70 = 77.1 %** (Wilson 66.0-85.4) | 56/70 = 80.0 % (69.2-87.7) |
| paired | both right 52, only Franken 2, only llama.cpp 4, both wrong 12; diff -2.9 pts, McNemar exact p = 0.6875: **NOT DISTINGUISHABLE at n = 70** | |
| truncated / mean completion tokens | 10 (at the gateway's 4 096 cap) / 1 373 | 7 (at 16 000) / 3 058 |
| needles 30k / 60k / 120k / 200k | **8/8 / 8/8 / 8/8 / 8/8**; 58 / 115 / 238 / 411 s | 8/8 / 8/8 / 8/8 / 8/8; 70 / 144 / 359 / 796 s |
| wall for the whole run | 53 min | 4 h 20 min |

**What this says.** The served engine -- native IQ3_S/IQ4_NL experts read by our kernels, the LDS-tiled prefill GEMM with its last-bits order change, f32 everywhere else -- is within llama.cpp's own spread on this sample: the two disagree on 6 of 70 items, 4:2, on a model whose router flips near-ties under any change of rounding (§L0-STEP2), and the earlier three-model run (§F11-QUALITY-1: GLM 80.0, DeepSeek 75.7, Qwen 72.9) sat in the same band. The one systematic handicap in this run is the gateway's 4 096-token reply cap on the Franken arm (10 truncations vs 7); the cap is the serving choice made for GLM on 2026-09-14 and is a knob, not the engine. Long-context retrieval is intact to 200k on the served QSA path (8/8 everywhere) and 1.9x faster than llama.cpp's at 200k. **The L0 quality gate of design §9.5 ("within the measured spread of llama.cpp's IQ3_S/IQ4_NL serving") is met; `FRANKEN_GEMM_LDS=1` stays the serving default.** Not resolved by this sample, by construction: differences under ~10 points; a 210-item run is the next size up if a finer number is ever needed.

## §L0-PERF-1 (2026-09-23): first performance pass after L0 -- prefill 1.63 -> 1.40 ms a token (cold 262k prompt 467 -> 354 s = 5.9 min), decode unchanged at 23.0 / 25.8 ms; the down gather made bit-identical and on; the per-row attention loop batched; the decode GEMV changes verified exact but worth nothing on the clock

**Prefill (commits `b025aac`, `7f33f14`, `64c14cf`, `b8848e8`).** (1) The down gather's divergence was `-ffp-contract=fast` choosing fused vs split multiply-add PER KERNEL by scheduling: the tiled gather kept every term fused, the per-assignment kernel split all but one (ISA op counts: 8 fma_mix / 16 fma / 48 fmac / 0 mul / 48 add against 8 / 0 / 1 / 7 / 13); restructured (scalar accumulators, m-loop outer, unroll disabled) the gather's multiset equals its twin's and the CPU emulation stays exact -- both expert stages gathered by default (mask 3). (2) The QSA stage's query rows batched into a grid axis: 3 launches per layer per chunk instead of 3 per row (~12 000 -> 60 a chunk; the per-row closed forms checked against the old host loop over 7.5 M combinations, 0 mismatches). (3) Tile and shape knobs (`--moe-tile`, `--expert-gather-serial`), each ISA-proven bit-neutral. **Measured (`~/bench/franken/perf1/`, chunk 256, `--gemm-lds 1`): 8 192 tokens 1.404 ms a token (1.63 before); per card per prompt token: trunk GEMM 0.47-0.48, expert gather 0.55-0.60, QSA rows 0.04 (0.19 before), busy 94-100 %. The 262 000-token cold prompt: 353.7 s = 5.9 min, 1.35 ms a token (467 s before; llama.cpp 17 min; design ~5 min).** The chunk-6-vs-chunk-1 gate on the default path: 1 604 taps, cos 1.000000 / max abs 0, STEP2 PASS.

**Decode (commit `c0c6545`, code in `7f33f14`).** Diagnosis from step 2b's numbers: per-projection bandwidth lines up on ONE axis, the contiguous bytes one wave reads, with a ~7 µs floor per launch; `hc_down+inject` was the only split GEMV and read 238 bytes a wave at 50 scattered offsets. Four changes, all T=1 only and ISA-verified fma-for-fma identical: split on the fast grid axis, the split reduce fused into the GEMV (32 launches fewer), the hc collapse folded into the gate GEMV (33 fewer), deeper load bursts. **Measured: decode 23.00 ms a token at short depth (22.7-23.3 before), 25.82 at 262k depth (26.06 before) -- launches 1 198 -> 1 004 per token, no time won.** The oracle pair (knobs off vs on, one binary) is bit-identical, 1 604 taps. The profile explains the null: `prof_gemv_small` (96 launches, 396 MB a card) runs at 97 GB/s on card 0 and 159-163 on cards 1-2 -- the small matrices are floor-bound, and fewer launches at the same floor per launch buys nothing when the remaining ones still each pay ~7 µs plus a short read. The decode agent's own reading stands: the largest lever left is not a kernel but the ~330 dependent dispatches a card (~2.4 ms of ~7.6) -- either a HIP graph of the token body (§M5 measured only 7 % on empty kernels; on real dependent kernels the dispatch gap may differ, to be measured) or genuinely fewer kernels, which needs grid-wide syncs. Card 0 is consistently slower on the small set (97 vs 160 GB/s) and carries the PLE upload; worth a look.

## §L0-PERF-2 (2026-09-23): HIP-graph replay of each card's decode token -- bit-identical, decode 23.0 -> 21.6-22.2 ms at short depth and **24.4 ms = 40.9 tok/s at 256k depth: the design's >= 40 target crossed**; a prefill slowdown on the same binary to be bisected

**What** (commit `79168b3`): `--hip-graph 1` captures each card's per-token layer body (and the head) once per position class and replays it; position, cache length and the QSA grids are device-resident, the boundary P2P stays host-issued between graph launches, prompt chunks stay eager. **Oracle (`~/bench/hg_chain.log`, `~/bench/franken/hg/`):** graph on vs off, one run serialised (`AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3`) and one not: 1 606 taps cos 1.000000 / max abs 0, `greedy_ids exact=1` on all 16 greedy tokens (every one through the graphs), STEP2 PASS. **Decode, A,B,B,A at a 262 144 allocation, short depth:** off 22.96, on 22.18, on 21.60, off 23.00 ms -- **~4-6 % faster**, host issue 2.85 -> 0.04 ms a token (5 launches instead of 1 004). **At 262 000 depth: 24.44 ms a token = 40.9 tok/s** (25.82 before, §L0-PERF-1).

**Card 0's slow small GEMVs (109 vs 163 GB/s)**: the prequeue-gate arm (card 0's stream held until the whole token is queued) did NOT close the gap -- the host-issue hypothesis is refuted; it follows card 0 (the physical card or its position) and stays open.

**Open, found in the same chain:** the 262 000-token prefill on this binary took 430 s (1.64 ms a token) against 354 s (1.35) on the previous one; prompt chunks do not use the graph, so the suspect is one of the parameterised kernels' device-read position or the re-capture guard firing on chunk-sized scratch growth. To be bisected (`--hip-graph 0` on the same binary vs the §L0-PERF-1 binary) before the graph becomes the serving default.

**Bisected the same afternoon (`~/bench/bisect_chain.log`, 32 768-token prefill, chunk 256, `--gemm-lds 1`, A,B,B,A): previous binary 1.202 / 1.228 ms a token, new binary with the graph off 1.212 / 1.221 -- the arms overlap, no regression in the code;** profiled, graph on 1.407 vs previous 1.473 with the same per-class split. The 262k difference (430 vs 354 s) is therefore the environment: `--time-prefill` feeds synthetic ids, so a 262k run gathers ~4 M random rows of the 28.8 GB n-gram table, and the benchmark path does not load it resident as the server does -- whether they come from RAM or NVMe depends on what GLM evicted in between (§PLE-GATHER). Follow-up: `--time-prefill` must load the table resident (FRANKEN_PLE_RESIDENT) so a long-prefill number is comparable run to run.

## §M2 (2026-09-23): expert usage for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash over 32 760 tokens -- DeepSeek is nearly resident-class (60 MB a token missed with 60 GB of experts resident), GLM streams ~1 GB a token; placement by histogram is the lever, token-to-token lookahead is weak

**Tool** `tools/hot-expert/franken/moe_hist.cpp` (commits `67523a9`, `bb4c890`, `ffabd90`): llama.cpp's `ffn_moe_topk` tap captured for every token of a 32 768-token prompt (the record itself as corpus), expert tensors held in host RAM by buffer override (raw libllama has no `--fit`; the first runs OOMed on card 0), trunk split over the three cards. Per layer: coverage of the hottest 5/10/25/50 % of experts, entropy, reuse of a token's experts by the next token and within 4, and -- hot set from the first half, measured on the second half -- the bytes a token must fetch that are not resident under a total expert budget. Raw: `~/bench/m2/{deepseek,glm}{,_b45,_b60}/summary.txt`.

| | DeepSeek-V4-Flash UD-IQ2_M | GLM-5.3-Flash UD-IQ4_XS |
|---|---|---|
| MoE layers x experts, top-k, bytes per expert | 43 x 256, top-6, 7.5 MB (83 GB of experts) | 42 x 288, top-8, 11.7 MB (141 GB of experts) |
| expert bytes a token reads | 1.94 GB | 3.92 GB |
| hottest 25 % cover | 44 % (layers 0-2) ... 70-83 % (later) | 38 % (layers 3-6) ... 60-73 % (later) |
| reused by the next token / within 4 | 30 % / 48 % | 25 % / 42 % |
| **missed bytes a token, 45 GB of experts resident** | **162 MB** (5 883 of 11 008 experts resident) | **1 395 MB** (3 768 of 12 096) |
| **missed bytes a token, 60 GB resident** | **60 MB** (7 884 resident) | **975 MB** (5 050 resident) |

**What this decides.** (1) **DeepSeek-V4-Flash at this quant is effectively a resident model on three cards**: 60 MB a token at 28-61 GB/s is 1-2 ms of stream -- it goes the Qwen3.8 route with a small miss path. (2) **GLM-5.3 streams ~1-1.4 GB a token** even with 45-60 GB of its experts resident: at the 61 GB/s three-card aggregate (§PCIE-STREAM) that is 16-23 ms a token of stream if fully overlapped, i.e. a streaming-bound ~30-45 tok/s ceiling against today's 5 tok/s on Colibri -- the case M4 (three cards streaming at once, the shared-link pair contending) must now measure. (3) **Placement by histogram (L2) is the lever**: later layers are strongly skewed. (4) **Temporal lookahead (L4) is weak**: under half of a token's experts recur within four tokens, so prefetching on reuse hides at most a fraction of the stream; the design's router-prediction lookahead (§3.1) stays an open question for a later measurement. (5) Replication (L3) is worth it only in the skewed layers.

## §M4 (2026-09-23): host->card streaming with all three cards at once, expert-sized pieces -- 28 GB/s a card alone, **36 GB/s for the shared-link pair together (18 each), 52 GB/s for all three**; the design's PCIe budget is 52, not 61, and the lone card should carry the larger stream share

**Harness** `tools/hot-expert/m1/m4_stream.hip` (commit `cbf0430`), pinned host buffers -> VRAM, pieces of 7.5 MB (DeepSeek expert) and 11.7 MB (GLM expert), 1 GB a "token", per-op blocking copies as §PCIE-STREAM measured; copy-correctness check PASS; run under `run_chain.sh ~/bench/m4_chain.sh`, `accept_live` PASS after. Raw `~/bench/m4/m4_*.txt`.

| configuration | per card | aggregate | 1 GB token, p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| any one card alone (83:00.0 / 86:00.0 / 48:00.0) | 27.7-28.0 GB/s | 28 | 35.5-36.0 ms |
| shared-link pair 83+86 together | ~18 each | **36.2** | 54.7-55.4 ms |
| non-shared pair 48+83 | 28 each | 55.9 | 35.6-36.0 ms |
| **all three at once** | 83/86 ~18, 48 ~28 | **52.2** | 57.6-58.4 (pair), 35.6 (lone) |
| all three, two copy streams per card | same | ~same | 56.3 / 58.1 / 35.2 |

Piece size (7.5 vs 11.7 MB) makes no difference. **What this decides:** (1) the three-card stream budget is **52 GB/s**, not the 61 recorded 2026-09-16 (different probe; this one is the expert-sized, all-three case); (2) the shared upstream link caps 83:00.0 + 86:00.0 at 36 together -- the design's §3.3 PCIe-aware assignment is required: the lone card (48:00.0) should take ~44 % of the streamed experts, not a third; (3) a second copy stream buys nothing. **For GLM-5.3 (§M2: ~1.0 GB a token missed at 60 GB resident): ~19 ms a token of stream at 52 GB/s if perfectly spread and overlapped with compute -> a ceiling near 40 tok/s, realistically 25-30.** The compute-under-copy arm reported the read kernel at 11-19 GB/s against its 663-690 baseline -- implausible (the kernel is VRAM-bound and copies do not touch its bandwidth at that scale); the arm's timing is suspect and is NOT recorded as a finding; to be re-measured with event timing when the streamed path is built.

## §L5-DS4-STEP1 (2026-09-24): DeepSeek-V4-Flash on the Franken engine's CPU arm -- layers 0-3 match llama.cpp (173/173 taps, lowest cos 0.99956, expert selections exact on 6 tokens, 533/544 on 136); Qwen3.8 bit-identical after the graph became model-dispatched

**What** (commit `a0cae9f`; `decode/DEEPSEEK4.md` is the architecture write-up): the decode graph dispatches by architecture (qwen4exp byte-identical: 1 592 float taps max abs 0 against the pre-change binary), deepseek4 implemented on the CPU backend: 43 layers -- 0-1 a 128-token raw attention window only, the 21 even layers 2-42 add 4-token compressed rows selected by an indexer (top 512), the 20 odd layers 3-41 add 128-token compressed rows all attended; 64 query heads over one shared K/V head with per-head sinks, four hyper-connection streams, a 128-point Hadamard transform, partial RoPE and its inverse, router: layers 0-2 by token id, then top-6 of 256 plus a shared expert. **KV at 256k: 6 880 B a token = 1.80 GB total, ~0.6 GB a card.** Six new weight decoders, bit-exact against ggml's own on 512 random blocks per format and real rows (0 mismatches): experts IQ2_XXS gate/up (IQ2_S on layer 26), IQ3_XXS down (MXFP4 on layers 26 and 42); trunk Q8_0 + Q5_K/Q6_K/BF16/F32; output Q4_K.

**Oracle** (llama.cpp CPU dump, `oracle_dump --stop-after-layer`, `no_populate.c` so the 85 GB file is not pre-read; `~/bench/franken/ds4gate/`): 6 tokens -- 173/173 taps, lowest cos 0.999575, layer outputs 0.99990-0.99991, all 24 expert selections exact; 136 tokens (exercises the 128-token compressed block and the raw window wrapping) -- 173/173, lowest 0.999558, compressed attention 0.99998, selections 533/544 (the 11 differences all in layer 3, one expert of six each, near-ties presumed, not yet verified). The lowest taps are the routed-expert outputs, consistent with llama.cpp's activation quantisation as on Qwen3.8 (not yet proven for these formats).

**Planned placement:** layers 0-14 / 15-28 / 29-42 on the three cards, ~20 GB of experts resident a card (69-73 %), ~24 GB in pinned host RAM, ~60 MB a token missed (§M2); miss path: a per-layer expert address table pointing to VRAM or to the pinned host copy, read by the same kernel (host-mapped reads over PCIe), and layers 0-2's token-id routing lets their misses be fetched at embed time.

**Next (L5 DeepSeek step 2):** GPU kernels for the six decoders and the DeepSeek-specific ops (sink attention over raw + selected compressed rows; the 64-head indexer scan; compressor pooling; four-stream mix; partial RoPE; Hadamard; the router), gated against this CPU arm's `--dump`; the miss path; batched prefill; the owed checks (head and greedy text on the whole model, a >2 048-token prompt so the top-512 selects, the activation-rounding check).

## §L5-DS4-STEP2 (2026-09-24): DeepSeek-V4-Flash on the three GPUs -- correct (220 taps cos >= 0.9999 against the CPU arm, 16 greedy tokens identical), first timing 91 ms a token = 11.0 tok/s with 262 144 cells allocated (llama.cpp 8 tok/s)

**What** (commit `5102cdb`, `decode/DEEPSEEK4.md` §9; Qwen3.8's 65 GPU kernels instruction-identical before/after): GPU kernels for the six new formats and the DeepSeek ops (sink attention over raw window + compressed rows, 64-head indexer scan -- arithmetic-bound, 48 VGPR after two spilling drafts -- top-512, compressor pooling, four-stream mix with Sinkhorn, partial RoPE, Hadamard, router incl. token-id routing). Placement 0-14 / 15-28 / 29-42 (+ head), ~20 GB of experts resident a card ranked by M2's whole-prompt histogram (2 653 / 2 597 / 2 623 experts), the rest in pinned host RAM read by the same kernels through a per-layer address table; VRAM 22.5-23.4 of 25.75 GB per card at 256k. **Gate (`~/bench/franken/ds4/`, 6 tokens + 16 greedy):** with `--sync-debug` 214 taps and without 220 taps, all cos >= 0.9999 against the CPU arm's dump; greedy `11111 14 305 436 344 834 294 270 1473 12734 11234 295 270 2058 16 983` identical in every run. **Timing: `ds4_decode_ms_median` 91.1 ms = 10.98 tok/s** (depth 53, 262 144 cells). Bytes a token ~2 GB resident + ~36-60 MB missed -> ~10-15 ms at the bandwidth bound: this first cut (byte-load expert GEMVs, host-mapped miss reads on the critical path) is ~6-9x off; profile next. One process slip on the way: the chain's first `make` ran inside a container (the target calls docker itself, error 127) and two runs lacked the wait for the previous process's VRAM to be freed (OOM at start); both fixed in `~/bench/ds4_chain.sh`.

## §L5-DS4-STEP3 (2026-09-24, first run): DeepSeek speed pass -- every path bit-identical (2 036 taps, greedy exact, graph replay exact) but 91 -> 82 ms a token; the profile shows three bugs, not tuning

Commits `c8afc6f`, `1fbb781`, `f5ec74c` (`DEEPSEEK4.md` §10): misses staged into a VRAM ring on a side stream as soon as the router picks (token-id layers 0-2 at embed time), LDS-staged 16-byte loads for expert and K-quant GEMV rows, Sinkhorn on 4 threads with the single thread's order, graph replay. Gate (`~/bench/franken/ds4/step3.txt`): new paths vs step 2's paths 2 036/2 036 bit-identical; CPU oracle PASS; `--hip-graph 1` bit-identical; greedy exact everywhere. **Timing: 82.2 ms a token (12.2 tok/s) at 262 144 cells.** Profile per card per token: **missed expert bytes 742 MB** (298 / 255 / 189) against the placement's 36 MB estimate and M2's 60 MB at 60 GB resident -- the hot-set ranking or its index mapping is wrong; **the four-stream mix 70.4 / 39.4 / 1.3 ms** with ~31-33 k launches and ~1 330-1 400 host syncs per token per card -- host-driven; **indexer scan 18.2 ms on card 0 vs 0.19 on cards 1-2**; trunk GEMVs 10-27 ms a card (probably inflated by the syncs). All sent back to the build with the numbers.

## §L5-DS4-STEP3b (2026-09-24): DeepSeek placement learned on mixed text -- misses 742 -> 276 MB a token, **decode 50.4 ms = 19.8 tok/s at 262 144 cells** (llama.cpp 8); the hot set depends on the kind of text

**Correction to §L5-DS4-STEP3:** the "host-driven mix", card-0 indexer and head costs were PROFILER artifacts (the 8 192-event pool overflowed during warm-up and the last class absorbed it; idle and upstream-wait time was charged to real classes; launch counts were totals since start) -- fixed in `79b94a1`, not engine bugs. The step-3 speed run had printed: 71.7 / 69.7 / 69.5 / 71.4 ms (graph off/on/on/off). **The 742 MB of misses was real and is a finding about placement:** M2's histogram came from the rig's technical record; measured with `--hit-report`, that hot set hits exactly as predicted on its own corpus (layer 3: 0.827 vs 0.836) and no better than random on prose (layer 4: 0.364 vs a random 0.348). **Which experts are hot depends on the domain of the text.**

**Short-term fix, run the same night:** histogram rebuilt on a mixed corpus (the 70 MMLU-Pro questions -- law, history, psychology, economics, maths, ... -- plus the technical record), `~/bench/m2/deepseek_mix/`, 60 GB budget; gate `~/bench/franken/ds4/step3b.txt`. Bit-identity, CPU oracle and graph replay all PASS (not_bitexact=0). **Misses on the gate's text: 276 MB a token** (742 before); per-layer measured hit 0.62-0.98 against predicted 0.90-0.98 (the gap is the domain again, smaller). **Decode, A,B,B,A at 262 144 cells: 52.50 / 50.50 / 50.38 / 52.65 ms -- 19.8 tok/s with graph replay** (82 -> 50 ms). Profile per card per token: L0 trunk GEMV 7.3-11.8 ms (~180 GB/s: DeepSeek's short 1 088-byte rows are this kernel's slow case -- shared with Qwen3.8), K-quant trunk 1.2-2.1 ms, the cards otherwise waiting upstream (single stream: expected).

**Next:** (1) adaptive placement -- learn the hot set online from the engine's own routing (EMA counts) and swap experts in the background (design L2); a fixed histogram cannot fit every domain. (2) The trunk GEMV on short rows (gated for both models). Projection with both: ~25-30 ms a token.

## §L5-DS4-ADAPT (2026-09-24): adaptive expert placement on DeepSeek -- bit-identical with swaps every round; over 8 448 prose tokens starting from the wrong (technical) placement, misses 474 -> 101 MB a token, hit rate 71-81 % -> 93-96 %

**What** (commit `bc946e2`, `decode/DEEPSEEK4.md` §12): the router kernel counts per layer which experts it picks and how many miss (no host sync); every 16 tokens each card reads its counters back asynchronously, keeps a decayed average (half-life 2 048 tokens), and swaps the hottest non-resident experts in for the coldest resident ones -- evict (table entry -> host copy), copy host->VRAM on a lowest-priority stream fenced behind the evictions, install only after a device-side wait on the copy's event -- capped at 64 MB a token a card, one batch in flight a card. Every expert keeps a pinned host copy (~84 GB pinned; fits with the gateway stopped).

**Gate (`~/bench/franken/ds4/step4.txt`):** adaptation on vs off, swaps every round at 512 MB a token: 6-token text + 16 greedy, eager and with graph replay, and 64 prose tokens -- every tap cos 1 / max abs 0 (2 014 taps), greedy ids exact, 250-500 swaps, `adapt_verify` 0 bad entries / 0 bad bytes on every card. **Trajectory, 8 448 prose tokens (MMLU-Pro text) from the technical-record placement, 262 144 cells, graph replay:** control (counters on, no swaps) hit 0.71 / 0.76 / 0.81 per card, **474 MB a token missed** (196 / 156 / 122); adaptive (64 MB a token a card) **hit 0.93 / 0.96 / 0.96, 101 MB a token missed** (47 / 28 / 26), 6 691 swaps, 51 GB moved over the run; the per-64-token trace falls from 666 MB at the first token to ~34-80 MB after ~2k tokens, with bumps where the text changes subject. **Decode at depth 8 479: 102.3 ms control, 88.8 ms adaptive** (the swap traffic is included).

**What this says.** Placement can learn the conversation's domain on the fly, without changing a bit of output -- the design's L2 in its adaptive form works. The absolute decode at 8.5k depth (89-102 ms) is well above the 50 ms at depth 53 (§L5-DS4-STEP3b): the depth cost of DeepSeek's attention/indexer path on this first-cut kernel set is the next thing to profile (Qwen3.8's attention added 2.8 ms from 6 to 262k tokens; DeepSeek's apparently ~40 ms by 8k), together with the trunk GEMV on short rows. DeepSeek also has no batched prefill yet (the 8k prompt went token by token).

## §L5-DS4-STEP5 (2026-09-24): DeepSeek batched prefill and the depth probe -- **no depth cost** (47.2 ms at depth 64, 47.7 at 8 192, 48.1 at 32 800: 21 tok/s); the 89-102 ms of §L5-DS4-ADAPT was the wrong placement, not depth; prefill 5.6-5.7 ms a token, 4.0 with the LDS GEMM

**What** (commit `d9310dc`, `DEEPSEEK4.md` §13): batched prefill (`--chunk`, rings sized for the chunk, one kernel per op so a chunk row equals the decode step, expert-major gather, two-bank pipelining across cards, `--time-prefill`); the indexer scan (four keys per lane group), top-512 (per-wave histogram, ordered output -- the one intended change: the old order came from an atomic and varied run to run past 2 048 tokens; the set is identical) and attention reworked to scale to 256k; `--probe-at D1,D2,..` times decode at several depths in one process. **Gates (`~/bench/franken/ds4/step5.txt`), all bit-identical (2 014 taps, not_bitexact=0):** decode against the previous binary, eager and graph; chunk 6 vs 1 (gather on and off); 136 tokens at chunks 7 / 32 / 128 and unpipelined; **2 200 prose tokens at chunk 256 vs 1, eager and graph -- the first GPU check with the top-512 actually selecting.**

**Depth probe** (mixed-corpus placement, 20 GB of experts a card, 262 144 cells, 32 tokens a depth): graph replay **47.2 / 47.7 / 47.3 ms at depth 64 / 8 192 / 64** (eager 48.8 / 49.5 / 49.2); **with the technical-record placement of step 4: 104.8 / 101.8 / 104.7 ms at the same depths.** So there is no depth cost: the step-4 slowdown was the placement's misses at every depth, and my rev-70 reading ("DeepSeek's decode grows with depth") was wrong -- corrected here. **Decode at 8 224 and 32 800 depth after a batched prefill: 47.6 and 48.1 ms = 21.0 / 20.8 tok/s.**

**Prefill (MMLU prose, 262 144 cells, chunk 256):** 8 192 tokens 5.72 ms a token (175 tok/s), 32 768 tokens 5.59 ms; chunk 512 5.94; **`--gemm-lds 1` (summation-order change, off by default) 3.98 ms a token (251 tok/s)**; expert gather off 7.58. llama.cpp on this model: 97 s for an 18-19k prompt (~5.2 ms a token, §F11-STEP0). The limit is reading the ~24 GB of non-resident experts over PCIe once a chunk.

## §L5-DS4-SERVE (2026-09-24): DeepSeek-V4-Flash on the Franken engine behind the owner's gateway -- `accept_live` PASS (twice)

Commit `4b7220f` (`ds4_serve.cpp`, `start_franken_ds4.sh`, `serve_alt.sh franken-ds4`; checkpoint split: raw-window and open compressor/indexer rings recurrent, closed blocks positional). CPU conformance 26/26. Served (`~/bench/serve_alt_franken_ds4.log`): **new chat B reused 4 608 of 4 653 tokens, ttft 0.91 / 0.96 s; follow-up 0.8 s; 399-443-token replies finish; a request behind an abandoned one 0.5 s; cold 4.6k tool block 21 s.** The browser half of `accept_ui` could not run: the Mac's bundled Chromium gets ERR_ADDRESS_UNREACHABLE for the rig while `curl` reaches it -- a macOS Local Network permission lost at the owner's re-login, not the engine. Quality comparison against llama.cpp's DeepSeek running (`~/bench/franken_quality/chain_ds4.log`).

**Browser path:** the Mac-side Chromium could not reach the LAN because this Claude session was (re)started over SSH inside `screen` -- macOS Local Network privacy has no app to attribute the browser to, blocks the LAN for non-Apple binaries (the internet works: example.com 200) while Apple's `curl`/`ssh` are exempt; the same restart explains the keychain `-25308` and the minimal PATH. Workaround with no permission needed: `ssh -f -N -L 13000:127.0.0.1:3000 rome` and `accept_ui.sh --url http://127.0.0.1:13000` (loopback is not subject to Local Network privacy). **A run through it at 06:50 UTC is INVALID and not recorded as a number:** it overlapped the DeepSeek quality run on the same single-slot engine (first browser chat queued 147 s behind a quality request, the quality prompts evicted the prefix, reused=0) -- the orchestrator broke its own one-benchmark-at-a-time rule. The on-screen number is re-taken on an idle engine.

**Quality (2026-09-24/25, `~/bench/franken_quality/{franken_ds4,deepseek_llama}.jsonl`; same 70 MMLU-Pro items and needles, reasoning xhigh, 16k budget, both through port 8081; the Franken arm with the 16 384 reply cap):** Franken 53/70 = 75.7 % (Wilson 64.5-84.2), llama.cpp 58/70 = 82.9 % (72.4-89.9); paired: both right 51, only llama.cpp 7, only Franken 2, both wrong 10; McNemar p = 0.18 -- **NOT DISTINGUISHABLE at n = 70.** But the gap has a specific shape that is a defect, not noise: **6 of the 7 items only llama.cpp got right are Franken answers that ran to the 16 000-token budget without stopping** (llama.cpp finished the same items in 613-14 166 tokens), 11 truncations against llama.cpp's 4; where both finished, lengths match (median 349 vs 396 tokens). So ~9 % of hard questions send the Franken DeepSeek into a generation that does not end -- a repetition loop, a missed end-of-turn/stop id, or a numerics drift that the reasoning never recovers from. To reproduce on one item (mmlu:570: Franken 16 000 tokens, llama.cpp 613) and read the tail of the output before anything else on DeepSeek.

**Reproduced (01:16-01:34 UTC, `~/bench/franken_quality/repro570/out.json`, `~/bench/repro570.sh`):** same prompt, temperature 0, xhigh: again 16 000 completion tokens, 65 780 characters of reasoning, no content -- a **verbatim three-sentence repetition loop** (the model "recalling" a marketing-textbook passage, cycling the same sentences to the budget). Greedy decoding loops on any engine sometimes (llama.cpp: 4 truncations in the run); Franken loops ~3x as often, so its greedy trajectory leaves llama.cpp's somewhere earlier. Next: llama.cpp's greedy token ids for this prompt, teacher-forced through the Franken engine, reporting the first position where the argmax differs and the logit margin there -- a near-tie (chance; normal sampling makes it rare) or a clear gap (a kernel bug).

**First-divergence result (02:04-02:25 UTC; `tools/hot-expert/greedy_ids.py` colibri `17b9d9b`, `--teacher-force` franken-engine `5a001b2`; `~/bench/franken/ds4/greedy_570.json`, `tf_570.txt`; synchronised and plain runs identical): NEAR-TIES, NOT A KERNEL BUG.** llama.cpp's own greedy continuation of this prompt (raw /completion, top-5 logprobs a step) did not finish within 1 024 tokens either. Teacher-forced along it, the Franken engine's argmax differs at **24 of 1 024 steps (2.3 %), every one a near-tie in both engines**: Franken's logit margin 0.001-0.51 (median ~0.13), llama.cpp's logprob margin for the same pair 0.01-1.05 (median ~0.13); first split at step 41 (Franken +0.11 for its token, llama.cpp +0.70 for the other). Same signature as Qwen3.8 (§L0-STEP2): llama.cpp quantises activations to 8 bits before every matmul, the Franken engine keeps f32; near-ties fall differently, the trajectories then separate, and whether a greedy trajectory drifts into a loop is chance. The quality verdict stands (not distinguishable, p = 0.18). Consequence for serving: loops are a greedy-decoding property -- the gateway should sample DeepSeek with its normal settings, not temperature 0; the quality harness keeps temperature 0 for comparability and its truncation counts carry this caveat.

**Browser acceptance on an idle engine (2026-09-25 04:50 UTC).** `accept_ui.sh` through an ssh tunnel to Open WebUI, DeepSeek-V4-Flash on the Franken engine behind the gateway, nothing else running: two new chats answered correctly ("Wednesday.", "11"), first token ON SCREEN 1.32 s and 1.31 s; rig-side accept_live PASS (warm new chat ttft 0.93 s with 4 608 of 4 653 tokens restored, follow-up 0.8 s, the request behind an abandoned one 0.5 s, a reply finishes on its own). The earlier 147 s reading was taken on top of the quality benchmark and is void. The first swap attempt that morning failed and reverted cleanly: the start scripts still defaulted to a binary inside this tree, which the move to frankenstack/franken-engine emptied (fixed `25fe95c`). DeepSeek is done for L5. GLM back in service 04:58 UTC.

| chunk 256 | 18.52 | 68.5 |
| chunk 512 | 16.77 | 67.1 |
| chunk 512 | 16.84 | 66.2 |
| chunk 256 | 18.73 | 66.8 |

| part | result |
|---|---|
| MMLU-Pro | 58/70 = 82.9 % (Wilson 95 % CI 72.4-89.9); 12 misses: 8 used the whole 16 000 tokens without an answer, 4 finished wrong; 5/5 in 8 of 14 categories, weakest health 2/5 and other 2/5 |
| needle | 8/8 at 30 000 (293 s), 60 000 (589 s), 120 000 (1 311 s), 200 000 tokens (2 190 s) |

**Two setup faults found and fixed during the run.** (1) The first launch started the QWEN engine on the GLM file: the chain exported FRANKEN_BIN globally and `start_franken_glm.sh` read it (fixed `8d0962a`: per-engine variables). (2) `start_franken_glm.sh` capped the gateway at `--max-tokens 4096` (Qwen/DeepSeek: 16384): 3 of the first 29 answers stopped at exactly 4 096; fixed (`3a15629`), those 3 were redone, the 26 that stopped on their own stand.

**Why the misses are not GLM's quality.** Greedy decoding with thinking loops: the model's own `generation_config.json` samples at temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95. The earlier Colibri GLM run (f11, thinking OFF, median answer 82 tokens) scored 56/70 and got two of today's loop questions right in under 520 tokens. So this run measures the engine under greedy decoding, not GLM as designed.

**Reference arm cut to the failures.** llama.cpp's GLM (`serve_alt.sh glm-llama`) decodes at ~4 tok/s on this rig (first three answers: 794, 728, 210 tokens in 198, 179, 55 s, all correct) against the Franken engine's ~15: its full greedy arm would take ~17-20 h. It was stopped after 4 answers (4/4 correct, all shared with Franken's 4/4). Queue (`~/bench/seq_glm2.sh`, after the checkpoint gate): (1) the Franken arm SAMPLED (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95; the gateway rejects per-request seeds), 70 questions, `franken_glm_t1p95.jsonl`; (2) llama.cpp greedy on the 12 questions Franken missed (`mmlu_franken_glm_miss12.json`), `glm_llama_miss12.jsonl` -- engine parity on the failure mode. Budget-exhausted answers now keep their last 1 500 characters (`tail`), so a loop is seen, not guessed.

**Sampled pass (14:47-18:36 UTC, `chain_glm_sampled.log`, `franken_glm_t1p95.jsonl`): temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 as GLM-5.3-Flash's generation_config says, otherwise identical (70 questions, xhigh, 16k budget, no needle).**

| run | correct | 95 % CI | ran out of the 16k budget | finished wrong |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| greedy | 58/70 = 82.9 % | 72.4-89.9 | 8 | 4 |
| sampled | 60/70 = 85.7 % | 75.7-92.1 | 4 | 6 |

Paired on the same 70: 1 only greedy right, 3 only sampled right, McNemar exact p = 0.63 -- not distinguishable. Of the 8 greedy loops, sampling answered 7: 2 right (mmlu:11491 in 6 498 tokens, mmlu:6077 in 697), 5 finished WRONG (6127, 6214, 1701, and two more) -- questions GLM gets wrong when it does answer; mmlu:11881 ran out again. **The budget-exhausted answers are not repetition loops:** their saved tails (last 1 500 characters) are all-distinct text -- GLM re-deriving a diffusion coefficient from Chapman-Enskog (11881), or having written "B is the answer" and still second-guessing a garbled option (12171). They are overthinking at reasoning xhigh against a 16k budget, not an engine fault. **Verdict: GLM on the Franken engine scores ~83-86 % on this sample; greedy decoding cost ~2 points, well inside the noise; the remaining misses are the model's (and the budget's), weakest in "other" (2/5) and health/engineering (3/5).** **Engine parity (18:37-02:15 UTC, `chain_glm_llama_miss12.log`, `glm_llama_miss12.jsonl`): llama.cpp's GLM-5.3-Flash UD-IQ4_XS, greedy, identical settings, on the 12 questions the Franken greedy arm missed -- 1 of 12 correct.** llama.cpp: 6 ran out of the 16k budget, 5 finished wrong, 1 right (mmlu:6077, 355 tokens, where Franken greedy ran out of budget and Franken SAMPLED answered it right in 697 -- a greedy near-tie, the pattern of §L5-DS4-SERVE). Franken on the same 12: 8 out of budget, 4 wrong; 5 are out of budget in both engines; mmlu:11491's llama.cpp tail had written "I'll go with H" (the right answer) and kept reconsidering -- the same overthinking. **Verdict: the Franken engine's GLM misses are the model's misses; on its failures llama.cpp recovers at most 1 of 12, so llama.cpp's score on the full sample can exceed Franken's by at most ~1 question (the converse, Franken right where llama.cpp is wrong, was not measured: llama.cpp at ~4 tok/s would need ~20 h for all 70). GLM-5.3-Flash on the Franken engine: quality = llama.cpp's, at ~4x the decode speed.**
