Do not repeat it per card; a pair-level, time-aligned version would be needed.

**Next, in order.** (1) The clock question needs a test that moves a clock, and that needs root on the rig (`power_dpm_force_performance_level`, `pp_dpm_fclk/socclk/mclk`, or a lower shader-clock cap to leave the power budget to the fabric): pin the levels at their maximum and re-run masks 0 / 29 / 30 / 31 (A,B,B,A, with `gpu_sampler.py`). If the in-flight rate rises toward the skeleton's, the lever is a clock/power policy set when the service starts; if not, clocks are a bystander. Owner decision: it changes the GPUs' power management on the rig. (2) An m7 arm whose consumer kernels are shaped like the engine's trunk GEMM (the engine's `k_gemm_lds`) and the experts' kernel, beside the probe's copies, with the sampler: it says whether a GEMM beside its own card's DMA slows it outside the engine (hardware interaction, then CU masking / grid size / a lower tile rate are the levers) or not (then the engine's cross-card traffic is the cause). Needs a kernel harness (Opus tier). (3) Independently of the cause, the trunk GEMMs and the expert kernels are the two classes worth 2.3-2.5 ms a token each on the critical path.

**Addendum to §M7-SKIPCLASS -- what the literature and a copy-engine trace added (2026-10-06, 06:25-06:30 UTC; owner asked for outside sources before more probes).** *Web / GitHub search* (8 web queries, ~15 GitHub issue queries across ROCm/clr, ROCm/ROCm, ROCm/rocm-systems; reddit.com is not reachable by the search or fetch tools): **no public report of this symptom** (host-to-device copies slowing while kernels run). What the sources did give: (a) ROCR docs: `HSA_ENABLE_SDMA` defaults to 1 for every copy direction; (b) CLR `flags.hpp`: copies below `GPU_FORCE_BLIT_COPY_SIZE` (16 KB) go through a blit kernel, P2P below `ROC_P2P_SDMA_SIZE` (1 MB) too -- the staged copies (11.67 MB) are above both, the helper write-backs (40 KB a slot) below the second; (c) docs: `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES` defaults to 4 and streams beyond it share hardware queues round-robin (the engine has more than four a card; consistent with the 16-queue gain and the idle gaps, not with the in-flight rate loss; CU-masked streams get queues of their own); (d) ROCm issue legacy-rocm-build#6289 (RDNA4, gfx1201, SMU14): the power-management firmware does not boost GFXCLK for compute in any standard profile; the reporter's workaround is `power_dpm_force_performance_level=manual` + `pp_power_profile_mode=5` (COMPUTE) or `profile_peak` -- a different chip and symptom (their GFXCLK stays at 41 MHz; ours boosts to ~3 GHz), but the same family: DPM heuristics tuned for graphics. On this card the profile table (`pp_power_profile_mode`) lists per-profile FCLK parameters, index 5 = COMPUTE, active = 0 BOOTUP_DEFAULT, level `auto`. An overclocking forum ties SOCCLK to the memory-clock table, in line with the measured co-movement of mclk / fclk / socclk (weak source). *rocprofv3 trace* (`glm_rocprof_chain.sh`, mask 0, 1 536 tokens, 8.53 ms/token under tracing): **27 507 host-to-device memory-copy records (one per staged `hipMemcpyAsync`), against 881 `__amd_rocclr_copyBuffer` kernels totalling 6.7 ms** (plus 490 `fillBufferAligned`, 206 ms, the initial clears): the HIP runtime does not turn the staged copies into its own blit kernels. The trace cannot say whether ROCr executes them on the SDMA engine or on its internal blit queue (the copy records carry no engine); circumstantial for SDMA: never more than two of a card's three rings copy at once (§L5-GLM-TIMELINE), as with two copy engines (the engine count of Navi31 is from memory, not checked here). The copy CSV of this rocprofv3 has NO size column: `rocprof_summary.py`'s "<64KB / 0 GB" bin is an artifact of that, ignore it. *Kernel GPU time over the three chunks, summed over the three cards:* `k_glm5_moe` (all three tile variants) 11.2 s = 7.3 ms a token (2.4 a card), the trunk GEMMs (`k_gemm_lds` 2.49 s + `k_gemm_batch<8,1>` 1.29 s) **3.78 s = 2.46 ms a token -- equal to the 2.45 ms their removal took off the period** (the experts' per-card share, 2.4, likewise matches their 2.33): suggestive that the trunk GEMM time is serialised into the period instead of hidden behind the DMA, not a mechanism (tracing perturbs kernel times, and the link-busy shares of the class timelines are higher than a pure serialisation would leave); `k_glm5_head_gemv_q8` 0.76 s = 0.5 ms a token (6 % of the prefill) is a kernel nobody has looked at. **The clock test therefore has a documented form, reversible with `echo auto > power_dpm_force_performance_level`:** `echo manual > .../power_dpm_force_performance_level; echo 5 > .../pp_power_profile_mode` (COMPUTE), or `echo profile_peak > .../power_dpm_force_performance_level`, on the three cards, then masks 0 / 29 / 30 / 31 as A,B,B,A with `gpu_sampler.py`. Root on the rig.

*Second pass of outside sources (2026-10-06, after the owner asked for it):* the freedesktop `drm/amd` tracker (public API, searched with six queries) has two kernel-7.0 host-to-device regressions on this GPU family -- #5537 (gfx1100, `AMDKFD_IOC_SVM` returns EAGAIN in a loop, ~90x slower H2D from **mmap'd file pages**, closed 2026-07-29) and #5530 (RDNA4, ~1.96 ms per 4 KB page for H2D from a **copy-on-write file mapping**, 931x, open). Both state that H2D from anonymous host memory, pageable or **pinned**, is unaffected; the engine's mirror is `hipHostMalloc` memory, so neither explains the in-flight rate loss of §M7-SKIPCLASS. They are the evidence that 6.17 -> 7.0 changed amdkfd's host-memory handling (this rig: 7.0.0-38), so booting 6.17 is the one test that separates a kernel regression from the hardware (needs a reboot of the rig; not done). No report of the symptom itself was found on GitHub (ROCm/clr, rocm-systems), the amd-gfx archive, or via web search; Reddit is blocked to every tool available here (even through Jina's reader, 403 "network policy"). Agent Reach (Panniantong/Agent-Reach 1.5.0) was vetted (source read for dynamic code, credential access, outbound hosts: clean for what a pattern scan sees) and installed in `~/.agent-reach/venv` on the Mac from the vetted copy with its pinned constraints, no extras, no `--system`, no login channels; its zero-config tier (web through Jina, RSS, GitHub, V2EX, Bilibili) added nothing the existing tools lacked; Exa search would need a global npm install and was not set up.

## §L5-GLM-CHUNK (2026-10-06): **a 1024-row prefill chunk is 12 % faster than 512 (9.606 -> 8.433 ms/token, ranges separate); the engine capped chunks at 512 in four places, the DMA bytes per token fall as 1/chunk, and the fit P(chunk) = 7.26 + 1198/chunk ms/token says chunk size alone is worth at most ~24 %: the rest is compute**

*Why this was looked at (outside sources, after the owner asked for them):* Reddit r/LocalLLaMA "Drastically improve prompt processing speed for --n-cpu-moe partially offloaded models" (2026-05-12, gpt-oss-120b on one 3090, llama.cpp micro-batch `-ub`): 512 -> 380 tok/s, 2048 -> 1112, 4096 -> 1682, 8192 -> 2091; the thread's explanation (and ik_llama.cpp PR #520's math) is that a bigger micro-batch amortises streaming the offloaded expert weights over PCIe across more tokens. X posts (@0xSero GLM-5.3-Flash on one 3090, 600-800 tok/s prefill; @Vault_Dweller31 1457 tok/s with pinned-RAM experts) are consistent with it and unverified. In our engine every chunk copies ALL the staged experts (92.5 GB, routing-independent: §L5-GLM-TIMELINE), so DMA bytes per token = 92.5 GB / chunk, and the chunk was capped: `glm5_graph.cpp` `Tm_ = min(max_chunk, 512)` and the CLI check, `glm5_gpu.inc` `moe_reserve` ("a chunk is at most 512 rows") and the chunk-plan kernel's LDS array `sid[512 * 8]` (1024 rows = 32 KB of the 64 KB; 2048 would need the ids read from global memory). The record's own §14.3 list had "chunk 1024" as an untested item.

*Experiment:* franken-engine `main` (8256d53) with the four caps raised to 1024 (`ckpt1006/build_chunk1024.sh`, binary `franken_decode_glm_chunk1024`, sha256 `5f1865be89ec4dbd`; an experiment tree, not merged). Chain `glm_chunk_chain.sh`, one process, 8 192 prose tokens, **65 536 cells** (see below), staged, `--gemm-lds 1`, `--glm-stage-mb 400` in both arms, A,B,B,A, 07:14-07:45 UTC, `~/bench/franken/glm5/chunk2/`:

| chunk | prefill ms/token, A / B | mean | tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 9.546 / 9.666 | 9.606 | 104.1 |
| **1024** | 8.415 / 8.451 | **8.433** | **118.6** |

**-12.2 %**, ranges 9.55-9.67 vs 8.42-8.45 do not overlap; the 2 048-token smoke arm of chunk 1024 read 8.00 (two chunks, pipeline fill included). Fitting P(chunk) = a + b / chunk to the two means: b = 1 198, **a = 7.26 ms/token** (compute and serialisation that no chunk size removes); P(2048) = 7.85, P(4096) = 7.55. Chunk 1024 takes half of what chunk size can give; 2048 would add ~0.6 ms. The floor `a` is where the bisect of §M7-SKIPCLASS points: trunk GEMMs 2.45, experts 2.33, attention + indexer 0.49, KDA 0.11.

*Memory:* **chunk 1024 does not fit the 262 144-cell context with a 400 MB ring** -- the first attempt (ctx 262 144, chunk 1024, ring 400) died on `hipMalloc` of the ring on dev 2 (devs 0/1 had 862 / 948 MB free at the ring allocation). The per-chunk scratch doubles (~+300 MB for the helper contexts of the two other owners, about as much for the owner's own rows buffers: ~+600 MB a card) and 262 144 cells cost 3.3 GB a card of cache against 0.8 GB at 65 536. At 65 536 cells chunk 1024 + ring 400 leaves 1.25-1.63 GB free a card. Fitting 256k is the next step (smaller ring, then `--expert-gb`).

*Bit-identity (the design says a chunk row is exactly the decode step at its position, so chunk size must not move a bit):* so far `long1024s` -- layers 0-3, the 2 200 prose tokens as 1024 + 1024 + 152 rows (the top-512 indexer regime), against the existing gpu5 reference `g2200` -- **124 taps, 0 not exact**. The full-model comparison (chunk 512 dump vs chunk 1024 oracle) is pending: its first attempt faulted ("Memory access fault by GPU node-1 ... Page not present") in the plain chunk-512 reference run, which was the second config of a process whose first config had run a chunk-1024 runner; it was re-ordered (reference first) and re-queued, with a stock-engine run of the same config as the fallback. Not yet attributed.

*Rig housekeeping learned on the way:* a crashed engine holds 194 GB resident in `D` state for ~6 minutes while the kernel unpins (apport also attaches) and the crash evicts the model from the page cache, so the NEXT load reads cold (15+ minutes instead of ~4): a crash costs the next chain too. `docker kill` did nothing useful.

*256k fit (`glm_chunk256k_chain.sh`, 07:43-07:54 UTC, `~/bench/franken/glm5/chunk256k/r256/`):* **chunk 1024 fits the full 262 144-cell context with a 256 MB ring** (`--glm-stage-mb 256`, regions of 42.7 MB = 2 experts, `--expert-gb 17` as served; the 400 MB ring OOMed on dev 2 at this context), and it is still faster: chunk 512 with the auto ring (the served baseline) **9.462 / 9.596** (mean 9.529, 104.9 tok/s) against chunk 1024 **8.508 / 8.559** (mean 8.534, 117.2 tok/s), **-10.4 %**, ranges separate; the 2 048-token smoke arm read 8.173. The margin is thin: after the runner is built the cards have **0.63 / 0.72 / 0.35 GB free** (chunk 1024 + ring 256) against 1.61 / 1.70 / 1.26 GB for chunk 512 with the auto ring; the served process adds slot, checkpoint and snapshot buffers on top, so it has to be re-checked in the served configuration before this is called shippable (the `--expert-gb 16` fallback was not needed and did not run).

## §L5-GLM-MOEBLK (2026-10-06): **an assignment-blocked routed-expert kernel for prefill chunks is bit-exact and takes the 8 192-token prefill from ~9.0 to ~7.5 ms/token (-16 %, chunk 512); combined with the 1024-row chunk it stays bit-exact against the stock chunk-512 reference**

Commissioned from the skip-bisect (§M7-SKIPCLASS: the routed-expert GEMMs are 2.33 ms a token on the critical path, 11.2 s of GPU time over three chunks, rocprofv3) and the kernel read: `k_glm5_moe<TY>` has one wave per weight row and, for each of the expert's ~14 (chunk 512) or ~28 (chunk 1024) assignments, **decodes the row again and re-reads that token's whole 16 KB x row from L2**. An Opus agent (briefed to build only, no GPU) wrote `k_glm5_moe_blk<TY, G>` (franken-engine branch `moe-regblock`, commit `f6c69e5`, one file, +104 lines, binary `franken_decode_glm_moeblk` sha256 `396d0cff496dfdbf`): the same grid, the same one-row staging, the same early returns; the wave takes the expert's assignments in groups of G (default 4; a remainder runs as groups of G/2 ... 1; n = 1 keeps the old loop body; the decode path keeps the old kernel untouched) and calls the existing block-dot functions once per assignment on the same staged block, so the decode work is shared. `FRANKEN_GLM_MOE_G` = 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 (read once a process; 1 = the old kernel for chunks). **Bit-identity argument** (agent, then checked by the gate): per (row, assignment) the lane accumulates the same 256-weight blocks in the same order with the same arguments, then the same `wave_sum`; only the interleaving of independent chains changes. The agent checked the gfx1100 assembly for the PREFILL.md 8.1 fused-multiply-add trap: 8 FMAs per block per assignment in the old kernel and in every new variant, no fused op split. VGPRs (IQ3_S / IQ4_XS / Q6_K): old 45 / 51 / 48, G=4 82 / 89 / 86 (16 waves), G=8 126 / 131 / 126 (IQ4_XS over 128), G=16 up to 186; LDS unchanged, no spills.

**Gate:** the standard `emb` gate (`glm5_emb_chain.sh`, EMB_WT at the worktree), rc 0, the four exact configs against the gpu5 references: `c32s2` 1 788 taps / `c512s` 1 788 / `c512sad` 1 788 (adaptation verified) / `long512s` 124, **0 not bit-exact in all four**. **Timing**, pf2 config (8 192 tokens, 262 144 cells, chunk 512, staged, LDS GEMM, ring auto), two configs a process, one process a group size (`glm_moeblk_chain.sh`, 08:13-08:45 UTC): **G=1 (the old kernel) 8.861 / 9.127** (mean 8.994); **G=4 7.540 / 7.500** (first process) and 9.777 / 7.138 (the second process: the first arm is an outlier, the second the best seen); **G=8 7.461 / 7.433** (mean 7.447). G=4 and G=8 differ by less than the ±0.4 run-to-run spread; the default stays 4. **-16 to -17 % against the old kernel** at chunk 512. The gate's own prefill arms read 7.506 / 7.519 (default path) and 7.824 / 7.894 (old embedding-upload path) against 8.864 / 8.895 and 9.228 / 9.240 for the stock merged build in §FRANKEN-INTEGRATION (a different chain: not interleaved).

**Combined with the 1024-row chunk** (`build_comb.sh`: `moe-regblock` + the four cap changes of §L5-GLM-CHUNK, binary `franken_decode_glm_comb` sha256 `4b5900e3d811787a`; `glm_comb_chain.sh`): **the full model, 2 200 prose tokens + 8 greedy decode tokens at chunk 1 024, run FIRST in a fresh process against the saved stock chunk-512 reference: 1 788 of 1 788 taps bit-exact** (`ex1024`, 18.3 s). **Chunk-size bit-identity, answered:** the earlier divergence (1 652 of 1 788 taps, first at layer 4) is **not a chunk-size effect**. With chunk 1024 as the FIRST config of a fresh process it is exact (stock kernel: `c1024first` 1 788 / 0; blocked kernel: `ex1024` 1 788 / 0); every config that runs AFTER a runner of a different chunk size in the same process diverges, even a chunk-512 one (`c512sanity` 1 652 not exact, `c1024again` 1 652). So the engine carries state across `--gate-plan` configs when the chunk size changes (the per-card chunk buffers are only ever grown in `moe_reserve`, and other state is derived from the first size); the service runs one chunk size a process and is the clean case, but a test that mixes chunk sizes in one process must put the exact config first (or restart). Not root-caused. Also: the second config of the combined chain died on `hipMalloc` (the process still held the 400 MB ring of its first config; ring 256 + 262 144 cells did not fit beside it): a ring that differs between configs of one process is not supported at this headroom.

**Combined timing (`glm_comb_chain.sh`, 08:43-09:10 UTC, binary `franken_decode_glm_comb` `4b5900e3d811787a` = `moe-regblock` + the 1024-row chunk; the pf2 config at the SERVED context: 8 192 tokens, 262 144 cells, chunk 1024, ring 256 MB, staged, LDS GEMM, two configs a process, one process a group size):** **G=8 6.290 / 6.289 ms/token (159.0 tok/s), G=4 6.410 / 6.408 (156.0 tok/s)** (the first G=4 process died on its second config, the ring/headroom problem noted above; its first config is the bit-exact `ex1024`). Against the stock engine at chunk 512 with the auto ring at the same context (§L5-GLM-CHUNK 256k fit: 9.462 / 9.596, mean 9.529) that is **-32.7 % (G=4) and -34.0 % (G=8): 1.5x the prefill speed, 105 -> 156-159 tok/s**, bit-exact (all 1 788 taps against the stock chunk-512 reference with G=4; G=8 was not gated for exactness: the standard `emb` gate with `FRANKEN_GLM_MOE_G=8` is the check, G=4 stays the default). The two wins stack as the bisect predicted: the kernel -16 % at chunk 512 (§L5-GLM-MOEBLK), the chunk -10 % on top. After the runner is built the cards have 0.57 / 0.66 / 0.28 GB free (the same margin as chunk 1024 alone). Prefill is 6.4 ms a token: the remaining compute floor is the trunk GEMMs (2.45), the rest of the experts, attention + indexer (0.49).

**In the serving path (`glm_serve_chunk_chain.sh`, 09:10-09:53 UTC, `~/bench/glmserve_chunk/`):** the real gateway + engine per arm (`start_franken_glm.sh`; only `FRANKEN_DOCKER_BIN` and B's three knobs differ), one warm-up request, then three cold ~8.3k-token prompts (slices of three documents, greedy, 4 tokens), prefill ms/token = the engine's own `prefill_s / prompt`. A = the merged main (`franken_dec_glm.integ`, chunk 512, snapshots every 512, stock expert kernel), B = `franken_dec_glm.comb` (`484a017e3e7f9b81`: blocked experts + chunk cap 1024 + the serve cap; `FRANKEN_GLM_CHUNK=1024 FRANKEN_SNAP_EVERY=1024 FRANKEN_GLM_STAGE_MB=256`). **A 9.483 / 10.190 / 10.228 and 9.272 / 9.986 / 10.035 (17 chunks each, 76-85 s a prompt); B 6.936 / 7.307 / 7.340 (9 chunks, 57-61 s): means 9.866 vs 7.194, `gate_ab_verdict` SEPARATED, -27.1 % on means, -20.8 % conservative (worst against best).** The served numbers are above the CLI's 6.4 (checkpoint snapshots, gateway, adaptation) but the ratio holds. **VRAM in service:** after the long prompts the cards hold 24 439 / 24 526 / 24 539 MiB (B) against 24 074-24 077 MiB (A) of 26 368 MiB: about 1.8 GB free a card, so the 0.28 GB margin of the CLI plan (before slots and snapshot buffers) does not bite in the served configuration. The second B arm did not start: `docker: Error response from daemon: Conflict. The container name "/franken_engine" is already in use` -- the previous arm's container was still being torn down (minutes, the kernel unpins 144 GB) and the chain waited only 30 s for the process; the chain now waits until the container is gone, so the arms ran A, B, A (B bracketed, one sample of three prompts). Not yet done for shipping: `accept_live.sh` / `accept_ui.sh` on the candidate (the rig is reserved), the push, the start-script defaults.

## §L5-GLM-HGBLK (2026-10-06): **a token x row blocked MLA head GEMV is bit-exact and takes the combined prefill from 6.41 to 6.02 ms/token (-6 %, 166 tok/s)**

Third item of the compute list (the rocprofv3 breakdown of §L5-GLM-MOEBLK: `k_glm5_head_gemv_q8` 763 ms over three 512-row chunks summed over the cards = ~0.5 ms a prompt token). The kernel has one wave per weight row of `rows_total = n_heads * W.rows` and, for each of the T tokens, re-loads and re-decodes the row's Q8_0 blocks and re-reads that token's x row; rows of the same head re-read the same x rows. An Opus agent (build only, no GPU) wrote `k_glm5_head_gemv_q8_blk` (franken-engine branch `head-gemv-blk`, commit `f39b449` on top of `chunk1024`, one file +99 lines; `FRANKEN_GLM_HG_G` = 1|2|4|8, default 4, 1 = the old kernel; `FRANKEN_GLM_HG_R` = 1|2|4, default 2; both read once; T = 1 keeps the old kernel): each wave takes R adjacent rows of one head (R lowered until it divides the rows per head: 512 and 256 today, so never) and tokens in groups of G with a G/2 ... 1 tail. **Bit-identity argument:** per (row, token) the source is the old expression (start at +0.0f, `+= fk_q8_0_lane_dot(block b, ...)` ascending, the same `wave_sum`); the agent counted the gfx1100 assembly for all 9 (G, R) instances: per block old = 3 loads, 1 `v_cvt_f32_i32`, 1 `v_fma_mix_f32 d*q` (addend `neg(0)`, the exact product), 1 `v_fmac_f32`; new = R cvt + R `fma_mix` + R*G `fmac`, exactly 5 `add_f32` per pair for the wave sum, no first-block peeling that would turn `fma(.,.,0)` into a multiply. Loads per FMA 3 -> 2/G + 1/R (1.0 at G4/R2). VGPRs old 21, G4/R2 47, G8/R4 88; no spills, no LDS, 16 waves a SIMD. Scripts and listings: `/home/ronald/src/hgblk_asm/`.

**Gates (`glm_hgblk_chain.sh`, binary `franken_decode_glm_hgblk` `65782f25370a2f5b`, 09:53-10:18 UTC):** the FULL model, 2 200 tokens + 8 greedy, chunk 1024 as the first config of a fresh process against the saved stock chunk-512 dump: **1 788 of 1 788 taps bit-exact**; the standard `emb` gate rc 0, the four exact configs `c32s2` 1 788 / `c512s` 1 788 / `c512sad` 1 788 / `long512s` 124, **0 not exact in all four**. **Timing** (8 192 tokens, 262 144 cells, chunk 1024, ring 256 MB, staged, LDS GEMM, default G4/R2, two configs a process): **6.011 / 6.032 ms/token (166.4 / 165.8 tok/s)** against 6.410 / 6.408 for the same build without it (§L5-GLM-MOEBLK combined, G = 4): **-6.2 %**, from a different chain; the old-kernel (`FRANKEN_GLM_HG_G=1`), repeat and G8/R4 processes of the same chain were refused (`REFUSED: a card holds 19374 MiB`: the previous process was still unpinning; the chain refused instead of waiting, now fixed) and are re-queued as a timing-only run. **Prefill, all three together, against the stock engine at the served context: 9.529 -> 6.02 ms/token = -36.8 %, 105 -> 166 tok/s.**

## §L5-GLM-SHIPPED (2026-10-06): **the combined build passed the acceptance gate after one defect found and fixed (snapshot spacing at a 1024-row chunk); it is installed as the served binary, branches pushed, service still off**

*Acceptance, first candidate (`franken_dec_glm.hgblk` `5787268c4c2345d8` = blocked experts + 1024-row chunk + blocked head GEMV; `FRANKEN_GLM_CHUNK=1024 FRANKEN_SNAP_EVERY=1024 FRANKEN_GLM_STAGE_MB=256`; `glm_accept_chain.sh`, `accept_live.sh` run inside the chain against its own gateway log):* checks 5 (no max_tokens: `finish=stop`, 365 tokens), 3 (API follow-up: 147 of 170 reused, 2.4 s), 4 (behind an abandoned request: 3.6 s) and the ledger invariant PASS; **check 2 FAILED: a new chat reused 4 096 of 4 575 tokens (needs >= prompt - 256) and its first token took 4.04 s against 1.84 s and 4 548 reused on the old build.** Cause (`snap_points()` in `glm5_serve.cpp`): a snapshot point closer than `chunk_ / 2` to the previous one is dropped, 256 at chunk 512 but 512 at chunk 1024, so the turn-boundary snapshot at the end of the shared tool block (~4 548) lost to the multiple of `FRANKEN_SNAP_EVERY` at 4 096. **Fix** (franken-engine `glm-prefill-final` `a1362d2`, one line plus a comment): the gap is `min(chunk_ / 2, 256)`: unchanged for chunk <= 512, the worst reuse shortfall stays under 256 tokens.

*Acceptance, the final candidate* (`franken_dec_glm.final` `90f5e845306f79e0` = `glm-prefill-final`): **`accept_live` PASS (rc 0)**: new chat A cold 30.4 s for 4 573 tokens (the old build's cold chat read 41 s), **chat B warm: 4 548 of 4 575 reused, first token 1.86 s**, check 5 `finish=stop` 278 tokens, check 3 146 of 169 reused in 2.2 s, check 4 4.8 s, ledger 1 checked / 0 mismatch / 0 broken. **`accept_ui` in a real Chromium through Open WebUI: chat A 2.31 s, chat B 2.56 s to the first token on screen, both warm** (the run with the unfixed snapshot gap read A 4.83 s, B 12.88 s: the engine took 4.2 s for each; the extra ~8 s of B was Open WebUI's own time).

*Harness facts learned (they cost four runs):* `accept_ui.sh` refuses while any process named `run_chain.sh` is alive (it takes it for a measurement), so the acceptance chain takes the rig lock itself and runs directly; its rig-side step finds the gateway log through `serve_alt.sh status` and falls back to the stale `~/glm53_server.log` for a gateway that serve_alt did not start, then polls that log for up to 60 minutes (its verdict is meaningless there): `glm_accept_chain.sh` therefore runs `accept_live.sh` itself with `GLM53_LOG` set, and the caller kills the rig-side phase of `accept_ui.sh`. The chain moves `~/bench/.dev_reserved` aside only for the run and a trap always restores it (checked after every run).

*Shipped (later the same day the chain was fast-forwarded into franken-engine `main`: `8256d53..a1362d2`, Gitea and the rig's repo, temporary worktrees removed; the branches below remain on Gitea):* franken-engine branches pushed to Gitea as NEW branches, `main` was still at `8256d53` then: `moe-regblock` f6c69e5, `chunk1024` 42d7ddc, `head-gemv-blk` f39b449, `glm-prefill-final` a1362d2 (a linear chain). `~/bench/franken_bin/franken_dec_glm` (the served path) now holds `franken_dec_glm.final`; `franken_dec_glm.ckpt` (`15dd3595830f6620`, the previous served build, byte-identical to what was in the slot) is the one-line rollback and still runs under the new defaults (it clamps the chunk to 512). `start_franken_glm.sh` defaults: `FRANKEN_GLM_CHUNK=1024`, `FRANKEN_SNAP_EVERY=1024`, `FRANKEN_GLM_STAGE_MB=256`. **The service is still off** (the rig is development-reserved); when the owner asks for GLM back the new build comes up. Prefill at the served context: **9.53 -> 6.02 ms/token (-36.8 %, 105 -> 166 tok/s) in the engine, 9.87 -> 7.19 through the gateway on cold ~8.3k prompts (-27 %), all bit-exact against the stock path.**

## §L5-GLM-VERIFYCOST (2026-10-06): **speculative decoding (MTP) does not pay on this rig: a 3-row step costs 6.2x a 1-row step with the existing in-place chunk path (the break-even is ~2.5x); the probe also shows the staged prefill path is a fixed ~2 s tax on every short chunk**

Question: GLM-5.3-Flash's GGUF carries the NextN/MTP head (`glm5next.nextn_predict_layers` = 1, `blk.45.nextn.eh_proj / enorm / hnorm / shared_head_norm` in the last shard, found by reading the headers), and llama.cpp merged support for the GLM_DSA architecture (PR 25980: the head concatenates the embedding with the trunk's last hidden state through `eh_proj` and runs one full block, dense MLA + sigmoid-gated MoE + shared expert; cumulative acceptance 0.83 / 0.65 / 0.49 at draft positions 1-3, mean length 2.98, 1.37x on a VRAM-resident model; greedy MTP-on and -off outputs are quality-equivalent, not byte-identical, there). Our decode is bound by streaming MISSED experts, and verifying k+1 rows needs the UNION of their experts (token-to-token overlap 13-25 %, §L4-LOOKAHEAD-STEP0), so whether it pays is a measurement.

Probe (`glm_verifycost_chain.sh`, 16:58-17:06 UTC, binary `franken_decode_glm_hgblk`, one process, chunk sizes descending, two configs each, the same 256 prose tokens, `--glm-prefill-stage 0` = a chunk reads only the experts its rows pick, in place over each card's link, adaptation held, LDS GEMM on):

| chunk | ms per token (a, b) | step ms | step / chunk-1 step |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 32.9, 35.1 | 34 | 1.0 |
| 2 | 92.7, 91.4 | 184 | 5.4 |
| 3 | 71.4, 70.1 | 212 | 6.2 |
| 4 | 58.8, 58.7 | 235 | 6.9 |
| 8 | 49.6, 40.1 | 321-396 | 9.4-11.6 |

**Verdict: no.** With ~2.5 tokens a verify step (acceptance 0.83 / 0.65) the break-even step cost is ~2.5x the 1-row step; the existing chunk path costs 5.4-6.9x at 2-4 rows, i.e. MTP verified through it would DECODE SLOWER (3 rows: 212 ms for ~2.5 tokens = 11.8 tok/s against 29 tok/s for T = 1 at this depth). A purpose-built multi-row decode step could only approach the bandwidth bound of the union (about 2.4x the bytes of one row for 3 rows, so ~2.4x the time for ~2.5 tokens): break-even to +10 %, for a large change (a multi-row decode plan, KDA state rollback on rejection, the MTP block itself). Not worth building while decode is miss-bound; lookahead prefetch (§L4-LOOKAHEAD-STEP0, ceiling +27 %) is the better decode lever, and it needs no new model path.

**Side finding (the useful one): short chunks are expensive.** The unstaged chunk path costs 40-90 ms a ROW at 2-8 rows. The SERVED path stages ALL the missed experts for every chunk of more than one row (`--glm-prefill-stage 1`: the staged lists are routing-independent, 92.5 GB a chunk): a 23-row follow-up pays ~2 s of fixed DMA whatever its size, which is the 2.2-2.4 s of the accept_live follow-up check (23 new rows) and of every chat turn. Staging pays off for big chunks and loses for small ones: the next measurement is the crossover (staged against unstaged ms per token at 16 ... 256 rows) and a per-chunk policy (stage only above it; both paths run the same kernel on the same bytes, so the results are bit-identical).

## §L5-GLM-STAGECROSS (2026-10-06): **staging a chunk's missed experts is now a net LOSS at every chunk size: in place is 23-77 % faster at 16-256 rows and 4-7 % faster at the served 512-1024 rows**

Follow-up to §L5-GLM-VERIFYCOST's side finding. The served prefill stages ALL the missed experts of a layer into a VRAM ring by DMA for every chunk of more than one row (`--glm-prefill-stage 1`, 92.5 GB a chunk, routing-independent); `--glm-prefill-stage 0` reads only the experts the chunk's rows pick, in place over each card's link, with the same kernel on the same bytes. Staging was introduced as "4 % faster, bit-identical" (§L5-GLM-STAGE, chunk 512, the old expert kernel, swaps held); the blocked expert kernel (§L5-GLM-MOEBLK) and the 1024-row chunk changed the balance.

**Small chunks** (`glm_stagecross_chain.sh`, 17:08-17:16 UTC, `franken_decode_glm_hgblk`, 512 prose tokens, 65 536 cells, one process, sizes descending): ms per token, in place against staged: **256 rows 8.66 vs 11.20, 128 rows 12.16 vs 18.86, 64 rows 14.34 vs 34.64, 32 rows 20.63 vs 65.97, 16 rows 29.26 vs 129.62** (the staged step is a flat ~2.1-2.9 s whatever the chunk holds: the fixed copy of everything; in place scales with the experts the rows pick: 0.47 s at 16 rows, 0.92 s at 64). A 23-row chat follow-up therefore paid ~2 s of staging.

**Production sizes** (`glm_stageprod_chain.sh`, 17:18-17:28 UTC, 8 192 tokens, 262 144 cells, LDS GEMM, adaptation held, ring 256 MB for the staged arms, one process): chunk 1024 A,B,B,A **staged 6.007 / 6.051, in place 5.774 / 5.792 ms/token (173 tok/s): -4.2 %, ranges separate**; chunk 512 staged 7.510, in place 6.978 (-7.1 %, one pair). **Decision: serve with staging OFF** (`FRANKEN_GLM_PREFILL_STAGE=0`): ~4 % faster long prefill, short follow-ups ~1.5 s sooner, no ring to allocate (256 MB a card free), less machinery. Same kernel, same bytes, so bit-identical in design; gated below before it is the default.

**Staging turned off in service (2026-10-06 17:30-17:51 UTC): exactness, acceptance, and what the user sees.** *Exactness* (`glm_inplace_exact_chain.sh`, binary `franken_decode_glm_hgblk`): the FULL model, 2 200 tokens + 8 greedy decode tokens, chunk 1024, `--glm-prefill-stage 0`, first config of a fresh process against the saved staged chunk-512 dump: **1 788 of 1 788 taps bit-exact**; the standard small-chunk exact configs with staging off: `c32u` 1 788 / `c512u` 1 788 (136 tokens + 8 greedy against `gpu5/g136_eager`) and `long512u` 124 (layers 0-3, 2 200 tokens against `gpu5/g2200`), **0 not exact in all four**. *Default changed:* `start_franken_glm.sh` `FRANKEN_GLM_PREFILL_STAGE` 1 -> 0 (relayed to the rig); the installed `franken_dec_glm` is unchanged (`90f5e845306f79e0`).

*Acceptance on the INSTALLED binary with the shipped defaults only* (`glm_accept_chain.sh` no longer overrides any knob: chunk 1024, snapshots 1024, staging off, `[serve-glm5] glm_prefill_stage=0 chunk=1024` in the engine log): **`accept_live` PASS**: new chat A cold 28.4 s for 4 573 tokens (30.4 s with staging, 41 s on the old build); **chat B warm: 4 548 of 4 575 reused, first token 0.86 s (1.86 s with staging)**; no-max_tokens reply `finish=stop` 281 tokens; **follow-up turn 147 of 170 reused, 1.1 s total (2.2-2.4 s with staging)**; behind an abandoned request 2.0 s; ledger 1 checked / 0 mismatch / 0 broken. **`accept_ui` in a real Chromium through Open WebUI: chat A 1.05 s, chat B 1.05 s to the first token on screen** (2.31 / 2.56 s with staging, 3.6-3.8 s on 2026-09-09). So the user-visible gain of turning staging off is about 1 s on every new chat that hits the prefix cache and ~1.1 s on every follow-up turn.

*A fault found on the way, not in the engine:* the first `accept_live` of this run failed checks 1-3 with empty results and NO request from Open WebUI in the gateway log: Open WebUI answered `Model not found` (HTTP 400) for `glm-5.3-flash`. It caches its model list; the chain started the checks one second after the gateway came up, after hours with the gateway down. A person's page load refreshes the list; the chain now does it (`ckpt1006/owui_refresh.sh`: `GET /api/models` from inside the container with a minted admin token, waits until the model is listed) before `accept_live`. Rerun inside the held chain: PASS as above.
